definitions: Figuratively, to give the signal that an activity, event, or phase is starting.

examples.sentence: Con el anuncio oficial, se cantó el playball y la campaña publicitaria empezó con fuerza.
examples.translation: With the official announcement, the signal was given and the advertising campaign started strongly.

examples.sentence: Cuando el CEO cantó el playball para el nuevo proyecto, todos los departamentos se pusieron en marcha.
examples.translation: When the CEO gave the signal to start the new project, all departments got moving.

examples.sentence: No cantaron el playball hasta que todos estuvieron listos para comenzar la conferencia virtual.
examples.translation: They didn't give the signal to start until everyone was ready to begin the virtual conference.

definitions: A seductive, alluring appeal that tempts someone toward a choice that is ultimately dangerous or harmful.

examples.sentence: Los jóvenes a menudo caen en el canto de sirena de las modas pasajeras que prometen éxito rápido.
examples.translation: Young people often fall for the siren song of passing fads that promise quick success.

examples.sentence: No te dejes engañar por el canto de sirena de esas ofertas que parecen demasiado buenas para ser verdad.
examples.translation: Don't be fooled by the siren call of those offers that seem too good to be true.

examples.sentence: El canto de sirena de la fama fácil puede arruinar carreras si no se tiene cuidado.
examples.translation: The siren song of easy fame can ruin careers if one is not careful.

definitions: A persuasive but misleading appeal used in advertising, politics, or rhetoric; a siren call.

examples.sentence: La publicidad usó un canto de sirena para atraer clientes, prometiendo productos milagrosos.
examples.translation: The advertising used a siren call to attract customers, promising miraculous products.

examples.sentence: Durante la campaña electoral, muchos políticos lanzaron cantos de sirena para ganar votos sin cumplir promesas.
examples.translation: During the electoral campaign, many politicians made misleading appeals to win votes without fulfilling promises.

examples.sentence: El canto de sirena de ese político engañó a muchos, pero pronto se descubrió la verdad.
examples.translation: That politician's siren call deceived many, but the truth was soon uncovered.

definitions: Any irresistible but deceptive attraction or promise that can lead to ruin or error.

examples.sentence: El canto de sirena de las inversiones rápidas llevó a Carlos a perder todo su dinero.
examples.translation: The siren call of quick investments led Carlos to lose all his money.

examples.sentence: Ella ignoró el canto de sirena de la oferta de trabajo en el extranjero, sospechando que no era legítima.
examples.translation: She ignored the siren call of the job offer abroad, suspecting it wasn't legitimate.

examples.sentence: El canto de sirena de la fama puede hacer que artistas jóvenes tomen decisiones equivocadas.
examples.translation: The siren call of fame can make young artists make wrong decisions.

definitions: A very small margin or narrow difference; a hair's breadth.

examples.sentence: Perdimos el partido por el canto de un duro, fue una jugada increíble al final.
examples.translation: We lost the game by a hair's breadth; it was an incredible play at the end.

examples.sentence: Estuve a punto de ganar la carrera, pero llegué segundo por el canto de un duro.
examples.translation: I was about to win the race, but I came in second by a very small margin.

examples.sentence: La diferencia entre el éxito y el fracaso fue tan pequeña que parecía el canto de un duro.
examples.translation: The difference between success and failure was so small it seemed like a hair's breadth.

definitions: To be just short of or almost achieve something; to be on the verge of, but not quite reaching, a given outcome.

examples.sentence: Estuvimos cantando el canto de un duro para alcanzar la meta, pero al final no fue suficiente.
examples.translation: We were just short of reaching the goal, but in the end it wasn't enough.

examples.sentence: Si hubieras estudiado un poco más, no estarías cantando el canto de un duro en el examen.
examples.translation: If you had studied a little more, you wouldn't be just barely failing the exam.

examples.sentence: El equipo cantó el canto de un duro y quedó eliminado en la última ronda del torneo.
examples.translation: The team fell just short and was eliminated in the last round of the tournament.

definitions: The song traditionally (and mythically) attributed to a swan at the moment of its death.

examples.sentence: Según la leyenda, el canto del cisne se escucha justo antes de que el ave muera.
examples.translation: According to legend, the swan's song is heard just before the bird dies.

examples.sentence: Los biólogos nunca han podido confirmar la existencia real del canto del cisne en la naturaleza.
examples.translation: Biologists have never been able to confirm the real existence of the swan's song in nature.

examples.sentence: El canto del cisne es un mito que ha inspirado a poetas y artistas durante siglos.
examples.translation: The swan's song is a myth that has inspired poets and artists for centuries.

examples.sentence: Algunos creen que el canto del cisne simboliza una última expresión de belleza antes de la muerte.
examples.translation: Some believe the swan's song symbolizes a final expression of beauty before death.

definitions: A person's final work, performance, action, or achievement produced at the end of a career or life, often regarded as their last notable contribution.

examples.sentence: La última película del director fue su canto del cisne antes de retirarse del cine.
examples.translation: The director's last film was his swan song before retiring from cinema.

examples.sentence: Ella dio su canto del cisne con esa novela, que fue reconocida mundialmente.
examples.translation: She gave her swan song with that novel, which was recognized worldwide.

examples.sentence: El músico ofreció un concierto memorable como canto del cisne de su carrera.
examples.translation: The musician gave a memorable concert as the swan song of his career.

definitions: To maneuver a vessel so as to ride out or survive a storm; literally to weather a storm at sea.

examples.sentence: El capitán logró capear el temporal y llevar el barco a puerto seguro durante la tormenta.
examples.translation: The captain managed to weather the storm and bring the ship safely to port during the storm.

examples.sentence: Mientras el mar se embravecía, la tripulación capeaba el temporal con gran habilidad.
examples.translation: As the sea grew rough, the crew maneuvered to ride out the storm skillfully.

examples.sentence: No todos los marineros saben capear el temporal cuando las olas son tan fuertes como esas.
examples.translation: Not all sailors know how to weather the storm when the waves are as strong as those.

examples.sentence: El barco fue dañado, pero logró capear el temporal gracias a la experiencia del capitán.
examples.translation: The ship was damaged, but it managed to weather the storm thanks to the captain's experience.

definitions: To endure, manage, or get through a difficult period or crisis by taking temporary measures to reduce harm or buy time.

examples.sentence: Durante la crisis económica, la empresa capeó el temporal ajustando gastos y evitando despidos.
examples.translation: During the economic crisis, the company weathered the storm by cutting costs and avoiding layoffs.

examples.sentence: Tendremos que capear el temporal hasta que la situación política se estabilice.
examples.translation: We will have to endure the difficult period until the political situation stabilizes.

examples.sentence: No es fácil capear el temporal cuando todo parece estar en contra, pero hay que intentarlo.
examples.translation: It's not easy to get through the crisis when everything seems against you, but one must try.

definitions: An impassive facial expression that deliberately reveals no emotion, reaction, or inner thought, used to conceal one's intentions.

examples.sentence: María mantuvo cara de póquer durante toda la negociación, sin mostrar ni una pizca de emoción.
examples.translation: Maria kept a poker face throughout the negotiation, showing not a hint of emotion.

examples.sentence: ¿Cómo haces para tener esa cara de póquer cuando recibes noticias tan inesperadas?
examples.translation: How do you manage to have that poker face when you receive such unexpected news?

examples.sentence: Aunque estaba nervioso, Pedro logró mantener una cara de póquer para no dar pistas a sus rivales.
examples.translation: Although he was nervous, Pedro managed to keep a poker face so as not to give clues to his rivals.

definitions: A person who habitually maintains an expressionless face in order to hide feelings or strategic intentions.

examples.sentence: Lucía es conocida por su cara de póquer; nunca revela lo que realmente piensa en el trabajo.
examples.translation: Lucia is known for her poker face; she never reveals what she really thinks at work.

examples.sentence: Los jugadores profesionales desarrollan una cara de póquer para no mostrar sus emociones en la mesa.
examples.translation: Professional players develop a poker face so as not to show their emotions at the table.

examples.sentence: Juan mantiene una cara de póquer incluso en situaciones muy estresantes, lo que lo hace un negociador eficaz.
examples.translation: Juan maintains a poker face even in very stressful situations, which makes him an effective negotiator.

definitions: A sullen or downcast facial expression indicating sadness, disappointment, or displeasure.

examples.sentence: Después de perder el partido, se quedó con cara larga toda la tarde sin querer hablar con nadie.
examples.translation: After losing the game, he had a long face all afternoon and didn't want to talk to anyone.

examples.sentence: No traigas esa cara larga a la fiesta, todos queremos pasar un buen rato esta noche.
examples.translation: Don't bring that long face to the party, we all want to have a good time tonight.

examples.sentence: Vi a Ana con cara larga cuando le dijeron que no había aprobado el examen final.
examples.translation: I saw Ana with a long face when they told her she hadn't passed the final exam.

definitions: A state of being visibly displeased or gloomy; a mood marked by sulkiness or dejection.

examples.sentence: Desde que comenzó la discusión, Pedro ha tenido cara larga y no ha querido participar más.
examples.translation: Since the argument started, Pedro has had a long face and hasn't wanted to participate anymore.

examples.sentence: La cara larga de los empleados reflejaba la decepción por la cancelación del bono anual.
examples.translation: The employees' long faces reflected their disappointment over the cancellation of the annual bonus.

examples.sentence: No me gusta verte con esa cara larga; ¿quieres contarme qué te pasa?
examples.translation: I don't like seeing you with that long face; do you want to tell me what's wrong?

definitions: A decision-making method by flipping a coin (heads or tails).

examples.sentence: No pudimos decidir quién pagaba la cuenta, así que optamos por cara o ceca.
examples.translation: We couldn't decide who would pay the bill, so we went with heads or tails.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que lo decida cara o ceca? Así evitamos discusiones y será justo.
examples.translation: Do you want me to decide by heads or tails? That way we avoid arguments and it will be fair.

examples.sentence: Para elegir el equipo, hicimos un cara o ceca rápido entre los capitanes.
examples.translation: To choose the teams, we did a quick heads or tails between the captains.

definitions: To stake something on a fifty-fifty chance; to risk or gamble on an outcome that is left to chance, often used in contexts like 'double or nothing'.

examples.sentence: Decidieron apostar todo cara o ceca, confiando en la suerte para ganar el doble o nada.
examples.translation: They decided to bet everything heads or tails, trusting luck to win double or nothing.

examples.sentence: Al final, cargar el riesgo cara o ceca fue una decisión arriesgada que no salió bien.
examples.translation: In the end, staking the risk heads or tails was a risky decision that didn't turn out well.

examples.sentence: Cuando no tenían otra opción, los jugadores resolvían el empate con una apuesta cara o ceca.
examples.translation: When they had no other option, the players resolved the tie with a heads or tails bet.

definitions: A method of decision-making by flipping a coin, using the two sides (heads or tails) to determine an outcome.

examples.sentence: Para decidir quién pagaba la cena, hicieron un cara o cruz justo en la mesa del restaurante.
examples.translation: To decide who would pay for dinner, they flipped a coin right at the restaurant table.

examples.sentence: El entrenador decidió el orden de los jugadores con un cara o cruz antes del partido.
examples.translation: The coach decided the players' order with a coin toss before the game.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, se usó un cara o cruz para elegir al representante del grupo.
examples.translation: In the meeting, a coin toss was used to choose the group's representative.

examples.sentence: Cuando no pudieron ponerse de acuerdo, optaron por un cara o cruz para resolver la disputa.
examples.translation: When they couldn't agree, they chose a coin toss to resolve the dispute.

definitions: By chance or luck; an outcome that depends on random events or uncertain factors.

examples.sentence: El resultado del juego fue pura cara o cruz, nadie sabía quién ganaría hasta el último momento.
examples.translation: The game's result was pure luck; no one knew who would win until the last moment.

examples.sentence: A veces, aceptar un trabajo es cuestión de cara o cruz cuando las ofertas son similares.
examples.translation: Sometimes accepting a job is a matter of chance when the offers are similar.

examples.sentence: No podemos controlar todo; algunas decisiones son simplemente cara o cruz en la vida.
examples.translation: We can't control everything; some decisions are just chance in life.

definitions: A tie-breaking procedure in which a random binary choice determines who wins, who pays, or which option is selected.

examples.sentence: Para desempatar, hicieron un cara o cruz que definió quién pasaría a la siguiente ronda.
examples.translation: To break the tie, they flipped a coin that decided who would advance to the next round.

examples.sentence: Cuando tenían que elegir al jefe del comité, usaron un cara o cruz para evitar conflictos.
examples.translation: When they had to choose the committee leader, they used a coin toss to avoid conflict.

examples.sentence: El cara o cruz fue la forma rápida y justa de decidir quién se quedaba con el último puesto disponible.
examples.translation: The coin toss was the quick and fair way to decide who got the last available position.

definitions: An expression used to indicate that the result is unpredictable or could go either way.

examples.sentence: No podemos predecir el resultado, es un verdadero cara o cruz en este tipo de situaciones.
examples.translation: We can't predict the outcome; it's a real toss-up in these kinds of situations.

examples.sentence: La suerte es cara o cruz cuando se trata de encontrar trabajo en este mercado tan competitivo.
examples.translation: Luck is a toss-up when it comes to finding a job in this competitive market.

examples.sentence: Decidir si mudarse o no fue cara o cruz, porque ambos caminos tenían ventajas y desventajas claras.
examples.translation: Deciding whether to move or not was a toss-up, because both paths had clear pros and cons.

definitions: To shift blame or responsibility onto someone else; to make another person bear the consequences for an error, failure, or wrongdoing.

examples.sentence: No puedes cargar el muerto a mí por el error que cometiste en el informe financiero.
examples.translation: You can't shift the blame onto me for the mistake you made in the financial report.

examples.sentence: Los políticos suelen cargar el muerto cuando hay escándalos para evitar perder popularidad.
examples.translation: Politicians often shift the blame when scandals arise to avoid losing popularity.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, Carlos intentó cargar el muerto al equipo de ventas, pero nadie le creyó.
examples.translation: In the meeting, Carlos tried to shift the blame onto the sales team, but no one believed him.

definitions: To saddle oneself or someone else with an onerous burden, task, or obligation that is undesirable or unfair.

examples.sentence: No quiero cargar el muerto de ese proyecto fallido; prefiero asumir solo mis responsabilidades.
examples.translation: I don't want to saddle myself with the burden of that failed project; I'd rather take only my responsibilities.

examples.sentence: A veces, sin querer, cargamos el muerto de otros y eso termina afectando nuestra reputación.
examples.translation: Sometimes, unintentionally, we take on others' burdens and that ends up affecting our reputation.

examples.sentence: María está cansada de cargar el muerto en la oficina, siempre le asignan las tareas más difíciles.
examples.translation: Maria is tired of being saddled with the burden at the office; she is always assigned the hardest tasks.

definitions: To act with excessive severity or force; to be heavy-handed in punishment, criticism, or enforcement.

examples.sentence: El profesor cargó la mano al castigar a los estudiantes por un error menor en el examen.
examples.translation: The teacher was heavy-handed punishing the students for a minor mistake on the exam.

examples.sentence: No deberías cargar la mano con las críticas; un poco de apoyo ayudaría más que juzgar tan duramente.
examples.translation: You shouldn't be so harsh with the criticism; a little support would help more than judging so severely.

examples.sentence: Cuando vio que el niño rompió el jarrón, cargaron la mano sin preguntarle qué pasó realmente.
examples.translation: When they saw the child broke the vase, they acted with excessive severity without asking what really happened.

definitions: To add too much of something (figuratively), such as emphasizing a point to the point of excess.

examples.sentence: En su discurso, cargó la mano con los elogios hacia su equipo, y algunos pensaron que exageraba.
examples.translation: In his speech, he overdid the praise for his team, and some thought he was exaggerating.

examples.sentence: No cargues la mano al describir el problema; solo necesitamos los hechos claros y concisos.
examples.translation: Don't overemphasize the problem; we just need the clear and concise facts.

examples.sentence: Cuando María contó la historia de lo que pasó, cargó la mano un poco para impactar a sus amigos.
examples.translation: When María told the story of what happened, she exaggerated a bit to impress her friends.

definitions: To go too far in an action or reaction; to overdo or exaggerate in conduct or treatment.

examples.sentence: Creo que cargaste la mano al reaccionar tan mal por un simple malentendido.
examples.translation: I think you went too far in reacting so badly over a simple misunderstanding.

examples.sentence: Si sigues cargando la mano en las discusiones, terminarás alejando a todos.
examples.translation: If you keep overdoing it in arguments, you will end up pushing everyone away.

examples.sentence: No quiero cargar la mano, pero tu comportamiento fue completamente inapropiado en la reunión.
examples.translation: I don't want to exaggerate, but your behavior was completely inappropriate in the meeting.

definitions: To exaggerate, overstate, or dramatize facts or a narrative beyond what is warranted.

examples.sentence: En su artículo, el periodista cargó las tintas al describir el escándalo político, haciéndolo parecer peor de lo que realmente fue.
examples.translation: In his article, the journalist exaggerated the political scandal, making it seem worse than it really was.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando los escritores cargan las tintas en sus novelas para dramatizar la historia.
examples.translation: I don't like it when writers overstate things in their novels to dramatize the story.

examples.sentence: Durante la discusión, cargó las tintas para que todos creyeran que su versión era la única verdad.
examples.translation: During the discussion, he exaggerated to make everyone believe that his version was the only truth.

definitions: To make a harsher or more emphatic criticism or depiction than is justified; to unduly intensify an account.

examples.sentence: El crítico cargó las tintas en su reseña y destruyó injustamente la reputación del artista.
examples.translation: The critic made an unduly harsh review and unfairly destroyed the artist's reputation.

examples.sentence: A veces es mejor no cargar las tintas cuando se habla de los errores de los demás para evitar conflictos.
examples.translation: Sometimes it's better not to exaggerate when talking about others' mistakes to avoid conflicts.

examples.sentence: En su informe, cargó las tintas para enfatizar los problemas, aunque no todos eran tan graves.
examples.translation: In his report, he overstated the problems to emphasize them, although not all were that serious.

definitions: To cause someone to be eliminated, physically harmed, or killed; to get rid of someone by violent means (colloquial, often vulgar).

examples.sentence: Dicen que el capo se la cargó al rival en una pelea callejera para asegurar su territorio.
examples.translation: They say the boss took out his rival in a street fight to secure his territory.

examples.sentence: Si no te cuidas, alguien podría cargártela en cualquier momento en ese barrio peligroso.
examples.translation: If you don't watch out, someone could get rid of you at any moment in that dangerous neighborhood.

examples.sentence: En la novela, el antagonista se la carga a varios personajes para quedarse con la herencia familiar.
examples.translation: In the novel, the antagonist eliminates several characters to keep the family inheritance.

definitions: To destroy or ruin someone's reputation, career, or position; to orchestrate someone's removal or downfall by hostile or underhanded methods.

examples.sentence: El político corrupto se la cargó a su rival con acusaciones falsas para ganar las elecciones.
examples.translation: The corrupt politician ruined his rival with false accusations to win the elections.

examples.sentence: Después del escándalo, la prensa se la cargó al actor y su carrera quedó destruida.
examples.translation: After the scandal, the press destroyed the actor's reputation and his career was ruined.

examples.sentence: El jefe se la cargó al empleado que no estaba presente para cubrir su propia negligencia.
examples.translation: The boss pinned the blame on the absent employee to cover up his own negligence.

definitions: To cause someone to suffer adverse consequences generally, including punishment, dismissal, or serious trouble.

examples.sentence: Si no cumples con las normas, te la vas a cargar y podrías perder tu puesto de trabajo.
examples.translation: If you don't comply with the rules, you'll get into trouble and could lose your job.

examples.sentence: El estudiante se la cargó cuando fue sorprendido copiando en el examen final.
examples.translation: The student got punished when he was caught cheating on the final exam.

examples.sentence: No quiero cargármela por algo que no hice, así que mejor me mantendré al margen de ese problema.
examples.translation: I don't want to get into trouble for something I didn't do, so it's better if I stay out of that problem.

definitions: To frame or pin culpability on someone so that they suffer the consequences.

examples.sentence: El jefe se la cargó al empleado para evitar que la empresa sufriera las consecuencias legales.
examples.translation: The boss framed the employee so the company would avoid legal consequences.

examples.sentence: En la novela policiaca, el detective se la cargó a un sospechoso inocente para cerrar el caso rápido.
examples.translation: In the detective novel, the detective pinned the blame on an innocent suspect to close the case quickly.

examples.sentence: No me gustaría que me la cargaran por un error que cometió todo el equipo.
examples.translation: I wouldn't like to be framed for a mistake that the whole team made.

definitions: The physical substance of a living person or animal; flesh as opposed to bone, spirit, or incorporeal matter.

examples.sentence: El doctor explicó que el cuerpo está formado por carne y sangre, no solo huesos y órganos.
examples.translation: The doctor explained that the body is made of flesh and blood, not just bones and organs.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase de biología, vimos cómo la carne y sangre se encargan de transportar nutrientes.
examples.translation: During biology class, we saw how flesh and blood are responsible for transporting nutrients.

examples.sentence: La herida afectó la carne y sangre del brazo, por eso fue necesario realizar una cirugía inmediata.
examples.translation: The wound affected the flesh and blood of the arm, so immediate surgery was necessary.

examples.sentence: El soldado sufrió daños en la carne y sangre debido a la explosión cercana.
examples.translation: The soldier suffered damage to his flesh and blood due to the nearby explosion.

definitions: The bodily, material aspect of a human being.

examples.sentence: La estatua parecía real, pero no tenía carne y sangre, era solo mármol y metal.
examples.translation: The statue looked real, but it had no flesh and blood, it was just marble and metal.

examples.sentence: Para entender la fragilidad humana, debemos recordar que todos somos carne y sangre.
examples.translation: To understand human fragility, we must remember we are all flesh and blood.

examples.sentence: El robot era impresionante, pero carecía de carne y sangre, por eso no podía sentir emociones.
examples.translation: The robot was impressive, but it lacked flesh and blood, so it couldn't feel emotions.

examples.sentence: Es fácil olvidar que detrás de cada decisión hay carne y sangre con sentimientos reales.
examples.translation: It's easy to forget that behind every decision there is flesh and blood with real feelings.

definitions: One's own blood relatives; members of one's immediate family or kin.

examples.sentence: Mi hermana y yo somos carne y sangre, siempre nos apoyamos en los momentos difíciles.
examples.translation: My sister and I are flesh and blood, we always support each other in difficult times.

examples.sentence: Aunque vivan lejos, la familia es carne y sangre y siempre mantienen el contacto.
examples.translation: Although they live far away, family is flesh and blood and they always keep in touch.

examples.sentence: Nunca olvides que somos carne y sangre, no máquinas, y necesitamos comprensión y cariño.
examples.translation: Never forget that we are flesh and blood, not machines, and we need understanding and affection.

definitions: A reminder of human vulnerability and mortality; an expression used to emphasize that someone is a mere human being subject to error, pain, and physical limitations.

examples.sentence: El cantante se presentó ante su público como carne y sangre, mostrando sus emociones reales en el escenario.
examples.translation: The singer appeared before his audience as flesh and blood, showing his real emotions on stage.

examples.sentence: A pesar de su fama, sigue siendo carne y sangre, con sus propias debilidades y sueños.
examples.translation: Despite his fame, he is still flesh and blood, with his own weaknesses and dreams.

examples.sentence: La película mostró que incluso los héroes son carne y sangre, vulnerables y humanos.
examples.translation: The movie showed that even heroes are flesh and blood, vulnerable and human.

definitions: A person regarded as a direct descendant or close relation (equivalent to 'flesh and blood').

examples.sentence: Ese niño es carne y sangre de mi abuelo, tiene sus mismos ojos y sonrisa.
examples.translation: That boy is my grandfather's flesh and blood, he has the same eyes and smile.

examples.sentence: Cuando veo a mis sobrinos, siento que son carne y sangre, una extensión de mi propia familia.
examples.translation: When I see my nephews, I feel they are flesh and blood, an extension of my own family.

examples.sentence: No importa cuán lejos estén, la carne y sangre siempre mantienen un lazo especial e irrompible.
examples.translation: No matter how far they are, flesh and blood always maintain a special and unbreakable bond.

definitions: A contrast to the supernatural or mechanical, stressing corporeal, emotional, or mortal qualities.

examples.sentence: En la novela, el héroe era carne y sangre, no un ser sobrenatural, lo que lo hacía más cercano al lector.
examples.translation: In the novel, the hero was flesh and blood, not a supernatural being, which made him more relatable to the reader.

examples.sentence: Aunque la inteligencia artificial avanza, nada reemplaza la carne y sangre y la empatía humana.
examples.translation: Although artificial intelligence advances, nothing replaces flesh and blood and human empathy.

examples.sentence: El robot podía realizar tareas complejas, pero carecía de carne y sangre, por eso no entendía el dolor ni el amor.
examples.translation: The robot could perform complex tasks, but it lacked flesh and blood, so it didn't understand pain or love.

definitions: A reliable or guaranteed move, option, or resource expected to produce a successful outcome.

examples.sentence: Para ganar la partida, siempre llevo a Ana; es nuestra carta segura en momentos difíciles.
examples.translation: To win the game, I always bring Ana; she is our sure card in difficult moments.

examples.sentence: El equipo confía en Carlos porque es la carta segura para anotar goles cuando más se necesita.
examples.translation: The team trusts Carlos because he is the reliable option to score goals when most needed.

examples.sentence: En las negociaciones, María es la carta segura para cerrar tratos importantes con éxito.
examples.translation: In negotiations, María is the guaranteed card to close important deals successfully.

definitions: A safe bet or fallback strategy used to ensure achievement of an objective.

examples.sentence: Si el plan A falla, siempre tenemos a Luis como carta segura para salvar la situación.
examples.translation: If plan A fails, we always have Luis as a safe bet to save the situation.

examples.sentence: En esta campaña publicitaria, el influencer es nuestra carta segura para atraer clientes.
examples.translation: In this advertising campaign, the influencer is our safe bet to attract customers.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes por la presentación, tengo una carta segura que hará que todo salga bien.
examples.translation: Don't worry about the presentation, I have a sure option that will make everything go well.

definitions: The home of one's aunt (literal meaning).

examples.sentence: Pasamos el fin de semana en la casa de tía Carmen, disfrutando de su jardín y comida casera.
examples.translation: We spent the weekend at Aunt Carmen's house, enjoying her garden and homemade food.

examples.sentence: La casa de tía Luisa está en el campo y es perfecta para desconectarnos un rato de la ciudad.
examples.translation: Aunt Luisa's house is in the countryside and is perfect for us to disconnect from the city for a while.

examples.sentence: Cuando era niño, siempre me gustaba visitar la casa de tía Rosa porque tenía muchos juguetes.
examples.translation: When I was a child, I always liked visiting Aunt Rosa's house because she had many toys.

examples.sentence: La casa de tía Elena está decorada con muchas antigüedades que cuentan la historia familiar.
examples.translation: Aunt Elena's house is decorated with many antiques that tell the family history.

definitions: Informal expression for temporary lodging or childcare provided by a relative; a convenient or familiar place to stay.

examples.sentence: Durante las vacaciones, me quedé en la casa de tía para que mis padres pudieran viajar tranquilos.
examples.translation: During the holidays, I stayed at my aunt's house so my parents could travel peacefully.

examples.sentence: Cuando mi mamá tuvo que trabajar en la noche, fui a la casa de tía para que me cuidaran.
examples.translation: When my mom had to work at night, I went to my aunt's house so they could take care of me.

examples.sentence: Para facilitar las cosas, mis primos se quedaron en la casa de tía mientras arreglaban su casa.
examples.translation: To make things easier, my cousins stayed at my aunt's house while they fixed their home.

definitions: A relative's residence where someone stays temporarily.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano pasó unos días en la casa de tía mientras se recuperaba de la cirugía.
examples.translation: My brother spent a few days at my aunt's house while recovering from surgery.

examples.sentence: La casa de tía Marta siempre ha sido un refugio para la familia en tiempos difíciles.
examples.translation: Aunt Marta's house has always been a refuge for the family in difficult times.

examples.sentence: Cuando visitamos la ciudad, nos quedamos en la casa de tía porque es más cómoda y acogedora.
examples.translation: When we visit the city, we stay at my aunt's house because it's more comfortable and cozy.

examples.sentence: La casa de tía Isabel está cerca de la escuela, por eso mis primos suelen pasar ahí las tardes.
examples.translation: Aunt Isabel's house is near the school, so my cousins usually spend their afternoons there.

definitions: A colloquial way to refer to being hosted by family for visits, holidays, or short-term care.

examples.sentence: Pasamos las fiestas en la casa de tía, donde siempre nos reciben con mucho cariño y comida deliciosa.
examples.translation: We spend the holidays at my aunt's house, where they always welcome us with lots of affection and delicious food.

examples.sentence: Cuando los padres trabajan, muchos niños se quedan en la casa de tía para que los cuiden durante el día.
examples.translation: When parents work, many children stay at their aunt's house so they can be looked after during the day.

examples.sentence: La casa de tía es el lugar al que vamos para sentirnos en familia cuando estamos lejos de casa.
examples.translation: The aunt's house is the place we go to feel like family when we are far from home.

definitions: To marry abruptly or under pressure as a result of an unexpected event that creates a perceived need to wed (often used of a pregnancy or social emergency).

examples.sentence: Después de enterarse del embarazo, decidieron casarse de penalti para no tener problemas sociales.
examples.translation: After finding out about the pregnancy, they decided to marry abruptly to avoid social problems.

examples.sentence: No me parece que casarse de penalti sea la mejor opción, pero en su situación no tuvieron mucho tiempo para pensar.
examples.translation: I don't think marrying suddenly is the best option, but in their situation they didn't have much time to think.

examples.sentence: Cuando Ana se enteró del compromiso, supo que era un casarse de penalti más que una boda planificada con calma.
examples.translation: When Ana found out about the engagement, she knew it was more of a rushed marriage than a calmly planned wedding.

definitions: To marry at the last minute or opportunistically, analogous to scoring from a penalty kick—decisive, sudden, and prompted by circumstance rather than long deliberation.

examples.sentence: Se casaron de penalti justo antes de que naciera el bebé, sin haber planeado nada con anticipación.
examples.translation: They married at the last minute just before the baby was born, without having planned anything in advance.

examples.sentence: Aunque no querían, terminaron casándose de penalti por la presión familiar y social.
examples.translation: Although they didn't want to, they ended up marrying suddenly due to family and social pressure.

examples.sentence: El novio explicó que casarse de penalti fue una decisión tomada en medio del caos, pero con la mejor intención.
examples.translation: The groom explained that marrying abruptly was a decision made amid chaos, but with the best intentions.

definitions: To enter into a marriage as a hurried or forced solution to a sudden problem rather than as a planned union.

examples.sentence: Casarse de penalti nunca fue su plan, pero la situación los obligó a tomar esa decisión apresurada.
examples.translation: Marrying suddenly was never their plan, but the situation forced them to make that rushed decision.

examples.sentence: El matrimonio fue un casarse de penalti para resolver un problema inesperado que surgió en la familia.
examples.translation: The wedding was a hurried marriage to solve an unexpected problem that arose in the family.

examples.sentence: No recomiendo casarse de penalti, pero a veces la vida te pone en situaciones que no puedes evitar.
examples.translation: I don't recommend marrying abruptly, but sometimes life puts you in situations you can't avoid.

definitions: The hard outer shell of a nut (literal meaning).

examples.sentence: Para abrir la nuez, primero hay que romper la cáscara de nuez con cuidado.
examples.translation: To open the walnut, you first have to carefully break the nutshell.

examples.sentence: Los niños aprendieron en clase que la cáscara de nuez protege la semilla en su interior.
examples.translation: The children learned in class that the nutshell protects the seed inside.

examples.sentence: Después de comer las nueces, guardé la cáscara de nuez para usarla en manualidades.
examples.translation: After eating the walnuts, I saved the nutshell to use it in crafts.

examples.sentence: La ardilla recogió varias cáscaras de nuez vacías para construir su nido.
examples.translation: The squirrel collected several empty nutshells to build its nest.

definitions: Something very small, narrow, or insignificant; a tiny or cramped space or object.

examples.sentence: Este apartamento es una verdadera cáscara de nuez, no cabe ni una mesa más.
examples.translation: This apartment is a real nutshell, there's not even room for one more table.

examples.sentence: Aunque el negocio es pequeño, no lo subestimes por parecer una cáscara de nuez.
examples.translation: Although the business is small, don’t underestimate it for looking like a nutshell.

examples.sentence: Me siento atrapado en esta oficina que parece una cáscara de nuez durante todo el día.
examples.translation: I feel trapped in this office that feels like a nutshell all day long.

definitions: A small, insubstantial vessel or dwelling; used figuratively to denote limited size or importance.

examples.sentence: Su barco es una auténtica cáscara de nuez, apenas resiste el oleaje fuerte.
examples.translation: His boat is an authentic nutshell, it barely withstands strong waves.

examples.sentence: Viven en una cáscara de nuez en el campo, con pocas comodidades pero mucha tranquilidad.
examples.translation: They live in a nutshell in the countryside, with few comforts but a lot of peace.

examples.sentence: No esperes mucho de ese proyecto, es una cáscara de nuez comparado con la competencia.
examples.translation: Don't expect much from that project, it's a nutshell compared to the competition.

definitions: A concise summary or brief statement (corresponding to 'in a nutshell').

examples.sentence: En una cáscara de nuez, el informe explica los puntos principales del plan de negocios.
examples.translation: In a nutshell, the report explains the main points of the business plan.

examples.sentence: Para que lo entiendas en cáscara de nuez, el problema es falta de comunicación.
examples.translation: To put it in a nutshell, the problem is a lack of communication.

examples.sentence: El profesor resumió la lección en cáscara de nuez para que los alumnos no se confundieran.
examples.translation: The teacher summarized the lesson in a nutshell so the students wouldn’t get confused.

definitions: Almost; nearly; very close to being the case.

examples.sentence: Casi casi termino el proyecto, solo me falta revisar algunos detalles.

examples.sentence: Estuvimos casi casi a punto de ganar el partido, pero el último gol nos lo impidió.
examples.translation: We were very close to winning the match, but the last goal prevented us.

examples.sentence: Casi casi llueve ayer, pero al final solo hubo un poco de viento.
examples.translation: It almost rained yesterday, but in the end there was only a bit of wind.

definitions: An emphatic or tentative approximation meaning 'pretty much' or 'just about', used to soften or hedge a statement.

examples.sentence: Casi casi te diría que esta es la mejor opción, aunque no estoy seguro del todo.
examples.translation: I’d pretty much say this is the best option, although I’m not completely sure.

examples.sentence: No entiendo casi casi nada del tema, mejor me explicas otra vez con calma.
examples.translation: I pretty much don’t understand anything about the topic; better explain it to me again calmly.

examples.sentence: Casi casi parece que él quiere venir, pero no lo ha confirmado aún.
examples.translation: It pretty much seems like he wants to come, but he hasn’t confirmed yet.

definitions: Used as a filler to indicate that something is on the verge of happening or very nearly complete.

examples.sentence: Estoy casi casi listo para salir, solo me falta ponerme los zapatos.
examples.translation: I’m just about ready to leave; I only need to put on my shoes.

examples.sentence: La construcción de la casa está casi casi terminada, falta la pintura final.
examples.translation: The house construction is nearly finished; the final painting is missing.

examples.sentence: El examen está casi casi completo, solo me quedan dos preguntas por responder.
examples.translation: The exam is almost complete; I only have two questions left to answer.

definitions: To catch something in flight, such as a thrown object or an insect (literal).

examples.sentence: El niño logró cazar al vuelo la pelota que le lanzó su padre en el parque.
examples.translation: The boy managed to catch the ball in flight that his father threw at the park.

examples.sentence: Mientras caminaba, intenté cazar al vuelo una mariposa que pasó cerca de mí.
examples.translation: While walking, I tried to catch a butterfly in flight that passed near me.

examples.sentence: En la clase de biología, aprendimos a cazar al vuelo insectos para estudiarlos mejor.
examples.translation: In biology class, we learned to catch insects in flight to study them better.

examples.sentence: Para la competencia, los atletas deben cazar al vuelo los discos que se lanzan con rapidez.
examples.translation: For the competition, athletes must catch in flight the discs that are thrown quickly.

definitions: To grasp or understand something immediately and without deliberation; to pick up an idea or point on the spot.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, Marta logró cazar al vuelo todas las ideas y las sintetizó perfectamente.
examples.translation: During the meeting, Marta managed to grasp all the ideas immediately and summarized them perfectly.

examples.sentence: No hace falta explicar mucho, él siempre caza al vuelo lo que se le dice sin problemas.
examples.translation: No need to explain much; he always picks up on what is said immediately without problems.

examples.sentence: ¿Viste cómo cazar al vuelo ese concepto que mencionó el profesor? Fue impresionante.
examples.translation: Did you see how he grasped that concept the professor mentioned right away? It was impressive.

definitions: To seize an opportunity or make use of something quickly as it arises.

examples.sentence: Cuando apareció la oportunidad de trabajo, Laura la cazó al vuelo y no la dejó escapar.
examples.translation: When the job opportunity appeared, Laura seized it immediately and didn’t let it slip away.

examples.sentence: El empresario sabe cazar al vuelo cada chance que le da el mercado para crecer.
examples.translation: The businessman knows how to seize every chance the market gives him to grow.

examples.sentence: Si quieres tener éxito, debes aprender a cazar al vuelo las oportunidades que surgen.
examples.translation: If you want to be successful, you must learn to seize the opportunities that arise quickly.

definitions: To catch them in flight (literal), where 'them' refers to objects or creatures in the air.

examples.sentence: Los niños intentaron cazarlas al vuelo, pero las mariposas eran demasiado rápidas para ellos.
examples.translation: The children tried to catch them in flight, but the butterflies were too fast for them.

examples.sentence: En el campo, los agricultores cazarlas al vuelo para proteger los cultivos de plagas voladoras.
examples.translation: In the countryside, farmers catch them in flight to protect crops from flying pests.

examples.sentence: Durante el verano, es común cazarlas al vuelo para observar diferentes especies de insectos.
examples.translation: During the summer, it’s common to catch them in flight to observe different insect species.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano tiene mucha habilidad para cazarlas al vuelo cuando jugamos a atrapar objetos.
examples.translation: My brother is very skilled at catching them in flight when we play catch.

definitions: To seize opportunities, correct errors, or act upon chances immediately as they arise; to intercept or address problems on the spot.

examples.sentence: El profesor siempre cazarlas al vuelo los errores en los exámenes para corregirlos rápido.
examples.translation: The teacher always catches errors on the spot in exams to correct them quickly.

examples.sentence: Si quieres tener éxito en el negocio, debes cazarlas al vuelo las oportunidades que aparezcan.
examples.translation: If you want to succeed in business, you must seize opportunities as soon as they appear.

examples.sentence: El entrenador cazarlas al vuelo las faltas de la defensa para ajustar la estrategia al instante.
examples.translation: The coach intercepts mistakes in defense immediately to adjust the strategy on the spot.

definitions: A literal spoken instruction used when dictating or clarifying letters, indicating the letter 'c' is intended instead of the letter 'b'.

examples.sentence: Cuando dicté mi nombre por teléfono, dije 'ce por be' para que no me confundieran con la letra b.
examples.translation: When I spelled my name over the phone, I said 'ce por be' so they wouldn’t confuse it with the letter b.

examples.sentence: En la clase de ortografía, el profesor explicó que 'ce por be' significa que se debe escribir con c y no con b.
examples.translation: In spelling class, the teacher explained that 'ce por be' means you must write with c and not b.

examples.sentence: Cuando me preguntaron la letra correcta, respondí 'ce por be' para aclarar la confusión.
examples.translation: When they asked me the correct letter, I replied 'ce por be' to clear up the confusion.

examples.sentence: Para evitar errores al deletrear, siempre uso la expresión 'ce por be' cuando hay duda entre letras.
examples.translation: To avoid mistakes when spelling, I always use the expression 'ce por be' when there’s doubt between letters.

definitions: A jocular or ironic expression (rare) meaning a mistaken or clumsy substitution, used to indicate that someone has confused two similar items or concepts.

examples.sentence: Eso que hiciste fue un verdadero 'ce por be', confundiste los dos conceptos completamente.
examples.translation: What you did was a real 'ce por be', you completely mixed up the two concepts.

examples.sentence: No entiendo cómo cometiste ese error, parece un típico caso de 'ce por be'.
examples.translation: I don’t understand how you made that mistake, it seems like a typical 'ce por be' case.

examples.sentence: Al explicar el problema, me di cuenta que había hecho un 'ce por be' al usar los términos incorrectos.
examples.translation: When explaining the problem, I realized I had made a 'ce por be' by using the wrong terms.

definitions: A formula used to indicate a substitution of one grapheme for another in spelling or transcription contexts.

examples.sentence: En la transcripción, se indicó 'ce por be' para corregir la letra mal escrita en el documento.
examples.translation: In the transcription, 'ce por be' was indicated to correct the wrongly written letter in the document.

examples.sentence: El editor usó la fórmula 'ce por be' para señalar la sustitución de una letra en el manuscrito.
examples.translation: The editor used the formula 'ce por be' to indicate the substitution of a letter in the manuscript.

examples.sentence: Durante la revisión, señalaron 'ce por be' para aclarar que la letra correcta es la c y no la b.
examples.translation: During the review, they marked 'ce por be' to clarify that the correct letter is c, not b.

examples.sentence: Cuando dictamos textos, es común usar 'ce por be' para evitar confusiones entre letras similares.
examples.translation: When dictating texts, it’s common to use 'ce por be' to avoid confusions between similar letters.

definitions: A derogatory expression for a person perceived to have very little intelligence or mental capacity; literally, 'mosquito brain'.

examples.sentence: No seas cerebro de mosquito, piensa un poco antes de actuar de esa manera tan tonta.
examples.translation: Don’t be a mosquito brain, think a little before acting so foolishly.

examples.sentence: Me llamó cerebro de mosquito porque olvidé las llaves otra vez, pero lo dijo en broma.
examples.translation: He called me mosquito brain because I forgot my keys again, but he said it jokingly.

examples.sentence: Aunque a veces parezco cerebro de mosquito, en realidad puedo concentrarme cuando quiero.
examples.translation: Although sometimes I seem like a mosquito brain, I can actually concentrate when I want to.

definitions: A teasing or mildly affectionate rebuke for someone acting absentmindedly or making a trivial error, less harsh than the pejorative sense.

examples.sentence: ¡Ay, cerebro de mosquito! ¿Cómo pudiste olvidar la tarea en casa otra vez?
examples.translation: Oh, mosquito brain! How could you forget the homework at home again?

examples.sentence: No te preocupes, todos tenemos momentos de cerebro de mosquito cuando estamos cansados.
examples.translation: Don’t worry, we all have mosquito brain moments when we’re tired.

examples.sentence: No seas cerebro de mosquito y revisa bien las instrucciones antes de empezar el examen.
examples.translation: Don’t be a mosquito brain and carefully review the instructions before starting the exam.

definitions: An insult implying someone is scatterbrained, forgetful, or incapable of serious or original thought.

examples.sentence: Ese chico es un cerebro de mosquito, nunca sabe qué decir en las reuniones importantes.
examples.translation: That guy is a mosquito brain; he never knows what to say in important meetings.

examples.sentence: No me gusta trabajar con gente que tiene cerebro de mosquito porque no aportan ideas claras.
examples.translation: I don’t like working with people who have mosquito brains because they don’t contribute clear ideas.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que intenta resolver un problema, demuestra que tiene cerebro de mosquito.
examples.translation: Every time he tries to solve a problem, he shows he has a mosquito brain.

definitions: A person or thing regarded as irrelevant, powerless, or without influence; literally, 'a zero on the left'.

examples.sentence: En esa junta, sentí que era un cero a la izquierda porque nadie escuchaba mis opiniones.
examples.translation: In that meeting, I felt like a zero on the left because no one listened to my opinions.

examples.sentence: Aunque trabaja duro, en la empresa lo consideran un cero a la izquierda sin posibilidades de ascenso.
examples.translation: Although he works hard, the company considers him a zero on the left with no chances of promotion.

examples.sentence: No te sientas como un cero a la izquierda, tu aporte es importante para el equipo aunque no lo notes.
examples.translation: Don’t feel like a zero on the left; your contribution is important to the team even if you don’t notice it.

definitions: A self-description expressing feelings of worthlessness, ineffectiveness, or social exclusion.

examples.sentence: A veces me siento cero a la izquierda cuando mis amigos hablan sin incluirme en la conversación.
examples.translation: Sometimes I feel like a zero on the left when my friends talk without including me in the conversation.

examples.sentence: Después de tantos rechazos, empecé a pensar que soy un cero a la izquierda en todo lo que hago.
examples.translation: After so many rejections, I began to think I’m a zero on the left in everything I do.

examples.sentence: No quiero ser un cero a la izquierda en mi propia familia, necesito que me valoren más.
examples.translation: I don’t want to be a zero on the left in my own family; I need them to value me more.

definitions: Someone who is treated as insignificant or whose opinions or actions are disregarded.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, me sentí como un cero a la izquierda porque nadie tomó en cuenta mis ideas.
examples.translation: In the meeting, I felt like a zero on the left because no one took my ideas into account.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué siempre tratas a Laura como un cero a la izquierda? Ella también aporta mucho al equipo.
examples.translation: Why do you always treat Laura like a zero on the left? She also contributes a lot to the team.

examples.sentence: Aunque él trabajó duro, en la empresa era un cero a la izquierda y nadie valoraba su esfuerzo.
examples.translation: Although he worked hard, in the company he was a zero on the left and no one valued his effort.

definitions: To bring an action, process, or story to a conclusion in a way that returns to or resolves its point of origin; to complete a cycle.

examples.sentence: Después de años de búsqueda, finalmente cerré el círculo y encontré las respuestas que necesitaba.
examples.translation: After years of searching, I finally closed the circle and found the answers I needed.

examples.sentence: María quiere cerrar el círculo con su novela, terminando justo donde empezó la historia.
examples.translation: Maria wants to close the circle with her novel, finishing right where the story began.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar el círculo de este proyecto, debemos revisar los primeros pasos y asegurarnos de que todo encaje.
examples.translation: To close the circle of this project, we must review the first steps and make sure everything fits.

definitions: To close a literal or figurative circle in ceremonial or group contexts, meaning to finish or seal a collective action or rite.

examples.sentence: En la ceremonia, todos los participantes cerraron el círculo para simbolizar la unión del grupo.
examples.translation: In the ceremony, all the participants closed the circle to symbolize the group's unity.

examples.sentence: Al finalizar el ritual, los chamanes cerraron el círculo y sellaron la energía positiva.
examples.translation: At the end of the ritual, the shamans closed the circle and sealed the positive energy.

examples.sentence: ¿Podrías ayudarme a cerrar el círculo en la reunión? Quiero que todos terminemos juntos este proceso.
examples.translation: Could you help me close the circle in the meeting? I want us all to finish this process together.

definitions: To conclude an investigation, project, or personal journey by addressing unresolved elements and restoring continuity with the beginning.

examples.sentence: El detective cerró el círculo al encontrar al sospechoso que conectaba todas las pistas.
examples.translation: The detective closed the circle upon finding the suspect who connected all the clues.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar el círculo de su viaje personal, Ana volvió al lugar donde todo comenzó.
examples.translation: To close the circle of her personal journey, Ana returned to the place where it all began.

examples.sentence: El equipo de investigación cerró el círculo después de resolver los detalles pendientes del caso.
examples.translation: The investigative team closed the circle after resolving the pending details of the case.

definitions: A coarse imperative telling someone to be quiet; equivalent to 'shut up' but strongly obscene.

examples.sentence: ¡Cierra el orto y escucha lo que te estoy diciendo, por favor!
examples.translation: Shut the hell up and listen to what I'm telling you, please!

examples.sentence: Cuando comenzaron a pelear, el jefe les gritó que cerraran el orto inmediatamente.
examples.translation: When they started fighting, the boss shouted at them to shut the hell up immediately.

examples.sentence: No me importa tu opinión, mejor cierra el orto y deja de molestar.
examples.translation: I don't care about your opinion, better shut your damn mouth and stop bothering.

definitions: A literal, obscene phrase referring to closing someone's anus; used figuratively as a crude command or insult.

examples.sentence: El término 'cerrar el orto' es una expresión vulgar que literalmente significa cerrar el ano de alguien.
examples.translation: The term 'cerrar el orto' is a vulgar expression that literally means to close someone's anus.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, alguien usó la frase 'cerrar el orto' como un insulto muy fuerte y grosero.
examples.translation: In the meeting, someone used the phrase 'cerrar el orto' as a very strong and rude insult.

examples.sentence: Aunque la expresión tiene un sentido literal obsceno, suele usarse figuradamente para mandar callar a alguien.
examples.translation: Although the expression has a literal obscene meaning, it is often used figuratively to tell someone to shut up.

examples.sentence: Nunca pensé que 'cerrar el orto' fuera una frase común en ciertos grupos de amigos tan informal y ofensiva.
examples.translation: I never thought 'cerrar el orto' was a common phrase in certain groups of friends so informal and offensive.

definitions: An aggressive or insulting way to demand silence or to shut down someone's speech.

examples.sentence: Cuando la discusión se salió de control, Pedro le dijo a su hermano que cerrara el orto de inmediato.
examples.translation: When the argument got out of control, Pedro told his brother to shut the hell up immediately.

examples.sentence: No pude soportar más las críticas y le pedí que cerrara el orto para poder concentrarme.
examples.translation: I couldn't stand the criticism anymore and asked him to shut the hell up so I could concentrate.

examples.sentence: El entrenador cerró el orto a los jugadores para que se concentraran en el partido y dejaran de quejarse.
examples.translation: The coach shut the players up so they would focus on the game and stop complaining.

definitions: To block or obstruct a route or thoroughfare so that people or vehicles cannot continue through.

examples.sentence: Durante la protesta, la policía cerró el paso en la avenida principal para controlar a la multitud.
examples.translation: During the protest, the police blocked the passage on the main avenue to control the crowd.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes cerrar el paso a los vehículos mientras se realiza la reparación en la carretera?
examples.translation: Can you block the passage for vehicles while the road repair is underway?

examples.sentence: Los manifestantes cerraron el paso en la entrada del edificio para impedir la llegada de los directivos.
examples.translation: The protesters blocked the passage at the building entrance to prevent the executives from arriving.

definitions: To interpose an obstacle or barrier that prevents physical passage.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar el paso, colocaron una barrera de madera frente a la puerta del almacén.
examples.translation: To block the passage, they placed a wooden barrier in front of the warehouse door.

examples.sentence: El guardia cerró el paso con una cadena para evitar que alguien entrara sin permiso.
examples.translation: The guard closed the passage with a chain to prevent anyone from entering without permission.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, se cerró el paso en el puente debido a la caída de árboles y escombros.
examples.translation: During the storm, the passage on the bridge was closed due to fallen trees and debris.

examples.sentence: El municipio decidió cerrar el paso en ese callejón para mejorar la seguridad del barrio.
examples.translation: The municipality decided to close the passage in that alley to improve neighborhood safety.

definitions: To prevent reinforcements, supplies, or hostile forces from reaching a destination by sealing off approaches or cutting routes.

examples.sentence: El ejército cerró el paso para evitar que las fuerzas enemigas recibieran refuerzos.
examples.translation: The army blocked the passage to prevent enemy forces from receiving reinforcements.

examples.sentence: Durante la operación, lograron cerrar el paso a los suministros que podían llegar al campamento rival.
examples.translation: During the operation, they managed to block the supply routes that could reach the rival camp.

examples.sentence: Los soldados cerraron el paso a la zona estratégica para impedir que el enemigo avanzara.
examples.translation: The soldiers closed the passage to the strategic area to prevent the enemy from advancing.

definitions: To close a strategic line of movement in order to stop enemy movement or support.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar el paso, colocaron minas terrestres que cortaban cualquier intento de movimiento enemigo.
examples.translation: To close the passage, they placed land mines that cut off any enemy movement attempts.

examples.sentence: El comandante ordenó cerrar el paso en los caminos principales para controlar la zona de conflicto.
examples.translation: The commander ordered to close the passage on the main roads to control the conflict zone.

examples.sentence: Con la intención de cerrar el paso, colocaron barricadas y puntos de control alrededor de la ciudad.
examples.translation: With the intention of closing the passage, they placed barricades and checkpoints around the city.

definitions: To figuratively prevent or hinder the progress, access, or influence of an idea, person, or process.

examples.sentence: El comité decidió cerrar el paso a nuevas ideas que podrían desviar el proyecto original.
examples.translation: The committee decided to block the progress of new ideas that could divert the original project.

examples.sentence: Intentaron cerrar el paso a su candidatura, pero ella siguió adelante con mucha determinación.
examples.translation: They tried to block her candidacy, but she went ahead with great determination.

examples.sentence: En la empresa, cerraron el paso a cualquier propuesta que no cumpliera con las normas internas.
examples.translation: In the company, they closed the way to any proposal that did not comply with internal regulations.

definitions: To stop the flow of a liquid or gas by closing a valve, tap, or channel.

examples.sentence: Si quieres evitar que se escape el gas, debes cerrar el paso de la llave principal.
examples.translation: If you want to prevent the gas from escaping, you must close the main valve.

examples.sentence: Antes de reparar la tubería, cerraron el paso para detener el flujo de agua.
examples.translation: Before repairing the pipe, they closed the passage to stop the water flow.

examples.sentence: El técnico cerró el paso del líquido mediante una válvula especial para evitar derrames.
examples.translation: The technician stopped the flow of liquid by closing the passage with a special valve to prevent spills.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar el paso del aire, simplemente gira la manija hacia la posición de cerrado.
examples.translation: To close the airflow, simply turn the handle to the closed position.

definitions: To make it difficult or impossible for something to advance or gain entry.

examples.sentence: Los guardias cerraron el paso para que los manifestantes no pudieran entrar al edificio.
examples.translation: The guards blocked the way so the protesters could not enter the building.

examples.sentence: La policía cerró el paso para impedir que los ladrones escaparan de la zona.
examples.translation: The police closed the way to prevent the thieves from escaping the area.

examples.sentence: Se cerró el paso a cualquier intento de infiltración durante la vigilancia nocturna.
examples.translation: The passage was closed to any infiltration attempt during the night watch.

definitions: To shut off the passage of a substance through a conduit.

examples.sentence: Para evitar fugas, cerraron el paso del fluido en la tubería principal con un tapón hermético.
examples.translation: To avoid leaks, they shut off the flow of fluid in the main pipe with a tight plug.

examples.sentence: El operario cerró el paso del gas en la instalación para realizar el mantenimiento seguro.
examples.translation: The operator shut off the gas flow in the facility to perform safe maintenance.

examples.sentence: Es importante cerrar el paso del agua antes de cambiar el grifo para evitar inundaciones.
examples.translation: It is important to shut off the water flow before changing the faucet to avoid flooding.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar el paso del aceite, giraron la válvula hacia la posición de cerrado total.
examples.translation: To shut off the oil flow, they turned the valve to the fully closed position.

definitions: To tell someone to be quiet; to order or urge someone to stop talking in a blunt or rude manner.

examples.sentence: Cuando empezó a quejarse sin parar, le dije que cerrara el pico de una vez.
examples.translation: When he started complaining nonstop, I told him to shut his mouth once and for all.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes cerrar el pico durante la película? Estoy tratando de concentrarme.
examples.translation: Can you shut up during the movie? I'm trying to concentrate.

examples.sentence: El maestro les pidió a los alumnos que cerraran el pico para poder continuar con la clase.
examples.translation: The teacher asked the students to shut up so he could continue the class.

definitions: To refrain from speaking; to keep silent, either deliberately or out of prudence.

examples.sentence: Prefiero cerrar el pico y no opinar para evitar problemas con mis compañeros.
examples.translation: I prefer to keep my mouth shut and not comment to avoid problems with my colleagues.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, cerró el pico y escuchó atentamente sin decir nada.
examples.translation: During the meeting, he kept silent and listened carefully without saying anything.

examples.sentence: Si quieres mantener la paz, a veces es mejor cerrar el pico y no discutir.
examples.translation: If you want to keep the peace, sometimes it's better to keep your mouth shut and not argue.

definitions: To stop talking, often by forceful or abrupt command.

examples.sentence: El jefe cerró el pico a los empleados que hablaban durante la presentación importante.
examples.translation: The boss shut the employees up who were talking during the important presentation.

examples.sentence: Cuando empezó la discusión, alguien cerró el pico a Juan para evitar que siguiera insultando.
examples.translation: When the argument started, someone shut Juan up to prevent him from continuing to insult.

examples.sentence: No pude evitar cerrar el pico cuando escuché las tonterías que decían en la reunión.
examples.translation: I couldn't help but shut up when I heard the nonsense they were saying in the meeting.

definitions: To stop speaking or remain silent.

examples.sentence: Después de la discusión, decidió cerrar la boca y no responder más mensajes.
examples.translation: After the argument, she decided to stop speaking and not reply to any more messages.

examples.sentence: Cuando le preguntaron sobre el tema delicado, cerró la boca y evitó dar detalles.
examples.translation: When asked about the sensitive topic, he kept silent and avoided giving details.

examples.sentence: Para evitar problemas, Juan cerró la boca y no comentó nada durante la reunión.
examples.translation: To avoid problems, Juan stopped talking and didn't comment during the meeting.

definitions: To tell someone to be quiet in a curt or forceful way; to silence someone.

examples.sentence: El profesor le dijo a Pedro que cerrara la boca porque estaba interrumpiendo la clase.
examples.translation: The teacher told Pedro to shut his mouth because he was interrupting the class.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué no cierras la boca un momento y escuchas lo que te están diciendo?
examples.translation: Why don't you shut up for a moment and listen to what they are telling you?

examples.sentence: Para que la discusión no se salga de control, todos deberían cerrar la boca y calmarse.
examples.translation: For the argument not to get out of control, everyone should shut up and calm down.

definitions: To refrain from commenting or making remarks.

examples.sentence: Prefirió cerrar la boca y no hacer comentarios que pudieran empeorar la situación.
examples.translation: He preferred to keep silent and not make comments that could worsen the situation.

examples.sentence: A veces es mejor cerrar la boca y escuchar antes de juzgar a los demás.
examples.translation: Sometimes it is better to keep silent and listen before judging others.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, cerraron la boca para analizar la información sin interrupciones.
examples.translation: During the meeting, they kept silent to analyze the information without interruptions.

definitions: To close or heal an opening, such as the mouth of a wound, so that it is no longer open.

examples.sentence: Después de la cirugía, el doctor explicó que la herida cerró la boca rápidamente sin infecciones.
examples.translation: After the surgery, the doctor explained that the wound closed quickly without infections.

examples.sentence: La cicatriz indica que la boca de la herida se cerró correctamente tras la intervención médica.
examples.translation: The scar indicates that the wound's opening closed properly after the medical intervention.

examples.sentence: El veterinario dijo que la boca de la lesión en el animal cerraría en pocos días con el tratamiento adecuado.
examples.translation: The vet said the opening of the lesion in the animal would close in a few days with proper treatment.

examples.sentence: Con cuidados constantes, la boca de la herida terminó cerrándose sin dejar marcas visibles.
examples.translation: With constant care, the wound's opening ended up closing without leaving visible marks.

definitions: To seal an aperture or lesion, either naturally through healing or through medical intervention.

examples.sentence: Para evitar filtraciones, el técnico cerró la boca de la tubería con un sellador especial.
examples.translation: To prevent leaks, the technician sealed the opening of the pipe with a special sealant.

examples.sentence: La boca del agujero se cerró rápidamente después de que aplicaron el parche adecuado.
examples.translation: The opening of the hole closed quickly after they applied the proper patch.

examples.sentence: El cirujano cerró la boca de la herida con puntos para acelerar la recuperación del paciente.
examples.translation: The surgeon closed the mouth of the wound with stitches to speed up the patient's recovery.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar la boca del recipiente, colocaron una tapa hermética que evitaba la entrada de aire.
examples.translation: To seal the opening of the container, they placed an airtight lid that prevented air from entering.

definitions: To bring up the rear of a procession, convoy, column, or march; to occupy the last position in an organized movement.

examples.sentence: En el desfile, la unidad de voluntarios cerró la marcha para cuidar que nadie se quedara atrás.
examples.translation: In the parade, the volunteer unit brought up the rear to ensure no one was left behind.

examples.sentence: Siempre prefiero cerrar la marcha en las excursiones para ayudar a quienes van más lentos.
examples.translation: I always prefer to bring up the rear on hikes to help those who walk slower.

examples.sentence: Los bomberos cerraron la marcha después del contingente para verificar que todo estuviera seguro.
examples.translation: The firefighters brought up the rear after the contingent to verify everything was safe.

definitions: To conclude or finish an event, series of actions, or sequence; to serve as the closing element of an activity.

examples.sentence: El discurso del director cerró la marcha de eventos en la ceremonia de graduación.
examples.translation: The director's speech concluded the series of events at the graduation ceremony.

examples.sentence: Para cerrar la marcha de la conferencia, organizaron un concierto para los asistentes.
examples.translation: To finish the conference lineup, they organized a concert for the attendees.

examples.sentence: El último equipo cerró la marcha del torneo con una exhibición de habilidades impresionante.
examples.translation: The last team closed the tournament with an impressive display of skills.

definitions: To act as the unit or element that closes or follows at the end of a formation.

examples.sentence: El batallón de reserva cerró la marcha del ejército durante el desfile militar.
examples.translation: The reserve battalion acted as the unit closing the army's march during the military parade.

examples.sentence: En la formación, el vehículo blindado cerraba la marcha para proteger a los demás.
examples.translation: In the formation, the armored vehicle closed the march to protect the others.

examples.sentence: Los escoltas cerraron la marcha para garantizar la seguridad del convoy presidencial.
examples.translation: The escorts closed the march to guarantee the safety of the presidential convoy.

examples.sentence: El grupo de apoyo cerraba la marcha para asistir a cualquier persona que tuviera problemas durante la caminata.
examples.translation: The support group closed the march to assist anyone who had problems during the walk.

definitions: To keep one's lips closed; to remain silent.

examples.sentence: Durante la discusión, prefirió cerrar los labios y no revelar su opinión sobre el asunto.
examples.translation: During the discussion, he preferred to keep his lips closed and not reveal his opinion on the matter.

examples.sentence: Para no empeorar la situación, María cerró los labios y guardó silencio en la reunión familiar.
examples.translation: To avoid worsening the situation, María kept her lips closed and remained silent at the family meeting.

examples.sentence: Cuando preguntaron por el secreto, todos cerraron los labios para no delatar al grupo.
examples.translation: When asked about the secret, everyone kept their lips closed to avoid betraying the group.

definitions: To silence someone, either by persuading, intimidating, or preventing them from speaking, sometimes permanently.

examples.sentence: El jefe cerró los labios a todos los empleados cuando comenzó la reunión sobre el despido masivo.
examples.translation: The boss silenced all the employees when the meeting about the mass layoffs began.

examples.sentence: No pude decir nada porque ella me cerró los labios con una mirada intimidante.
examples.translation: I couldn't say anything because she silenced me with an intimidating look.

examples.sentence: Si quieres evitar problemas, mejor cerrar los labios sobre ese asunto delicado.
examples.translation: If you want to avoid trouble, it's better to keep silent about that delicate matter.

definitions: To refrain from speaking or making statements.

examples.sentence: Ante las preguntas incómodas, Juan prefirió cerrar los labios y no responder.
examples.translation: Faced with uncomfortable questions, Juan preferred to keep silent and not answer.

examples.sentence: Siempre me cierro los labios cuando no quiero dar detalles personales en público.
examples.translation: I always keep my lips closed when I don't want to give personal details in public.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué te cierras los labios cada vez que hablamos del futuro de la empresa?
examples.translation: Why do you keep silent every time we talk about the company's future?

definitions: To ensure that a person does not disclose information or speak about a matter.

examples.sentence: El abogado cerró los labios a su cliente para que no revelara detalles del caso.
examples.translation: The lawyer silenced his client so that he wouldn't reveal details of the case.

examples.sentence: Nos cerraron los labios con un acuerdo de confidencialidad muy estricto.
examples.translation: They made us keep silent with a very strict confidentiality agreement.

examples.sentence: No lograron cerrar los labios del testigo, que contó toda la verdad en el juicio.
examples.translation: They didn't manage to silence the witness, who told the whole truth at the trial.

definitions: To withdraw or retreat into the countryside or to a rural setting, often implying a deliberate removal from social life or public affairs.

examples.sentence: Después del escándalo político, el senador decidió cerrarse de campiña y alejarse del ruido de la ciudad.
examples.translation: After the political scandal, the senator decided to retreat to the countryside and get away from the city's noise.

examples.sentence: Si la presión en la oficina aumenta, tal vez me cierre de campiña para despejar la mente y recargar energías.
examples.translation: If the pressure at the office increases, maybe I'll withdraw to the countryside to clear my mind and recharge.

examples.sentence: Cuando María se jubiló, se cerró de campiña y comenzó a vivir en una pequeña finca en las montañas.
examples.translation: When María retired, she withdrew to the countryside and started living on a small farm in the mountains.

definitions: To become secluded or isolated from others, either physically by moving to a rural area or figuratively by cutting oneself off from social interaction.

examples.sentence: Desde que perdió contacto con sus amigos, Pablo se ha cerrado de campiña y apenas sale de su casa.
examples.translation: Since losing contact with his friends, Pablo has become secluded and hardly leaves his house.

examples.sentence: A veces me siento tan abrumada que solo quiero cerrarme de campiña y no hablar con nadie por un tiempo.
examples.translation: Sometimes I feel so overwhelmed that I just want to isolate myself and not talk to anyone for a while.

examples.sentence: No entienden por qué Juan se cerró de campiña después de la crisis familiar; ahora vive completamente aislado.
examples.translation: They don't understand why Juan shut himself off after the family crisis; now he lives completely isolated.

definitions: To adopt rustic, old-fashioned, or conservative habits and attitudes associated with rural life.

examples.sentence: Mi abuelo se cerró de campiña y empezó a usar ropa y costumbres de hace medio siglo.
examples.translation: My grandfather adopted rustic habits and started wearing clothes and customs from half a century ago.
