examples.translation: You can earn at least a hundred euros with that temporary job, though not much more than that.

examples.sentence: Cuando menos, deberíamos tener suficiente comida para todos los invitados esta noche.
examples.translation: At least, we should have enough food for all the guests tonight.

definitions: Used adverbially to mean "at the moment you least expect it" or "unexpectedly."

examples.sentence: Cuando menos te lo esperes, recibirá una oferta de trabajo que cambiará su vida.
examples.translation: When you least expect it, he will receive a job offer that will change his life.

examples.sentence: Estábamos tranquilamente en casa cuando menos, sonó el teléfono con malas noticias.
examples.translation: We were peacefully at home when, unexpectedly, the phone rang with bad news.

examples.sentence: Ella aparece cuando menos la necesitas, justo para complicar las cosas.
examples.translation: She shows up when you least need her, just to complicate things.

definitions: Indicates a conservative upper bound or maximum; meaning 'at most' or 'no more than'.

examples.sentence: Cuando mucho, tendremos que esperar dos semanas más para recibir el pedido completo.
examples.translation: At most, we will have to wait two more weeks to receive the full order.

examples.sentence: Puedes gastar cuando mucho 50 euros en regalos, no debemos excedernos este año.
examples.translation: You can spend at most 50 euros on gifts; we shouldn’t exceed that this year.

examples.sentence: El viaje durará, cuando mucho, tres horas si no hay tráfico en el camino.
examples.translation: The trip will last at most three hours if there’s no traffic on the way.

definitions: Functions as a hedge to downplay a statement, equivalent to 'if anything, at best'; implies the estimate is generous or unlikely to be exceeded.

examples.sentence: No es que sea un experto, cuando mucho soy un aficionado que ha leído algunos libros.
examples.translation: It’s not that I’m an expert; if anything, I’m an amateur who has read a few books.

examples.sentence: Cuando mucho, esa solución solo ayudará un poco, pero no resolverá el problema por completo.
examples.translation: At best, that solution will only help a little, but it won’t solve the problem completely.

examples.sentence: Puedes llamarme cuando mucho dos veces al día; necesito tiempo para concentrarme en el trabajo.
examples.translation: You can call me at most twice a day; I need time to focus on work.

definitions: Used to limit a quantity, duration, or degree to the speaker's estimate of the highest possible amount.

examples.sentence: Cuando mucho, la reunión durará una hora, así que no te preocupes por el tiempo.
examples.translation: At most, the meeting will last one hour, so don’t worry about the time.

examples.sentence: Podemos esperar cuando mucho cinco invitados más, ya que el espacio es limitado.
examples.translation: We can expect at most five more guests, since space is limited.

examples.sentence: Ella podrá correr cuando mucho cinco kilómetros hoy, porque no se siente del todo bien.
examples.translation: She’ll be able to run at most five kilometers today because she’s not feeling completely well.

definitions: A numeric expression equal to three quarters (3/4); literally 'a quarter and a half' (1/4 + 1/2 = 3/4).

examples.sentence: Para la receta necesitas un cuarto y mitad de kilo de harina para que la masa tenga buena textura.
examples.translation: For the recipe you need three quarters of a kilo of flour so the dough has a good texture.

examples.sentence: Compré un cuarto y mitad de pan porque éramos muchos en la cena y queríamos que alcanzara para todos.
examples.translation: I bought three quarters of a loaf of bread because there were many of us at dinner and we wanted it to be enough for everyone.

examples.sentence: El arquitecto utilizó un cuarto y mitad de las piezas disponibles para construir el muro principal.
examples.translation: The architect used three quarters of the available pieces to build the main wall.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, acordaron donar un cuarto y mitad del presupuesto a causas benéficas este año.
examples.translation: In the meeting, they agreed to donate three quarters of the budget to charitable causes this year.

definitions: An informal measurement phrase used in everyday speech or recipes to denote approximately three quarters of a unit.

examples.sentence: Pon un cuarto y mitad de taza de azúcar para que el pastel quede dulce pero no empalagoso.
examples.translation: Put three quarters of a cup of sugar so the cake is sweet but not too much.

examples.sentence: Cuando cocines arroz, usa un cuarto y mitad de litro de agua para que quede perfecto.
examples.translation: When you cook rice, use three quarters of a liter of water so it turns out perfect.

examples.sentence: La receta pide un cuarto y mitad de kilo de carne molida para preparar las albóndigas familiares.
examples.translation: The recipe calls for three quarters of a kilo of ground meat to prepare the family meatballs.

definitions: Used to indicate a proportion, fraction, or quantity corresponding to three quarters.

examples.sentence: En la encuesta, un cuarto y mitad de los participantes prefirieron la opción A sobre la B.
examples.translation: In the survey, three quarters of the participants preferred option A over B.

examples.sentence: Se estima que un cuarto y mitad del presupuesto se destinará a mejorar la infraestructura escolar.
examples.translation: It is estimated that three quarters of the budget will be allocated to improving school infrastructure.

examples.sentence: El 75% de la clase, o sea un cuarto y mitad, aprobó el examen final con notas sobresalientes.
examples.translation: 75% of the class, that is three quarters, passed the final exam with outstanding grades.

definitions: Refers to a very small number of people; a handful of attendees or participants.

examples.sentence: En la reunión solo había cuatro gatos, pero logramos avanzar con el proyecto.
examples.translation: There were only a handful of people at the meeting, but we managed to make progress on the project.

examples.sentence: Cuando fui al concierto, éramos cuatro gatos y el ambiente era muy íntimo.
examples.translation: When I went to the concert, there were very few people and the atmosphere was very intimate.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes por la fiesta, seguro que vienen cuatro gatos como siempre.
examples.translation: Don't worry about the party, surely only a small number of people will come as usual.

definitions: Can carry a dismissive or disparaging nuance, implying insignificance or lack of influence of the few people present.

examples.sentence: No vale la pena hacer caso a esa protesta, solo eran cuatro gatos sin influencia.
examples.translation: It's not worth paying attention to that protest, it was just a few insignificant people.

examples.sentence: La manifestación fue un fracaso; éramos cuatro gatos y no logramos nada.
examples.translation: The demonstration was a failure; there were only a handful of attendees and we achieved nothing.

examples.sentence: Dicen que quieren cambiar las reglas, pero son cuatro gatos que nadie escucha.
examples.translation: They say they want to change the rules, but they are a few people no one listens to.

definitions: Used to express that an event or group is sparsely attended or of little numerical importance.

examples.sentence: La conferencia estaba tan vacía que parecía que solo habían cuatro gatos interesados.
examples.translation: The conference was so empty it seemed like only a few people were interested.

examples.sentence: Aunque el equipo de voluntarios era cuatro gatos, hicieron un gran trabajo en la limpieza.
examples.translation: Although the volunteer team was just a handful, they did a great job cleaning.

examples.sentence: En la reunión de vecinos solo se presentaron cuatro gatos, así que no se tomaron decisiones importantes.
examples.translation: Only a few neighbors showed up at the meeting, so no important decisions were made.

definitions: A derogatory or teasing term for a person who wears eyeglasses; equivalent to English 'four-eyes.'

examples.sentence: En el colegio, los niños solían llamar 'cuatro ojos' a Pedro por sus gafas.
examples.translation: At school, the kids used to call Pedro 'four eyes' because of his glasses.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que me digan 'cuatro ojos', es un apodo que suena muy mal.
examples.translation: I don't like being called 'four eyes'; it sounds very bad.

examples.sentence: Aunque es solo una broma, a veces el mote de 'cuatro ojos' puede ser hiriente.
examples.translation: Although it's just a joke, sometimes the nickname 'four eyes' can be hurtful.

definitions: A descriptive, non-pejorative reference to someone who wears glasses, used in casual speech.

examples.sentence: María, la chica de cuatro ojos, siempre tiene los apuntes muy organizados.
examples.translation: Maria, the girl with glasses, always has her notes very organized.

examples.sentence: Le dicen cuatro ojos, pero él nunca se ha tomado mal el apodo.
examples.translation: They call him four eyes, but he has never taken the nickname badly.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, el cuatro ojos del grupo sugirió una solución muy acertada.
examples.translation: In the meeting, the glasses-wearer of the group suggested a very good solution.

definitions: Often used as an insulting nickname or taunt aimed at someone who wears spectacles.

examples.sentence: Los compañeros de clase no dejaban en paz a Luis y le decían cuatro ojos todo el tiempo.
examples.translation: The classmates wouldn't leave Luis alone and kept calling him four eyes all the time.

examples.sentence: Cuando llegó nuevo al barrio, le pusieron de inmediato el apodo de cuatro ojos.
examples.translation: When he arrived new to the neighborhood, they immediately gave him the nickname four eyes.

examples.sentence: No aguanto que me llamen cuatro ojos, es un insulto que me molesta mucho.
examples.translation: I can't stand being called four eyes; it's an insult that bothers me a lot.

definitions: Proverbial expression asserting that collaboration or having additional observers improves perception, judgment, or problem solving; similar to 'two heads are better than one.'
idiom: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

examples.sentence: Dicen que cuatro ojos ven más que dos, por eso siempre reviso mis informes con Ana.
examples.translation: They say two heads are better than one, so I always review my reports with Ana.
examples.matched_span: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

examples.sentence: Si tienes dudas, mejor pide ayuda, porque cuatro ojos ven más que dos.
examples.translation: If you have doubts, better ask for help, because two heads are better than one.
examples.matched_span: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

examples.sentence: En el equipo de trabajo aplicamos el dicho de que cuatro ojos ven más que dos para evitar errores.
examples.translation: In the work team we apply the saying that two heads are better than one to avoid mistakes.
examples.matched_span: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

definitions: Used to justify double-checking, teamwork, or consulting another person to avoid mistakes.
idiom: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

examples.sentence: No firmes ese contrato sin que lo revise alguien más, recuerda que cuatro ojos ven más que dos.
examples.translation: Don't sign that contract without someone else reviewing it; remember that two heads are better than one.
examples.matched_span: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

examples.sentence: Cuando planeamos el evento, dos personas lo organizan mejor porque cuatro ojos ven más que dos.
examples.translation: When we plan the event, two people organize it better because two heads are better than one.
examples.matched_span: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

examples.sentence: Siempre le pido a mi colega que revise mis cálculos; cuatro ojos ven más que dos, después de todo.
examples.translation: I always ask my colleague to check my calculations; two heads are better than one, after all.
examples.matched_span: cuatro ojos ven más que dos

definitions: A literal request to tell a story about cowboys or a Western-style tale.

examples.sentence: Anoche le pedí a mi abuelo que me cuente una de vaqueros antes de dormir.
examples.translation: Last night I asked my grandfather to tell me a cowboy story before going to sleep.

examples.sentence: En el campamento, los niños se reunieron alrededor del fuego para escuchar una de vaqueros.
examples.translation: At the camp, the children gathered around the fire to listen to a cowboy tale.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes contarme una de vaqueros? Me encantan esas historias del oeste.
examples.translation: Can you tell me a cowboy story? I love those Western tales.

examples.sentence: Durante el viaje, el guía narró una de vaqueros que mantuvo a todos atentos.
examples.translation: During the trip, the guide told a cowboy story that kept everyone attentive.

definitions: A dismissive or ironic remark used to indicate disbelief or to ask for an entertaining, fanciful story instead of a serious account.

examples.sentence: ¿De verdad crees que ganará la lotería? Cuéntame una de vaqueros, no te creo.
examples.translation: Do you really think you'll win the lottery? Tell me a tall tale; I don't believe you.

examples.sentence: Cuando me dijo que había visto un ovni, le respondí: 'Cuéntame una de vaqueros'.
examples.translation: When he told me he saw a UFO, I replied: 'Tell me a tall tale.'

examples.sentence: Si piensas que eso es posible, mejor cuéntame una de vaqueros para distraernos.
examples.translation: If you think that's possible, better tell me a tall tale to distract us.

definitions: An invitation to change the subject to something clearly fictional or lighthearted.

examples.sentence: Después de tanto hablar de problemas, Juan dijo: 'Bueno, cuéntame una de vaqueros para cambiar el tema'.
examples.translation: After talking so much about problems, Juan said: 'Well, tell me a tall tale to change the subject.'

examples.sentence: Cuando la reunión se puso tensa, Marta pidió a todos que contaran una de vaqueros para relajar el ambiente.
examples.translation: When the meeting got tense, Marta asked everyone to tell a tall tale to lighten the mood.

examples.sentence: No sabía qué decir, así que le pedí que me contara una de vaqueros para distraernos un rato.
examples.translation: I didn’t know what to say, so I asked him to tell me a tall tale to distract us for a while.

definitions: Fanciful calculations or plans based on hypothetical or uncertain future events; equivalent to 'counting your chickens before they hatch.'

examples.sentence: Estás haciendo cuentas de la lechera si crees que esa inversión te hará rico en un mes.
examples.translation: You're counting your chickens before they hatch if you think that investment will make you rich in a month.

examples.sentence: No hagas cuentas de la lechera con ese proyecto, todavía falta mucho para ver resultados.
examples.translation: Don’t make fanciful plans with that project; there’s still a long way to see results.

examples.sentence: Cuando planean sus vacaciones, siempre hacen cuentas de la lechera y luego se decepcionan.
examples.translation: When they plan their vacations, they always make fanciful calculations and then get disappointed.

definitions: Making optimistic assumptions about gains or benefits before they are secured.

examples.sentence: No cuentes tus ganancias antes de tiempo, no hagas cuentas de la lechera.
examples.translation: Don’t count your earnings before time, don’t make fanciful assumptions.

examples.sentence: Los vendedores hicieron cuentas de la lechera sobre cuántos productos venderían este mes.
examples.translation: The sellers made optimistic assumptions about how many products they would sell this month.

examples.sentence: Si sigues haciendo cuentas de la lechera, podrías acabar decepcionado cuando no se cumplan tus expectativas.
examples.translation: If you keep making fanciful assumptions, you might end up disappointed when your expectations aren’t met.

definitions: A dismissive expression meaning 'I do not believe you' or 'spare me that story,' telling the speaker to take their tale elsewhere.

examples.sentence: Me contó que ganó la lotería, pero le respondí: 'Cuéntaselo a Rita, que a mí no me creo eso'.
examples.translation: He told me he won the lottery, but I replied: 'Tell that to Rita, I don’t believe that.'

examples.sentence: Cuando escucho esas excusas, siempre digo: 'Cuéntaselo a Rita, que yo no me lo trago'.
examples.translation: When I hear those excuses, I always say: 'Tell that to Rita, I’m not buying it.'

examples.sentence: No te molestes en explicarme más, cuéntaselo a Rita si quieres que alguien te crea.
examples.translation: Don’t bother explaining more to me; tell that to Rita if you want someone to believe you.

definitions: Used to indicate incredulity and to reject a claim as implausible or unconvincing.

examples.sentence: Cuando dijo que terminó el trabajo en una hora, todos respondimos: 'Cuéntaselo a Rita'.
examples.translation: When he said he finished the work in an hour, we all responded: 'Tell that to Rita.'

examples.sentence: No voy a creer esa historia tan absurda, mejor cuéntaselo a Rita y déjame en paz.
examples.translation: I’m not going to believe that absurd story; better tell that to Rita and leave me alone.

examples.sentence: Ella me dijo que había visto un fantasma, pero le dije: 'Cuéntaselo a Rita, que no me asusta'.
examples.translation: She told me she saw a ghost, but I said: 'Tell that to Rita, I’m not scared.'

definitions: An implausible or fanciful story; a tall tale presented as true.

examples.sentence: Siempre cuenta un cuento chino cuando no quiere hacerse responsable de sus errores.
examples.translation: He always tells a tall tale when he doesn’t want to take responsibility for his mistakes.

examples.sentence: No le creas, eso es un cuento chino para evitar explicaciones.
examples.translation: Don’t believe him; that’s a tall tale to avoid explanations.

examples.sentence: Me contaron un cuento chino tan increíble que no pude evitar reírme.
examples.translation: They told me such an incredible tall tale that I couldn’t help laughing.

definitions: A fabricated account or excuse used to deceive, mislead, or distract someone.

examples.sentence: Su excusa fue un cuento chino para que no sospecháramos nada.
examples.translation: His excuse was a fabricated story so we wouldn’t suspect anything.

examples.sentence: Cuando le preguntaron por qué llegó tarde, soltó un cuento chino que nadie creyó.
examples.translation: When they asked him why he was late, he told a made-up story that no one believed.

examples.sentence: No te dejes engañar por ese cuento chino, todo es una mentira para distraerte.
examples.translation: Don’t be fooled by that fabricated story; it’s all a lie to distract you.

definitions: A dismissive label applied to information regarded as nonsense or unbelievable.

examples.sentence: ¿En serio vas a creer ese cuento chino que inventó para justificarse?
examples.translation: Are you seriously going to believe that nonsense he made up to justify himself?

examples.sentence: Para mí, todo ese discurso fue un cuento chino sin sentido ni pruebas.
examples.translation: For me, that whole speech was nonsense without sense or proof.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que intenta convencerme, sólo me dice cuentos chinos para confundirme.
examples.translation: Every time he tries to convince me, he just tells me nonsense to confuse me.

definitions: A cynical term for a scam, trick, or deliberate falsehood.

examples.sentence: Lo que ofrecían en esa promoción resultó ser un cuento chino para estafar a la gente.
examples.translation: What they offered in that promotion turned out to be a scam to cheat people.

examples.sentence: No caigas en ese cuento chino, es una trampa para robar datos personales.
examples.translation: Don’t fall for that scam; it’s a trick to steal personal data.

examples.sentence: La historia que contó sobre el premio fue un cuento chino para sacar dinero a sus amigos.
examples.translation: The story he told about the prize was a scam to get money from his friends.

definitions: The classical cornucopia, a mythological horn that symbolizes abundance and prosperity.

examples.sentence: En la pintura, el cuerno de la abundancia simboliza la prosperidad y la fertilidad.
examples.translation: In the painting, the cornucopia symbolizes prosperity and fertility.

examples.sentence: Durante la fiesta, colocaron un cuerno de la abundancia lleno de frutas y flores.
examples.translation: During the party, they placed a cornucopia full of fruits and flowers.

examples.sentence: El museo exhibe un cuerno de la abundancia antiguo que data de la época romana.
examples.translation: The museum exhibits an ancient cornucopia dating back to Roman times.

examples.sentence: El cuerno de la abundancia es un símbolo clásico que representa la riqueza y el bienestar.
examples.translation: The cornucopia is a classic symbol representing wealth and well-being.

definitions: A plentiful supply or source of plenty; anything that provides abundant resources, goods, or variety.

examples.sentence: La región tiene un cuerno de la abundancia en cuanto a recursos naturales se refiere.
examples.translation: The region has an abundant supply of natural resources.

examples.sentence: Este mercado es un verdadero cuerno de la abundancia para quienes buscan variedad de productos.
examples.translation: This market is a true cornucopia for those looking for a variety of products.

examples.sentence: El chef preparó un plato con ingredientes de un cuerno de la abundancia que impresionó a todos.
examples.translation: The chef prepared a dish with ingredients from a cornucopia that impressed everyone.

definitions: A command ordering people to drop to the ground immediately and lie flat in order to avoid incoming fire or danger.

examples.sentence: El sargento gritó '¡cuerpo a tierra!' justo cuando comenzaron los disparos.
examples.translation: The sergeant shouted 'drop to the ground!' just as the shooting started.

examples.sentence: Al escuchar la alarma, todos hicieron cuerpo a tierra para no ser alcanzados por las balas.
examples.translation: Upon hearing the alarm, everyone dropped to the ground to avoid being hit by bullets.

examples.sentence: Durante el simulacro de ataque, el instructor ordenó cuerpo a tierra a los cadetes.
examples.translation: During the attack drill, the instructor ordered the cadets to drop to the ground.

examples.sentence: El comandante insistió en que, ante cualquier amenaza, todos debían hacer cuerpo a tierra inmediatamente.
examples.translation: The commander insisted that, at any threat, everyone must immediately drop to the ground.

definitions: To take cover or go to ground; to hide or lie low to avoid detection or danger.

examples.sentence: Cuando vieron a la policía llegar, los manifestantes hicieron cuerpo a tierra para evitar arrestos.
examples.translation: When they saw the police arrive, the protesters took cover to avoid arrests.

examples.sentence: En la zona de conflicto, los periodistas aprendieron a hacer cuerpo a tierra para protegerse.
examples.translation: In the conflict zone, journalists learned to go to ground to protect themselves.

examples.sentence: Al percibir el peligro, el grupo hizo cuerpo a tierra hasta que pasó la amenaza.
examples.translation: Upon sensing danger, the group took cover until the threat passed.

definitions: To adopt a prone or flat position on the ground as an immediate protective measure.

examples.sentence: El soldado hizo cuerpo a tierra para protegerse del fuego enemigo que avanzaba rápido.
examples.translation: The soldier dropped to the ground to protect himself from the advancing enemy fire.

examples.sentence: ¡Cuerpo a tierra! gritó el oficial cuando comenzaron las explosiones cercanas.
examples.translation: 'Drop to the ground!' shouted the officer when the explosions started nearby.

examples.sentence: La gente hizo cuerpo a tierra en el parque cuando comenzaron a caer los fragmentos del edificio.
examples.translation: People dropped to the ground in the park when debris started falling from the building.

definitions: To be laid to rest in the earth; to be buried (used in literary or formal contexts).

examples.sentence: En el poema, describen cómo el héroe fue cuerpo a tierra tras la batalla final.
examples.translation: In the poem, they describe how the hero was laid to rest after the final battle.

examples.sentence: El escritor usa la expresión cuerpo a tierra para hablar de la muerte y el entierro.
examples.translation: The writer uses the expression 'laid to the ground' to speak about death and burial.

examples.sentence: Cuando alguien dice que fue cuerpo a tierra, puede referirse a haber sido enterrado.
examples.translation: When someone says they were 'laid to the ground,' it can refer to having been buried.

definitions: A playful or affectionate way to refer to a person's physical body, often highlighting its appeal or robustness.

examples.sentence: Después de meses sin verse, Laura le dijo a Carlos que extrañaba su cuerpo serrano.
examples.translation: After months without seeing each other, Laura told Carlos she missed his attractive body.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta todos admiraban el cuerpo serrano de la bailarina principal.
examples.translation: At the party, everyone admired the robust and appealing body of the lead dancer.

examples.sentence: Juan siempre se ha cuidado mucho para mantener su cuerpo serrano y saludable.
examples.translation: Juan has always taken good care of himself to maintain his fit and attractive body.

definitions: The physical body regarded as distinct from the soul; the corporeal self (used in reflective or literary contexts).

examples.sentence: En el poema, el autor reflexiona sobre la fragilidad del cuerpo serrano frente al paso del tiempo.
examples.translation: In the poem, the author reflects on the fragility of the physical body in the face of the passage of time.

examples.sentence: Durante la meditación, intenté separar el alma del cuerpo serrano para entender mejor mi existencia.
examples.translation: During meditation, I tried to separate the soul from the physical body to better understand my existence.

examples.sentence: El filósofo argumentaba que el cuerpo serrano es solo un vehículo temporal para el espíritu eterno.
examples.translation: The philosopher argued that the physical body is only a temporary vehicle for the eternal spirit.

examples.sentence: En la novela, la protagonista siente cómo su cuerpo serrano se debilita mientras su mente permanece fuerte.
examples.translation: In the novel, the protagonist feels how her physical body weakens while her mind remains strong.

definitions: An expression used to praise someone's attractive, well-formed physique.

examples.sentence: Cuando vi a Carlos en la playa, no pude evitar admirar su cuerpo serrano, tan definido y atlético.
examples.translation: When I saw Carlos at the beach, I couldn't help but admire his attractive, well-defined physique.

examples.sentence: María siempre presume de su cuerpo serrano porque entrena todos los días en el gimnasio.
examples.translation: María always boasts about her well-formed body because she trains every day at the gym.

examples.sentence: No es solo cuestión de salud, sino también de autoestima mantener un cuerpo serrano como el de Ana.
examples.translation: It's not just about health, but also self-esteem to maintain an attractive physique like Ana's.

definitions: An expression meaning that an event is inevitable and will occur after some time; only a matter of time.

examples.sentence: La llegada del invierno es cuestión de tiempo; pronto tendremos que preparar la casa para el frío.
examples.translation: The arrival of winter is just a matter of time; soon we’ll have to prepare the house for the cold.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que Juan logrará ese ascenso? Sí, es cuestión de tiempo antes de que lo consigan.
examples.translation: Do you think Juan will get that promotion? Yes, it’s only a matter of time before he achieves it.

examples.sentence: Aunque todavía no ha sucedido, es cuestión de tiempo que la verdad salga a la luz.
examples.translation: Although it hasn’t happened yet, it’s a matter of time before the truth comes out.

definitions: Something likely to happen soon or eventually, the timing being the only remaining uncertainty.

examples.sentence: Con la economía mejorando paulatinamente, es cuestión de tiempo que los empleos aumenten.
examples.translation: With the economy gradually improving, it’s likely that jobs will increase soon.

examples.sentence: El lanzamiento del nuevo producto es cuestión de tiempo; solo falta ultimar algunos detalles.
examples.translation: The launch of the new product is imminent; just some final details remain.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes, la oportunidad que esperas es cuestión de tiempo para que llegue a ti.
examples.translation: Don’t worry, the opportunity you’re waiting for is likely to come to you soon.

definitions: A crude expression for a very remote, isolated, or hard-to-reach place; the middle of nowhere.

examples.sentence: Nos tocó acampar en el culo del mundo, sin señal ni tiendas cerca, pero la experiencia valió la pena.
examples.translation: We had to camp in the middle of nowhere, without signal or stores nearby, but the experience was worth it.

examples.sentence: La cabaña de mi abuelo está en el culo del mundo, tan aislada que solo llegas después de horas en coche.
examples.translation: My grandfather’s cabin is in the middle of nowhere, so isolated you only get there after hours by car.

examples.sentence: Para llegar a ese pueblo remoto, tienes que atravesar caminos que parecen llevar al culo del mundo.
examples.translation: To get to that remote village, you have to cross roads that seem to lead to the middle of nowhere.

definitions: A dismissive way to describe a place perceived as insignificant, backward, or inconveniently distant.

examples.sentence: No quiero vivir en ese pueblo; está en el culo del mundo y no tiene nada que ofrecer.
examples.translation: I don’t want to live in that town; it’s in the middle of nowhere and has nothing to offer.

examples.sentence: La oficina está en el culo del mundo, lejos de todo, lo que complica mucho el transporte de los empleados.
examples.translation: The office is in the middle of nowhere, far from everything, which makes employee transportation difficult.

examples.sentence: Para las grandes empresas, ese mercado es el culo del mundo, sin potencial ni desarrollo.
examples.translation: For big companies, that market is the middle of nowhere, with no potential or development.

definitions: A person who is restless or unable to stay in one place; someone who frequently moves, travels, or changes activities.

examples.sentence: No puede quedarse quieto ni un segundo; siempre fue un culo inquieto, viajando de un lugar a otro.
examples.translation: He can’t stay still for a second; he has always been restless, traveling from one place to another.

examples.sentence: María es un culo inquieto que no para de buscar nuevas aventuras y proyectos en los que involucrarse.
examples.translation: María is restless and never stops looking for new adventures and projects to get involved in.

examples.sentence: Aunque terminó la universidad, sigue siendo un culo inquieto y ya planea su próximo viaje al extranjero.
examples.translation: Even after finishing university, he remains restless and is already planning his next trip abroad.

definitions: A derogatory term for someone perceived as sexually restless or promiscuous; sexually impulsive.

examples.sentence: Pedro tiene fama de culo inquieto; nunca se queda con la misma pareja por mucho tiempo.
examples.translation: Pedro is known as being sexually restless; he never stays with the same partner for long.

examples.sentence: No me sorprende que Carla haya terminado con él; dicen que es un culo inquieto y no sabe comprometerse.
examples.translation: I’m not surprised Carla broke up with him; they say he’s promiscuous and can’t commit.

examples.sentence: No quiero juzgar, pero parece que Juan es un culo inquieto y no se conforma con relaciones serias.
examples.translation: I don’t want to judge, but it seems Juan is sexually impulsive and doesn’t settle for serious relationships.

definitions: Someone prone to constant activity, change, or adventure; a habitual wanderer or drifter.

examples.sentence: Como un verdadero culo inquieto, Andrés ha vivido en cinco países diferentes en los últimos diez años.
examples.translation: Like a true restless wanderer, Andrés has lived in five different countries in the last ten years.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano es un culo inquieto que siempre busca cambiar de trabajo y ciudad para no aburrirse.
examples.translation: My brother is someone prone to constant activity who always looks to change jobs and cities to avoid boredom.

examples.sentence: No se puede negar que Luisa es un culo inquieto; cada mes tiene una nueva afición o proyecto en marcha.
examples.translation: There’s no denying that Luisa is constantly active; every month she has a new hobby or project going on.

definitions: To take precautionary measures in order to avoid possible harm or risk; to act preventively even if the danger is uncertain.

examples.sentence: Para curarse en salud, Marta siempre lleva un paraguas aunque el pronóstico indique sol.
examples.translation: To be safe, Marta always carries an umbrella even if the forecast says it will be sunny.

examples.sentence: Nos curamos en salud instalando alarmas de seguridad antes de que ocurriera algún robo en el edificio.
examples.translation: We took precautionary measures by installing security alarms before any robbery happened in the building.

examples.sentence: Aunque no parecía necesario, decidieron curarse en salud y revisar dos veces todos los documentos legales.
examples.translation: Although it didn’t seem necessary, they decided to act preventively and double-check all the legal documents.

definitions: To take steps intended to cover oneself legally, reputationally, or procedurally so as to avoid blame or liability.

examples.sentence: El abogado recomendó curarse en salud y guardar todas las pruebas en caso de futuras demandas.
examples.translation: The lawyer recommended covering themselves legally and keeping all evidence in case of future lawsuits.

examples.sentence: Para curarse en salud, la empresa documentó cada paso del proceso para evitar responsabilidades.
examples.translation: To protect itself, the company documented every step of the process to avoid liabilities.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre se cura en salud enviando correos confirmando las reuniones y acuerdos por escrito.
examples.translation: She always protects herself by sending emails confirming meetings and agreements in writing.

definitions: To protect oneself in advance against future problems by adopting conservative or defensive actions.

examples.sentence: Para curarse en salud, el entrenador hizo que todos los jugadores se sometieran a chequeos médicos antes del torneo.
examples.translation: To avoid future problems, the coach made all players undergo medical check-ups before the tournament.

examples.sentence: Aunque el clima parecía estable, decidieron curarse en salud y preparar el equipo para posibles tormentas.
examples.translation: Although the weather seemed stable, they decided to act cautiously and prepare the equipment for possible storms.

examples.sentence: El director curó en salud solicitando un informe detallado para anticipar cualquier inconveniente en el proyecto.
examples.translation: The manager protected himself in advance by requesting a detailed report to anticipate any issues in the project.

definitions: To adopt a precautionary or redundant measure as a safeguard, often out of caution or suspicion rather than necessity.

examples.sentence: Aunque parecía exagerado, el comité decidió curarse en salud y contratar seguridad extra para el evento.
examples.translation: Although it seemed excessive, the committee decided to err on the side of caution and hire extra security for the event.

examples.sentence: Para curarse en salud, Juan llevó copias adicionales de todos los formularios, por si acaso los originales se perdían.
examples.translation: To be safe, Juan brought extra copies of all forms in case the originals got lost.

examples.sentence: Ella curó en salud reservando dos hoteles diferentes, por si uno cancelaba la reserva a último momento.
examples.translation: She played it safe by booking two different hotels in case one canceled the reservation at the last minute.

definitions: A graphical representation that relates subjective well‑being or happiness to another variable (commonly age), often showing a U‑shaped relationship with a midlife dip.

examples.sentence: La curva de la felicidad muestra que muchas personas experimentan una caída en su bienestar durante la mediana edad.
examples.translation: The happiness curve shows that many people experience a dip in well-being during middle age.

examples.sentence: Los psicólogos utilizaron la curva de la felicidad para analizar cómo varía la satisfacción a lo largo de la vida.
examples.translation: Psychologists used the happiness curve to analyze how satisfaction varies throughout life.

examples.sentence: Según la curva de la felicidad, después de los 50 años, la mayoría de las personas tiende a sentirse más contenta.
examples.translation: According to the happiness curve, after age 50, most people tend to feel happier.

examples.sentence: La curva de la felicidad se representa gráficamente con una forma de U que refleja altibajos emocionales.
examples.translation: The happiness curve is graphically represented with a U shape that reflects emotional highs and lows.

definitions: Any curve or diagram figuratively described as representing levels of happiness or satisfaction across a sequence or life stage.

examples.sentence: En la conferencia mostraron una curva de la felicidad para ilustrar cómo cambia la satisfacción en diferentes países.
examples.translation: At the conference they showed a happiness curve to illustrate how satisfaction changes in different countries.

examples.sentence: La curva de la felicidad en ese estudio representaba la relación entre ingresos y bienestar subjetivo.
examples.translation: The happiness curve in that study represented the relationship between income and subjective well-being.

examples.sentence: Al observar la curva de la felicidad, se puede entender mejor la evolución del estado de ánimo durante la vida laboral.
examples.translation: By observing the happiness curve, we can better understand the evolution of mood during working life.

examples.sentence: La curva de la felicidad es una herramienta útil para analizar cómo pequeños cambios impactan en la satisfacción personal.
examples.translation: The happiness curve is a useful tool to analyze how small changes impact personal satisfaction.

definitions: A statistical or conceptual curve used in psychology, economics, or sociology to illustrate how experienced happiness changes over time or across groups.

examples.sentence: Los sociólogos compararon la curva de la felicidad entre distintos grupos demográficos para estudiar desigualdades.
examples.translation: Sociologists compared the happiness curve among different demographic groups to study inequalities.

examples.sentence: La curva de la felicidad también se usa en economía para evaluar la relación entre consumo y bienestar emocional.
examples.translation: The happiness curve is also used in economics to evaluate the relationship between consumption and emotional well-being.

examples.sentence: En psicología, la curva de la felicidad ayuda a explicar por qué algunas etapas de la vida parecen más satisfactorias que otras.
examples.translation: In psychology, the happiness curve helps explain why some life stages seem more satisfying than others.

examples.sentence: La representación gráfica de la curva de la felicidad facilita la comprensión de conceptos abstractos sobre el bienestar humano.
examples.translation: The graphical representation of the happiness curve facilitates understanding of abstract concepts about human well-being.

definitions: A metaphorical expression for the rise and fall of contentment or well‑being in a particular context.

examples.sentence: Después de la crisis, muchas personas pasaron por una curva de la felicidad personal que subió y bajó rápidamente.
examples.translation: After the crisis, many people went through a personal happiness curve that rose and fell quickly.

examples.sentence: El gerente explicó que la curva de la felicidad en la empresa refleja el ánimo de los empleados durante el proyecto.
examples.translation: The manager explained that the happiness curve in the company reflects employees’ mood during the project.

examples.sentence: En la relación de pareja, a veces uno experimenta una curva de la felicidad que depende de las circunstancias externas.
examples.translation: In a relationship, sometimes one experiences a happiness curve that depends on external circumstances.

definitions: To do something repeatedly or persistently; to continue an action again and again without stopping.

examples.sentence: Dale que dale con las mismas preguntas, ya te respondí todo lo que sabía.
examples.translation: You keep asking the same questions again and again, I already told you everything I knew.

examples.sentence: Cuando el niño no entiende la lección, el profesor dale que dale hasta que todos comprendan.
examples.translation: When the child doesn’t understand the lesson, the teacher keeps at it persistently until everyone understands.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que me repitas las cosas dale que dale; prefiero que me expliques claramente una sola vez.
examples.translation: I don’t like you repeating things over and over; I prefer you explain clearly just once.

definitions: An exhortation meaning 'go on' or 'keep at it', used to urge someone to continue an activity with energy or persistence.

examples.sentence: ¡Dale que dale, sigue practicando hasta que domines esa canción en la guitarra!
examples.translation: Keep at it, keep practicing until you master that song on the guitar!

examples.sentence: El entrenador le dijo al equipo: 'Dale que dale, no se rindan hasta ganar el campeonato.'
examples.translation: The coach told the team: 'Go on, don’t give up until you win the championship.'

examples.sentence: Si quieres mejorar tu español, dale que dale estudiando todos los días sin falta.
examples.translation: If you want to improve your Spanish, keep at it by studying every day without fail.

definitions: To persist in speaking or acting about something, often to the point of annoyance or monotony.

examples.sentence: Juan dale que dale con su teoría de conspiración, ya nadie aguanta escucharlo más.
examples.translation: Juan keeps going on and on with his conspiracy theory; no one can stand listening to him anymore.

examples.sentence: Mi tía dale que dale hablando siempre de la familia, hasta que me aburro completamente.
examples.translation: My aunt goes on and on always talking about family, until I get completely bored.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, el jefe dale que dale con el mismo tema hasta que todos perdimos la paciencia.
examples.translation: In the meeting, the boss kept at it with the same topic until we all lost patience.

definitions: To engage in an activity repeatedly and vigorously, often with a strong physical or sexual connotation.

examples.sentence: Durante la fiesta, ellos estuvieron dale que te pego toda la noche sin descanso.
examples.translation: During the party, they kept at it all night without resting.

examples.sentence: No sé cómo aguantan ese ritmo dale que te pego en el gimnasio, es agotador.
examples.translation: I don’t know how they endure that non-stop pace at the gym; it’s exhausting.

examples.sentence: Los bailarines practicaron dale que te pego hasta perfeccionar cada movimiento de la coreografía.
examples.translation: The dancers practiced relentlessly until perfecting every move of the choreography.

definitions: To do something over and over again in a relentless or frenetic manner, not necessarily sexual; to persist energetically in an action.

examples.sentence: El equipo trabajó dale que te pego para terminar el proyecto antes del plazo establecido.
examples.translation: The team worked tirelessly to finish the project before the deadline.

examples.sentence: Aunque estaba cansada, siguió dale que te pego estudiando para el examen final.
examples.translation: Although she was tired, she kept at it studying relentlessly for the final exam.

examples.sentence: En la fábrica, los empleados estuvieron dale que te pego para cumplir con la demanda de producción.
examples.translation: At the factory, the workers worked non-stop to meet the production demand.

definitions: To carry out prolonged, intense, and rhythmic action without interruption.

examples.sentence: La máquina funcionó dale que te pego durante horas sin detenerse ni un momento.
examples.translation: The machine ran nonstop for hours without stopping for a moment.

examples.sentence: Ellos tocaron dale que te pego hasta que el público comenzó a aplaudir con entusiasmo.
examples.translation: They played relentlessly until the audience began applauding enthusiastically.

examples.sentence: En el partido, el equipo atacó dale que te pego para lograr el gol de la victoria.
examples.translation: In the match, the team pressed relentlessly to score the winning goal.

definitions: To make something known to the public or to a specific audience; to disclose or announce information, facts, or results.

examples.sentence: La empresa decidió dar a conocer sus nuevos productos en una conferencia de prensa internacional.
examples.translation: The company decided to announce its new products at an international press conference.

examples.sentence: Antes de dar a conocer los resultados, el comité revisó cuidadosamente todos los datos obtenidos.
examples.translation: Before making the results known, the committee carefully reviewed all the data collected.

examples.sentence: El cantante va a dar a conocer su nuevo álbum en un concierto que se transmitirá en vivo.
examples.translation: The singer is going to release his new album in a concert that will be broadcast live.

definitions: To publish or release information so that it becomes widely available or officially communicated.

examples.sentence: La editorial planea dar a conocer la novela la próxima primavera para captar la atención del público.
examples.translation: The publishing house plans to release the novel next spring to attract public attention.

examples.sentence: Para dar a conocer los avances científicos, los investigadores publicaron un artículo en una revista reconocida.
examples.translation: To make the scientific advances known, the researchers published an article in a renowned journal.

examples.sentence: El museo dará a conocer la exposición temporal a través de una campaña en redes sociales.
examples.translation: The museum will unveil the temporary exhibition through a social media campaign.

definitions: To introduce a person, work, product, or idea to an audience with the aim of publicizing it or increasing its recognition.

examples.sentence: El festival sirve para dar a conocer artistas emergentes y sus obras al gran público.
examples.translation: The festival serves to introduce emerging artists and their works to the general public.

examples.sentence: Queremos dar a conocer esta innovadora tecnología en la próxima feria internacional de ciencias.
examples.translation: We want to showcase this innovative technology at the next international science fair.

examples.sentence: El autor dio a conocer su último libro en una presentación llena de seguidores y prensa especializada.
examples.translation: The author introduced his latest book at a presentation filled with fans and specialized press.

definitions: To promote or present something so that it gains visibility or becomes known within a community or market.

examples.sentence: La campaña publicitaria busca dar a conocer la marca entre los jóvenes consumidores urbanos.
examples.translation: The advertising campaign aims to promote the brand among young urban consumers.

examples.sentence: Para dar a conocer el proyecto comunitario, organizaron una jornada de puertas abiertas en el barrio.
examples.translation: To publicize the community project, they organized an open house day in the neighborhood.

examples.sentence: La empresa dio a conocer su compromiso con la sostenibilidad mediante un comunicado oficial.
examples.translation: The company made its commitment to sustainability known through an official statement.

definitions: To give birth; to bring a child into the world through childbirth.

examples.sentence: María dio a luz a su primer hijo en un hospital cercano y tanto ella como el bebé están bien.
examples.translation: María gave birth to her first child in a nearby hospital and both she and the baby are fine.

examples.sentence: El doctor explicó que dar a luz puede ser un proceso largo y requiere mucha paciencia y apoyo.
examples.translation: The doctor explained that giving birth can be a long process and requires a lot of patience and support.

examples.sentence: Después de horas de trabajo de parto, finalmente dio a luz a una niña sana y hermosa.
examples.translation: After hours of labor, she finally gave birth to a healthy and beautiful girl.

examples.sentence: Mi tía dará a luz en diciembre, y toda la familia está emocionada por la llegada del bebé.
examples.translation: My aunt will give birth in December, and the whole family is excited about the baby’s arrival.

definitions: To publish or release a work; to make a written or artistic creation publicly available.

examples.sentence: El escritor dio a luz una novela que rápidamente se convirtió en un éxito de ventas.
examples.translation: The writer published a novel that quickly became a bestseller.

examples.sentence: La editorial dio a luz una nueva colección de poesía contemporánea que ha recibido excelentes críticas.
examples.translation: The publisher released a new collection of contemporary poetry that has received excellent reviews.

examples.sentence: Tras meses de trabajo, el pintor dio a luz una serie de cuadros inspirados en la naturaleza.
examples.translation: After months of work, the painter brought forth a series of paintings inspired by nature.

definitions: To be able to cope with a workload or demand; to have sufficient capacity, time, or resources to handle current tasks.

examples.sentence: Con tantos pedidos, la tienda no daba abasto para atender a todos los clientes a tiempo.
examples.translation: With so many orders, the store couldn’t cope with serving all the customers on time.

examples.sentence: No sé cómo vas a dar abasto con tantas tareas pendientes antes del fin de semana.
examples.translation: I don’t know how you will manage with so many tasks pending before the weekend.

examples.sentence: La cocina del restaurante daba abasto incluso en las horas pico gracias a su eficiente equipo.
examples.translation: The restaurant’s kitchen was able to cope even during peak hours thanks to its efficient team.

definitions: To be enough or sufficient (of supplies, resources, or means) to meet needs or demands.

examples.sentence: Con la comida que compramos, creo que va a dar abasto para todos los invitados.
examples.translation: With the food we bought, I think it will be enough for all the guests.

examples.sentence: No sé si el presupuesto que tenemos dará abasto para cubrir todos los gastos del proyecto.
examples.translation: I don't know if the budget we have will be sufficient to cover all the project expenses.

examples.sentence: Cuando trabajaba en la tienda, muchas veces no daba abasto con la cantidad de clientes que llegaban en época de rebajas.
examples.translation: When I worked at the store, many times I couldn't keep up with the number of customers that came during the sales season.

definitions: To ruin or wreck plans, projects, hopes, reputation, or other endeavors; to cause something to fail or come to nothing.

examples.sentence: Si no entregas el informe a tiempo, vas a dar al traste con toda la presentación que habíamos preparado.
examples.translation: If you don't submit the report on time, you will ruin the entire presentation we had prepared.

examples.sentence: Pensé que el plan iba a funcionar, pero al final todo dio al traste cuando se canceló el evento por la lluvia.
examples.translation: I thought the plan was going to work, but in the end everything fell apart when the event was cancelled due to rain.

examples.sentence: No permitas que un malentendido dé al traste con vuestra amistad después de tantos años.
examples.translation: Don't let a misunderstanding wreck your friendship after so many years.

definitions: To catch up with or overtake someone or something that is ahead.

examples.sentence: Corrí tan rápido como pude para dar alcance a mis compañeros que ya estaban en la cima del cerro.
examples.translation: I ran as fast as I could to catch up with my companions who were already at the top of the hill.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que lograrás dar alcance al autobús si sales ahora de la estación?
examples.translation: Do you think you will catch up with the bus if you leave the station now?

examples.sentence: Ella siempre me da alcance cuando corro por el parque, no importa cuántas vueltas dé.
examples.translation: She always catches up with me when I run in the park, no matter how many laps I do.

definitions: To reach or attain a level, amount, or target; to come up to a required standard or figure.

examples.sentence: Después de varios meses de esfuerzo, finalmente di alcance a la meta de ventas establecida por la empresa.
examples.translation: After several months of effort, I finally reached the sales target set by the company.

examples.sentence: No creo que hoy demos alcance al número de clientes que necesitamos para cerrar el trimestre con éxito.
examples.translation: I don't think today we will reach the number of clients we need to close the quarter successfully.

examples.sentence: Si seguimos trabajando así, daremos alcance a los estándares de calidad que exige el mercado internacional.
examples.translation: If we keep working like this, we will reach the quality standards required by the international market.

definitions: To deliver, notify, or bring something to the attention of a person of authority (archaic or formal usage).

examples.sentence: El secretario dará alcance al informe al director antes de la reunión de esta tarde.
examples.translation: The secretary will deliver the report to the director before this afternoon's meeting.

examples.sentence: Se dio alcance a la policía sobre el incidente ocurrido en la fábrica para que tomaran cartas en el asunto.
examples.translation: The police were notified about the incident at the factory so they could take action.

examples.sentence: Los documentos fueron dados alcance a la autoridad competente para su revisión y análisis.
examples.translation: The documents were brought to the attention of the competent authority for review and analysis.

definitions: To give or hand over an object, amount, favor, or assistance to someone.

examples.sentence: María me dio el libro que había pedido para la clase de literatura.
examples.translation: María gave me the book I had requested for literature class.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes darme un poco de agua? Tengo mucha sed después de correr.
examples.translation: Can you give me some water? I'm very thirsty after running.

examples.sentence: El profesor dio una explicación clara para que todos entendieran el tema difícil.
examples.translation: The teacher gave a clear explanation so everyone understood the difficult topic.

examples.sentence: Nos dieron las llaves del apartamento justo cuando llegamos a la recepción.
examples.translation: They handed us the apartment keys just as we arrived at the reception.

definitions: To threaten to hit, punish, or retaliate against someone (colloquial threat).

examples.sentence: Si sigues molestando, te voy a dar algo que no olvidarás.
examples.translation: If you keep bothering me, I'm going to give you something you won't forget.

examples.sentence: Cuando el niño tomó la galleta sin permiso, su hermana le dijo que le iba a dar algo cuando llegara mamá.
examples.translation: When the boy took the cookie without permission, his sister told him she would punish him when mom arrived.

examples.sentence: No le des algo a ese tipo, que solo busca problemas.
examples.translation: Don't threaten that guy; he's just looking for trouble.

definitions: Used impersonally to indicate suffering a sudden intense physical or emotional reaction (for example, fainting, a shock, or extreme agitation): literally, to be overcome by something.

examples.sentence: Cuando vio la noticia, le dio algo y se desmayó en el acto.
examples.translation: When she saw the news, she was overcome and fainted on the spot.

examples.sentence: Me dio algo sentir el frío tan intenso de repente, tuve que sentarme un momento.
examples.translation: It hit me suddenly how intense the cold was; I had to sit down for a moment.

examples.sentence: A Juan le dio algo cuando escuchó la verdad sobre lo que había pasado en la reunión.
examples.translation: Juan was overwhelmed when he heard the truth about what happened at the meeting.

definitions: To cause revulsion or disgust in someone; to be physically or sensorially repellent.

examples.sentence: La comida en ese restaurante me dio asco, no pude terminar el plato.
examples.translation: The food at that restaurant disgusted me; I couldn't finish the dish.

examples.sentence: Ver cómo maltrataban a los animales realmente me da asco.
examples.translation: Seeing how the animals were mistreated really disgusts me.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que paso por esa basura en la calle, me da asco el olor que emana.
examples.translation: Every time I pass by that garbage on the street, the smell disgusts me.

definitions: To inspire moral contempt or strong dislike; to be odious or despicable.

examples.sentence: Me da asco la corrupción que hay en algunos políticos que solo buscan su beneficio personal.
examples.translation: I am disgusted by the corruption in some politicians who only seek their own benefit.

examples.sentence: Esa actitud mezquina me da asco; no puedo creer que alguien sea tan egoísta.
examples.translation: That petty attitude disgusts me; I can't believe someone could be so selfish.

examples.sentence: Nos dio asco ver cómo se aprovechaban de los más vulnerables sin ningún remordimiento.
examples.translation: It disgusted us to see how they took advantage of the most vulnerable without remorse.

definitions: To be described as disgusting or nauseating.

examples.sentence: La película era tan mala que daba asco desde el primer minuto.
examples.translation: The movie was so bad that it was disgusting from the first minute.

examples.sentence: Ese olor a comida podrida da asco en cualquier lugar donde se perciba.
examples.translation: That smell of rotten food is disgusting anywhere it is noticed.

examples.sentence: El estado del baño público era tan desagradable que daba asco usarlo.
examples.translation: The condition of the public bathroom was so unpleasant that it was disgusting to use it.

definitions: To experience self-disgust or feel nauseated by one’s own actions or condition (reflexive use: darse asco).

examples.sentence: Después de hacer trampa en el examen, se dio asco a sí mismo al no poder mirarse al espejo.
examples.translation: After cheating on the exam, he felt self-disgust and couldn't look at himself in the mirror.

examples.sentence: Me doy asco cuando recuerdo cómo traté a mis amigos en esa época tan difícil.
examples.translation: I feel disgusted with myself when I remember how I treated my friends during that difficult time.

examples.sentence: Ella se dio asco por no defender sus principios cuando tuvo la oportunidad.
examples.translation: She felt self-disgust for not standing up for her principles when she had the chance.

definitions: To placate or soothe someone with insubstantial words, empty promises, or token gestures rather than with meaningful action.

examples.sentence: El político intentó dar atol con el dedo prometiendo cambios que nunca llegaron.
examples.translation: The politician tried to placate with empty promises that never materialized.

examples.sentence: No me des atol con el dedo; quiero soluciones reales a los problemas de la comunidad.
examples.translation: Don't soothe me with empty words; I want real solutions to the community's problems.

examples.sentence: Siento que nos están dando atol con el dedo para que no protestemos por la situación actual.
examples.translation: I feel like they are placating us with insubstantial words so we don't protest the current situation.

definitions: To deceive or mislead someone by talking placatingly while offering no real solution.

examples.sentence: Nos dieron atol con el dedo durante meses y al final no pasó nada de lo prometido.
examples.translation: They misled us for months with soothing words and in the end, nothing promised happened.

examples.sentence: El jefe dio atol con el dedo diciendo que habría aumentos, pero nunca cumplió.
examples.translation: The boss deceived us by saying there would be raises, but he never fulfilled it.

examples.sentence: No permitas que te den atol con el dedo; exige respuestas claras y acciones concretas.
examples.translation: Don't let them fool you with empty words; demand clear answers and concrete actions.

definitions: To placate or soothe someone with insubstantial words, empty promises, or token gestures rather than with meaningful action.

examples.sentence: El gerente dio atole con el dedo a los empleados para evitar que se quejaran del ambiente laboral.
examples.translation: The manager placated the employees with empty promises to prevent complaints about the work environment.

examples.sentence: Se dieron atole con el dedo durante la negociación y no lograron ningún acuerdo real.
examples.translation: They soothed each other with insubstantial talk during the negotiation and achieved no real agreement.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando me dan atole con el dedo; prefiero que me digan la verdad aunque sea dura.
examples.translation: I don't like it when they soothe me with empty words; I prefer to be told the truth even if it's harsh.

definitions: To deceive or mislead someone by talking placatingly while offering no real solution.

examples.sentence: El representante dio atole con el dedo a los campesinos para que no protestaran por la falta de apoyo.
examples.translation: The representative misled the farmers with soothing talk so they wouldn't protest the lack of support.

examples.sentence: Durante años, la empresa dio atole con el dedo a sus trabajadores prometiendo mejoras que nunca llegaron.
examples.translation: For years, the company deceived its workers with empty promises of improvements that never came.

examples.sentence: No dejes que te den atole con el dedo en las reuniones; exige que cumplan lo que prometen.
examples.translation: Don't let them fool you with empty talk in meetings; demand that they fulfill what they promise.

definitions: To pay attention to someone or something; to take notice.

examples.sentence: No le des bola a los rumores que circulan por la oficina, son solo habladurías sin fundamento.
examples.translation: Don't pay attention to the rumors going around the office; they're just baseless chatter.

examples.sentence: Si no le das bola a las instrucciones, podrías cometer errores graves en el proyecto.
examples.translation: If you don't pay attention to the instructions, you could make serious mistakes on the project.

examples.sentence: Los estudiantes no le daban bola a la explicación del profesor y por eso reprobaron el examen.
examples.translation: The students weren't paying attention to the teacher's explanation and that's why they failed the exam.

definitions: To show romantic or sexual interest in someone (colloquial use: dar bola a alguien).

examples.sentence: Desde que Carla le dio bola a ese chico en la fiesta, no ha dejado de hablar de él.
examples.translation: Since Carla showed interest in that guy at the party, she hasn't stopped talking about him.

examples.sentence: ¿Le diste bola a Marcos cuando te habló o estabas distraída con el teléfono?
examples.translation: Did you pay attention to Marcos when he talked to you or were you distracted by your phone?

examples.sentence: No le des bola a ese tipo, solo quiere aprovecharse de ti.
examples.translation: Don't give that guy any attention; he just wants to take advantage of you.

definitions: To respond to or give consideration or heed to a person’s remarks or actions.

examples.sentence: El jefe siempre le da bola a las ideas creativas que propone el equipo de diseño.
examples.translation: The boss always pays heed to the creative ideas proposed by the design team.

examples.sentence: Cuando hablas con ella, asegúrate de que te dé bola para que entienda bien el mensaje.
examples.translation: When you talk to her, make sure she pays attention so she understands the message well.

examples.sentence: No le dieron bola a las quejas de los clientes y eso afectó la reputación de la empresa.
examples.translation: They didn't pay attention to the customers' complaints and that affected the company's reputation.

definitions: To bounce or rebound (used of a ball or other object).

examples.sentence: La pelota dio bote varias veces antes de entrar en la portería.
examples.translation: The ball bounced several times before entering the goal.

examples.sentence: Cuando tiré la piedra al agua, dio bote y formó varias ondas en la superficie.
examples.translation: When I threw the stone into the water, it bounced and created several ripples on the surface.

examples.sentence: Los niños estaban jugando con la pelota que daba bote constantemente en el patio.
examples.translation: The children were playing with the ball that kept bouncing constantly in the yard.

examples.sentence: El balón dio un bote inesperado y salió fuera de la cancha.
examples.translation: The ball gave an unexpected bounce and went out of the field.

definitions: To cause a vehicle or ride to jolt or give short, abrupt shocks; to jerk in motion.

examples.sentence: Durante el viaje en carretera, el autobús daba bote por el mal estado del camino.
examples.translation: During the road trip, the bus jolted because of the poor condition of the road.

examples.sentence: Cuando el camión pasó por el bache, dio bote y todos los pasajeros se asustaron.
examples.translation: When the truck went over the pothole, it jolted and all the passengers got scared.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que el asiento del coche dé bote cuando conduzco por caminos irregulares.
examples.translation: I don't like that the car seat jolts when I drive on uneven roads.

examples.sentence: El tren empezó a dar bote cuando entró en la zona de vías antiguas y desgastadas.
examples.translation: The train began to jolt when it entered the area of old and worn tracks.

definitions: To make a surface or object move in a series of short, abrupt upward motions.

examples.sentence: El resorte dio bote al ser comprimido y luego liberado rápidamente.
examples.translation: The spring bounced when compressed and then released quickly.

examples.sentence: Al saltar sobre el trampolín, el cuerpo da bote y se impulsa hacia arriba.
examples.translation: When jumping on the trampoline, the body bounces and propels upwards.

examples.sentence: La pelota de goma dio bote varias veces antes de detenerse en el suelo.
examples.translation: The rubber ball bounced several times before stopping on the ground.

examples.sentence: El resorte del reloj daba bote debido a un daño interno en el mecanismo.
examples.translation: The clock spring was bouncing because of internal damage in the mechanism.

definitions: To make small jumps or hops; to spring up repeatedly.

examples.sentence: El conejo daba brincos por el campo mientras buscaba comida.
examples.translation: The rabbit was hopping through the field while looking for food.

examples.sentence: Los niños daban brincos de alegría cuando vieron llegar el circo a la ciudad.
examples.translation: The children were jumping with joy when they saw the circus arrive in town.

examples.sentence: El gato daba brincos intentando atrapar la luz reflejada en la pared.
examples.translation: The cat was making small jumps trying to catch the light reflected on the wall.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase de gimnasia, los alumnos daban brincos para calentar los músculos.
examples.translation: During gym class, the students were hopping to warm up their muscles.

definitions: To jump for joy; to express great happiness or excitement by jumping.

examples.sentence: Cuando le dieron la noticia del ascenso, dio brincos de felicidad frente a todos sus compañeros.
examples.translation: When he received the news of the promotion, he jumped for joy in front of all his coworkers.

examples.sentence: No podía dejar de dar brincos al saber que había ganado el premio mayor en la lotería.
examples.translation: She couldn't stop jumping for joy after learning she had won the grand prize in the lottery.

examples.sentence: Los niños dieron brincos de emoción al ver que la escuela organizaría una fiesta.
examples.translation: The children jumped with excitement upon hearing that the school would organize a party.

definitions: To frolic, romp about, or move about playfully; to go out to have fun or behave in a lively, playful manner.

examples.sentence: Los cachorros daban brincos por toda la casa mientras jugaban entre ellos.
examples.translation: The puppies were frolicking all over the house while playing with each other.

examples.sentence: Luego de la tormenta, los niños dieron brincos en los charcos como si no les importara mojarse.
examples.translation: After the storm, the children frolicked in the puddles as if they didn't mind getting wet.

examples.sentence: En la reunión familiar, los primos dieron brincos por el jardín mientras disfrutaban del día soleado.
examples.translation: At the family gathering, the cousins romped around the garden while enjoying the sunny day.

definitions: Used in negative constructions (e.g., 'no estar para dar brincos') to indicate not being in a mood or physical condition for lively activity or play.

examples.sentence: No estoy para dar brincos hoy; necesito descansar después del largo viaje.
examples.translation: I'm not in the mood to jump around today; I need to rest after the long trip.

examples.sentence: Después de la operación, mi abuelo no estaba para dar brincos y prefería estar tranquilo en casa.
examples.translation: After the surgery, my grandfather wasn't up for lively activity and preferred to stay calm at home.

examples.sentence: No está para dar brincos con tanta lluvia y frío, mejor quedémonos adentro.
examples.translation: He's not in the mood to be lively with so much rain and cold; we'd better stay inside.

definitions: To consume or finish something completely, especially food or drink.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, todos dieron buena cuenta del buffet y no quedó ni una migaja.
examples.translation: At the party, everyone finished the buffet completely and not a crumb was left.

examples.sentence: Después de la caminata, los excursionistas dieron buena cuenta de las provisiones que llevaban.
examples.translation: After the hike, the hikers consumed all the supplies they had brought.

examples.sentence: No quedaba mucho vino porque los invitados dieron buena cuenta de la botella durante la cena.
examples.translation: There wasn't much wine left because the guests finished the bottle during dinner.

definitions: To deal with, defeat, or dispose of decisively; to take care of an opponent, obstacle, or task effectively.

examples.sentence: El equipo local dio buena cuenta de sus rivales y ganó el campeonato con autoridad.
examples.translation: The local team decisively defeated their opponents and won the championship with authority.

examples.sentence: Logramos dar buena cuenta de todos los problemas técnicos y entregamos el proyecto a tiempo.
examples.translation: We managed to deal effectively with all technical problems and delivered the project on time.

examples.sentence: Ella dio buena cuenta del desafío y superó todas las expectativas de sus entrenadores.
examples.translation: She took care of the challenge and exceeded all her coaches' expectations.

definitions: To give a clear, satisfactory account of one's actions; to account for or justify conduct.

examples.sentence: En la entrevista, el candidato dio buena cuenta de su experiencia y habilidades profesionales.
examples.translation: In the interview, the candidate gave a clear and satisfactory account of his experience and professional skills.

examples.sentence: El acusado dio buena cuenta de sus acciones y finalmente fue absuelto por falta de pruebas.
examples.translation: The defendant accounted for his actions and was ultimately acquitted due to lack of evidence.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, el gerente dio buena cuenta de los resultados obtenidos en el último trimestre.
examples.translation: During the meeting, the manager gave a clear account of the results obtained in the last quarter.

definitions: To reject someone's romantic advances or to spurn a suitor.

examples.sentence: Después de varias citas, Laura le dio calabazas a Carlos porque no sentía la chispa.
examples.translation: After several dates, Laura rejected Carlos because she didn't feel the spark.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes si te dio calabazas; seguro encontrarás a alguien que te valore más.
examples.translation: Don't worry if she spurned you; surely you'll find someone who values you more.

examples.sentence: Pedro estaba muy triste porque Marta le dio calabazas justo antes de la fiesta de graduación.
examples.translation: Pedro was very sad because Marta rejected him right before the graduation party.

definitions: To fail someone in an examination or to give a failing grade.

examples.sentence: María estaba muy nerviosa porque sabía que si el profesor le daba calabazas, no podría pasar el curso.
examples.translation: María was very nervous because she knew that if the teacher failed her, she wouldn't be able to pass the course.

examples.sentence: ¿Te acuerdas cuando Pedro dio calabazas a todos en el examen final? Fue un desastre total.
examples.translation: Do you remember when Pedro failed everyone in the final exam? It was a total disaster.

examples.sentence: No quiero que me den calabazas en esta materia, por eso estoy estudiando tanto últimamente.
examples.translation: I don't want to fail this subject, that's why I've been studying so much lately.

definitions: To give someone leeway or room to act; to allow or encourage a behavior, rumor, or initiative to develop.

examples.sentence: El director decidió dar cancha a los jóvenes para que propusieran nuevas ideas sin restricciones.
examples.translation: The director decided to give the youngsters leeway to propose new ideas without restrictions.

examples.sentence: No deberías darle cancha a esos rumores porque solo están creando problemas innecesarios.
examples.translation: You shouldn't give room to those rumors because they're just causing unnecessary problems.

examples.sentence: Si le das cancha a ese tipo de comportamientos, pronto será difícil controlarlos.
examples.translation: If you allow that kind of behavior leeway, soon it will be hard to control them.

definitions: To give a person an opportunity to perform or play (e.g., in sport or work), to let someone take part or gain experience.

examples.sentence: El entrenador decidió dar cancha a los jugadores jóvenes para que ganaran experiencia en el campo.
examples.translation: The coach decided to give the young players a chance to gain experience on the field.

examples.sentence: Cuando yo era novato, siempre me dieron cancha en el trabajo para aprender y mejorar.
examples.translation: When I was a rookie, they always gave me opportunities at work to learn and improve.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que deberíamos darle cancha a Ana en este proyecto? Podría aportar ideas frescas.
examples.translation: Do you think we should give Ana a chance in this project? She could bring fresh ideas.

definitions: To close, shelve, or discontinue a case, investigation, or matter; to officially end attention to an issue.

examples.sentence: El juez decidió dar carpetazo al caso por falta de pruebas suficientes.
examples.translation: The judge decided to close the case due to lack of sufficient evidence.

examples.sentence: Después de meses de investigación, la policía dio carpetazo al asunto y archivó el expediente.
examples.translation: After months of investigation, the police shelved the matter and filed the report.

examples.sentence: No podemos dar carpetazo a este problema sin antes buscar una solución definitiva.
examples.translation: We can't close this problem without first looking for a definitive solution.

definitions: To sweep an issue under the rug or terminate it prematurely to avoid scrutiny or responsibility; to cover up.

examples.sentence: La empresa dio carpetazo a las acusaciones para evitar un escándalo mayor.
examples.translation: The company swept the accusations under the rug to avoid a bigger scandal.

examples.sentence: Me da la impresión de que están dando carpetazo al tema para no asumir responsabilidades.
examples.translation: I get the impression that they are covering up the issue to avoid taking responsibility.

examples.sentence: No dejes que den carpetazo a esta denuncia; es importante que se investigue a fondo.
examples.translation: Don't let them sweep this complaint under the carpet; it's important that it is thoroughly investigated.

definitions: To tease or rib someone in a playful, jocular manner.

examples.sentence: En la reunión todos le daban carrilla a Carlos por su forma divertida de contar historias.
examples.translation: In the meeting, everyone teased Carlos about his funny way of telling stories.

examples.sentence: No le des tanta carrilla a Ana, que ya está cansada después de un día largo.
examples.translation: Don't tease Ana so much, she's already tired after a long day.

examples.sentence: Cuando éramos niños, mis amigos siempre me daban carrilla por perder en los juegos.
examples.translation: When we were kids, my friends always teased me for losing in the games.

definitions: To mock or taunt someone in a more pointed or provocative way.

examples.sentence: Los compañeros le daban carrilla a Juan por ese error en público, lo que lo incomodó bastante.
examples.translation: The coworkers mocked Juan for that mistake in public, which made him quite uncomfortable.

examples.sentence: No permitas que te den carrilla en el trabajo; tienes derecho a que te respeten.
examples.translation: Don't let them taunt you at work; you have the right to be respected.
