examples.translation: The notary certified the legality of the contract by stamping his official signature on the document.

examples.sentence: Para que el acuerdo sea válido, alguien debe dar fe de que ambas partes lo firmaron voluntariamente.
examples.translation: For the agreement to be valid, someone must formally witness that both parties signed it voluntarily.

examples.sentence: En la ceremonia, el juez dio fe de que el matrimonio se realizó conforme a la ley.
examples.translation: At the ceremony, the judge certified that the marriage was performed according to the law.

definitions: To vouch for or confirm the accuracy or veracity of a statement or fact.

examples.sentence: Puedo dar fe de que el informe es correcto porque revisé todos los datos personalmente.
examples.translation: I can vouch for the report’s accuracy because I personally reviewed all the data.

examples.sentence: El experto dio fe de la veracidad de los resultados tras realizar varias pruebas rigurosas.
examples.translation: The expert confirmed the truthfulness of the results after conducting several rigorous tests.

examples.sentence: Nosotros damos fe de que las declaraciones presentadas en la reunión son ciertas y completas.
examples.translation: We confirm that the statements presented at the meeting are true and complete.

definitions: To cause someone to feel a desire or urge to do something (often used impersonally: 'me da/da(n) ganas de...').

examples.sentence: Esta canción me da ganas de bailar cada vez que la escucho en la radio.
examples.translation: This song makes me want to dance every time I hear it on the radio.

examples.sentence: No me da ganas de salir hoy porque está lloviendo mucho y me siento cansado.
examples.translation: I don’t feel like going out today because it’s raining a lot and I feel tired.

examples.sentence: Si me das ganas de viajar, empiezo a planear mi próximo destino inmediatamente.
examples.translation: If you make me want to travel, I immediately start planning my next destination.

definitions: To provoke an emotional reaction that prompts an impulse or inclination (positive or negative).

examples.sentence: Ver esas películas tristes siempre me da ganas de llorar, aunque trate de aguantarme.
examples.translation: Watching those sad movies always makes me want to cry, even if I try to hold it back.

examples.sentence: La injusticia me da ganas de levantar la voz y luchar por un cambio real en la sociedad.
examples.translation: Injustice makes me want to raise my voice and fight for real change in society.

examples.sentence: La actitud grosera de Pedro me dio ganas de responderle con la misma rudeza, pero preferí mantener la calma.
examples.translation: Pedro’s rude attitude made me want to respond with the same rudeness, but I preferred to stay calm.

definitions: To deceive someone by substituting an inferior or fraudulent item for one of promised or expected higher quality.

examples.sentence: En el mercado, me dieron gato por liebre y terminé pagando mucho más por un producto de mala calidad.
examples.translation: At the market, they tricked me by giving me a cat instead of a hare and I ended up paying much more for a low-quality product.

examples.sentence: No dejes que te den gato por liebre cuando compres electrónica usada; revisa bien antes de pagar.
examples.translation: Don’t let them cheat you when buying used electronics; check carefully before paying.

examples.sentence: Los turistas a veces son víctimas de vendedores que les dan gato por liebre con souvenirs falsos.
examples.translation: Tourists are sometimes victims of sellers who deceive them by giving fake souvenirs.

definitions: To swindle or cheat a person in a commercial or exchange context by passing off a counterfeit or inferior product as genuine.

examples.sentence: Los comerciantes inescrupulosos dieron gato por liebre al vender productos caducados como si estuvieran frescos.
examples.translation: Unscrupulous merchants swindled by selling expired products as if they were fresh.

examples.sentence: No me gusta comprar en esa tienda porque siempre dan gato por liebre y no cumplen con lo prometido.
examples.translation: I don’t like shopping at that store because they always cheat and don’t deliver what they promise.

examples.sentence: En esa transacción, nos dieron gato por liebre y tuvimos que reclamar para que nos devolvieran el dinero.
examples.translation: In that transaction, they swindled us and we had to complain to get our money back.

definitions: To mislead or trick someone by presenting false information or a dishonest proposition as if it were true.

examples.sentence: El político dio gato por liebre con sus promesas de campaña, ya que no cumplió nada de lo anunciado.
examples.translation: The politician misled people with his campaign promises, as he didn’t fulfill any of what he announced.

examples.sentence: Me di cuenta de que me dieron gato por liebre cuando el producto no funcionaba como decían en la publicidad.
examples.translation: I realized I was tricked when the product didn’t work as advertised.

examples.sentence: No permitas que te den gato por liebre en contratos engañosos que solo buscan aprovecharse de ti.
examples.translation: Don’t allow yourself to be tricked by deceptive contracts that only seek to take advantage of you.

definitions: To perpetrate a deception or fraud beyond literal goods, including promises, statements, or agreements.

examples.sentence: El jefe dio gato por liebre al prometer un aumento que nunca llegó, dejando a los empleados decepcionados.
examples.translation: The boss perpetrated a deception by promising a raise that never came, leaving the employees disappointed.

examples.sentence: En la negociación, dieron gato por liebre al ofrecer condiciones que parecían buenas pero ocultaban cláusulas abusivas.
examples.translation: In the negotiation, they deceived by offering terms that seemed good but hid abusive clauses.

examples.sentence: No caigas en la trampa de dar gato por liebre en tus acuerdos; sé siempre honesto con los demás.
examples.translation: Don’t fall into the trap of deceiving others in your agreements; always be honest with others.

definitions: To strike or deliver a physical blow to someone or something.

examples.sentence: El boxeador dio un golpe fuerte en el rostro de su oponente durante el combate y ganó el round.
examples.translation: The boxer delivered a strong blow to his opponent’s face during the fight and won the round.

examples.sentence: No dispares, solo le di un golpe en el brazo para detenerlo sin lastimarlo gravemente.
examples.translation: Don’t shoot, I only hit him on the arm to stop him without seriously hurting him.

examples.sentence: El carpintero dio un golpe con el martillo para clavar el clavo en la madera correctamente.
examples.translation: The carpenter struck with the hammer to drive the nail into the wood properly.

examples.sentence: María dio un golpe en la mesa para llamar la atención de todos los presentes en la reunión.
examples.translation: María hit the table to get the attention of everyone present at the meeting.

definitions: To hit or impact with force.

examples.sentence: El coche dio un golpe contra el muro y quedó dañado en la parte delantera.
examples.translation: The car hit the wall and was damaged in the front part.

examples.sentence: La pelota dio un golpe fuerte en la ventana y casi la rompe por completo.
examples.translation: The ball struck the window hard and almost broke it completely.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, un rayo dio un golpe en el árbol y lo partió en dos.
examples.translation: During the storm, lightning struck the tree and split it in two.

examples.sentence: El tren dio un golpe seco al detenerse bruscamente en la estación final.
examples.translation: The train gave a sharp jolt when it stopped abruptly at the final station.

definitions: (Typically used in the negative: no dar golpe) To refrain from working or making any effort; to idle or loaf.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano no da golpe en todo el día, solo se queda acostado viendo televisión sin hacer nada.
examples.translation: My brother doesn’t lift a finger all day, he just lies down watching TV without doing anything.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué no das golpe y me ayudas a limpiar la casa en vez de estar sentado todo el tiempo?
examples.translation: Why don’t you do some work and help me clean the house instead of just sitting all the time?

examples.sentence: Desde que perdió su empleo, no ha dado ni un golpe y pasa los días sin hacer nada productivo.
examples.translation: Since he lost his job, he hasn’t done a thing and spends his days doing nothing productive.

definitions: To carry out a sudden, decisive action that yields a large gain, often used for a lucrative criminal act such as a robbery or heist (equivalent to 'pull off the job' or 'make the score').

examples.sentence: Los ladrones dieron un golpe en la joyería durante la noche y se llevaron una gran cantidad de piedras preciosas.
examples.translation: The thieves pulled off a heist at the jewelry store during the night and took a large amount of precious stones.

examples.sentence: Si van a dar un golpe, deben planearlo muy bien para no ser atrapados por la policía.
examples.translation: If they are going to pull off the job, they must plan it very well to avoid being caught by the police.

examples.sentence: La banda dio un golpe inesperado en el banco central y desapareció antes de que llegara la seguridad.
examples.translation: The gang carried out an unexpected heist at the central bank and disappeared before security arrived.

definitions: To adopt a habitually inactive or lazy lifestyle, performing little or no productive work.

examples.sentence: Desde que se jubiló, mi tío da golpe y pasa sus días sin hacer ninguna actividad laboral.
examples.translation: Since he retired, my uncle has been idle and spends his days without doing any work.

examples.sentence: Ella prefiere dar golpe y disfrutar de la vida en lugar de estar estresada por el trabajo todo el tiempo.
examples.translation: She prefers to loaf around and enjoy life instead of being stressed about work all the time.

examples.sentence: No puedo permitir que mis hijos den golpe; es importante que aprendan el valor del esfuerzo desde jóvenes.
examples.translation: I can’t allow my children to be lazy; it’s important they learn the value of effort from a young age.

definitions: To execute a coup or bold strategic move (e.g., political coup), especially when described as 'dar un golpe'.

examples.sentence: El general decidió dar un golpe de estado para tomar el control del país y derrocar al gobierno corrupto.
examples.translation: The general decided to execute a coup to take control of the country and overthrow the corrupt government.

examples.sentence: Si dan un golpe político, la estabilidad de la región podría verse gravemente afectada durante meses.
examples.translation: If they carry out a political coup, the region’s stability could be severely affected for months.

examples.sentence: Durante la historia, varios países han dado golpes para cambiar sus regímenes de manera abrupta.
examples.translation: Throughout history, several countries have executed coups to abruptly change their regimes.

definitions: To cause a feeling of discomfort, repulsion, or squeamishness; to make someone feel uneasy or creeped out.

examples.sentence: Me da grima tocar esas telas ásperas porque siento que me raspan la piel y es muy incómodo.
examples.translation: It creeps me out to touch those rough fabrics because I feel like they scrape my skin and it’s very uncomfortable.

examples.sentence: La película me dio grima en varias escenas por lo sangrientas y violentas que eran.
examples.translation: The movie made me feel uneasy in several scenes because of how bloody and violent they were.

examples.sentence: Cuando vi el insecto en la cocina, me dio grima y tuve que salir rápidamente para calmarme.
examples.translation: When I saw the insect in the kitchen, it made me feel creeped out and I had to leave quickly to calm down.

definitions: To provoke an instinctive negative physical reaction such as shuddering, chills, or aversion.

examples.sentence: La sensación de tener las uñas largas me da grima y me provoca un escalofrío inmediato.
examples.translation: The feeling of having long nails gives me the creeps and causes an immediate shudder.

examples.sentence: A muchas personas les da grima escuchar ciertos sonidos como el de una pizarra rayándose o un tenedor en un plato.
examples.translation: Many people feel uneasy hearing certain sounds like a chalkboard being scratched or a fork on a plate.

examples.sentence: Ver sangre me da grima y prefiero no mirar cuando alguien se lastima en las películas o la vida real.
examples.translation: Seeing blood makes me feel squeamish and I prefer not to look when someone gets hurt in movies or real life.

definitions: To schedule or assign a specific time for an appointment, meeting, or service.

examples.sentence: El doctor me dio hora para el próximo martes por la tarde.
examples.translation: The doctor scheduled me an appointment for next Tuesday afternoon.

examples.sentence: ¿Podrías darme hora para la reunión de mañana? Necesito organizar mi agenda.
examples.translation: Could you set a time for tomorrow's meeting? I need to organize my schedule.

examples.sentence: La secretaria siempre da hora con mucha anticipación para evitar confusiones.
examples.translation: The secretary always assigns appointments well in advance to avoid confusion.

definitions: To provide a time slot to a person for attendance, consultation, or reservation.

examples.sentence: Me dieron hora para la consulta con el psicólogo a las diez de la mañana.
examples.translation: They gave me a time slot for the psychologist consultation at ten in the morning.

examples.sentence: Si quieres asistir a la charla, tienes que dar hora antes del viernes.
examples.translation: If you want to attend the talk, you need to book a slot before Friday.

examples.sentence: Nos dieron hora para la visita guiada a las tres en punto, así que no llegues tarde.
examples.translation: They scheduled us a time slot for the guided tour at three o'clock, so don't be late.

definitions: To be of no importance or consequence to someone; to not matter to a person.

examples.sentence: A Juan le da igual si vamos al cine o al teatro, mientras salgamos juntos.
examples.translation: Juan doesn't care whether we go to the cinema or the theater, as long as we go together.

examples.sentence: No me da igual que olvides mi cumpleaños, esperaba más atención de tu parte.
examples.translation: It does matter to me if you forget my birthday; I expected more attention from you.

examples.sentence: A ella le da igual el color del coche, sólo quiere que sea cómodo y seguro.
examples.translation: She doesn't care about the color of the car, she just wants it to be comfortable and safe.

definitions: To express indifference regarding a choice, outcome, or opinion.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres té o café? Me da igual, lo que prefieras está bien para mí.
examples.translation: Do you want tea or coffee? I don't mind, whatever you prefer is fine with me.

examples.sentence: Me da igual si llegamos temprano o tarde, lo importante es que disfrutemos el viaje.
examples.translation: I don't care if we arrive early or late, the important thing is to enjoy the trip.

examples.sentence: Podrías elegir el restaurante, a mí me da igual mientras haya opciones vegetarianas.
examples.translation: You could choose the restaurant, I don't mind as long as there are vegetarian options.

definitions: To indicate that two or more options or outcomes are equivalent in effect; to make no difference to the result.

examples.sentence: Puedes venir el martes o el jueves, me da igual, ambos días me funcionan igual de bien.
examples.translation: You can come on Tuesday or Thursday, it makes no difference to me, both days work equally well.

examples.sentence: Nos da igual que el partido sea aquí o allá, lo importante es ganar el campeonato.
examples.translation: It doesn't matter to us whether the match is here or there, the important thing is to win the championship.

examples.sentence: Para el examen, me da igual usar bolígrafo azul o negro; lo que cuenta es el contenido.
examples.translation: For the exam, it makes no difference whether I use a blue or black pen; the content is what counts.

definitions: To state that different alternatives lead to the same consequence or are interchangeable.

examples.sentence: Si tomamos el camino corto o el largo, nos va a dar igual, porque el tráfico está denso en ambos.
examples.translation: Whether we take the short or long route, it will be the same, because traffic is heavy on both.

examples.sentence: No importa si compras el modelo A o el B, al final te va a dar igual porque las funciones son similares.
examples.translation: It doesn't matter if you buy model A or B, in the end it will be the same because the features are similar.

examples.sentence: Puedes elegir cualquier color para la pared, me va a dar igual; todos combinan con los muebles.
examples.translation: You can choose any color for the wall, it will be the same to me; they all match the furniture.

definitions: To flatter someone excessively or insincerely in order to gain favor or achieve a purpose.

examples.sentence: Carlos siempre le da jabón al jefe para que le apruebe los días libres.
examples.translation: Carlos always flatters the boss to get his days off approved.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando me dan jabón, prefiero que me digan la verdad sin rodeos.
examples.translation: I don't like it when they flatter me; I prefer to be told the truth straight.

examples.sentence: Si quieres que te ayuden, tendrás que dar jabón un poco, pero sin exagerar.
examples.translation: If you want them to help you, you'll have to flatter a little, but not too much.

definitions: To polish, gloss over, or otherwise try to make something appear better than it really is; to give superficial improvement or spin.

examples.sentence: El político dio jabón a su imagen pública, pero no cumplió ninguna promesa.
examples.translation: The politician glossed over his public image, but didn't fulfill any promises.

examples.sentence: No dejes que te den jabón con esas ofertas que suenan demasiado buenas para ser verdad.
examples.translation: Don't let them polish things over with those offers that sound too good to be true.

examples.sentence: La empresa intentó dar jabón al informe para que pareciera que los resultados eran mejores.
examples.translation: The company tried to gloss over the report to make the results look better.

definitions: To pester, annoy, or bore someone persistently, often by repeating requests or complaints.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano no para de dar la barrila con que quiere jugar a la consola todo el día.
examples.translation: My brother keeps pestering me about wanting to play the console all day.

examples.sentence: No le des la barrila a mamá con tus quejas, que ya está cansada después del trabajo.
examples.translation: Don't pester mom with your complaints, she's already tired after work.

examples.sentence: Aunque le dijimos que no, sigue dándonos la barrila para salir esta noche.
examples.translation: Even though we told him no, he keeps annoying us to go out tonight.

definitions: To bother, pester, or nag someone by talking repeatedly about the same subject or by making persistent demands.

examples.sentence: Pedro me dio la brasa todo el día con sus historias del trabajo.
examples.translation: Pedro bothered me all day with his work stories.

examples.sentence: No le des la brasa a Ana con ese tema, que ya está cansada de escucharlo.
examples.translation: Don't nag Ana about that topic; she's tired of hearing it.

examples.sentence: Los vecinos dieron la brasa varias veces por el ruido de la fiesta.
examples.translation: The neighbors repeatedly bothered us because of the noise from the party.

definitions: To bore someone with long or tedious talk; to be a nuisance through repeated or insistent behavior.

examples.sentence: El profesor me dio la brasa con que tenía que mejorar mis notas para pasar el curso.
examples.translation: The teacher nagged me that I had to improve my grades to pass the course.

examples.sentence: No aguanto que me den la brasa con la dieta todo el tiempo, necesito un descanso.
examples.translation: I can't stand being nagged about the diet all the time; I need a break.

examples.sentence: Mis amigos me dieron la brasa para que saliera con ellos, aunque yo prefería quedarme en casa.
examples.translation: My friends kept pestering me to go out with them, even though I preferred to stay home.

definitions: To confront a situation or person directly, especially by accepting responsibility, blame, or consequences.

examples.sentence: Cuando surgió el problema, Elena decidió dar la cara y asumir la responsabilidad.
examples.translation: When the problem arose, Elena decided to face it and take responsibility.

examples.sentence: No todos los políticos están dispuestos a dar la cara cuando se les cuestiona.
examples.translation: Not all politicians are willing to confront questions when challenged.

examples.sentence: Aunque fue difícil, el director dio la cara ante la prensa y explicó la situación.
examples.translation: Although it was difficult, the director faced the press and explained the situation.

definitions: To show oneself publicly or appear in person to face questions, criticism, or duty.

examples.sentence: El acusado tuvo que dar la cara en el juicio y responder a todas las preguntas.
examples.translation: The defendant had to appear in court and answer all the questions.

examples.sentence: Después del escándalo, el cantante dio la cara públicamente para aclarar los rumores.
examples.translation: After the scandal, the singer appeared publicly to clarify the rumors.

examples.sentence: Siempre es mejor dar la cara y enfrentar las críticas con honestidad.
examples.translation: It's always better to face things directly and confront criticism honestly.

definitions: To bore or pester someone with long, tedious, or repetitive talk; to lecture or nag insistently.

examples.sentence: No le des la chapa a Luis con lo mismo de siempre, que ya estamos cansados de escucharlo.
examples.translation: Don't bore Luis with the same old stuff; we're tired of hearing it.

examples.sentence: Mi jefe me dio la chapa toda la mañana con las nuevas reglas de la empresa.
examples.translation: My boss lectured me all morning about the new company rules.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que hablamos, me das la chapa con tus problemas y no me dejas ni hablar.
examples.translation: Every time we talk, you bore me with your problems and don't let me speak.

definitions: To turn one's back; to turn physically away from someone or something.

examples.sentence: El niño dio la espalda a su padre cuando se enojó por el castigo.
examples.translation: The boy turned his back on his father when he was angry about the punishment.

examples.sentence: Durante la discusión, Marta le dio la espalda a Juan y se fue de la habitación.
examples.translation: During the argument, Marta turned her back on Juan and left the room.

examples.sentence: No le des la espalda a tus amigos en los momentos difíciles, siempre necesitan apoyo.
examples.translation: Don't turn your back on your friends in difficult times; they always need support.

examples.sentence: El perro dio la espalda al extraño y se alejó lentamente sin mostrar agresión.
examples.translation: The dog turned its back to the stranger and walked away slowly without showing aggression.

definitions: To abandon, shun, or refuse to help someone or something; to ignore or refuse to face a person, duty, problem, or cause.

examples.sentence: Después de la pelea, ella le dio la espalda y no quiso saber nada más de él.
examples.translation: After the fight, she abandoned him and didn't want to know anything more about him.

examples.sentence: La empresa le dio la espalda a sus empleados durante la crisis y no ofreció ayuda.
examples.translation: The company turned its back on its employees during the crisis and offered no help.

examples.sentence: No podemos dar la espalda a los problemas sociales, debemos actuar con responsabilidad.
examples.translation: We can't ignore social problems; we must act responsibly.

definitions: To feel like doing something; to have the desire or will to do something.

examples.sentence: Hoy me da la gana salir a caminar y disfrutar del parque.
examples.translation: Today I feel like going for a walk and enjoying the park.

examples.sentence: Si me diera la gana, podría aprender a tocar guitarra en poco tiempo.
examples.translation: If I felt like it, I could learn to play guitar in a short time.

examples.sentence: No hizo nada porque no le daba la gana trabajar ese día.
examples.translation: He did nothing because he didn't feel like working that day.

definitions: Used impersonally to mean 'to please' or 'to be one's wish' (as in 'hacer lo que me da la gana' = 'to do as I please').

examples.sentence: Ella hace lo que le da la gana sin importar lo que piensen los demás.
examples.translation: She does whatever she pleases regardless of what others think.

examples.sentence: Aquí nadie me dice qué hacer, hago lo que me da la gana.
examples.translation: No one tells me what to do here; I do as I please.

examples.sentence: Si te diera la gana, podrías cambiar de opinión y ayudar con el proyecto.
examples.translation: If you felt like it, you could change your mind and help with the project.

definitions: For a clock or timepiece to strike or chime in order to indicate the hour.

examples.sentence: El reloj antiguo de la iglesia da la hora con un sonido fuerte y claro cada hora.
examples.translation: The old church clock chimes loudly and clearly every hour.

examples.sentence: Cuando el reloj da la hora, todos paran para escuchar la campana.
examples.translation: When the clock strikes the hour, everyone stops to listen to the bell.

examples.sentence: El reloj de la torre da la hora desde hace más de un siglo sin fallar.
examples.translation: The tower clock has been chiming the hour for over a century without failing.

examples.sentence: En el pueblo, es tradición que el reloj de la plaza dé la hora al mediodía con cinco campanadas.
examples.translation: In the town, it is a tradition that the square clock chimes five times at noon.

definitions: To tell someone the current time; to provide the time on request.

examples.sentence: ¿Me puedes dar la hora? No llevo reloj y necesito saber si es tarde.
examples.translation: Can you tell me the time? I don't wear a watch and need to know if it's late.

examples.sentence: El guardia de seguridad dio la hora a los visitantes que preguntaban en la entrada.
examples.translation: The security guard told the time to visitors who asked at the entrance.

examples.sentence: Cuando le di la hora exacta, se sorprendió de lo rápido que había pasado el día.
examples.translation: When I told him the exact time, he was surprised at how fast the day had gone.

examples.sentence: Si me das la hora, puedo calcular cuánto tiempo falta para la reunión.
examples.translation: If you tell me the time, I can calculate how much time is left until the meeting.

definitions: To annoy, pester, or bother someone persistently; to hassle or make a nuisance of oneself to others.

examples.sentence: No me des la lata con tus problemas, tengo suficiente con los míos.
examples.translation: Don't bother me with your problems; I have enough of my own.

examples.sentence: Los niños dieron la lata toda la mañana hasta que les dimos un juego nuevo.
examples.translation: The kids annoyed us all morning until we gave them a new game.

examples.sentence: Si sigues dándome la lata, no voy a poder concentrarme en el trabajo.
examples.translation: If you keep bothering me, I won't be able to concentrate on work.

definitions: To cause trouble or recurrent inconvenience, as with a persistent problem, ailment, or obstacle.

examples.sentence: La avería del coche me está dando la lata desde hace semanas y no sé cuándo se arreglará.
examples.translation: The car breakdown has been causing me trouble for weeks and I don't know when it will be fixed.

examples.sentence: Ese problema de salud le dio la lata durante mucho tiempo antes de mejorar.
examples.translation: That health problem troubled him for a long time before he got better.

examples.sentence: La conexión a internet da la lata a menudo y es difícil trabajar en línea.
examples.translation: The internet connection often causes trouble and it's hard to work online.

definitions: To pester, nag, or annoy people repeatedly; to make a nuisance of oneself by persistent complaining, demanding, or bothering.

examples.sentence: María no dejaba de dar la murga con sus problemas durante toda la cena.
examples.translation: María kept nagging with her problems throughout the entire dinner.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué me das la murga cada vez que llego tarde? Ya entendí la lección.
examples.translation: Why do you keep pestering me every time I arrive late? I already got the lesson.

examples.sentence: Los vecinos estaban hartos porque el perro no dejaba de dar la murga con sus ladridos por la noche.
examples.translation: The neighbors were fed up because the dog wouldn't stop annoying with its barking at night.

definitions: To attract attention or stand out in an excessive, inappropriate, or ostentatious way, often producing a negative impression.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, Juan dio la nota con ese traje tan llamativo que nadie pudo ignorar.
examples.translation: At the party, Juan attracted attention with that flashy suit that no one could ignore.

examples.sentence: No quiero dar la nota en la reunión, así que elegiré un atuendo más sobrio.
examples.translation: I don't want to stand out in an inappropriate way at the meeting, so I'll choose a more sober outfit.

examples.sentence: Siempre da la nota cuando entra a un lugar con su comportamiento exagerado.
examples.translation: He always attracts attention by behaving in an exaggerated way when entering a place.

definitions: To make a scene or cause a commotion by behaving loudly, conspicuously, or provocatively.

examples.sentence: No debiste dar la nota gritando en el restaurante, eso incomodó a todos.
examples.translation: You shouldn't have made a scene by shouting in the restaurant; it made everyone uncomfortable.

examples.sentence: Si sigues dando la nota con tus protestas, podrían pedirte que salgas del evento.
examples.translation: If you keep causing a commotion with your protests, they might ask you to leave the event.

examples.sentence: Ella dio la nota cuando empezó a discutir en voz alta durante la conferencia.
examples.translation: She made a scene when she started arguing loudly during the conference.

definitions: To produce or sound a musical note or pitch (literal musical sense).

examples.sentence: El piano dio la nota correcta al comienzo del concierto, marcando el tono para toda la pieza.
examples.translation: The piano produced the correct note at the start of the concert, setting the tone for the entire piece.

examples.sentence: Cuando toques la guitarra, asegúrate de dar la nota justo en el momento indicado.
examples.translation: When you play the guitar, make sure to sound the note exactly at the right moment.

examples.sentence: El violinista dio la nota aguda con gran precisión durante su solo.
examples.translation: The violinist produced the high note with great precision during his solo.

examples.sentence: No se escuchó bien porque el saxofón no dio la nota esperada en la última parte.
examples.translation: It didn't sound good because the saxophone didn't produce the expected note in the last part.

definitions: To give a mark, grade, or formal note about someone's performance or condition (e.g., to assign a score or issue a written note).

examples.sentence: El profesor dio la nota final a cada estudiante después del examen de matemáticas.
examples.translation: The teacher gave the final grade to each student after the math exam.

examples.sentence: Nos dieron la nota de presentación con algunos comentarios para mejorarla.
examples.translation: They gave us the grade for the presentation with some comments to improve it.

examples.sentence: Antes de irnos, el jefe dio la nota sobre el desempeño del equipo este trimestre.
examples.translation: Before leaving, the boss gave the note about the team's performance this quarter.

examples.sentence: La enfermera dio la nota médica que certificaba la incapacidad temporal del paciente.
examples.translation: The nurse gave the medical note certifying the patient's temporary incapacity.

definitions: To give someone the floor in a meeting, assembly, or public event; to allow another person to speak.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, el presidente dio la palabra a Ana para que explicara su propuesta.
examples.translation: During the meeting, the president gave Ana the floor to explain her proposal.

examples.sentence: Me dieron la palabra al final para expresar mis dudas sobre el proyecto.
examples.translation: They gave me the floor at the end to express my doubts about the project.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes darme la palabra un momento? Quiero aclarar un punto importante.
examples.translation: Can you give me the floor for a moment? I want to clarify an important point.

definitions: To give one's word or make a promise; to pledge verbally to do or uphold something.

examples.sentence: Te doy la palabra que cumpliré con todo lo que prometí en el contrato.
examples.translation: I give you my word that I will fulfill everything I promised in the contract.

examples.sentence: Nos dieron la palabra de que las obras finalizarían a tiempo, pero no fue así.
examples.translation: They gave us their word that the works would finish on time, but it wasn't so.

examples.sentence: Si me das la palabra de que no lo repetirás, te contaré lo sucedido.
examples.translation: If you give me your word that you won't repeat it, I'll tell you what happened.

definitions: To proclaim or deliver a religious message or the teachings of a faith (e.g., to preach the Word).

examples.sentence: El pastor dio la palabra con un sermón que conmovió a toda la congregación.
examples.translation: The pastor preached the Word with a sermon that moved the entire congregation.

examples.sentence: Cada domingo, la madre Teresa daba la palabra en la iglesia del pueblo.
examples.translation: Every Sunday, Mother Teresa delivered the Word in the village church.

examples.sentence: Durante la ceremonia, el obispo dio la palabra para enseñar sobre la fe y la esperanza.
examples.translation: During the ceremony, the bishop preached the Word to teach about faith and hope.

definitions: To add, pour, or stir a sauce into or over a dish; to give a dish its sauce.

examples.sentence: Mi abuela siempre da la salsa con mucho cariño para que la paella quede perfecta.
examples.translation: My grandmother always adds the sauce with much care so that the paella turns out perfect.

examples.sentence: Después de cocinar el pollo, dio la salsa por encima antes de servirlo en la mesa.
examples.translation: After cooking the chicken, she poured the sauce over it before serving it at the table.

examples.sentence: Si das la salsa con cuidado y la mezclas bien, el guiso tendrá un sabor delicioso.
examples.translation: If you add the sauce carefully and stir it well, the stew will have a delicious flavor.

examples.sentence: No olvides dar la salsa justo antes de que los invitados lleguen para que esté fresca.
examples.translation: Don't forget to add the sauce just before the guests arrive so that it is fresh.

definitions: To pester, nag, or bother someone persistently; to be a continual annoyance through repeated complaints, demands, or tedious talk.

examples.sentence: Pedro no paraba de dar la tabarra con sus historias aburridas durante el viaje.
examples.translation: Pedro wouldn't stop bothering with his boring stories during the trip.

examples.sentence: ¿Podrías dejar de dar la tabarra? Estoy intentando concentrarme en el trabajo.
examples.translation: Could you stop pestering? I'm trying to concentrate on work.

examples.sentence: Los niños dieron la tabarra hasta que les compramos los juguetes nuevos.
examples.translation: The kids nagged persistently until we bought them new toys.

definitions: To measure up to expectations or requirements; to perform adequately or be up to the task.

examples.sentence: Laura dio la talla en la entrevista y consiguió el trabajo que quería.
examples.translation: Laura measured up in the interview and got the job she wanted.

examples.sentence: Si no das la talla en este proyecto, tendremos que buscar a alguien más competente.
examples.translation: If you don't measure up in this project, we'll have to look for someone more competent.

examples.sentence: El equipo dio la talla a pesar de las dificultades y ganó el campeonato.
examples.translation: The team performed adequately despite the difficulties and won the championship.

definitions: To breastfeed an infant; to feed a baby with milk directly from the mother's breast.

examples.sentence: La madre dio la teta a su bebé durante toda la noche para calmarlo.
examples.translation: The mother breastfed her baby throughout the night to calm him.

examples.sentence: Cuando di la teta, sentí una conexión muy especial con mi hijo.
examples.translation: When I breastfed, I felt a very special connection with my son.

examples.sentence: Ella no pudo dar la teta por problemas de salud y optó por la leche de fórmula.
examples.translation: She couldn't breastfeed due to health problems and opted for formula milk.

examples.sentence: Dar la teta es un acto natural que beneficia tanto a la madre como al bebé.
examples.translation: Breastfeeding is a natural act that benefits both mother and baby.

definitions: To apply the final coat of paint, varnish, or similar finishing layer to a surface.

examples.sentence: Terminé de dar la última mano de pintura en la puerta antes de que oscureciera.
examples.translation: I finished applying the final coat of paint on the door before it got dark.

examples.sentence: Nos pidieron dar la última mano de barniz para proteger mejor la mesa de madera.
examples.translation: They asked us to apply the final coat of varnish to better protect the wooden table.

examples.sentence: El carpintero dio la última mano de laca y dejó el mueble con un acabado brillante.
examples.translation: The carpenter applied the final coat of lacquer and left the furniture with a shiny finish.

examples.sentence: Antes de entregar el proyecto, di la última mano de pintura para que todo estuviera perfecto.
examples.translation: Before delivering the project, I applied the final coat of paint so that everything was perfect.

definitions: To give the finishing touches to a work, task, or project; to complete the last phase of something.

examples.sentence: Estamos dando la última mano al informe para presentarlo mañana en la reunión.
examples.translation: We are putting the finishing touches on the report to present it tomorrow at the meeting.

examples.sentence: Cuando dieron la última mano al proyecto, todos respiraron aliviados por el trabajo terminado.
examples.translation: When they gave the finishing touches to the project, everyone breathed a sigh of relief for the completed work.

examples.sentence: Si das la última mano al diseño esta semana, podremos lanzarlo en la fecha prevista.
examples.translation: If you put the finishing touches on the design this week, we can launch it on the scheduled date.

definitions: To apply the final brushstroke to a painting or painted surface.

examples.sentence: El pintor dio la última pincelada y la obra quedó lista para la exposición.
examples.translation: The painter applied the final brushstroke and the work was ready for the exhibition.

examples.sentence: Después de dar la última pincelada, el lienzo mostró colores vivos y detalles precisos.
examples.translation: After applying the final brushstroke, the canvas showed vivid colors and precise details.

examples.sentence: El artista dio la última pincelada con cuidado para no arruinar el acabado.
examples.translation: The artist carefully gave the final brushstroke so as not to ruin the finish.

examples.sentence: Antes de dar la última pincelada, se aseguró de que todo estuviera perfectamente seco.
examples.translation: Before applying the final brushstroke, he made sure everything was perfectly dry.

definitions: To add the final detail or finishing touch that completes a work, plan, or composition.

examples.sentence: El escritor dio la última pincelada a su novela antes de enviarla a la editorial.
examples.translation: The writer added the final touch to his novel before sending it to the publisher.

examples.sentence: Cuando dieron la última pincelada al plan de negocio, todos sintieron que estaba completo y sólido.
examples.translation: When they added the finishing touch to the business plan, everyone felt it was complete and solid.

examples.sentence: Si quieres impresionar, da la última pincelada con una presentación impecable y segura.
examples.translation: If you want to impress, add the finishing touch with a flawless and confident presentation.

definitions: To pester, nag, or bother someone persistently by repeatedly bringing up a subject or making demands.

examples.sentence: Mi jefe me dio la vara todo el día para que terminara el informe antes del lunes.
examples.translation: My boss nagged me all day to finish the report before Monday.

examples.sentence: No me des la vara con tus quejas, mejor busca una solución al problema.
examples.translation: Don't bother me with your complaints; better find a solution to the problem.

examples.sentence: Los estudiantes dieron la vara al profesor hasta que les aclaró la duda.
examples.translation: The students kept pestering the teacher until he clarified their doubt.

definitions: To bore others with long, repetitive moralizing, lecturing, or proselytizing about a particular topic.

examples.sentence: Pedro siempre da la vara hablando de política, y la gente termina aburrida.
examples.translation: Pedro always bores others by lecturing about politics, and people end up bored.

examples.sentence: No quiero que me des la vara con sermones sobre hábitos saludables, gracias.
examples.translation: I don't want you to bore me with lectures about healthy habits, thanks.

examples.sentence: Cuando das la vara con tus discursos moralizadores, muchos prefieren cambiar de tema.
examples.translation: When you bore others with your moralizing speeches, many prefer to change the subject.

definitions: To threaten or give someone a hard time; in some contexts used as a mild threat of physical punishment or confrontation (context-dependent).

examples.sentence: Si me das la vara otra vez, te juro que no voy a soportarlo más.
examples.translation: If you threaten me again, I swear I won't put up with it anymore.

examples.sentence: Los matones del barrio solían dar la vara a los más débiles para intimidarlos.
examples.translation: The neighborhood bullies used to give a hard time to the weaker ones to intimidate them.

examples.sentence: No es necesario que me des la vara; podemos resolver esto hablando con calma.
examples.translation: It's not necessary to threaten me; we can solve this by talking calmly.

definitions: To raise the alarm; to alert people or authorities to an immediate danger, emergency, or urgent threat.

examples.sentence: Cuando vieron el incendio, rápidamente dieron la voz de alarma para evacuar el edificio.
examples.translation: When they saw the fire, they quickly raised the alarm to evacuate the building.

examples.sentence: El guardia dio la voz de alarma al detectar movimientos sospechosos en el perímetro.
examples.translation: The guard raised the alarm upon detecting suspicious movements in the perimeter.

examples.sentence: Es importante dar la voz de alarma ante cualquier señal de peligro para prevenir accidentes.
examples.translation: It's important to raise the alarm at any sign of danger to prevent accidents.

definitions: To warn the public or relevant parties about a significant problem, risk, or developing situation in order to prompt attention or action.

examples.sentence: Los científicos dieron la voz de alarma sobre el rápido deterioro del medio ambiente.
examples.translation: Scientists warned the public about the rapid deterioration of the environment.

examples.sentence: Las autoridades dieron la voz de alarma tras detectar un aumento en los casos de enfermedad.
examples.translation: Authorities warned after detecting an increase in disease cases.

examples.sentence: Cuando dieron la voz de alarma sobre la crisis económica, muchos comenzaron a prepararse.
examples.translation: When they raised the alarm about the economic crisis, many began to prepare.

definitions: To delay or procrastinate deliberately; to stall or give the runaround when asked to do something or to answer.

examples.sentence: El político dio largas a las preguntas difíciles para evitar comprometerse con una respuesta clara.
examples.translation: The politician delayed difficult questions to avoid committing to a clear answer.

examples.sentence: No me des largas, dime si aceptarás la propuesta o no de una vez.
examples.translation: Don't stall me; tell me if you will accept the proposal or not at once.

examples.sentence: La empresa dio largas a la solicitud de aumento de sueldo durante meses sin dar una respuesta definitiva.
examples.translation: The company procrastinated on the salary increase request for months without giving a definitive answer.

definitions: To take long walks; to walk for an extended period (used with caminatas or similar collocations).

examples.sentence: Ayer di largas caminatas por el parque para despejar mi mente después del trabajo.
examples.translation: Yesterday I took long walks in the park to clear my mind after work.

examples.sentence: Nos gusta dar largas caminatas por la playa al atardecer los fines de semana.
examples.translation: We like to take long walks on the beach at sunset on weekends.

examples.sentence: Durante las vacaciones, dimos largas caminatas por las montañas para disfrutar del paisaje.
examples.translation: During the holidays, we took long walks through the mountains to enjoy the scenery.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres dar largas caminatas conmigo esta tarde para hacer ejercicio juntos?
examples.translation: Do you want to take long walks with me this afternoon to exercise together?

definitions: To postpone dealing with an issue or person, often by making excuses or avoiding a decision.

examples.sentence: El banco dio largas a la solicitud de la hipoteca con varias excusas y retrasos.
examples.translation: The bank postponed dealing with the mortgage application with various excuses and delays.

examples.sentence: No me des largas, necesito una respuesta clara sobre el contrato cuanto antes.
examples.translation: Don't postpone dealing with me; I need a clear answer about the contract as soon as possible.

examples.sentence: Cuando le pregunté sobre su participación, empezó a dar largas para no comprometerse.
examples.translation: When I asked him about his participation, he started stalling to avoid committing.

definitions: To continue or extend until a very late hour; to become very late into the night or early morning.

examples.sentence: Anoche dimos las tantas celebrando el cumpleaños de Ana con amigos y música.
examples.translation: Last night we stayed up until very late celebrating Ana's birthday with friends and music.

examples.sentence: No me gusta dar las tantas en el trabajo porque al día siguiente estoy agotado.
examples.translation: I don't like staying up very late at work because the next day I'm exhausted.

examples.sentence: Si seguimos preparando el evento, daremos las tantas y no tendremos descanso.
examples.translation: If we keep preparing the event, we will stay up very late and have no rest.

definitions: To be out or occupied until the small hours.

examples.sentence: Ella suele dar las tantas en los bares con sus amigos durante los fines de semana.
examples.translation: She is often out until the early hours in bars with her friends on weekends.

examples.sentence: Los estudiantes dieron las tantas estudiando para los exámenes finales en la biblioteca.
examples.translation: The students stayed up very late studying for final exams in the library.

examples.sentence: No me gusta dar las tantas porque prefiero descansar bien para el día siguiente.
examples.translation: I don't like staying out until very late because I prefer to rest well for the next day.

definitions: To cause someone to wait a long time; to delay someone significantly, often implying they will wait until a very late hour.

examples.sentence: Me hicieron dar las uvas esperando dos horas para que me atendieran en el médico.
examples.translation: They made me wait a long time, literally until the grapes, waiting two hours to be seen by the doctor.

examples.sentence: Si sigues dando las uvas, no llegaré a tiempo al cine para la película.
examples.translation: If you keep making me wait a long time, I won't get to the cinema on time for the movie.

examples.sentence: No quería hacerte dar las uvas, pero el tráfico estaba terrible y llegué tarde.
examples.translation: I didn't want to keep you waiting so long, but the traffic was terrible and I arrived late.

definitions: To keep someone waiting unnecessarily or to postpone attention or action for an extended period.

examples.sentence: María me dio las uvas toda la tarde antes de contestar mi mensaje.
examples.translation: María kept me waiting all afternoon before answering my message.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué me das las uvas cuando te pido ayuda urgente?
examples.translation: Why do you keep me waiting unnecessarily when I ask you for urgent help?

examples.sentence: Nos dieron las uvas en la oficina porque el jefe no llegó hasta muy tarde.
examples.translation: They kept us waiting at the office because the boss didn’t arrive until very late.

definitions: To greet someone by saying 'good morning'; to offer a conventional morning salutation on meeting someone.

examples.sentence: Cada mañana, cuando llego al trabajo, siempre doy los buenos días a mis compañeros.
examples.translation: Every morning, when I arrive at work, I always say good morning to my colleagues.

examples.sentence: ¿Le diste los buenos días a la señora que vive en el apartamento de al lado?
examples.translation: Did you say good morning to the lady who lives in the apartment next door?

examples.sentence: No olvides dar los buenos días al profesor antes de empezar la clase.
examples.translation: Don’t forget to say good morning to the teacher before starting class.

examples.sentence: Siempre damos los buenos días a los vecinos cuando salimos a pasear al perro.
examples.translation: We always say good morning to the neighbors when we go out to walk the dog.

definitions: To provoke, egg on, or incite someone to act, often by teasing, goading, or stirring up agitation.

examples.sentence: No le des manija a Juan, que se enoja con cualquier broma.
examples.translation: Don’t provoke Juan, he gets angry with any joke.

examples.sentence: Mis amigos me dieron manija para que le pidiera una cita a Clara.
examples.translation: My friends egged me on to ask Clara out on a date.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que empiezan a discutir, alguien siempre le da manija para que la pelea continúe.
examples.translation: Every time they start arguing, someone always provokes them to keep the fight going.

definitions: To hype up or excite someone; to generate enthusiasm, interest, or emotional arousal about an event or idea.

examples.sentence: El entrenador nos dio manija antes del partido para motivarnos al máximo.
examples.translation: The coach hyped us up before the match to motivate us fully.

examples.sentence: Ayer en la reunión, el jefe nos dio manija hablando del nuevo proyecto revolucionario.
examples.translation: Yesterday at the meeting, the boss got us excited by talking about the revolutionary new project.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué siempre le das manija a los chicos con esas historias de terror?
examples.translation: Why do you always hype the kids up with those scary stories?

definitions: To give someone a motive or push to respond or take action, typically in a provocative way.

examples.sentence: El comentario negativo le dio manija para responder con dureza en la reunión.
examples.translation: The negative comment gave him a push to respond harshly in the meeting.

examples.sentence: No le des manija con ese tema, que después se pone a discutir sin parar.
examples.translation: Don’t give him a motive with that topic, because then he starts arguing nonstop.

examples.sentence: Me dieron manija para que protestara por el mal servicio en el restaurante.
examples.translation: They gave me a push to complain about the bad service at the restaurant.

definitions: To reverse the movement of a vehicle; to back up.

examples.sentence: Para salir del estacionamiento, primero tienes que dar marcha atrás con cuidado.
examples.translation: To leave the parking lot, you first have to back up carefully.

examples.sentence: El conductor dio marcha atrás lentamente para evitar chocar con el poste.
examples.translation: The driver reversed slowly to avoid hitting the pole.

examples.sentence: Cuando el espacio estaba muy justo, el autobús dio marcha atrás para intentarlo de nuevo.
examples.translation: When the space was too tight, the bus backed up to try again.

examples.sentence: Siempre doy marcha atrás cuando veo que hay niños jugando cerca del camino.
examples.translation: I always back up when I see children playing near the road.

definitions: To withdraw from a decision, promise, agreement, or position; to back down or renege.

examples.sentence: El presidente dio marcha atrás en la decisión tras la presión social.
examples.translation: The president backed down on the decision after social pressure.

examples.sentence: No puedo creer que hayan dado marcha atrás con el acuerdo después de tanto esfuerzo.
examples.translation: I can’t believe they withdrew from the agreement after so much effort.

examples.sentence: Si das marcha atrás ahora, perderás la confianza de todo el equipo.
examples.translation: If you back down now, you will lose the trust of the whole team.

definitions: To move or go backwards physically.

examples.sentence: Durante la caminata, tuvimos que dar marcha atrás cuando vimos la tormenta acercándose.
examples.translation: During the hike, we had to move backwards when we saw the storm approaching.

examples.sentence: El niño dio marcha atrás con miedo al ver el perro grande.
examples.translation: The boy stepped back fearfully when he saw the big dog.

examples.sentence: El coche dio marcha atrás para dejar pasar a los peatones.
examples.translation: The car moved backwards to let the pedestrians pass.

examples.sentence: Al salir del garaje, siempre doy marcha atrás para asegurar que no haya nadie detrás.
examples.translation: When leaving the garage, I always back up to make sure no one is behind.

definitions: To change one's mind or turn back on a course of action, often after hesitation.

examples.sentence: Después de pensarlo bien, dio marcha atrás y no firmó el contrato.
examples.translation: After thinking it over, he changed his mind and didn’t sign the contract.

examples.sentence: No creo que debamos dar marcha atrás ahora que el proyecto está avanzando tan bien.
examples.translation: I don’t think we should turn back now that the project is progressing so well.

examples.sentence: Si das marcha atrás, ¿qué explicación le darás al equipo?
examples.translation: If you change your mind, what explanation will you give to the team?

definitions: To undo or reverse a previous action or policy.

examples.sentence: El gobierno tuvo que dar marcha atrás y cancelar la reforma tras las protestas masivas.
examples.translation: The government had to undo the reform and cancel it after massive protests.

examples.sentence: Dieron marcha atrás en la política de impuestos debido a la fuerte oposición.
examples.translation: They reversed the tax policy due to strong opposition.

examples.sentence: Si queremos conservar a los clientes, no podemos dar marcha atrás en la calidad del servicio.
examples.translation: If we want to keep customers, we can’t undo the quality of the service.

definitions: To offer something valuable, beautiful, or refined to people who will not appreciate it; to waste good things on those who do not recognize their worth.

examples.sentence: No tiene sentido dar margaritas a los cerdos cuando no valoran el esfuerzo que haces.
examples.translation: There’s no point in offering precious things to those who don’t value your effort.

examples.sentence: Siempre que le compro libros raros, siento que le doy margaritas a los cerdos porque no los lee.
examples.translation: Whenever I buy him rare books, I feel like I’m casting pearls before swine because he doesn’t read them.
examples.matched_span: le doy margaritas a los cerdos

examples.sentence: Dimos margaritas a los cerdos al preparar ese banquete para personas que no aprecian la comida gourmet.
examples.translation: We wasted a gourmet banquet on people who don’t appreciate fine food.

examples.sentence: No des margaritas a los cerdos si sabes que no lo van a valorar, mejor invierte ese tiempo en ti mismo.
examples.translation: Don’t offer something valuable to those who won’t appreciate it; better invest that time in yourself.

definitions: Equivalent to 'to cast pearls before swine'—to give something precious to someone who cannot or will not value it.

examples.sentence: Intentar explicar la obra a ese público fue dar margaritas a los cerdos; no entendían nada.
examples.translation: Trying to explain the play to that audience was casting pearls before swine; they didn’t understand anything.

examples.sentence: Le di un regalo muy especial, pero creo que fue dar margaritas a los cerdos porque no lo valoró.
examples.translation: I gave him a very special gift, but I think it was casting pearls before swine because he didn’t appreciate it.

examples.sentence: No pierdas tiempo discutiendo con personas que no quieren entender; es como dar margaritas a los cerdos.
examples.translation: Don’t waste time arguing with people who don’t want to understand; it’s like casting pearls before swine.

definitions: To cause a great deal of trouble, worry, or annoyance.
idiom: dar más mal que un hijo tonto

examples.sentence: Ese proyecto me dio más mal que un hijo tonto; siempre surgían problemas inesperados.
examples.translation: That project caused me more trouble than a foolish child; unexpected problems kept arising.
examples.matched_span: dio más mal que un hijo tonto

examples.sentence: No sé por qué te metiste en eso, te va a dar más mal que un hijo tonto.
examples.translation: I don’t know why you got involved in that; it’s going to cause you lots of trouble.
examples.matched_span: dar más mal que un hijo tonto

examples.sentence: La reforma educativa dio más mal que un hijo tonto porque nadie estaba de acuerdo con ella.
examples.translation: The educational reform caused a lot of trouble because no one agreed with it.
examples.matched_span: dio más mal que un hijo tonto

definitions: To create more problems or difficulties than would be reasonably expected.
idiom: dar más mal que un hijo tonto

examples.sentence: El nuevo sistema dio más mal que un hijo tonto: no funcionaba y generaba constantes quejas.
examples.translation: The new system caused more problems than expected; it didn’t work and generated constant complaints.
examples.matched_span: dio más mal que un hijo tonto

examples.sentence: Esta decisión nos va a dar más mal que un hijo tonto, mejor pensemos otra opción.
examples.translation: This decision will cause us more trouble than it’s worth; better to think of another option.
examples.matched_span: dar más mal que un hijo tonto

examples.sentence: No quiero dar más mal que un hijo tonto, así que prefiero no involucrarme en ese asunto.
examples.translation: I don’t want to cause more trouble than necessary, so I prefer not to get involved in that matter.
examples.matched_span: dar más mal que un hijo tonto

definitions: To be far superior to someone or something; to outclass or outperform decisively.

examples.sentence: En matemáticas, Laura le da mil vueltas a sus compañeros; siempre saca las mejores notas.
examples.translation: In math, Laura outclasses her classmates; she always gets the best grades.

examples.sentence: Este nuevo modelo de teléfono le da mil vueltas al anterior en velocidad y diseño.
examples.translation: This new phone model is far superior to the previous one in speed and design.

examples.sentence: No necesito competir con ellos porque sé que les doy mil vueltas en experiencia.
examples.translation: I don’t need to compete with them because I know I outperform them in experience.

definitions: To waste time or delay by taking many detours or by beating around the bush; to take a long time to arrive at a point.

examples.sentence: Estuvimos dando mil vueltas antes de decidir qué película ver, perdimos mucho tiempo.
examples.translation: We wasted a lot of time beating around the bush before deciding which movie to watch.

examples.sentence: Deja de dar mil vueltas y dime cuál es el problema real.
examples.translation: Stop wasting time and tell me what the real problem is.

examples.sentence: Siempre da mil vueltas para no contestar directamente a las preguntas incómodas.
examples.translation: He always beats around the bush to avoid answering uncomfortable questions directly.

definitions: To make multiple attempts, maneuvers, or rounds of effort in order to achieve or resolve something.

examples.sentence: Tuvimos que dar mil vueltas para conseguir todos los permisos necesarios.
examples.translation: We had to make multiple attempts to get all the necessary permits.

examples.sentence: El detective dio mil vueltas antes de encontrar una pista importante en el caso.
examples.translation: The detective made many maneuvers before finding an important clue in the case.

examples.sentence: Si das mil vueltas, al final conseguirás resolver el problema, solo ten paciencia.
examples.translation: If you keep trying in many ways, you will eventually solve the problem—just be patient.

definitions: To kill; to cause the death of a person or animal.

examples.sentence: El cazador dio muerte al ciervo después de una larga espera en el bosque.
examples.translation: The hunter killed the deer after a long wait in the forest.

examples.sentence: Durante la guerra, muchos soldados dieron muerte a sus enemigos en combate.
examples.translation: During the war, many soldiers killed their enemies in combat.

examples.sentence: El veterinario tuvo que dar muerte al animal porque estaba gravemente herido.
examples.translation: The vet had to euthanize the animal because it was severely injured.

examples.sentence: Los depredadores dan muerte a sus presas para alimentarse y sobrevivir.
examples.translation: Predators kill their prey to feed and survive.

definitions: To execute or order the execution of someone as a legal, military, or official act.

examples.sentence: Durante el juicio, el juez dio muerte legalmente al acusado tras la condena.
examples.translation: During the trial, the judge legally sentenced the defendant to death.

examples.sentence: El general ordenó dar muerte a los prisioneros rebeldes para evitar futuras insurrecciones.
examples.translation: The general ordered the execution of the rebel prisoners to prevent future uprisings.

examples.sentence: En aquella época, dar muerte a los traidores era una práctica común en la guerra.
examples.translation: At that time, executing traitors was a common practice in war.

definitions: To put to death, whether deliberately or as the result of an action.

examples.sentence: La plaga dio muerte a muchas plantas en el jardín durante el verano.
examples.translation: The plague killed many plants in the garden during the summer.

examples.sentence: El veneno que usaron dio muerte a varios animales en el área protegida.
examples.translation: The poison they used caused the death of several animals in the protected area.

examples.sentence: El accidente dio muerte a tres personas y dejó heridas a otras cinco.
examples.translation: The accident caused the death of three people and injured five others.

definitions: To put an end to, destroy, or neutralize something nonphysical (for example, an idea, habit, or problem).

examples.sentence: Esa noticia dio muerte a todas nuestras esperanzas de ganar el concurso.
examples.translation: That news put an end to all our hopes of winning the contest.

examples.sentence: La crisis económica dio muerte a varios proyectos que estaban en marcha.
examples.translation: The economic crisis destroyed several projects that were underway.

examples.sentence: Su negativa dio muerte a cualquier posibilidad de reconciliación entre ellos.
examples.translation: Her refusal put an end to any possibility of reconciliation between them.

definitions: To do any work or make any effort; used negatively in the set expression 'no dar palo al agua' to mean to do nothing, not lift a finger, or be idle.

examples.sentence: En esta empresa, algunos trabajadores no dan palo y solo esperan el sueldo a fin de mes.
examples.translation: In this company, some workers don’t lift a finger and just wait for their paycheck at the end of the month.

examples.sentence: No puedo creer que Juan no dé palo al agua y deje todo el trabajo para los demás.
examples.translation: I can’t believe Juan does nothing and leaves all the work for others.

examples.sentence: Si no quieres dar palo, mejor no te ofrezcas para esta tarea tan difícil.
examples.translation: If you don’t want to do any work, better not volunteer for this difficult task.

definitions: To act without a clear plan or adequate information, making random, unguided attempts; to gropingly try different approaches in the hope that one will work.

examples.sentence: Sin un plan claro, estamos dando palos de ciego y perdiendo tiempo valioso.
examples.translation: Without a clear plan, we are acting blindly and wasting valuable time.

examples.sentence: No puedes seguir dando palos de ciego; necesitas información concreta para avanzar.
examples.translation: You can’t keep groping around; you need concrete information to move forward.

examples.sentence: Los investigadores dieron palos de ciego al principio, pero luego encontraron la pista correcta.
examples.translation: The investigators made random attempts at first, but then they found the right clue.

definitions: To undertake futile or aimless actions, often to appear busy or to give the impression of activity despite lacking a coherent strategy.

examples.sentence: Aunque parece que trabajan mucho, en realidad solo están dando palos de ciego sin resultados claros.
examples.translation: Although they seem to work hard, they are actually making futile efforts without clear results.

examples.sentence: Dieron palos de ciego durante semanas antes de lograr cualquier avance en el proyecto.
examples.translation: They made aimless attempts for weeks before achieving any progress on the project.

examples.sentence: No me gusta dar palos de ciego; prefiero tener un plan definido antes de actuar.
examples.translation: I don’t like acting blindly; I prefer to have a defined plan before acting.

definitions: To notify the appropriate authorities or officials about an incident or event; to file an official report with police, emergency services, or other public bodies.

examples.sentence: Después del accidente, llamé a la policía para dar parte de lo sucedido.
examples.translation: After the accident, I called the police to report what happened.

examples.sentence: El conductor dio parte a su aseguradora inmediatamente tras el choque.
examples.translation: The driver reported the incident to his insurance company immediately after the crash.

examples.sentence: ¿Ya diste parte a las autoridades sobre el robo en la tienda?
examples.translation: Have you already reported the theft at the store to the authorities?

definitions: To give a formal account or dispatch to a superior or to an official record; to report facts, status, or outcomes for administrative or military purposes.

examples.sentence: El oficial dio parte al mando superior sobre el avance en la operación.
examples.translation: The officer gave a report to the superior command about the progress in the operation.

examples.sentence: Cada noche, el guardia da parte de cualquier novedad en el cuartel.
examples.translation: Every night, the guard reports any news at the barracks.

examples.sentence: El piloto dio parte sobre las condiciones meteorológicas antes de despegar.
examples.translation: The pilot gave a report on weather conditions before taking off.

definitions: To arouse pity or compassion in others; to be the cause of someone feeling sorry for a person or situation.

examples.sentence: La historia de aquel perro abandonado me dio pena y decidí ayudarlo.
examples.translation: The story of that abandoned dog made me feel sorry and I decided to help it.

examples.sentence: Me da pena ver a los niños sin acceso a educación en esa comunidad.
examples.translation: It makes me sad to see children without access to education in that community.

examples.sentence: A veces me da pena admitir que no puedo hacer más por ellos.
examples.translation: Sometimes it makes me sad to admit that I can’t do more for them.

definitions: To be pitiable, pathetic, or of such poor quality that it provokes embarrassment or a negative judgment; to reflect badly on someone or something.

examples.sentence: El concierto fue tan malo que realmente me dio pena haber gastado dinero en la entrada.
examples.translation: The concert was so bad that it was truly embarrassing to have spent money on the ticket.

examples.sentence: Su actitud irresponsable da pena y hace que los demás lo juzguen mal.
examples.translation: His irresponsible attitude is pathetic and makes others judge him badly.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que mi equipo dé pena en los partidos importantes.
examples.translation: I don’t like my team to be pitiful in important matches.

definitions: To give rise to or provide grounds for something, such as rumors, speculation, or a particular consequence.

examples.sentence: Esa declaración dio pie a muchos rumores sobre su renuncia.
examples.translation: That statement gave rise to many rumors about his resignation.

examples.sentence: La falta de pruebas dio pie a la especulación en los medios de comunicación.
examples.translation: The lack of evidence provided grounds for speculation in the media.

examples.sentence: Su error dio pie a una investigación interna en la empresa.
examples.translation: His mistake gave rise to an internal investigation in the company.

definitions: Used in set phrases such as 'dar pie con bola' to mean to manage correctly, to get things right, or to perform a task successfully.

examples.sentence: Con esa jugada, el equipo dio pie con bola y ganó el partido sin problemas.
examples.translation: With that play, the team got it right and won the match easily.

examples.sentence: El nuevo empleado dio pie con bola desde el primer día y sorprendió a todos con su eficiencia.
examples.translation: The new employee managed everything correctly from day one and surprised everyone with his efficiency.

examples.sentence: Si quieres tener éxito, tienes que dar pie con bola en cada presentación que hagas.
examples.translation: If you want to succeed, you have to get things right in every presentation you make.

definitions: In the construction 'dar pie atrás', to yield ground, to back down, or to retreat from a previously held position or course of action.

examples.sentence: Después de tantas discusiones, finalmente decidieron dar pie atrás y reconsiderar el proyecto.
examples.translation: After so many arguments, they finally decided to back down and reconsider the project.

examples.sentence: No voy a dar pie atrás en mis convicciones, aunque la presión sea fuerte.
examples.translation: I’m not going to yield ground on my convictions, even if the pressure is strong.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que la empresa dará pie atrás en la propuesta tras las críticas recibidas?
examples.translation: Do you think the company will retreat from the proposal after the criticism received?

definitions: To kill someone; to order or carry out an execution.

examples.sentence: Se rumorea que ese capo ordenó dar piso a varios enemigos para consolidar su poder.
examples.translation: It’s rumored that that boss ordered to kill several enemies to consolidate his power.

examples.sentence: No creo que vayan a dar piso a nadie sin antes investigar bien la situación.
examples.translation: I don’t think they will kill anyone without first thoroughly investigating the situation.

examples.sentence: El sicario fue contratado para dar piso a un traidor del cartel.
examples.translation: The hitman was hired to kill a traitor of the cartel.

examples.sentence: Si le dan piso, nadie sabrá quién fue responsable de la traición.
examples.translation: If they kill him, no one will know who was responsible for the betrayal.

definitions: To beat, defeat, or physically assault someone decisively.

examples.sentence: En el partido de ayer, el equipo rival nos dio piso con un marcador aplastante.
examples.translation: In yesterday’s match, the opposing team beat us decisively with an overwhelming score.

examples.sentence: No deberías meterte con él, porque te podría dar piso sin pensarlo dos veces.
examples.translation: You shouldn’t mess with him, because he could beat you up without thinking twice.

examples.sentence: Cuando llegaron a la pelea, los tipos les dieron piso en menos de cinco minutos.
examples.translation: When they got to the fight, the guys beat them decisively in less than five minutes.

definitions: To have someone killed; to send someone to be killed.

examples.sentence: Se sospecha que el político corrupto dio piso a varios testigos para evitar escándalos.
examples.translation: It’s suspected that the corrupt politician had several witnesses killed to avoid scandals.

examples.sentence: La organización decidió dar piso a quien filtró la información interna.
examples.translation: The organization decided to have killed anyone who leaked the internal information.

examples.sentence: No me sorprendería si la mafia dio piso al informante que los traicionó.
examples.translation: I wouldn’t be surprised if the mafia had the informant who betrayed them killed.

definitions: To humiliate or decisively defeat someone in a conflict, competition, or confrontation.

examples.sentence: En la discusión, me dio piso con argumentos que no pude refutar.
examples.translation: In the argument, he humiliated me decisively with arguments I couldn’t refute.

examples.sentence: Ella le dio piso al rival en el debate con una presentación impecable.
examples.translation: She decisively defeated the opponent in the debate with a flawless presentation.

examples.sentence: No quiero que me den piso en la reunión, así que preparé bien mis puntos.
examples.translation: I don’t want to be humiliated in the meeting, so I prepared my points well.

definitions: To fail to attend an agreed meeting or date; to stand someone up by not showing up.

examples.sentence: Me dieron plantón en la cita y tuve que esperar una hora en el café solo.
examples.translation: They stood me up at the date and I had to wait an hour alone at the café.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué siempre me das plantón cuando más te necesito?
examples.translation: Why do you always stand me up when I need you the most?

examples.sentence: No quiero que me des plantón otra vez; por favor, avísame si no puedes venir.
examples.translation: I don’t want you to stand me up again; please let me know if you can’t come.

definitions: To cancel or neglect an appointment without prior notice, leaving the other person waiting.

examples.sentence: El cliente dio plantón a última hora y perdimos una oportunidad importante.
examples.translation: The client canceled last minute and we lost an important opportunity.

examples.sentence: No me gusta dar plantón a nadie, pero esta vez surgió un imprevisto grave.
examples.translation: I don’t like to cancel on anyone, but this time a serious unforeseen event came up.

examples.sentence: Si vas a dar plantón, por lo menos avísame con tiempo para no esperarte.
examples.translation: If you’re going to cancel, at least let me know in time so I don’t wait for you.

definitions: To consider or declare that something is finished, closed, or complete.

examples.sentence: El juez dio por concluido el juicio tras escuchar todas las pruebas.
examples.translation: The judge declared the trial finished after hearing all the evidence.

examples.sentence: Después de cinco horas de negociación, se dio por concluido el acuerdo entre las partes.
examples.translation: After five hours of negotiation, the agreement between the parties was considered complete.

examples.sentence: Dieron por concluido el proyecto porque ya no había fondos para continuar.
examples.translation: They considered the project finished because there was no more funding to continue.

definitions: To treat a matter as terminated or no longer subject to further discussion or action.

examples.sentence: El director dio por concluido el debate y pidió pasar a otro tema.
examples.translation: The director treated the debate as over and asked to move on to another topic.

examples.sentence: No podemos dar por concluido el problema hasta hallar una solución definitiva.
examples.translation: We can’t consider the problem terminated until we find a definitive solution.

examples.sentence: Ella dio por concluida la discusión y salió de la sala molesta.
examples.translation: She treated the discussion as finished and left the room upset.

definitions: To force someone to engage in anal sex; used literally in a sexual and violent sense.

examples.sentence: La escena mostraba cómo el agresor le dio por el culo a la víctima, causando gran conmoción.
examples.translation: The scene showed how the aggressor forced the victim into anal sex, causing great shock.

examples.sentence: El acusado confesó que le había dado por el culo a la víctima durante el ataque.
examples.translation: The defendant confessed that he had forced the victim into anal sex during the attack.

examples.sentence: En el relato, se describe cómo el prisionero fue dado por el culo como parte de la tortura.
examples.translation: The account describes how the prisoner was anally raped as part of the torture.

examples.sentence: La policía encontró pruebas de que el agresor le dio por el culo a varias personas.
examples.translation: The police found evidence that the attacker anally assaulted several people.

definitions: To treat someone extremely badly, to abuse or violate someone physically or sexually.
