definitions: To hit one's head repeatedly, either against an object or in the act of headbutting another person (literal physical meaning).

examples.sentence: El toro comenzó a darse de cabezadas contra la puerta tratando de salir del corral.
examples.translation: The bull started headbutting the door trying to get out of the pen.

examples.sentence: Durante el partido, el jugador se dio de cabezadas con un rival en una jugada accidentada.
examples.translation: During the match, the player headbutted an opponent in an accidental play.

examples.sentence: El niño se dio de cabezadas contra la pared mientras jugaba en casa sin supervisión.
examples.translation: The child bumped his head repeatedly against the wall while playing at home unsupervised.

examples.sentence: Para defenderse, el animal se dio de cabezadas con el agresor hasta lograr alejarlo.
examples.translation: To defend itself, the animal headbutted the aggressor until managing to push him away.

definitions: To nod forward repeatedly because of drowsiness (to doze off while sitting), producing brief jerking head movements.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, me sentí tan cansado que me di de cabezadas varias veces sin darme cuenta.
examples.translation: During the meeting, I felt so tired that I nodded off repeatedly without realizing it.

examples.sentence: El profesor se dio de cabezadas porque la clase era muy aburrida y tenía sueño.
examples.translation: The teacher nodded forward repeatedly because the class was very boring and he was sleepy.

examples.sentence: Cuando el sueño me atacó, me di de cabezadas mientras escuchaba la conferencia.
examples.translation: When sleepiness hit me, I nodded repeatedly while listening to the lecture.

definitions: To persist in a futile or self-defeating action; to repeatedly clash with an obstacle or difficulty in a way that produces no productive outcome (figurative use).

examples.sentence: El equipo se dio de cabezadas intentando resolver el problema sin avanzar un solo paso.
examples.translation: The team persisted in a futile way trying to solve the problem without making any progress.

examples.sentence: Nos dimos de cabezadas con la burocracia durante meses sin lograr obtener los permisos necesarios.
examples.translation: We repeatedly clashed with bureaucracy for months without managing to get the necessary permits.

examples.sentence: Si sigues dándote de cabezadas contra ese obstáculo, solo perderás tiempo y energía.
examples.translation: If you keep banging your head against that obstacle, you'll only waste time and energy.

definitions: To receive repeated rejections, especially in a romantic or courtship context; to be turned down multiple times.

examples.sentence: Después de darse de calabazadas con varias chicas, finalmente decidió dejar de buscar pareja por un tiempo.
examples.translation: After being rejected by several girls, he finally decided to stop looking for a partner for a while.

examples.sentence: No quiero darme de calabazadas otra vez, así que prefiero conocer gente poco a poco antes de ilusionarme.
examples.translation: I don't want to be rejected again, so I prefer to get to know people slowly before getting my hopes up.

examples.sentence: Juan se dio de calabazadas muchas veces antes de encontrar a alguien que realmente le correspondiera.
examples.translation: Juan faced many rejections before finding someone who truly reciprocated his feelings.

definitions: To strike or knock one's head (or to hit someone on the head), either literally or figuratively; to suffer blows to the head.

examples.sentence: Mientras jugaba al fútbol, se dio de calabazadas contra la portería y tuvo que salir del partido por el dolor.
examples.translation: While playing soccer, he hit his head against the goal and had to leave the game due to the pain.

examples.sentence: El niño se dio de calabazadas contra la mesa varias veces mientras intentaba alcanzar el juguete.
examples.translation: The child bumped his head repeatedly against the table while trying to reach the toy.

examples.sentence: Los participantes se dieron de calabazadas durante la competencia de lucha libre sin quejarse.
examples.translation: The participants headbutted each other during the wrestling competition without complaining.

examples.sentence: Me di de calabazadas con la puerta al salir rápido y todavía siento el golpe en la frente.
examples.translation: I hit my head against the door when leaving quickly and I still feel the bump on my forehead.

definitions: To suffer a string of failures or refusals in attempts to obtain something.

examples.sentence: La empresa se dio de calabazadas tratando de entrar en un mercado saturado sin éxito.
examples.translation: The company suffered a string of failures trying to enter a saturated market without success.

examples.sentence: Me he dado de calabazadas con varios bancos porque ninguno aprueba mi préstamo.
examples.translation: I have faced repeated rejections from several banks because none approve my loan.

examples.sentence: No te des de calabazadas intentando convencer a alguien que no quiere cambiar de opinión.
examples.translation: Don't persist in futile attempts to convince someone who doesn't want to change their mind.

definitions: To come up against unexpectedly; to encounter or collide head-on with an obstacle, difficulty, refusal, or opposing attitude.

examples.sentence: Nos dimos de narices con el tráfico y llegamos tarde a la conferencia.
examples.translation: We unexpectedly encountered heavy traffic and arrived late to the conference.

examples.sentence: El equipo se dio de narices con un problema técnico que paralizó la producción durante horas.
examples.translation: The team came up against a technical problem that halted production for hours.

examples.sentence: Cuando intenté hablar con el jefe, me di de narices con su negativa rotunda a escuchar nuevas ideas.
examples.translation: When I tried to talk to the boss, I was abruptly confronted with his outright refusal to listen to new ideas.

definitions: To be abruptly confronted with an unpleasant reality or barrier.

examples.sentence: Nos dimos de narices con la realidad de que el presupuesto no alcanzaba para todo lo planeado.
examples.translation: We were abruptly confronted with the reality that the budget was not enough for all the plans.

examples.sentence: Te darás de narices con la verdad si investigas más a fondo sobre esa empresa.
examples.translation: You will be abruptly confronted with the truth if you investigate that company more deeply.

examples.sentence: Se dio de narices con la negativa de sus padres cuando les contó sus planes de mudarse al extranjero.
examples.translation: He was abruptly confronted with his parents' refusal when he told them about his plans to move abroad.

definitions: To escape or make a break away, especially from custody or confinement; to flee.

examples.sentence: El preso se dio el bote durante la noche y la policía aún lo busca.
examples.translation: The prisoner escaped during the night and the police are still searching for him.

examples.sentence: Si no quieres problemas, no te des el bote cuando te asignen tareas difíciles en el trabajo.
examples.translation: If you don't want trouble, don't run away when you're assigned difficult tasks at work.

examples.sentence: Durante la protesta, varios manifestantes se dieron el bote para evitar ser arrestados.
examples.translation: During the protest, several demonstrators fled to avoid being arrested.

definitions: To win a jackpot or take the pot in a game or pool; to claim a pooled prize.

examples.sentence: Anoche me di el bote en el póker y gané todo el dinero acumulado en la mesa.
examples.translation: Last night I took the pot in poker and won all the money accumulated on the table.

examples.sentence: El equipo se dio el bote al ganar el torneo después de una final muy reñida.
examples.translation: The team claimed the jackpot by winning the tournament after a very close final.

examples.sentence: Si apuestas bien, puedes darte el bote y llevarte un premio muy grande en el casino.
examples.translation: If you bet well, you can take the pot and win a very big prize at the casino.

definitions: To have sexual relations with someone; to get lucky or 'hook up' with another person.

examples.sentence: Después de tantas citas, finalmente Ana y Carlos se dieron el filete anoche.
examples.translation: After so many dates, Ana and Carlos finally got lucky last night.

examples.sentence: No creo que Marta se dé el filete con alguien nuevo tan rápido después de su ruptura.
examples.translation: I don't think Marta will hook up with someone new so soon after her breakup.

examples.sentence: ¿Te diste el filete en la fiesta o solo bailaste con ella?
examples.translation: Did you get lucky at the party or did you just dance with her?

definitions: To make out passionately with someone; to engage in prolonged intimate kissing or heavy petting, often in public.

examples.sentence: En el concierto, Marcos y Lucía se dieron el lote sin importar la gente alrededor.
examples.translation: At the concert, Marcos and Lucía made out passionately regardless of the people around.

examples.sentence: ¿Viste cómo se dieron el lote en el parque? No pudieron dejar de besarse.
examples.translation: Did you see how they made out in the park? They couldn’t stop kissing.

examples.sentence: Aunque no suelo hacerlo, me di el lote con Paula aquella noche en la fiesta de cumpleaños.
examples.translation: Although I usually don’t, I made out with Paula that night at the birthday party.

definitions: To flirt or behave amorously in a demonstrative way; to pair off in a romantic or sexual manner.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, Juan y Elena se dieron el lote coquetamente frente a todos sus amigos.
examples.translation: At the gathering, Juan and Elena flirted openly in front of all their friends.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando la gente se da el lote en público, prefiero algo más discreto.
examples.translation: I don’t like when people flirt openly in public; I prefer something more discreet.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué se están dando el lote tan descaradamente? Parecen una pareja recién enamorada.
examples.translation: Why are they flirting so blatantly? They look like a newly in love couple.

definitions: To engage in public displays of intense affection or necking.

examples.sentence: Los jóvenes se dieron el lote en la plaza, sin importar las miradas de los transeúntes.
examples.translation: The young couple engaged in public displays of affection in the square, without caring about passersby’s looks.

examples.sentence: Cuando se dieron el lote frente a la escuela, todos los estudiantes comenzaron a reírse.
examples.translation: When they necked in front of the school, all the students started laughing.

examples.sentence: No es habitual que se den el lote tan abiertamente en un lugar público, pero ellos lo hicieron.
examples.translation: It’s not usual for them to show such intense affection publicly, but they did.

definitions: To live in great luxury; to lead a very comfortable, opulent life.

examples.sentence: Desde que heredó la fortuna, Doña Isabel se da la gran vida disfrutando viajes y joyas.
examples.translation: Since she inherited the fortune, Doña Isabel lives the high life enjoying trips and jewels.

examples.sentence: El empresario se da la gran vida en su mansión con piscinas y coches de lujo.
examples.translation: The businessman lives in great luxury in his mansion with pools and luxury cars.

examples.sentence: Si pudieras verte, te darías la gran vida, viajando por todo el mundo sin preocupaciones.
examples.translation: If you could see yourself, you would live the high life, traveling around the world without worries.

definitions: To splurge or treat oneself to a short period of conspicuous luxury or showy enjoyment.

examples.sentence: Después de cobrar su bono, se dio la gran vida con una cena en un restaurante cinco estrellas.
examples.translation: After receiving his bonus, he splurged on a dinner at a five-star restaurant.

examples.sentence: Yo me daría la gran vida este fin de semana si ganara la lotería aunque sea por un día.
examples.translation: I would treat myself to a luxurious time this weekend if I won the lottery, even just for a day.

examples.sentence: No se dieron la gran vida durante las vacaciones, pero compraron algunos caprichos caros.
examples.translation: They didn’t splurge fully during the holidays, but they bought some expensive treats.

definitions: To indulge oneself in extravagant pleasures and high-end consumption.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que gana un premio, se da la gran vida comprando ropa de diseñador y saliendo a fiestas exclusivas.
examples.translation: Every time he wins an award, he indulges himself in designer clothes and exclusive parties.

examples.sentence: Aunque no suele hacerlo, esta vez se dio la gran vida con un spa y un masaje de lujo.
examples.translation: Although he usually doesn’t, this time he indulged himself with a spa and a luxury massage.

examples.sentence: Me doy la gran vida los fines de semana, disfrutando vinos caros y cenas elegantes con mis amigos.
examples.translation: I indulge myself on weekends, enjoying expensive wines and elegant dinners with my friends.

definitions: To show off or pretend to have greater importance, status, or ability than one actually has.

examples.sentence: Juan se da pisto en la oficina diciendo que es el responsable de todos los proyectos exitosos.
examples.translation: Juan shows off at the office by saying he’s responsible for all the successful projects.

examples.sentence: No te des pisto con ese coche viejo; sabemos que no es tuyo realmente.
examples.translation: Don’t show off with that old car; we know it’s not really yours.

examples.sentence: Aunque no sabe mucho, María se da pisto en las reuniones para parecer experta.
examples.translation: Although she doesn’t know much, María pretends to be important in meetings to seem like an expert.

definitions: To claim credit for something one did not do, or to give the impression of being responsible for a favourable outcome.

examples.sentence: Se dio pisto diciendo que había cerrado el trato, aunque en realidad fue su compañero quien lo hizo.
examples.translation: He took credit saying he closed the deal, although it was actually his partner who did it.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que te des pisto con cosas que no hiciste, eso es engañar a los demás.
examples.translation: I don’t like that you claim credit for things you didn’t do; that’s deceiving others.

examples.sentence: Ella se dio pisto de haber organizado el evento, pero todos saben que no fue así.
examples.translation: She claimed she organized the event, but everyone knows that wasn’t true.

definitions: To boast or post oneself ostentatiously in order to impress others.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, Pedro se dio pisto mostrando su nuevo reloj mientras todos lo miraban.
examples.translation: At the party, Pedro boasted ostentatiously by showing off his new watch while everyone watched.

examples.sentence: No tienes que darte pisto para impresionar a nadie, sé tú mismo y te valorarán más.
examples.translation: You don’t have to boast to impress anyone; be yourself and they will value you more.

examples.sentence: Ellos se dieron pisto con sus logros académicos para que los invitaran al evento formal.
examples.translation: They boasted about their academic achievements so they would be invited to the formal event.

definitions: To dress or adorn oneself in a showy or fashionable manner to project elegance.

examples.sentence: Para la boda, Claudia se dio postín con un vestido elegante y joyas brillantes.
examples.translation: For the wedding, Claudia dressed up in an elegant dress and sparkling jewelry.

examples.sentence: No suele darse postín, pero esta vez se arregló mucho para la cena con sus jefes.
examples.translation: She usually doesn’t dress up, but this time she dressed very nicely for the dinner with her bosses.

examples.sentence: Cuando se dio postín para la gala, todos comentaron lo bien que lucía.
examples.translation: When she dressed up for the gala, everyone commented on how good she looked.

definitions: To put on airs or affect a refined, fashionable appearance in order to impress others.

examples.sentence: Carlos se dio postín en la reunión, actuando como si fuera el director de la compañía.
examples.translation: Carlos put on airs at the meeting, acting as if he were the company director.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué te das postín con ese acento extranjero si no eres de allá?
examples.translation: Why do you put on airs with that foreign accent if you’re not from there?

examples.sentence: Ella se dio postín para impresionar a sus colegas, fingiendo ser más culta de lo que es.
examples.translation: She put on airs to impress her colleagues, pretending to be more cultured than she is.

definitions: To hurry; to act or move more quickly in order to finish or reach something sooner.

examples.sentence: Nos tenemos que dar prisa si queremos llegar a tiempo al cine antes de que empiece la película.
examples.translation: We have to hurry if we want to get to the cinema before the movie starts.

examples.sentence: El profesor dijo que nos diéramos prisa para entregar el proyecto antes del viernes.
examples.translation: The teacher said we should hurry to submit the project before Friday.

examples.sentence: ¿Te puedes dar prisa? El autobús no espera mucho y ya está por salir.
examples.translation: Can you hurry? The bus doesn’t wait long and it’s about to leave.

definitions: To make haste; to expedite one's actions or movements.

examples.sentence: Para evitar problemas, el equipo se dio prisa en solucionar el fallo técnico cuanto antes.
examples.translation: To avoid problems, the team made haste to fix the technical failure as soon as possible.

examples.sentence: Si te das prisa, tal vez alcances a coger el tren de las seis.
examples.translation: If you hurry, maybe you’ll catch the six o’clock train.

examples.sentence: Nos dimos prisa porque la tormenta se acercaba y no queríamos quedar atrapados en el campo.
examples.translation: We hurried because the storm was approaching and we didn’t want to get stuck in the countryside.

definitions: To give it (the feminine object) to someone; to hand over or deliver a feminine noun referent to another person.

examples.sentence: Le di la carta y se la dársela tan pronto como llegó a la oficina de correos.
examples.translation: I gave her the letter and she handed it over as soon as she arrived at the post office.

examples.sentence: Cuando María me pidió el libro, no dudé en dársela para que pudiera estudiar mejor.
examples.translation: When María asked me for the book, I didn’t hesitate to give it to her so she could study better.

examples.sentence: ¿Me puedes dársela a Laura? Ella está esperando esa carpeta en la recepción.
examples.translation: Can you give it to Laura? She’s waiting for that folder at reception.

examples.sentence: Nos encargaron dársela a la profesora antes de que empezara la clase.
examples.translation: We were tasked with giving it to the teacher before class started.

definitions: To grant or bestow something (such as an opportunity, role, or favour) upon someone.

examples.sentence: El jefe decidió dársela a Sofía para que lidere el nuevo proyecto de innovación.
examples.translation: The boss decided to grant Sofía the opportunity to lead the new innovation project.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que le dársela a Ana el puesto de gerente será una buena decisión para la empresa?
examples.translation: Do you think giving Ana the manager position will be a good decision for the company?

examples.sentence: Nos dieron la responsabilidad de dársela a la directora una vez que terminamos el informe.
examples.translation: We were given the responsibility to hand it to the director once we finished the report.

examples.sentence: Voy a dársela a Carla porque tiene más experiencia en este tipo de tareas.
examples.translation: I’m going to give it to Carla because she has more experience in this type of task.

definitions: To relinquish or cede something (typically a possession or right) to someone else.

examples.sentence: La familia decidió dársela a la vecina para que cuidara la mascota durante sus vacaciones.
examples.translation: The family decided to give it to the neighbor so she could take care of the pet during their vacation.

examples.sentence: No quisieron conservar la herencia y prefirieron dársela a la caridad.
examples.translation: They didn’t want to keep the inheritance and preferred to cede it to charity.

examples.sentence: El dueño tuvo que dársela al banco como garantía para obtener el préstamo.
examples.translation: The owner had to relinquish it to the bank as collateral to get the loan.

examples.sentence: Finalmente, el gobierno decidió dársela a la organización para que administre el fondo.
examples.translation: Finally, the government decided to cede it to the organization to manage the fund.

definitions: To assign possession, custody, or responsibility of a feminine object to another party.

examples.sentence: El maestro les pidió que dársela a la estudiante encargada de repartir los exámenes.
examples.translation: The teacher asked them to assign it to the student in charge of handing out the exams.

examples.sentence: Nos encargaron dársela a la coordinadora para que pudiera revisar el material antes de la conferencia.
examples.translation: We were assigned to give it to the coordinator so she could review the material before the conference.

examples.sentence: El hospital decidió dársela a la enfermera responsable de la sala para que cuide los medicamentos.
examples.translation: The hospital decided to assign it to the nurse responsible for the ward to take care of the medication.

examples.sentence: Por favor, dársela a la recepcionista para que la archive correctamente.
examples.translation: Please, give it to the receptionist so she can file it correctly.

definitions: To trick or deceive someone, especially by using an easy or clever ruse; to pull a fast one on someone.

examples.sentence: Juan me dársela con queso cuando me dijo que el examen se había cancelado; al final sí lo tuvimos.
examples.translation: Juan tricked me when he said the exam was canceled; in the end, we did have it.

examples.sentence: No te dejes dársela con queso por ese vendedor, siempre usa trucos para vender más caro.
examples.translation: Don’t let that salesman pull a fast one on you; he always uses tricks to sell at a higher price.

examples.sentence: Me dársela con queso haciéndome creer que la oferta era real, pero era solo una promoción falsa.
examples.translation: They tricked me into believing the offer was real, but it was just a fake promotion.

definitions: To manage to get away with something by means of cunning or flattery.

examples.sentence: Con un poco de halagos logró dársela con queso y evitar la multa que le correspondía.
examples.translation: With a bit of flattery, he managed to get away with the fine he was supposed to pay.

examples.sentence: No creas que puedes dársela con queso a tu jefe sin que se dé cuenta de tus errores.
examples.translation: Don’t think you can fool your boss with flattery without him noticing your mistakes.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre sabe cómo dársela con queso para salir bien parada en cualquier situación difícil.
examples.translation: She always knows how to get away with things by being cunning in any difficult situation.

definitions: To deceive or outwit others; to gain an advantage over someone through trickery or smooth talk.

examples.sentence: En la negociación, intentó dárselas con queso para obtener condiciones más favorables.
examples.translation: In the negotiation, he tried to outwit others to get better conditions.

examples.sentence: No te dejes dárselas con queso por ese político; sus promesas son solo palabras vacías.
examples.translation: Don’t let that politician fool you; his promises are just empty words.

examples.sentence: Pedro se las dio con queso para no pagar la deuda, usando excusas y engaños.
examples.translation: Pedro got away with not paying the debt by using excuses and tricks.

definitions: To evade responsibility or consequences by means of a sly or facile stratagem.

examples.sentence: Ella logró dárselas con queso para evitar la responsabilidad del accidente.
examples.translation: She managed to evade responsibility for the accident by clever means.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que podrá dárselas con queso y no cumplir con sus compromisos esta vez también?
examples.translation: Do you think he’ll be able to get away with not fulfilling his commitments this time as well?

examples.sentence: Los acusados intentaron dárselas con queso, pero la evidencia fue irrefutable.
examples.translation: The accused tried to evade consequences, but the evidence was irrefutable.

definitions: To pose as or pretend to be something one is not; to affect a particular quality or role (often with the implication of affectation or arrogance).

examples.sentence: No te das las de experto en cocina si no sabes ni freír un huevo.
examples.translation: Don’t pretend to be a cooking expert if you don’t even know how to fry an egg.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, Ana se dio las de sabia y corrigió al jefe frente a todos.
examples.translation: During the meeting, Ana acted like she was knowledgeable and corrected the boss in front of everyone.

examples.sentence: Se da las de importante solo porque tiene un cargo pequeño en la empresa.
examples.translation: He acts important just because he has a small position in the company.

definitions: To boast or put on airs about possessing a skill, status, or characteristic that one does not genuinely have.

examples.sentence: Luis se da las de gran orador, pero en realidad nadie entiende lo que dice.
examples.translation: Luis boasts about being a great speaker, but in reality no one understands what he says.

examples.sentence: No te des las de experto si apenas estás aprendiendo; es mejor ser humilde.
examples.translation: Don’t boast about being an expert if you’re just learning; it’s better to be humble.

examples.sentence: Ellos se dieron las de exitosos empresarios, aunque su negocio apenas comienza.
examples.translation: They boasted as successful entrepreneurs, even though their business is just starting.

definitions: Truly; genuinely; really—used to emphasize that something is real, sincere, or serious.

examples.sentence: Este amor es de a deveras, no como los juegos que hemos tenido antes.
examples.translation: This love is real, not like the games we had before.

examples.sentence: Si quieres que confíe en ti, tienes que quererme de a deveras y no solo decirlo.
examples.translation: If you want me to trust you, you have to love me genuinely and not just say it.

examples.sentence: Cuando habla de sus sueños, se nota que es de a deveras y no solo fantasía.
examples.translation: When he talks about his dreams, you can tell it’s sincere and not just fantasy.

definitions: In earnest; with genuine intent or effect (used to stress that a condition or quality is not merely nominal).

examples.sentence: Esta vez vamos de a deveras con el proyecto, no será un simple trámite más.
examples.translation: This time we’re serious with the project; it won’t be just another formality.

examples.sentence: Si quieres cambiar las cosas, tienes que actuar de a deveras y con compromiso real.
examples.translation: If you want to change things, you have to act in earnest and with real commitment.

examples.sentence: El equipo trabajó de a deveras para ganar el campeonato, sin distracciones ni excusas.
examples.translation: The team worked seriously to win the championship, without distractions or excuses.

definitions: On foot; walking rather than using a vehicle.

examples.sentence: Prefiero ir de a pie al trabajo para aprovechar y hacer algo de ejercicio cada día.
examples.translation: I prefer to go to work on foot to take advantage and get some exercise every day.

examples.sentence: Cuando era niño, siempre iba de a pie a la escuela porque vivía cerca.
examples.translation: When I was a child, I always went to school on foot because I lived nearby.

examples.sentence: Si llueve, no podré ir de a pie al supermercado y tendré que tomar un taxi.
examples.translation: If it rains, I won’t be able to walk to the supermarket and will have to take a taxi.

examples.sentence: Después de la cena, salimos de a pie para disfrutar el aire fresco de la noche.
examples.translation: After dinner, we went out on foot to enjoy the fresh night air.

definitions: Ordinary; commonplace; referring to ordinary people or the common person (as in 'ciudadano de a pie').

examples.sentence: El ciudadano de a pie suele enfrentar dificultades que los políticos no comprenden.
examples.translation: The ordinary citizen usually faces difficulties that politicians don’t understand.

examples.sentence: Las decisiones afectan a la gente de a pie más que a los grandes empresarios.
examples.translation: The decisions affect ordinary people more than big businessmen.

examples.sentence: Como ciudadano de a pie, me preocupa la falta de servicios básicos en mi barrio.
examples.translation: As an ordinary citizen, I’m concerned about the lack of basic services in my neighborhood.

definitions: Foot (as a military term): referring to infantry or soldiers who fight on foot (e.g., 'soldado de a pie').

examples.sentence: El soldado de a pie es la base fundamental del ejército en cualquier conflicto bélico.
examples.translation: The infantry soldier is the fundamental base of the army in any armed conflict.

examples.sentence: Durante la batalla, los soldados de a pie avanzaron bajo el fuego enemigo con valentía.
examples.translation: During the battle, the infantry soldiers advanced under enemy fire with bravery.

examples.sentence: El general ordenó a los soldados de a pie que fortificaran la posición antes del amanecer.
examples.translation: The general ordered the infantry soldiers to fortify the position before dawn.

definitions: Gradually; little by little; progressively over time in small increments.

examples.sentence: De a poco, Marta fue mejorando su técnica de pintura hasta alcanzar un nivel profesional.
examples.translation: Little by little, Marta improved her painting technique until she reached a professional level.

examples.sentence: El equipo de fútbol va de a poco ascendiendo en la tabla de posiciones tras cada partido ganado.
examples.translation: The soccer team is gradually climbing the standings after every match won.

examples.sentence: Aunque no lo notes, tu español mejora de a poco con cada conversación que tienes.
examples.translation: Even if you don’t notice it, your Spanish improves little by little with every conversation you have.

definitions: In small amounts; a little at a time; piecemeal (used for distributing, taking, or removing something bit by bit).

examples.sentence: María distribuyó los regalos de a poco para que todos recibieran algo.
examples.translation: María distributed the gifts bit by bit so that everyone got something.

examples.sentence: No tomes todo el dinero de a poco; mejor guarda un poco para más tarde.
examples.translation: Don't take all the money in small amounts; better save some for later.

examples.sentence: El profesor fue entregando las hojas de examen de a poco para evitar aglomeraciones.
examples.translation: The teacher handed out the exam sheets bit by bit to avoid crowds.

definitions: Slowly, by stages rather than all at once.

examples.sentence: Poco a poco, de a poco, la empresa fue recuperándose tras la crisis.
examples.translation: Little by little, bit by bit, the company was recovering after the crisis.

examples.sentence: No esperes resultados inmediatos; el éxito llega de a poco con esfuerzo constante.
examples.translation: Don't expect immediate results; success comes slowly with constant effort.

examples.sentence: De a poco iremos implementando los cambios para que nadie se sienta abrumado.
examples.translation: Little by little we will implement the changes so that no one feels overwhelmed.

definitions: Very gradually; in very small amounts; bit by bit with emphasis on the smallness of each increment.

examples.sentence: Después de la operación, Juan mejoró de a poquitos cada día.
examples.translation: After the surgery, Juan improved very gradually each day.

examples.sentence: De a poquitos, voy aprendiendo a tocar la guitarra sin frustrarme.
examples.translation: Bit by bit, I'm learning to play the guitar without getting frustrated.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes, la recuperación será de a poquitos, paso a paso.
examples.translation: Don't worry, the recovery will be very gradual, step by step.

definitions: Doing or consuming something only in tiny portions or small, repeated doses.

examples.sentence: Mi abuela toma su medicina de a poquitos para no sentir malestar.
examples.translation: My grandmother takes her medicine in tiny doses to avoid feeling unwell.

examples.sentence: Durante la dieta, comía chocolate de a poquitos para no romperla completamente.
examples.translation: During the diet, she ate chocolate in very small amounts to not break it completely.

examples.sentence: Los niños disfrutan el helado de a poquitos para que dure más tiempo.
examples.translation: The children enjoy the ice cream in tiny portions so it lasts longer.

definitions: At a stretch; for a continuous period of time (e.g., days at a time).

examples.sentence: Estuve estudiando de a tiro toda la noche para el examen final.
examples.translation: I was studying at a stretch all night for the final exam.

examples.sentence: Los trabajadores hicieron la jornada de a tiro para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.
examples.translation: The workers did the shift continuously to finish the project on time.

examples.sentence: ¿Podrás leer ese libro de a tiro o prefieres hacerlo en varias sesiones?
examples.translation: Can you read that book in one go or do you prefer to do it in several sessions?

definitions: Per stint or occurrence; occurring in consecutive runs rather than intermittently.

examples.sentence: Los partidos se juegan de a tiro, sin descansos largos entre ellos.
examples.translation: The matches are played per stint, without long breaks between them.

examples.sentence: La fábrica opera de a tiro, con turnos seguidos sin interrupciones.
examples.translation: The factory operates per occurrence, with consecutive shifts without interruptions.

examples.sentence: Los ensayos serán de a tiro para aprovechar mejor el tiempo.
examples.translation: The rehearsals will be done in consecutive runs to make better use of the time.

definitions: From here to there; back and forth; indicating movement or distribution between places.

examples.sentence: Vi a los niños corriendo de acá para acullá en el parque sin parar.
examples.translation: I saw the children running from here to there in the park nonstop.

examples.sentence: Los mensajes iban de acá para acullá entre los equipos durante la emergencia.
examples.translation: Messages went back and forth between the teams during the emergency.

examples.sentence: El correo se mueve de acá para acullá hasta llegar a su destino final.
examples.translation: The mail moves from here to there until it reaches its final destination.

definitions: Here and there; about; moving to different places (often with a slightly old-fashioned or literary tone).

examples.sentence: Las ideas flotaban de acá para acullá en la reunión, sin un rumbo fijo.
examples.translation: Ideas floated here and there in the meeting, without a fixed direction.

examples.sentence: En la novela, los personajes se mueven de acá para acullá por distintos países.
examples.translation: In the novel, the characters move about to different places across countries.

examples.sentence: Los turistas paseaban de acá para acullá admirando las vistas del pueblo.
examples.translation: The tourists wandered here and there admiring the views of the town.

definitions: From here to there; back and forth; moving repeatedly between two or more places.

examples.sentence: Luis va de acá para allá entre el trabajo y la universidad todos los días.
examples.translation: Luis goes back and forth between work and university every day.

examples.sentence: Los niños corren de acá para allá jugando sin parar en el jardín.
examples.translation: The children run from here to there playing nonstop in the garden.

examples.sentence: Durante la feria, los vendedores se movían de acá para allá ofreciendo sus productos.
examples.translation: During the fair, the vendors moved back and forth offering their products.

definitions: All over the place; going around from one place to another (can be literal movement or figurative busyness).

examples.sentence: He estado de acá para allá todo el día resolviendo trámites burocráticos.
examples.translation: I have been going all over the place all day handling bureaucratic paperwork.

examples.sentence: Ella anda de acá para allá con mil cosas en la cabeza, sin descanso.
examples.translation: She goes around all over the place with a thousand things on her mind, without rest.

examples.sentence: Los técnicos se movieron de acá para allá intentando arreglar la falla en tiempo récord.
examples.translation: The technicians went all over the place trying to fix the fault in record time.

definitions: An imperative interjection telling someone to hold on physically, usually because of imminent movement or danger.

examples.sentence: ¡De agárrate bien que el bus va a tomar la curva rápido!
examples.translation: Hold on tight because the bus is going to take the curve fast!

examples.sentence: Cuando el barco empezó a balancearse, el capitán gritó: «¡De agárrate!»
examples.translation: When the boat started rocking, the captain shouted: 'Hold on!'

examples.sentence: Por favor, de agárrate fuerte antes de que arranque el ascensor.
examples.translation: Please, hold on tight before the elevator starts.

examples.sentence: De agárrate que esta montaña rusa tiene muchas bajadas inesperadas.
examples.translation: Hold on because this roller coaster has many unexpected drops.

definitions: A warning used figuratively to tell someone to prepare for a sudden or intense event or revelation.

examples.sentence: De agárrate porque la noticia que voy a darte te va a sorprender mucho.
examples.translation: Brace yourself because the news I'm about to give you will surprise you a lot.

examples.sentence: Amigo, de agárrate, la reunión de mañana será intensa y llena de sorpresas.
examples.translation: Friend, brace yourself; tomorrow's meeting will be intense and full of surprises.

examples.sentence: Si quieres escuchar el final de la historia, de agárrate que viene lo mejor.
examples.translation: If you want to hear the end of the story, brace yourself because the best part is coming.

definitions: A literal warning to hold on because there is a curve ahead, typically used in vehicular contexts.

examples.sentence: De agárrate que hay curva a la derecha, el conductor avisó a los pasajeros.
examples.translation: Hold on, there's a curve to the right, the driver warned the passengers.

examples.sentence: Antes de entrar a la carretera montañosa, el guía dijo: «De agárrate que hay curva».
examples.translation: Before entering the mountain road, the guide said: 'Hold on because there is a curve.'

examples.sentence: De agárrate que hay curva, la señal estaba justo antes del tramo peligroso.
examples.translation: Hold on because there is a curve, the sign was right before the dangerous stretch.

examples.sentence: El ciclista gritó: «¡De agárrate que hay curva!» para alertar a sus compañeros.
examples.translation: The cyclist shouted: 'Hold on because there is a curve!' to alert his companions.

definitions: A figurative admonition meaning 'brace yourself' or 'get ready for a surprise or difficulty that is coming.'

examples.sentence: De agárrate que hay curva en el proyecto, los próximos meses serán complicados.
examples.translation: Brace yourself because there’s a twist in the project; the next months will be complicated.

examples.sentence: Cuando me habló de los cambios, pensé: de agárrate que hay curva en esta historia.
examples.translation: When he told me about the changes, I thought: brace yourself there’s a twist in this story.

examples.sentence: La conferencia empezó tranquila, pero de agárrate que hay curva cuando llegó el invitado sorpresa.
examples.translation: The conference started calmly, but brace yourself because there’s a twist when the surprise guest arrived.

definitions: A warning to hold on because there are curves ahead; used literally when anticipating a winding road or sudden motion.

examples.sentence: De agárrate que hay curvas en esta carretera, conduce con cuidado.
examples.translation: Hold on because there are curves on this road, drive carefully.

examples.sentence: Antes de salir, el guía dijo: «De agárrate que hay curvas durante todo el trayecto».
examples.translation: Before leaving, the guide said: 'Hold on because there are curves throughout the whole trip.'

examples.sentence: De agárrate que hay curvas, avisó el conductor mientras tomaba la ruta montañosa.
examples.translation: Hold on because there are curves, the driver warned while taking the mountain route.

examples.sentence: El autobús frenó bruscamente y alguien gritó: «¡De agárrate que hay curvas!»
examples.translation: The bus braked suddenly and someone shouted: 'Hold on because there are curves!'

definitions: A figurative expression meaning 'brace yourself' for multiple upcoming difficulties, surprises, or complications.

examples.sentence: De agárrate que hay curvas en el negocio, porque vienen varios problemas seguidos.
examples.translation: Brace yourself because there are multiple twists in the business; several problems are coming in a row.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuché el plan, pensé: de agárrate que hay curvas, esto no será fácil.
examples.translation: When I heard the plan, I thought: brace yourself there are twists, this won't be easy.

examples.sentence: La película tiene una trama complicada, de agárrate que hay curvas hasta el final.
examples.translation: The movie has a complicated plot; brace yourself because there are twists until the end.

definitions: An emphatic warning meaning 'hold on and do not move,' used literally to tell someone to stay still during sudden motion.
idiom: de agárrate y no te menees

examples.sentence: De agárrate y no te menees cuando el tren arranque para no caerte.
examples.translation: Hold on and don't move when the train starts so you don't fall.
examples.matched_span: De agárrate y no te menees

examples.sentence: Durante la turbulencia en el avión, el piloto pidió: «De agárrate y no te menees».
examples.translation: During the turbulence on the plane, the pilot requested: 'Hold on and don't move.'
examples.matched_span: De agárrate y no te menees

examples.sentence: El bote comenzó a balancearse y el capitán gritó: «¡De agárrate y no te menees!»
examples.translation: The boat started to rock and the captain shouted: 'Hold on and don't move!'
examples.matched_span: De agárrate y no te menees

examples.sentence: Para evitar accidentes, el instructor dijo: «De agárrate y no te menees durante el simulacro».
examples.translation: To avoid accidents, the instructor said: 'Hold on and don't move during the drill.'
examples.matched_span: De agárrate y no te menees

definitions: A figurative admonition meaning 'brace yourself and remain calm or passive' in anticipation of a strong reaction, surprise, or chaotic situation.
idiom: de agárrate y no te menees

examples.sentence: De agárrate y no te menees, que lo que viene será difícil de manejar emocionalmente.
examples.translation: Brace yourself and stay calm; what’s coming will be hard to handle emotionally.
examples.matched_span: De agárrate y no te menees

examples.sentence: Antes de la reunión con el jefe, me dije: de agárrate y no te menees para no perder la calma.
examples.translation: Before the meeting with the boss, I told myself: brace yourself and don’t move so you don’t lose your calm.
examples.matched_span: de agárrate y no te menees

examples.sentence: El ambiente en la casa estaba tenso, así que me aconsejaron: de agárrate y no te menees.
examples.translation: The atmosphere at home was tense, so they advised me: brace yourself and don’t move.
examples.matched_span: de agárrate y no te menees

definitions: By some means; by some method or process, without specifying how.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, logramos terminar el proyecto a tiempo, aunque con dificultades.
examples.translation: By some means, we managed to finish the project on time, despite difficulties.

examples.sentence: No sé cómo, pero de alguna manera la reunión se resolvió sin conflictos.
examples.translation: I don't know how, but somehow the meeting was resolved without conflicts.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, ella consiguió el apoyo necesario para su campaña política.
examples.translation: By some means, she got the necessary support for her political campaign.

definitions: In a certain way; to some extent; used to qualify a statement by indicating approximation or partial truth.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, este lugar me recuerda a mi infancia, aunque no sé por qué.
examples.translation: In a certain way, this place reminds me of my childhood, although I don’t know why.

examples.sentence: El resultado fue, de alguna manera, satisfactorio para todos los involucrados.
examples.translation: The outcome was, to some extent, satisfactory for everyone involved.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, él siempre encuentra la forma de salir adelante en los momentos difíciles.
examples.translation: In a certain way, he always finds a way to get ahead in difficult times.

definitions: Somehow; used to indicate that something will happen or be achieved despite uncertainty about the means.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, vamos a conseguir los recursos para completar el proyecto.
examples.translation: Somehow, we are going to get the resources to complete the project.

examples.sentence: Aunque no tengo un plan claro, de alguna manera resolveré esta situación.
examples.translation: Although I don’t have a clear plan, somehow I will solve this situation.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, ella logró convencer al jurado a pesar de las dudas iniciales.
examples.translation: Somehow, she managed to convince the jury despite the initial doubts.

definitions: As a discourse hedge used to soften a claim or express reservation about the precision of a description.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, este informe refleja las preocupaciones del equipo, aunque no todas.
examples.translation: Somewhat, this report reflects the team's concerns, although not all.

examples.sentence: El autor describe la situación de alguna manera, pero sin entrar en detalles específicos.
examples.translation: The author describes the situation in a certain way, but without going into specific details.

examples.sentence: De alguna manera, podríamos decir que el proyecto fue un éxito, aunque con reservas.
examples.translation: In a way, we could say that the project was a success, albeit with reservations.

definitions: Belonging to or associated with the social elite; of high social status.

examples.sentence: Ella proviene de una familia de alto standing y siempre ha tenido acceso a lo mejor.
examples.translation: She comes from a high social standing family and has always had access to the best.

examples.sentence: En esa zona viven personas de alto standing que disfrutan de privilegios exclusivos.
examples.translation: In that area, people of high social status live and enjoy exclusive privileges.

examples.sentence: Su educación de alto standing le abrió puertas en el mundo empresarial.
examples.translation: His high-status education opened doors for him in the business world.

definitions: Used to describe a person, establishment, or service that is exclusive or associated with wealth and prestige.

examples.sentence: El restaurante es de alto standing, con chefs reconocidos internacionalmente.
examples.translation: The restaurant is upscale, with internationally recognized chefs.

examples.sentence: Contrataron un servicio de catering de alto standing para la boda de lujo.
examples.translation: They hired a high-end catering service for the luxury wedding.

examples.sentence: El hotel ofrece alojamiento de alto standing para clientes exigentes.
examples.translation: The hotel offers high-status accommodations for demanding clients.

definitions: Of superior quality or luxury; high-end, upscale.

examples.sentence: Compré un reloj de alto standing que combina diseño y tecnología avanzada.
examples.translation: I bought a luxury watch that combines design and advanced technology.

examples.sentence: La marca es conocida por sus productos de alto standing y calidad excepcional.
examples.translation: The brand is known for its high-end products and exceptional quality.

examples.sentence: Su coche nuevo es de alto standing, con acabados de lujo y motor potente.
examples.translation: His new car is upscale, with luxury finishes and a powerful engine.

definitions: Used to indicate that goods, accommodations, or professional services are of premium standard.

examples.sentence: Contrataron un abogado de alto standing para manejar el caso más delicado.
examples.translation: They hired a top-notch lawyer to handle the most delicate case.

examples.sentence: El spa ofrece tratamientos de alto standing para clientes que buscan exclusividad.
examples.translation: The spa offers premium treatments for clients seeking exclusivity.

examples.sentence: Los apartamentos cuentan con servicios de alto standing, como gimnasio y piscina privada.
examples.translation: The apartments feature premium services such as a gym and private pool.

definitions: Ambitious, high-level, or of great scope and sophistication.

examples.sentence: Pedro tiene proyectos de altos vuelos que podrían cambiar la industria tecnológica.
examples.translation: Pedro has ambitious projects that could change the tech industry.

examples.sentence: La universidad lanzó un programa de altos vuelos para formar líderes internacionales.
examples.translation: The university launched a high-level program to train international leaders.

examples.sentence: El discurso del presidente fue de altos vuelos, lleno de ideas innovadoras y complejas.
examples.translation: The president's speech was ambitious, full of innovative and complex ideas.

definitions: Applied to projects, institutions, conversations, or people to indicate notable excellence, prestige, or complexity.

examples.sentence: Esa empresa es de altos vuelos, con proyectos que superan las expectativas del mercado.
examples.translation: That company is prestigious, with projects that exceed market expectations.

examples.sentence: Tuve una conversación de altos vuelos con expertos en inteligencia artificial.
examples.translation: I had a high-level conversation with experts in artificial intelligence.

examples.sentence: El instituto de investigación desarrolla estudios de altos vuelos en biotecnología.
examples.translation: The research institute develops prestigious studies in biotechnology.

definitions: Pretentious, grandiose, or excessive in manner or expression.

examples.sentence: Sus ideas son de altos vuelos, pero a veces parecen desconectadas de la realidad.
examples.translation: His ideas are grandiose, but sometimes they seem disconnected from reality.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, su discurso fue de altos vuelos, con un tono pretencioso y exagerado.
examples.translation: During the meeting, his speech was pompous, with a pretentious and exaggerated tone.

examples.sentence: No me gustan las presentaciones de altos vuelos que no aportan soluciones prácticas.
examples.translation: I don’t like grandiose presentations that don’t provide practical solutions.

definitions: Used to criticize talk, ideas, or behavior as overly lofty or pompous without substance.

examples.sentence: Ese político habla de altos vuelos, pero sus propuestas carecen de sustancia real.
examples.translation: That politician talks pompously, but his proposals lack real substance.

examples.sentence: Las ideas de altos vuelos de la propuesta son bonitas, pero poco aplicables en la práctica.
examples.translation: The lofty ideas of the proposal are nice, but hardly applicable in practice.

examples.sentence: Criticaron su comportamiento de altos vuelos porque parecía querer impresionar sin ser sincero.
examples.translation: They criticized his pompous behavior because he seemed to want to impress without being sincere.

definitions: Belonging to an earlier time; former or previous.

examples.sentence: Esa costumbre es de antes, cuando mis abuelos todavía vivían en el campo.
examples.translation: That custom is from before, when my grandparents still lived in the countryside.

examples.sentence: Recuerdo los libros de antes que tenían un olor muy particular y diferente al de ahora.
examples.translation: I remember the books from before that had a very particular smell different from today's.

examples.sentence: Los estilos de moda de antes vuelven cada cierto tiempo, aunque con cambios modernos.
examples.translation: Fashion styles from before come back every so often, although with modern changes.

definitions: Used to refer to a person, thing, state, or situation that existed at an earlier moment.

examples.sentence: Mi amigo Juan era un poco más tímido de antes y ahora habla con mucha confianza.
examples.translation: My friend Juan was a bit more shy before, and now he speaks with a lot of confidence.

examples.sentence: ¿Te acuerdas de la casa de antes? Estaba justo al lado del parque, pero ya no existe.
examples.translation: Do you remember the house from before? It was right next to the park, but it no longer exists.

examples.sentence: La situación política de antes era muy diferente a la que vivimos hoy día.
examples.translation: The political situation from before was very different from what we live today.

definitions: As before; in the way or condition that existed previously.

examples.sentence: Sigo trabajando en el proyecto de antes porque aún no está terminado.
examples.translation: I keep working on the project as before because it is not finished yet.

examples.sentence: La tienda abrió de antes a después sin cambiar sus horarios habituales.
examples.translation: The store opened as before without changing its usual hours.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que prepare la cena de antes o prefieres probar algo nuevo esta vez?
examples.translation: Do you want me to prepare dinner as before or would you prefer to try something new this time?

examples.sentence: Aunque hubo algunos cambios, el sistema funciona de antes sin mayores problemas.
examples.translation: Although there were some changes, the system works as before without major problems.

definitions: Used to express a return to or comparison with a previous state or habit.

examples.sentence: Después de las vacaciones, Juan volvió a su rutina de antes sin falta.
examples.translation: After the holidays, Juan returned to his usual routine as before without fail.

examples.sentence: No quiero que las cosas cambien, prefiero que todo siga de antes.
examples.translation: I don't want things to change; I prefer that everything stays as before.

examples.sentence: Aunque intentó mejorar, al final volvió a sus malos hábitos de antes.
examples.translation: Although he tried to improve, in the end he reverted to his bad habits from before.

definitions: Remarkable or outstanding; worthy of being preserved as a classic.

examples.sentence: El discurso de Clara fue de antología; todos quedaron impresionados con su elocuencia.
examples.translation: Clara's speech was outstanding; everyone was impressed by her eloquence.

examples.sentence: Esa jugada en el partido fue de antología y seguro la recordaremos por mucho tiempo.
examples.translation: That play in the match was remarkable and we will surely remember it for a long time.

examples.sentence: La actuación de la banda anoche fue de antología, simplemente perfecta en cada canción.
examples.translation: The band's performance last night was outstanding, simply perfect in every song.

definitions: Applied to performances, works, actions, or traits that are exceptionally memorable for their quality or impact.

examples.sentence: El concierto de anoche fue de antología; pocas veces se ve tanta energía y talento juntos.
examples.translation: Last night's concert was exceptional; you rarely see so much energy and talent together.

examples.sentence: Su respuesta en la reunión fue de antología, dejó sin palabras a todos los presentes.
examples.translation: His response in the meeting was unforgettable, it left everyone speechless.

examples.sentence: El cuadro expuesto en el museo es de antología; una obra maestra que merece admiración.
examples.translation: The painting displayed in the museum is outstanding; a masterpiece worthy of admiration.

definitions: Notoriously extreme or outrageous in a way that makes it memorable.

examples.sentence: La fiesta de anoche fue de antología, con situaciones tan locas que nadie podrá olvidar.
examples.translation: Last night's party was outrageously memorable, with such crazy situations that no one will forget.

examples.sentence: Su berrinche fue de antología, la gente no sabía si reír o preocuparse.
examples.translation: Her tantrum was notoriously extreme, people didn't know whether to laugh or worry.

examples.sentence: Esa película tiene escenas de antología por lo impactantes y exageradas que son.
examples.translation: That movie has notoriously outrageous scenes because of how impactful and exaggerated they are.

definitions: Used ironically to describe blunders, excuses, or behaviors that are remarkably bad, absurd, or excessive.

examples.sentence: Su excusa para no venir fue de antología; nadie pudo creerla ni por un segundo.
examples.translation: His excuse for not coming was ridiculously bad; no one could believe it for a second.

examples.sentence: La manera en que trató al cliente fue de antología, una falta de respeto total.
examples.translation: The way he treated the customer was absurdly bad, a total lack of respect.

examples.sentence: Esa metedura de pata fue de antología, todo el mundo se dio cuenta y se rió sin parar.
examples.translation: That blunder was remarkably bad; everyone noticed and laughed nonstop.

definitions: Current problems are the direct consequences of past actions or decisions.

examples.sentence: No me sorprende que haya problemas financieros ahora; de aquellos polvos, estos lodos.
examples.translation: I'm not surprised there are financial problems now; from those past troubles come these consequences.

examples.sentence: Cuando alguien actúa sin pensar, debe aceptar las consecuencias; de aquellos polvos, estos lodos.
examples.translation: When someone acts without thinking, they must accept the consequences; you reap what you sow.

examples.sentence: El mal estado de la carretera es culpa de años de abandono; de aquellos polvos, estos lodos.
examples.translation: The bad state of the road is due to years of neglect; this is the result of what happened before.

examples.sentence: Los conflictos actuales en el país vienen de decisiones equivocadas del pasado; de aquellos polvos, estos lodos.
examples.translation: The current conflicts in the country come from wrong decisions made in the past; you reap what you sow.

definitions: Equivalent to 'you reap what you sow' or 'this is the result of what happened before.'

examples.sentence: No puedes quejarte del trabajo si no pusiste esfuerzo; de aquellos polvos, estos lodos.
examples.translation: You can't complain about the job if you didn't put in effort; you reap what you sow.

examples.sentence: Si no cuidas tu salud, tarde o temprano lo pagarás; de aquellos polvos, estos lodos.
examples.translation: If you don't take care of your health, sooner or later you will pay for it; this is the result of what happened before.

examples.sentence: La mala reputación de la empresa es producto de la negligencia pasada; de aquellos polvos, estos lodos.
examples.translation: The company's bad reputation is the result of past negligence; you reap what you sow.

definitions: A hyperbolic intensifier used to indicate a very large amount, great extent, or extensive knowledge; equivalent to 'a whole lot' or 'far and wide'.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta había gente de aquí a Lima; no cabía ni un alma más.
examples.translation: At the party there were people from here to Lima; there wasn't room for another soul.

examples.sentence: Mi abuela sabe de aquí a Lima sobre remedios caseros para cualquier dolencia.
examples.translation: My grandmother knows a whole lot about home remedies for any ailment.

examples.sentence: Tengo tareas de aquí a Lima para entregar antes de fin de semana, no sé cómo las voy a terminar.
examples.translation: I have a whole lot of homework to turn in before the weekend; I don't know how I'll finish it.

definitions: From this moment forward; henceforth; indicates that from the stated point in time a rule, condition, or situation will apply.

examples.sentence: De aquí en adelante, todas las reuniones serán virtuales para mayor comodidad.
examples.translation: From now on, all meetings will be virtual for greater convenience.

examples.sentence: A partir de hoy, de aquí en adelante, debemos respetar las nuevas normas de seguridad.
examples.translation: Starting today, from now on, we must respect the new safety rules.

examples.sentence: El entrenador anunció que de aquí en adelante, los entrenamientos serán más intensos.
examples.translation: The coach announced that from now on, the training sessions will be more intense.

definitions: From this point onward in space or sequence; literally 'from here onward' when describing physical direction or continuation.

examples.sentence: De aquí en adelante, sigue el camino recto hasta llegar al puente.
examples.translation: From here onward, follow the straight path until you reach the bridge.

examples.sentence: Se puede ver el crecimiento del edificio de aquí en adelante, desde la colina se aprecia bien.
examples.translation: You can see the building's growth from here onward; it is well visible from the hill.

examples.sentence: De aquí en adelante, la carretera desciende suavemente hasta el valle.
examples.translation: From here onward, the road gently descends to the valley.

examples.sentence: Colocaron la señalización de aquí en adelante para indicar el área en construcción.
examples.translation: They placed the signage from here onward to indicate the construction area.

definitions: Colloquial intensifier placed after a noun to indicate a high degree, seriousness, severity, or notable quality; equivalent to 'really', 'terribly', or 'a real/serious (one)'.

examples.sentence: Esa película es un aburrimiento de aquí te espero; no la recomiendo para nada.
examples.translation: That movie is terribly boring; I don't recommend it at all.

examples.sentence: El examen de matemáticas fue un reto de aquí te espero, nadie pudo terminarlo completo.
examples.translation: The math exam was really tough; no one could finish it completely.

examples.sentence: Tiene una alergia de aquí te espero que le impide salir en primavera.
examples.translation: He has a really severe allergy that prevents him from going out in spring.

definitions: Descriptive phrase for a person who is formidable, strong-willed, combative, or not to be trifled with; 'a force to be reckoned with' or 'difficult to handle'.

examples.sentence: María es una mujer de armas tomar, siempre defiende sus ideas con firmeza.
examples.translation: Maria is a formidable woman; she always defends her ideas firmly.

examples.sentence: No te metas con Pedro, es de armas tomar y no se deja intimidar fácilmente.
examples.translation: Don't mess with Pedro; he's a force to be reckoned with and doesn't get intimidated easily.

examples.sentence: Para negociar con ese jefe, necesitas ser de armas tomar y no ceder ante presiones.
examples.translation: To negotiate with that boss, you need to be strong-willed and not give in to pressure.

definitions: Thoroughly; from top to bottom; used to indicate a complete search, inspection, or review of a place or thing.

examples.sentence: Buscamos el documento de arriba abajo y no lo encontramos en ninguna parte.
examples.translation: We searched the document from top to bottom and couldn't find it anywhere.

examples.sentence: La policía revisó la casa de arriba abajo buscando pistas sobre el robo.
examples.translation: The police thoroughly searched the house looking for clues about the robbery.

examples.sentence: Antes de entregar el informe, lo revisé de arriba abajo para evitar errores.
examples.translation: Before submitting the report, I checked it thoroughly to avoid mistakes.

definitions: With visual scrutiny from head to toe; to look someone up and down.

examples.sentence: Cuando entró, me miró de arriba abajo como si fuera un extraño en su casa.
examples.translation: When he entered, he looked me up and down as if I were a stranger in his house.

examples.sentence: El jefe la miró de arriba abajo antes de aprobar su propuesta.
examples.translation: The boss gave her a thorough look from head to toe before approving her proposal.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando la gente me mira de arriba abajo sin decir nada.
examples.translation: I don't like it when people look me up and down without saying anything.

definitions: Literally from top to bottom in a vertical sense; indicating movement or orientation along a vertical axis.

examples.sentence: El agua cayó de arriba abajo durante toda la tormenta sin cesar.
examples.translation: The water fell from top to bottom during the whole storm without stopping.

examples.sentence: El ascensor se movió de arriba abajo varias veces antes de detenerse en el piso correcto.
examples.translation: The elevator moved up and down several times before stopping on the correct floor.

examples.sentence: Colgaron la bandera de arriba abajo por error y nadie se dio cuenta hasta el día siguiente.
examples.translation: They hung the flag upside down by mistake and no one noticed until the next day.

examples.sentence: La cortina se deslizó de arriba abajo suavemente al abrir la ventana.
examples.translation: The curtain slid from top to bottom smoothly when opening the window.

definitions: Belonging to or owned by the author; relating to an author's legal rights or copyrights (e.g., "author's" as in copyright).

examples.sentence: El contrato de autor garantiza que el creador reciba derechos por su obra.
examples.translation: The author's contract ensures that the creator receives rights for their work.

examples.sentence: La ley protege las obras de autor para evitar que se reproduzcan sin permiso.
examples.translation: The law protects author's works to prevent them from being reproduced without permission.

examples.sentence: El sello de autor aparece en las primeras páginas del libro para identificar al escritor.
examples.translation: The author's mark appears on the first pages of the book to identify the writer.

examples.sentence: Se aplicaron las normas de derecho de autor para registrar la nueva canción.
examples.translation: The copyright rules were applied to register the new song.

definitions: Characteristic of a particular author's creative voice or style; authorial in quality.

examples.sentence: Esa novela tiene un estilo muy de autor, con una voz narrativa única.
examples.translation: That novel has a very authorial style, with a unique narrative voice.

examples.sentence: El cineasta es reconocido por sus películas de autor que exploran temas profundos.
examples.translation: The filmmaker is recognized for his auteur films that explore deep themes.

examples.sentence: Los cuadros de esta exposición reflejan el sello de autor del pintor contemporáneo.
examples.translation: The paintings in this exhibition reflect the artistic signature of the contemporary painter.

definitions: Used sarcastically to indicate someone who affects the airs or pretensions of an author or creator ("acting like an author").

examples.sentence: Juan siempre se cree muy de autor cuando escribe poemas en su blog, pero nadie los lee.
examples.translation: Juan always acts like such an author when he writes poems on his blog, but no one reads them.

examples.sentence: Ella se muestra de autor en las reuniones, como si sus ideas fueran las únicas válidas.
examples.translation: She acts authorial in meetings, as if her ideas were the only valid ones.

examples.sentence: No seas tan de autor, baja un poco los humos y escucha lo que dicen los demás.
examples.translation: Don't be so pretentious; tone it down and listen to what others say.

definitions: Produced or conceived by a named creator, often implying originality, artistic intent, or a signature/atelier quality (used in arts, cuisine, wine, etc.).

examples.sentence: Este vino es de autor, elaborado por un reconocido enólogo con técnicas innovadoras.
examples.translation: This wine is an auteur product, made by a renowned winemaker with innovative techniques.

examples.sentence: La carta del restaurante ofrece platos de autor que combinan sabores tradicionales y modernos.
examples.translation: The restaurant menu offers signature dishes that combine traditional and modern flavors.

examples.sentence: El vestido que lleva es una pieza de autor, confeccionada a mano por un diseñador famoso.
examples.translation: The dress she is wearing is a signature piece, handmade by a famous designer.

definitions: Morally base, contemptible, or despicable; of low character.

examples.sentence: No quiero tratar con gente de baja estofa que solo busca aprovecharse de los demás.
examples.translation: I don't want to deal with contemptible people who only seek to take advantage of others.

examples.sentence: Esos actos de corrupción son propios de personas de baja estofa sin valores.
examples.translation: Those acts of corruption belong to despicable people without values.

examples.sentence: La novela describe personajes de baja estofa involucrados en crímenes y engaños.
examples.translation: The novel describes low-character characters involved in crimes and deceit.

definitions: Belonging to a low, disreputable social class; coarse or seedy in manners or background.

examples.sentence: El barrio está lleno de gente de baja estofa que ha caído en malas compañías.
examples.translation: The neighborhood is full of low-class people who have fallen into bad company.

examples.sentence: Su comportamiento de baja estofa sorprendió a todos en la reunión social.
examples.translation: His coarse behavior surprised everyone at the social gathering.

examples.sentence: Esa pandilla está formada por jóvenes de baja estofa que no respetan las normas.
examples.translation: That gang is made up of seedy youths who don't respect the rules.

definitions: Free of charge; without payment; gratis.

examples.sentence: Nos regalaron las entradas para el concierto de balde, fue una sorpresa increíble.
examples.translation: They gave us free tickets to the concert; it was an incredible surprise.

examples.sentence: En la feria, muchas muestras se entregaban de balde para promocionar los productos.
examples.translation: At the fair, many samples were given free of charge to promote the products.

examples.sentence: No pagues por ese curso, ahora lo ofrecen de balde durante una semana de prueba.
examples.translation: Don't pay for that course; now they offer it free of charge during a trial week.

definitions: In vain; to no avail; without achieving the desired result.

examples.sentence: Intenté convencerlo de que cambiara de opinión, pero fue todo de balde.
examples.translation: I tried to convince him to change his mind, but it was all in vain.

examples.sentence: Los esfuerzos del equipo fueron de balde porque el proyecto fue cancelado.
examples.translation: The team's efforts were to no avail because the project was canceled.

examples.sentence: Llamaron al médico temprano, pero su visita fue de balde; el paciente ya había mejorado.
examples.translation: They called the doctor early, but his visit was in vain; the patient had already improved.

definitions: Denoting the flag under which a ship sails; indicating the vessel's nationality or registry.

examples.sentence: El barco navega bajo bandera española y cumple con todas las regulaciones nacionales.
examples.translation: The ship sails under the Spanish flag and complies with all national regulations.

examples.sentence: Para registrar la embarcación, es necesario especificar la bandera de la que depende.
examples.translation: To register the vessel, it is necessary to specify the flag under which it sails.

examples.sentence: La compañía decidió cambiar la bandera del buque para facilitar trámites internacionales.
examples.translation: The company decided to change the ship's flag to facilitate international procedures.

examples.sentence: El capitán informó que el barco lleva bandera de Malta desde el año pasado.
examples.translation: The captain reported that the ship has been flying the Maltese flag since last year.

definitions: Exceptional, outstanding, or first-rate (used to praise a person or thing).

examples.sentence: Su actuación en el torneo fue de bandera, ganando todos los partidos sin perder un set.
examples.translation: His performance in the tournament was outstanding, winning all matches without losing a set.

examples.sentence: El servicio del restaurante fue de bandera, atento y rápido en todo momento.
examples.translation: The restaurant service was exceptional, attentive and fast at all times.

examples.sentence: La película es de bandera, con efectos especiales impresionantes y una historia emocionante.
examples.translation: The movie is first-rate, with impressive special effects and an exciting story.

definitions: Relating to flag rank or the status of a flag officer in naval or military contexts.

examples.sentence: El almirante alcanzó el rango de oficial de bandera tras una carrera ejemplar.
examples.translation: The admiral reached flag officer rank after an exemplary career.

examples.sentence: Los oficiales de bandera tienen responsabilidades especiales en la flota naval.
examples.translation: Flag officers have special responsibilities in the naval fleet.

examples.sentence: El desfile militar contó con la presencia de varios oficiales de bandera destacados.
examples.translation: The military parade included several distinguished flag officers.

examples.sentence: Para acceder al puesto de oficial de bandera se requiere amplia experiencia y méritos.
examples.translation: To access the position of flag officer, extensive experience and merits are required.

definitions: Having a mustache; characterized by the presence of facial hair on the upper lip.

examples.sentence: El hombre de bigotes que viste de traje es el director de la empresa.
examples.translation: The man with a mustache wearing a suit is the company director.

examples.sentence: Desde joven, Carlos siempre fue de bigotes y orgulloso de su estilo clásico.
examples.translation: Since he was young, Carlos always had a mustache and was proud of his classic style.

examples.sentence: En la foto familiar, mi abuelo aparece de bigotes y con su sombrero favorito.
examples.translation: In the family photo, my grandfather appears with a mustache and his favorite hat.

examples.sentence: Para la obra de teatro, el actor se dejó crecer bigotes para parecer más viejo.
examples.translation: For the play, the actor grew a mustache to look older.

definitions: Informal label used to identify or refer to a person by their mustache ("the mustached one").

examples.sentence: El tipo de bigotes que lleva Jorge siempre llama la atención en las reuniones familiares.
examples.translation: The kind of mustache Jorge sports always draws attention at family gatherings.

examples.sentence: ¿Has visto al de bigotes que trabaja en la cafetería? Siempre es muy amable con los clientes.
examples.translation: Have you seen the mustached guy who works at the café? He's always very friendly with customers.

examples.sentence: María siempre sabía que era el de bigotes porque nadie más tenía ese estilo tan peculiar en el barrio.
examples.translation: María always knew it was the mustached one because no one else had that peculiar style in the neighborhood.

examples.sentence: Los niños del vecindario llamaban 'el de bigotes' al hombre que repartía periódicos todos los días temprano.
examples.translation: The neighborhood kids called the man who delivered newspapers every morning 'the mustached one.'

definitions: An old colloquial dismissive expression used to label something or someone as ridiculous, worthless, or contemptible.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuché esa idea para arreglar el problema, pensé que era pura cosa de bóbilis.
examples.translation: When I heard that idea to fix the problem, I thought it was pure nonsense.

examples.sentence: No le prestes atención, todo lo que dice es de bóbilis y no tiene sentido alguno.
examples.translation: Don't pay attention to him, everything he says is rubbish and makes no sense.

examples.sentence: Esa película fue un desastre total, un guion de bóbilis que nadie entendía.
examples.translation: That movie was a total disaster, a ridiculous script that nobody understood.

definitions: An emphatic reduplicative particle formerly used to intensify a statement, roughly equivalent to 'utterly' or 'completely'.

examples.sentence: Te lo digo de bóbilis, esta vez el proyecto va a funcionar sin problemas.
examples.translation: I'm telling you utterly, this time the project will work without problems.

examples.sentence: De bóbilis no habrá otra oportunidad como esta para viajar al extranjero.
examples.translation: Completely, there won't be another opportunity like this to travel abroad.

examples.sentence: Me cansé de explicarlo de bóbilis, pero nadie me escuchó.
examples.translation: I got tired of explaining it utterly, but no one listened to me.

definitions: A jocular or derogatory tag appended to a statement to express scorn or derision.

examples.sentence: Claro que no me interesa ese asunto, es de bóbilis, no merece mi atención.
examples.translation: Of course I’m not interested in that matter, it’s rubbish, it doesn’t deserve my attention.

examples.sentence: ¿Vas a seguir con esas excusas de bóbilis? Ya sabemos que no son verdad.
examples.translation: Are you going to keep with those ridiculous excuses? We already know they aren’t true.

examples.sentence: Su opinión sobre el tema es de bóbilis, ni siquiera sabe de qué habla.
examples.translation: His opinion about the subject is nonsense, he doesn’t even know what he’s talking about.

definitions: Acting in the capacity of a firefighter; occupying the role or post of a firefighter.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano trabaja de bombero desde hace diez años y ha salvado muchas vidas.
examples.translation: My brother has worked as a firefighter for ten years and has saved many lives.
