examples.sentence: Se gastó las fuerzas tratando de convencer a alguien que no quería cambiar de opinión.
examples.translation: He exhausted himself trying to convince someone who didn’t want to change their mind.

definitions: To trick, deceive, or get the better of someone; to play a prank on or take advantage of another person.

examples.sentence: No te dejes gastárselas por esos vendedores que solo quieren estafarte.
examples.translation: Don’t let those salespeople trick you; they only want to scam you.

examples.sentence: Cuando éramos niños, mis primos siempre me gastaban las, pero yo aprendí a defenderme.
examples.translation: When we were kids, my cousins always played tricks on me, but I learned to defend myself.

examples.sentence: Se las gastó muy bien en la negociación y logró un mejor contrato para su empresa.
examples.translation: He outsmarted them in the negotiation and got a better contract for his company.

definitions: To manage one's affairs independently; to fend for oneself without outside help.

examples.sentence: Después de mudarse a otra ciudad, tuvo que gobernárselas solo sin ayuda de nadie.
examples.translation: After moving to another city, he had to manage on his own without anyone’s help.

examples.sentence: No esperes que te solucionen todo, aprende a gobernárselas en las dificultades.
examples.translation: Don’t expect everything to be solved for you; learn to fend for yourself in difficulties.

examples.sentence: Ella se gobernó sola durante años y ahora es una persona muy independiente.
examples.translation: She managed on her own for years and now she is a very independent person.

definitions: To handle a difficult situation resourcefully or cleverly; to cope effectively with challenges.

examples.sentence: Cuando la crisis llegó, supo gobernárselas y sacar adelante la empresa con ingenio.
examples.translation: When the crisis came, she knew how to handle it and move the business forward cleverly.

examples.sentence: No siempre es fácil gobernárselas en situaciones complicadas, pero él lo logró con éxito.
examples.translation: It’s not always easy to cope effectively in complicated situations, but he succeeded.

examples.sentence: Si quieres tener éxito, tienes que gobernárselas y no depender de nadie más.
examples.translation: If you want to succeed, you have to manage things yourself and not depend on anyone else.

definitions: A sudden turn of the helm; an abrupt change of course by a ship or boat (literal nautical maneuver).

examples.sentence: El capitán dio un golpe de timón para evitar chocar contra las rocas cercanas.
examples.translation: The captain made a sudden turn of the helm to avoid crashing into nearby rocks.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, el golpe de timón fue tan brusco que muchos pasajeros se asustaron.
examples.translation: During the storm, the sudden turn of the helm was so abrupt that many passengers got scared.

examples.sentence: El timonel tuvo que hacer varios golpes de timón para mantener el barco en curso.
examples.translation: The helmsman had to make several sudden turns of the helm to keep the ship on course.

examples.sentence: Cuando el viento cambió, el piloto realizó un golpe de timón para aprovecharlo mejor.
examples.translation: When the wind changed, the pilot made a sudden turn of the helm to take better advantage of it.

definitions: A decisive or abrupt change of direction, policy, or strategy; a prompt reversal or corrective action intended to alter the course of events (figurative).

examples.sentence: El nuevo director dio un golpe de timón en la estrategia para mejorar las ventas rápidamente.
examples.translation: The new director made a decisive change in strategy to improve sales quickly.

examples.sentence: Después de varios meses de pérdidas, la empresa necesitaba un golpe de timón urgente.
examples.translation: After several months of losses, the company needed an urgent course correction.

examples.sentence: ¿No crees que es hora de un golpe de timón en la política ambiental del país?
examples.translation: Don’t you think it’s time for a decisive change in the country’s environmental policy?

definitions: Gradually; little by little; in slow, successive increments (literally 'drop by drop').

examples.sentence: El ahorro se hizo gota a gota porque no teníamos mucho dinero para gastar.
examples.translation: The savings were made little by little because we didn’t have much money to spend.

examples.sentence: Paciencia, los resultados llegan gota a gota cuando se trabaja con constancia.
examples.translation: Be patient, results come gradually when you work consistently.

examples.sentence: El progreso en la rehabilitación fue gota a gota, pero finalmente pudo caminar de nuevo.
examples.translation: The progress in rehabilitation was little by little, but eventually she could walk again.

definitions: By small partial payments or contributions; in installments or in very small amounts over time.

examples.sentence: Pagué la deuda gota a gota porque no tenía el dinero completo para saldarla de una vez.
examples.translation: I paid the debt in installments because I didn’t have the full money to settle it all at once.

examples.sentence: Se financió el proyecto gota a gota con pequeñas donaciones de la comunidad.
examples.translation: The project was funded gradually with small donations from the community.

examples.sentence: El préstamo se devuelve gota a gota para que sea más accesible para todos.
examples.translation: The loan is repaid little by little to make it more accessible to everyone.

definitions: An intravenous drip or infusion device that administers fluid drop by drop; a drip.

examples.sentence: El paciente recibió líquidos por vía intravenosa gota a gota durante toda la noche.
examples.translation: The patient received fluids intravenously drop by drop throughout the night.

examples.sentence: El médico ajustó la velocidad del gota a gota para que la medicación fuera efectiva.
examples.translation: The doctor adjusted the intravenous drip rate to make the medication effective.

examples.sentence: Colocaron un gota a gota para hidratar al enfermo que no podía beber agua.
examples.translation: They placed an IV drip to hydrate the patient who couldn’t drink water.

examples.sentence: El enfermero revisó el gota a gota y cambió el frasco cuando se terminó el líquido.
examples.translation: The nurse checked the IV drip and changed the bottle when the fluid ran out.

definitions: To enjoy something intensely; to take pleasure in an experience, possession, or life itself; to live it up.

examples.sentence: Después de tanto trabajo, nos merecemos gozarla este fin de semana en la playa.
examples.translation: After so much work, we deserve to really enjoy ourselves this weekend at the beach.

examples.sentence: Cuando viajo, me gusta gozarla al máximo probando la comida local y conociendo gente nueva.
examples.translation: When I travel, I like to enjoy it to the fullest by trying local food and meeting new people.

examples.sentence: Si alguna vez tienes la oportunidad de vivir en el campo, gozarla no te costará trabajo.
examples.translation: If you ever have the chance to live in the countryside, you will enjoy it effortlessly.

definitions: To engage in or derive sexual gratification from sexual activity (colloquial and vulgar usage).

examples.sentence: Dicen que en la fiesta, los jóvenes realmente la gozaron y no pararon hasta la madrugada.
examples.translation: They say at the party the young people really enjoyed themselves and didn’t stop until dawn.

examples.sentence: No es común hablar de eso abiertamente, pero algunos aseguran que la gozaron mucho esa noche.
examples.translation: It’s not common to talk about that openly, but some claim they had a lot of fun that night.

examples.sentence: Se nota que la pareja la goza cuando están juntos, siempre se ven felices y cariñosos.
examples.translation: It shows that the couple enjoys their intimacy when they are together; they always look happy and affectionate.

definitions: To imprint or fix something firmly and permanently in the memory or consciousness; to etch into the mind (figurative).

examples.sentence: La imagen del accidente se me grabó a fuego y no puedo olvidarla.
examples.translation: The image of the accident is etched in my mind and I can't forget it.

examples.sentence: Desde niño, mi abuela me grabó a fuego la importancia de la honestidad.
examples.translation: Since I was a child, my grandmother ingrained the importance of honesty deeply in me.

examples.sentence: No se me grabará a fuego esa lección si no la practico constantemente.
examples.translation: That lesson won't be firmly fixed in my memory if I don't practice it constantly.

definitions: To burn or brand a mark into a material or surface using heat; to engrave by burning (literal).

examples.sentence: El artesano grabó a fuego su firma en la madera antes de entregarla.
examples.translation: The craftsman burned his signature into the wood before delivering it.

examples.sentence: ¿Podrías grabar a fuego este símbolo en la piel del cuero para que no se desgaste?
examples.translation: Could you burn this symbol into the leather so it doesn’t wear off?

examples.sentence: Los vaqueros grababan a fuego las marcas para identificar al ganado.
examples.translation: The cowboys branded the cattle to identify them.

examples.sentence: La placa fue grabada a fuego para asegurar su durabilidad en exteriores.
examples.translation: The plaque was engraved by burning to ensure its durability outdoors.

definitions: The cinema or the motion-picture medium presented on large screens; 'the big screen' as a reference to theatrical films and the film industry.

examples.sentence: Mi sueño siempre ha sido ver una de mis historias en la gran pantalla.
examples.translation: My dream has always been to see one of my stories on the big screen.

examples.sentence: Este director ha trabajado duro para llegar a la gran pantalla y ahora es famoso.
examples.translation: This director has worked hard to reach the big screen and is now famous.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que las series de televisión podrán reemplazar a la gran pantalla algún día?
examples.translation: Do you think TV series will be able to replace the big screen someday?

definitions: A large physical screen or display used for projecting images or video, such as a cinema screen or a large television/projector screen (literal).

examples.sentence: Colocaron una gran pantalla en el auditorio para proyectar la conferencia.
examples.translation: They installed a large screen in the auditorium to project the conference.

examples.sentence: Durante la fiesta, la gran pantalla mostró fotos de cuando éramos niños.
examples.translation: During the party, the big screen showed photos of when we were kids.

examples.sentence: El cine cuenta con una gran pantalla que mide más de veinte metros de ancho.
examples.translation: The cinema has a large screen that measures more than twenty meters wide.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes ajustar el brillo de la gran pantalla? Está demasiado intenso para mis ojos.
examples.translation: Can you adjust the brightness of the big screen? It’s too intense for my eyes.

definitions: A single small particle of sand; a tiny granular fragment.

examples.sentence: Un solo grano de arena puede ser arrastrado por el viento fácilmente.
examples.translation: A single grain of sand can be easily carried away by the wind.

examples.sentence: Observamos cómo cada grano de arena brillaba bajo el sol del atardecer.
examples.translation: We watched how each grain of sand sparkled under the sunset sun.

examples.sentence: El grano de arena quedó atrapado entre las páginas del libro viejo.
examples.translation: The grain of sand got trapped between the pages of the old book.

examples.sentence: En la playa, cada grano de arena tiene una forma y tamaño únicos.
examples.translation: On the beach, each grain of sand has a unique shape and size.

definitions: A small contribution or effort toward a larger goal; one person's modest share in a collective endeavor (as in poner su grano de arena).

examples.sentence: Aunque sea un pequeño grano de arena, mi ayuda puede marcar la diferencia en este proyecto.
examples.translation: Even if it’s a small contribution, my help can make a difference in this project.

examples.sentence: Cada voluntario puso su grano de arena para que la campaña fuera un éxito.
examples.translation: Each volunteer put in their small effort so the campaign would be a success.

examples.sentence: No subestimes tu grano de arena, porque muchos granos juntos forman una playa.
examples.translation: Don’t underestimate your small contribution, because many grains together make a beach.

definitions: A trivial or insignificant matter; something of negligible importance (often used in expressions meaning to exaggerate a minor issue, e.g., making a mountain out of a grain of sand).

examples.sentence: No hagas una montaña de un grano de arena; el problema no es tan grave.
examples.translation: Don’t make a mountain out of a grain of sand; the problem isn’t that serious.

examples.sentence: Clara suele exagerar cualquier detalle, como si un grano de arena fuera una tormenta.
examples.translation: Clara tends to exaggerate any detail, as if a grain of sand were a storm.

examples.sentence: Deja de preocuparte por ese grano de arena y concéntrate en lo importante.
examples.translation: Stop worrying about that trivial matter and focus on what’s important.

definitions: An individual unit marking the passage of time in an hourglass; a metaphor for fleeting moments or the final seconds of a period.

examples.sentence: Mientras el grano de arena caía en el reloj de arena, sabía que el tiempo se acababa.
examples.translation: As the grain of sand fell in the hourglass, I knew the time was running out.

examples.sentence: Cada grano de arena representa segundos que no volverán jamás.
examples.translation: Each grain of sand represents seconds that will never return.

examples.sentence: Contábamos los granos de arena para medir cuánto faltaba para el final del juego.
examples.translation: We counted the grains of sand to measure how much time was left until the end of the game.

examples.sentence: El grano de arena que escapó marcó el comienzo de un nuevo ciclo en su vida.
examples.translation: The grain of sand that slipped marked the beginning of a new cycle in his life.

definitions: A person or thing that is a persistent nuisance or irritation; a 'pain in the ass.'

examples.sentence: Desde que llegó ese nuevo compañero, se ha convertido en un verdadero grano en el culo para todo el equipo.
examples.translation: Since that new colleague arrived, he has become a real pain in the ass for the whole team.

examples.sentence: No soporto a Marta, es un grano en el culo con sus constantes quejas.
examples.translation: I can’t stand Marta, she’s a pain in the ass with her constant complaints.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué siempre tienes que ser un grano en el culo cuando tratamos de organizarnos?
examples.translation: Why do you always have to be a pain in the ass when we try to get organized?

definitions: A vexing problem or obstacle that complicates matters and is hard to get rid of.

examples.sentence: El retraso en los pagos fue un grano en el culo para la empresa durante todo el trimestre.
examples.translation: The delay in payments was a thorn in the side for the company throughout the quarter.

examples.sentence: Ese problema legal se convirtió en un grano en el culo que complicó la venta del inmueble.
examples.translation: That legal problem became a nuisance that complicated the sale of the property.

examples.sentence: Aunque intentaron ignorarlo, la filtración de información siguió siendo un grano en el culo para el gobierno.
examples.translation: Although they tried to ignore it, the information leak remained a persistent problem for the government.

definitions: Literally, a pimple or blemish on the buttock.

examples.sentence: Después del verano, le salió un grano en el culo que le dolía cada vez que se sentaba.
examples.translation: After summer, he got a pimple on his butt that hurt every time he sat down.

examples.sentence: No pude ir a la playa porque tenía un grano en el culo que me molestaba mucho.
examples.translation: I couldn’t go to the beach because I had a pimple on my butt that was very annoying.

examples.sentence: ¿Te has fijado en ese grano en el culo de Juan? Parece que le está dando problemas.
examples.translation: Have you noticed that pimple on Juan’s butt? It seems to be causing him problems.

examples.sentence: Se aplicó crema para el grano en el culo y pronto desapareció la inflamación.
examples.translation: He applied cream for the pimple on his butt and the swelling soon went away.

definitions: Done with delicacy, restraint, or ceremonial care; handled gently or with special courtesy (equivalent to 'with kid gloves').

examples.sentence: El jefe manejó la situación con guante blanco, evitando conflictos innecesarios.
examples.translation: The boss handled the situation with kid gloves, avoiding unnecessary conflicts.

examples.sentence: Siempre trato a mis clientes con guante blanco para mantener una buena relación profesional.
examples.translation: I always treat my clients delicately to maintain a good professional relationship.

examples.sentence: No había necesidad de ser tan duro; podrías haber actuado con guante blanco y todo habría salido mejor.
examples.translation: There was no need to be so harsh; you could have acted with care and everything would have gone better.

definitions: Relating to nonviolent, professional, or financial wrongdoing; 'white-collar' in the sense of crimes committed through fraud, deception, or abuse of position (as in ladrón de guante blanco).

examples.sentence: Se descubrió que era un ladrón de guante blanco que estafaba a sus clientes con contratos fraudulentos.
examples.translation: It was discovered he was a white-collar thief who defrauded his clients with fraudulent contracts.

examples.sentence: Los crímenes de guante blanco suelen ser más difíciles de detectar porque no implican violencia física.
examples.translation: White-collar crimes are usually harder to detect because they don’t involve physical violence.

examples.sentence: No creas que porque es un delito de guante blanco es menos grave; el daño económico puede ser enorme.
examples.translation: Don’t think that because it’s a white-collar crime it’s less serious; the economic damage can be huge.

definitions: A symbol of refinement, cleanliness, or high social standing; associated with elegance, ceremonial attire, or meticulous care.

examples.sentence: En la ceremonia, todos los mayordomos llevaban guante blanco como señal de elegancia y respeto.
examples.translation: At the ceremony, all the butlers wore white gloves as a sign of elegance and respect.

examples.sentence: Su impecable guante blanco demostraba la meticulosidad con la que cuidaba cada detalle del evento.
examples.translation: His spotless white glove showed the meticulous care he took with every detail of the event.

examples.sentence: Cuando entró al salón, la mujer lucía un guante blanco que combinaba con su vestido de gala.
examples.translation: When she entered the hall, the woman wore a white glove that matched her evening gown.

examples.sentence: El mayordomo fue reconocido por su guante blanco, símbolo de su alta posición social y limpieza.
examples.translation: The butler was recognized by his white glove, a symbol of his high social standing and cleanliness.

definitions: To keep or hold a parcel, package, or bulky object; literal sense.

examples.sentence: Por favor, guarda el bulto en la bodega mientras organizamos la mudanza.
examples.translation: Please keep the package in the storage room while we organize the move.

examples.sentence: ¿Quién se encargará de guardar el bulto con los documentos importantes durante la reunión?
examples.translation: Who will hold the parcel with the important documents during the meeting?

examples.sentence: Guardamos el bulto en el rincón para que no estorbara mientras pintábamos la casa.
examples.translation: We kept the bulky package in the corner so it wouldn’t get in the way while we painted the house.

examples.sentence: El encargado guardó el bulto con mucho cuidado para evitar que se dañara.
examples.translation: The person in charge carefully kept the package to prevent it from being damaged.

definitions: To accept blame or responsibility on behalf of others; to cover for someone or act as a scapegoat.

examples.sentence: Cuando su amigo fue acusado, él decidió guardar el bulto y asumir la culpa para protegerlo.
examples.translation: When his friend was accused, he chose to take the blame to protect him.

examples.sentence: No puedes guardar el bulto siempre; llega un momento en que debes decir la verdad.
examples.translation: You can’t always take the blame; there comes a time when you have to tell the truth.

examples.sentence: Ella guardó el bulto para que nadie sospechara que ella había cometido el error.
examples.translation: She took the blame so that no one would suspect she had made the mistake.

definitions: To keep a low profile or refrain from attracting attention, especially to avoid trouble or responsibility.

examples.sentence: Para evitar problemas, decidió guardar el bulto y no involucrarse en la discusión.
examples.translation: To avoid trouble, he decided to keep a low profile and not get involved in the argument.

examples.sentence: Durante la crisis, varios empleados prefirieron guardar el bulto y no expresar sus opiniones.
examples.translation: During the crisis, several employees preferred to keep a low profile and not express their opinions.

examples.sentence: Si quieres pasar desapercibido, lo mejor es guardar el bulto y no llamar la atención.
examples.translation: If you want to go unnoticed, the best thing is to keep a low profile and not attract attention.

definitions: To stay at home to look after and protect the house; to house-sit or act as caretaker in someone's absence.

examples.sentence: Mientras los dueños viajaban, su vecino se encargó de guardar la casa y alimentar a los gatos.
examples.translation: While the owners traveled, their neighbor took care of house-sitting and feeding the cats.

examples.sentence: Nos pidieron guardar la casa durante el fin de semana para evitar robos.
examples.translation: They asked us to look after the house during the weekend to prevent burglaries.

examples.sentence: Guardar la casa no es solo cerrar las puertas; también implica mantenerla en buen estado.
examples.translation: House-sitting is not just locking the doors; it also means keeping it in good condition.

examples.sentence: El joven aceptó guardar la casa mientras sus padres estaban de viaje de negocios.
examples.translation: The young man agreed to house-sit while his parents were on a business trip.

definitions: To remain at home while others go out; to keep the household running or maintain the home during an absence.

examples.sentence: Ella decidió guardar la casa mientras sus amigos salían a la fiesta de cumpleaños.
examples.translation: She decided to stay home while her friends went to the birthday party.

examples.sentence: Cuando el resto de la familia se fue de vacaciones, papá se quedó guardando la casa.
examples.translation: When the rest of the family went on vacation, dad stayed home to keep the house running.

examples.sentence: Guardar la casa ese día fue importante para evitar que entraran ladrones durante la tormenta.
examples.translation: Staying home that day was important to prevent burglars from entering during the storm.

definitions: To maintain an outward appearance of normality, respectability, or decorum in order to avoid embarrassment, scandal, or social disapproval.

examples.sentence: A pesar de los rumores, Marta siempre supo guardar las apariencias para que nadie sospechara.
examples.translation: Despite the rumors, Marta always maintained appearances so no one would suspect.

examples.sentence: En la reunión familiar, Juan se esforzó por guardar las apariencias aunque estaba muy triste.
examples.translation: At the family gathering, Juan tried hard to keep up appearances even though he was very sad.

examples.sentence: Guardar las apariencias es común en ciertos círculos sociales para evitar escándalos.
examples.translation: Maintaining appearances is common in certain social circles to avoid scandals.

definitions: To carry on with superficial or formal behaviors mainly for the sake of public perception rather than from genuine conviction.

examples.sentence: Solo estaba guardando las apariencias cuando fingió que todo estaba bien con su jefe.
examples.translation: He was just putting on a front when he pretended everything was fine with his boss.

examples.sentence: Muchas veces las parejas guardan las apariencias para que nadie note sus problemas reales.
examples.translation: Many times couples maintain appearances so that no one notices their real problems.

examples.sentence: Guardar las apariencias puede ser agotador cuando no refleja lo que realmente sientes.
examples.translation: Keeping up appearances can be exhausting when it doesn’t reflect what you really feel.

definitions: To maintain physical space between oneself and others; to keep physically apart.

examples.sentence: Durante la pandemia, todos debíamos guardar las distancias en los espacios públicos.
examples.translation: During the pandemic, we all had to keep physical distance in public spaces.

examples.sentence: Por favor, guarda las distancias cuando estés en la fila para evitar contagios.
examples.translation: Please keep your distance when you’re in line to avoid contagion.

examples.sentence: El entrenador insistió en que los jugadores guardaran las distancias durante el calentamiento.
examples.translation: The coach insisted that the players keep their distances during warm-up.

examples.sentence: No siempre es fácil guardar las distancias cuando hay tanta gente en un evento pequeño.
examples.translation: It’s not always easy to keep distances when there are so many people at a small event.

definitions: To keep emotional or social distance; to avoid closeness, involvement, or familiarity with someone or something.

examples.sentence: Desde que discutieron, Ana ha estado guardando las distancias con Carlos para evitar conflictos.
examples.translation: Since they argued, Ana has been keeping her distance from Carlos to avoid conflicts.

examples.sentence: Prefiero guardar las distancias con ese grupo porque no comparto sus valores.
examples.translation: I prefer to keep my distance from that group because I don’t share their values.

examples.sentence: A veces es necesario guardar las distancias emocionales para proteger tu bienestar.
examples.translation: Sometimes it’s necessary to keep emotional distance to protect your well-being.

definitions: To keep something for oneself; to reserve or retain an item, opportunity, or advantage rather than share it.

examples.sentence: Guardé el último trozo de pizza para mí; no quería compartirlo con nadie más.
examples.translation: I kept the last slice of pizza for myself; I didn’t want to share it with anyone else.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué te guardas la información si podríamos beneficiarnos todos?
examples.translation: Why do you keep the information to yourself when we could all benefit?

examples.sentence: Si guardas la oportunidad para más tarde, podrías perderla sin darte cuenta.
examples.translation: If you keep the opportunity for later, you might lose it without realizing.

definitions: To withhold information or to keep a matter secret instead of revealing it to others.

examples.sentence: No te guardes la verdad; es mejor que todos sepamos lo que realmente pasó.
examples.translation: Don’t withhold the truth; it’s better if we all know what really happened.

examples.sentence: Ella se guardó la noticia del ascenso para sorprendernos en la reunión.
examples.translation: She kept the promotion news to herself to surprise us at the meeting.

examples.sentence: A veces es difícil no guardarse ciertos secretos que podrían hacer daño.
examples.translation: Sometimes it’s hard not to keep certain secrets that could hurt.

definitions: To pocket or hide an object on one's person for private use.

examples.sentence: El ladrón guardó la joya en el bolsillo, sin que nadie se diera cuenta.
examples.translation: The thief pocketed the jewel without anyone noticing.

examples.sentence: Guardaba el reloj antiguo en la caja para protegerlo del polvo y la humedad.
examples.translation: He kept the old watch in the box to protect it from dust and moisture.

examples.sentence: Durante el concierto, me guardé el programa para recordarlo después.
examples.translation: During the concert, I kept the program for later remembrance.

examples.sentence: Ella se guardó la carta en el bolso y no la mostró a nadie más.
examples.translation: She hid the letter in her purse and didn’t show it to anyone else.

definitions: To keep feelings, complaints, or emotions to oneself; to suppress emotional expression rather than share it.

examples.sentence: Aunque estaba molesto, decidió guardársela para no empeorar la situación.
examples.translation: Although he was upset, he chose to keep it to himself to avoid making things worse.

examples.sentence: No te guardes la tristeza; hablar con alguien puede ayudarte a sentirte mejor.
examples.translation: Don’t keep your sadness to yourself; talking to someone can help you feel better.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre se guarda las quejas y prefiere no mostrar sus verdaderos sentimientos.
examples.translation: She always keeps her complaints to herself and prefers not to show her true feelings.

definitions: An emphatic, playful way to say that something is very cool, excellent, or fashionable (a rhyming intensifier built on guay).

examples.sentence: Ese coche deportivo es guay de Paraguay, todos quieren uno igual.
examples.translation: That sports car is really cool, everyone wants one just like it.

examples.sentence: La fiesta de anoche estuvo guay de Paraguay, con buena música y ambiente increíble.
examples.translation: Last night’s party was totally awesome, with great music and an incredible atmosphere.

examples.sentence: No sabía que tus dibujos fueran tan guay de Paraguay, deberías mostrárselos a más gente.
examples.translation: I didn’t know your drawings were so cool; you should show them to more people.

definitions: An emphatic colloquial expression meaning 'really cool' or 'awesome'; used to intensify the adjective guay by rhyme and humor.

examples.sentence: Esa chaqueta que llevas es guay del Paraguay, me encanta tu estilo.
examples.translation: That jacket you’re wearing is really cool, I love your style.

examples.sentence: ¡Qué guay del Paraguay está este concierto! Nunca había visto tanta energía en el público.
examples.translation: This concert is really awesome! I’ve never seen so much energy in the audience.

examples.sentence: Su forma de bailar es guay del Paraguay; todos querían aprender esos pasos.
examples.translation: His way of dancing is super cool; everyone wanted to learn those moves.

definitions: Used either as a descriptive label (that is guay del Paraguay) or as an exclamation to praise something as very fashionable or excellent.

examples.sentence: Si buscas un lugar guay del Paraguay para pasar las vacaciones, te recomiendo esta playa.
examples.translation: If you’re looking for a really cool place to spend your vacation, I recommend this beach.

examples.sentence: ¡Guay del Paraguay! Ese nuevo videojuego es el mejor que he probado en años.
examples.translation: Awesome! That new video game is the best I’ve tried in years.

examples.sentence: La decoración de la casa está guay del Paraguay; se ve moderna y acogedora a la vez.
examples.translation: The house decoration is really cool; it looks modern and cozy at the same time.

definitions: A final detail or element that completes, perfects, or enhances something already good; the finishing touch.

examples.sentence: El pastel estaba delicioso, pero la guinda de la tarta fue la decoración con frutas frescas que añadió Ana.
examples.translation: The cake was delicious, but the cherry on top was the fresh fruit decoration that Ana added.

examples.sentence: Cuando terminamos de pintar la casa, instalar las luces LED fue la guinda de la tarta que la hizo perfecta.
examples.translation: When we finished painting the house, installing the LED lights was the finishing touch that made it perfect.

examples.sentence: No esperaba que Juan trajera su guitarra a la cena, eso fue la guinda de la tarta para una noche ya inolvidable.
examples.translation: I didn't expect Juan to bring his guitar to dinner; that was the cherry on top for an already unforgettable night.

definitions: An additional part that crowns or makes something especially appealing or satisfying.

examples.sentence: El concierto fue increíble, y la aparición sorpresa del cantante invitado fue la guinda de la tarta para todos los fans.
examples.translation: The concert was incredible, and the surprise appearance of the guest singer was the crowning touch for all the fans.

examples.sentence: La novela tenía un gran argumento, pero el final inesperado fue la guinda de la tarta que la hizo especial.
examples.translation: The novel had a great plot, but the unexpected ending was the finishing touch that made it special.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, la tarta personalizada con fotos fue la guinda de la tarta que encantó a todos los invitados.
examples.translation: At the party, the personalized cake with photos was the cherry on top that delighted all the guests.

definitions: To suspect that something hidden, deceptive, or dubious is taking place; to feel that there is more to a situation than appears.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuché esa explicación tan confusa, supe que había gato encerrado y decidí investigar más a fondo.
examples.translation: When I heard that confusing explanation, I knew something was fishy and decided to investigate further.

examples.sentence: ¿No te parece raro que Pedro no haya contestado el teléfono? Creo que hay gato encerrado en todo esto.
examples.translation: Doesn't it seem strange to you that Pedro hasn't answered the phone? I think there's something suspicious going on.

examples.sentence: La policía sospechaba que había gato encerrado en el caso, por eso no daban detalles al público.
examples.translation: The police suspected that something was hidden in the case, which is why they weren't giving details to the public.

definitions: To believe that a secret or unexplained factor is involved; to sense that something is fishy.

examples.sentence: Cuando Marta no quiso explicar por qué llegó tarde, sentí que había gato encerrado y no le pregunté más.
examples.translation: When Marta didn't want to explain why she was late, I felt there was something fishy and didn't ask further.

examples.sentence: No me creo esa historia tan perfecta; seguro que hay gato encerrado detrás de esas palabras.
examples.translation: I don't believe that perfect story; surely there's a hidden secret behind those words.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, la actitud evasiva del jefe hizo pensar a todos que había gato encerrado en el proyecto.
examples.translation: In the meeting, the boss's evasive attitude made everyone think there was something shady about the project.

definitions: When used with the preposition 'con' (habérselas con), to have to deal with, confront, or cope with a person, obstacle, or difficult situation.

examples.sentence: Tuve que habérmelas con varios clientes difíciles antes de cerrar el trato exitosamente.
examples.translation: I had to deal with several difficult clients before successfully closing the deal.

examples.sentence: Si quieres entrar en esa empresa, vas a habérselas con un proceso de selección muy riguroso.
examples.translation: If you want to get into that company, you'll have to confront a very rigorous selection process.

examples.sentence: Cuando Marta se mudó sola, tuvo que habérselas con muchos problemas inesperados al principio.
examples.translation: When Marta moved out on her own, she had to cope with many unexpected problems at first.

definitions: To manage or handle a difficult circumstance; to contend with something onerous or unpleasant.

examples.sentence: No sé cómo logró habérselas con tantas tareas en tan poco tiempo, fue impresionante.
examples.translation: I don't know how she managed to handle so many tasks in such a short time; it was impressive.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, los vecinos tuvieron que habérselas para mantener la calma y protegerse.
examples.translation: During the storm, the neighbors had to manage to stay calm and protect themselves.

examples.sentence: Aunque el examen fue complicado, Pedro supo habérselas y sacó una buena nota.
examples.translation: Although the exam was difficult, Pedro knew how to cope and got a good grade.

definitions: As a clitic combination with the auxiliary 'haber' (e.g., habérselas + past participle), to indicate that someone has had, obtained, or been the recipient of an action affecting an object referred to by the clitics; a syntactic form used to express that an action was performed with reference to particular direct or indirect objects.

examples.sentence: María se las ha arreglado para terminar el informe antes de la fecha límite.
examples.translation: María has managed to finish the report before the deadline.

examples.sentence: Nos hemos las visto con varios problemas técnicos durante la presentación, pero al final funcionó todo bien.
examples.translation: We have dealt with several technical problems during the presentation, but in the end, everything worked well.

examples.sentence: ¿Te has las arreglado para contactar con el proveedor después del cambio de número?
examples.translation: Have you managed to get in touch with the supplier after the number change?

examples.sentence: Ellos se las han tenido con muchas dificultades para adaptar el proyecto a los nuevos requisitos.
examples.translation: They have had to deal with many difficulties to adapt the project to the new requirements.

definitions: To manage, get by, or make do (similar to 'to cope' or 'to fend for oneself'), often implying resourcefulness in difficult circumstances.

examples.sentence: Desde que perdió el empleo, ha tenido que habérselas para pagar las cuentas y cuidar a sus hijos.
examples.translation: Since losing his job, he has had to make do to pay the bills and take care of his children.

examples.sentence: Si te quedas sin comida, tendrás que habérselas con lo que encuentres en la despensa.
examples.translation: If you run out of food, you'll have to make do with whatever you find in the pantry.

examples.sentence: Durante el viaje, nos las tuvimos que arreglar con recursos muy limitados y aun así disfrutamos mucho.
examples.translation: During the trip, we had to manage with very limited resources and still enjoyed ourselves a lot.

definitions: Used in spoken or written contexts to indicate that someone took, gave, hid, or otherwise dealt with something (the precise meaning depends on the accompanying clitic pronouns and participle).

examples.sentence: El ladrón se las ha ingeniado para esconder el botín en un lugar que nadie sospecha.
examples.translation: The thief has managed to hide the loot in a place nobody suspects.

examples.sentence: ¿Cómo te las has arreglado para entregar el paquete antes que nadie? Fue un gran esfuerzo.
examples.translation: How did you manage to deliver the package before anyone else? It was a great effort.

examples.sentence: Ellos se las han dado con tanta rapidez que nadie pudo detenerlos a tiempo.
examples.translation: They dealt with it so quickly that no one could stop them in time.

definitions: Everything that exists or could exist; all manner of things; the whole lot.

examples.sentence: En el mercado encontré de habido y por haber: frutas, verduras, artesanías y ropa de todo tipo.
examples.translation: At the market, I found all sorts of things: fruits, vegetables, crafts, and clothes of every kind.

examples.sentence: La biblioteca tiene libros de habido y por haber, desde novelas clásicas hasta ensayos contemporáneos.
examples.translation: The library has books of all kinds, from classic novels to contemporary essays.

examples.sentence: Durante la feria, vendían productos de habido y por haber, lo que hizo la visita muy entretenida.
examples.translation: During the fair, they sold everything imaginable, which made the visit very entertaining.

definitions: A phrase used to indicate an exhaustive or very large assortment of items, actions, or accusations.

examples.sentence: El acusado recibió todo tipo de acusaciones de habido y por haber, algunas sin fundamento claro.
examples.translation: The defendant received all kinds of accusations, some without clear foundation.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, se mencionaron problemas de habido y por haber que complicaron el acuerdo final.
examples.translation: In the meeting, all sorts of problems were mentioned that complicated the final agreement.

examples.sentence: El informe detalla incidentes de habido y por haber relacionados con la gestión del proyecto.
examples.translation: The report details all sorts of incidents related to the management of the project.

definitions: An expression used when a person who has just been mentioned appears or becomes relevant; equivalent to 'speak of the devil.'

examples.sentence: Estábamos hablando justo sobre Ana cuando, hablando del rey de Roma, apareció en la puerta.
examples.translation: We were just talking about Ana when, speak of the devil, she appeared at the door.

examples.sentence: Hablando del rey de Roma, el profesor acaba de entrar justo cuando mencionábamos su nombre.
examples.translation: Speak of the devil, the professor just came in right as we were mentioning his name.

examples.sentence: Mientras comentábamos lo que hizo Luis, hablando del rey de Roma, él nos sorprendió con su presencia.
examples.translation: While we were commenting on what Luis did, speak of the devil, he surprised us by showing up.

definitions: A conversational cue signaling that someone referenced has arrived or unexpectedly become part of the situation being discussed.

examples.sentence: Estábamos planeando la sorpresa y, hablando del rey de Roma, apareció justo a tiempo para escucharnos.
examples.translation: We were planning the surprise and, speak of the devil, he appeared just in time to hear us.

examples.sentence: Hablando del rey de Roma, justo cuando pensábamos en llamar a Marta, recibimos su llamada.
examples.translation: Speak of the devil, just as we thought about calling Marta, we received her call.

examples.sentence: ¿Hablando del rey de Roma? Acaba de llegar justo cuando la conversación giraba en torno a él.
examples.translation: Speak of the devil? He just arrived right when the conversation was about him.

definitions: To speak rapidly and without pause, as if words flowed in a torrent.

examples.sentence: Cuando Carlos se pone nervioso, habla a chorros y apenas puedo seguirle el ritmo.
examples.translation: When Carlos gets nervous, he talks rapidly and I can barely keep up with him.

examples.sentence: No pude interrumpirla porque hablaba a chorros y no dejaba espacio para que nadie más hablara.
examples.translation: I couldn't interrupt her because she was speaking in torrents and didn't give anyone else a chance.

examples.sentence: En la presentación, Marta habló a chorros para cubrir todo el material en poco tiempo.
examples.translation: In the presentation, Marta talked rapidly to cover all the material in a short time.

definitions: To speak with strong feeling or emphasis, giving voluble and energetic expression to one’s thoughts.

examples.sentence: Durante el debate, Juan habló a chorros con tanta pasión que convenció a varios asistentes.
examples.translation: During the debate, Juan spoke energetically with such passion that he convinced several attendees.

examples.sentence: A veces, cuando está emocionada, habla a chorros y todos escuchan atentos cada palabra.
examples.translation: Sometimes, when she's excited, she talks energetically and everyone listens carefully to every word.

examples.sentence: En la reunión familiar, mi abuelo habló a chorros sobre sus aventuras de juventud.
examples.translation: At the family gathering, my grandfather spoke at length about his youth adventures.

definitions: To talk at great length or with abundant verbiage.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando Pedro habla a chorros sin parar; a veces se vuelve difícil seguir sus ideas.
examples.translation: I don't like it when Pedro talks nonstop; sometimes it's hard to follow his ideas.

examples.sentence: Ella habló a chorros durante la entrevista, explicando cada detalle con abundancia de palabras.
examples.translation: She talked at great length during the interview, explaining every detail with abundant words.

examples.sentence: Los políticos suelen hablar a chorros en sus discursos para enfatizar sus propuestas.
examples.translation: Politicians often talk at length in their speeches to emphasize their proposals.

definitions: To speak very quickly and in a disordered or incoherent way.

examples.sentence: Después de varias copas, Miguel empezó a hablar carburo y nadie entendía lo que decía.
examples.translation: After several drinks, Miguel began to talk gibberish and no one understood what he was saying.

examples.sentence: No intentes preguntarle ahora, está hablando carburo y no tiene sentido lo que dice.
examples.translation: Don't try to ask him now, he's speaking incoherently and what he says doesn't make sense.

examples.sentence: Cuando se puso nerviosa, empezó a hablar carburo y se enredó en sus propias palabras.
examples.translation: When she got nervous, she started speaking quickly and incoherently, getting tangled in her own words.

definitions: To talk excessively, often producing exaggerated, implausible, or careless statements.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, Luis habló carburo y exageró los detalles hasta que perdimos interés.
examples.translation: In the meeting, Luis talked excessively and exaggerated the details until we lost interest.

examples.sentence: No le hagas caso cuando habla carburo; suele decir cosas sin mucho sentido ni fundamento.
examples.translation: Don't pay attention when he talks nonsense; he usually says things without much sense or foundation.

examples.sentence: A veces, cuando está emocionado, habla carburo y crea confusión entre los oyentes.
examples.translation: Sometimes, when he's excited, he talks excessively and causes confusion among listeners.

definitions: To speak in a clear, polished, and well‑structured manner, as if reciting from a book.

examples.sentence: Laura habla como un libro cuando explica los conceptos, siempre clara y ordenada.
examples.translation: Laura speaks clearly and orderly when explaining concepts, as if reading from a book.

examples.sentence: Durante el examen oral, el profesor habló como un libro y no dejó lugar a dudas.
examples.translation: During the oral exam, the professor spoke precisely and left no room for doubts.

examples.sentence: Si quieres dar una buena presentación, intenta hablar como un libro para que te entiendan bien.
examples.translation: If you want to give a good presentation, try to speak clearly and well-structured so you're well understood.

definitions: To present information precisely and authoritatively, using correct or textbook language.

examples.sentence: El abogado habló como un libro durante el juicio, usando términos jurídicos correctos y precisos.
examples.translation: The lawyer spoke authoritatively during the trial, using correct and precise legal terms.

examples.sentence: Marcos siempre habla como un libro cuando presenta sus argumentos en clase, demostrando dominio del tema.
examples.translation: Marcos always speaks authoritatively when presenting his arguments in class, showing command of the subject.

examples.sentence: Para que el informe sea convincente, tienes que hablar como un libro y respaldar todo con datos claros.
examples.translation: For the report to be convincing, you have to speak precisely and back everything up with clear data.

definitions: To repeat mechanically what others say, like a parrot; to echo phrases without understanding.

examples.sentence: El niño habla como un loro y repite todas las frases que escucha sin entender su significado.
examples.translation: The child talks like a parrot and repeats all the phrases he hears without understanding their meaning.

examples.sentence: No confíes en sus palabras, solo habla como un loro y no piensa por sí mismo.
examples.translation: Don't trust his words, he just parrots what others say and does not think for himself.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase, varios estudiantes hablaban como loros, repitiendo sin analizar lo que decía el profesor.
examples.translation: During class, several students talked like parrots, repeating without analyzing what the teacher said.

definitions: To chatter incessantly or talk a great deal in a trivial or superficial manner.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, Marta hablaba como un loro, sin parar y sin aportar ideas nuevas.
examples.translation: In the meeting, Marta chattered incessantly without stopping and without contributing new ideas.

examples.sentence: No soporto cuando Pedro habla como un loro; siempre habla mucho pero dice poco importante.
examples.translation: I can't stand it when Pedro talks non-stop; he always talks a lot but says little of importance.

examples.sentence: Mis abuelas solían hablar como loros durante horas, compartiendo historias y chismes del barrio.
examples.translation: My grandmothers used to chatter endlessly for hours, sharing stories and neighborhood gossip.

definitions: To imitate or repeat words and phrases mechanically, as a parrot does.

examples.sentence: El loro del vecino habla como un papagayo y repite cada palabra que escucha de nosotros.
examples.translation: The neighbor's parrot talks like a parrot and repeats every word it hears from us.

examples.sentence: Cuando los niños aprenden a hablar, a veces hablan como un papagayo, imitando sin entender.
examples.translation: When children learn to speak, sometimes they talk like a parrot, imitating without understanding.

examples.sentence: En la obra de teatro, el actor principal hablaba como un papagayo para mostrar su falta de originalidad.
examples.translation: In the play, the lead actor spoke like a parrot to show his lack of originality.

examples.sentence: Mi sobrino habla como un papagayo y ya repite canciones enteras que escucha en la radio.
examples.translation: My nephew talks like a parrot and already repeats entire songs he hears on the radio.

definitions: To speak repetitively or thoughtlessly, often echoing others rather than expressing original ideas.

examples.sentence: En las discusiones, Marta habla como un papagayo, repitiendo siempre los mismos argumentos sin pensar.
examples.translation: In discussions, Marta talks like a parrot, always repeating the same arguments without thinking.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando los políticos hablan como un papagayo, porque no aportan ideas nuevas.
examples.translation: I don't like it when politicians talk like parrots because they don't bring new ideas.

examples.sentence: A veces siento que en esa reunión todos hablaron como papagayos, sin aportar nada original.
examples.translation: Sometimes I feel that in that meeting everyone talked like parrots, without contributing anything original.

definitions: To address God in prayer, petition, or conversation, either aloud or silently.

examples.sentence: Todas las noches, antes de dormir, me gusta hablar con Dios para pedir tranquilidad y fuerza.
examples.translation: Every night before sleeping, I like to talk to God to ask for peace and strength.

examples.sentence: Durante la ceremonia, muchos fieles hablaron con Dios en oración silenciosa y profunda.
examples.translation: During the ceremony, many faithful spoke to God in silent and deep prayer.

examples.sentence: Al enfrentar dificultades, hablar con Dios me da esperanza y claridad para seguir adelante.
examples.translation: When facing difficulties, talking to God gives me hope and clarity to move forward.

examples.sentence: En el retiro espiritual, aprendí a hablar con Dios no solo en voz alta, sino también en mi interior.
examples.translation: In the spiritual retreat, I learned to talk to God not only aloud but also within myself.

definitions: To claim or describe having direct communication with a divine being, implying revelation, guidance, or prophetic insight.

examples.sentence: El profeta afirmaba que hablaba con Dios y recibía mensajes para guiar a su comunidad.
examples.translation: The prophet claimed he spoke with God and received messages to guide his community.

examples.sentence: María aseguró que había hablado con Dios y que eso le había cambiado la vida por completo.
examples.translation: María said she had spoken with God and that it had completely changed her life.

examples.sentence: Se dice que algunos santos podían hablar con Dios y transmitir sus revelaciones a los demás.
examples.translation: It is said that some saints could talk with God and transmit His revelations to others.

definitions: To hold a private, solemn, or deeply personal conversation, used metaphorically to indicate speaking to an authority, conscience, or an ultimately inaccessible interlocutor.

examples.sentence: Después del accidente, sentí que tenía que hablar con Dios para encontrar paz interior.
examples.translation: After the accident, I felt I had to talk with God to find inner peace.

examples.sentence: A veces, cuando no sé qué hacer, hablo con Dios en silencio y reflexiono sobre mis decisiones.
examples.translation: Sometimes, when I don't know what to do, I talk with God silently and reflect on my decisions.

examples.sentence: Antes de tomar una decisión importante, me gusta hablar con Dios para buscar guía y claridad.
examples.translation: Before making an important decision, I like to talk with God to seek guidance and clarity.

definitions: To communicate nonverbally by means of eye contact, facial expression, or gaze, conveying meaning or emotion without speech.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, Laura habló con los ojos para mostrar su desacuerdo sin interrumpir.
examples.translation: During the meeting, Laura spoke with her eyes to show her disagreement without interrupting.

examples.sentence: Los dos amigos se hablaron con los ojos desde el otro lado de la habitación, sin decir una palabra.
examples.translation: The two friends spoke with their eyes from across the room, without saying a word.

examples.sentence: En la película, el protagonista se comunica con los ojos para expresar su amor oculto.
examples.translation: In the movie, the protagonist communicates with his eyes to express his hidden love.

examples.sentence: A veces, hablar con los ojos es más efectivo que mil palabras en una discusión intensa.
examples.translation: Sometimes, speaking with the eyes is more effective than a thousand words in an intense argument.

definitions: To express thoughts or feelings silently, using the eyes as the principal instrument of communication.

examples.sentence: En el concierto, los músicos se hablaban con los ojos para coordinar cada cambio sin decir nada.
examples.translation: At the concert, the musicians spoke with their eyes to coordinate every change without saying anything.

examples.sentence: Cuando Ana estaba triste, su hermano le habló con los ojos para ofrecerle apoyo sin palabras.
examples.translation: When Ana was sad, her brother spoke to her with his eyes to offer support without words.

examples.sentence: En la entrevista, el candidato habló con los ojos y transmitió sinceridad y confianza.
examples.translation: In the interview, the candidate spoke with his eyes and conveyed sincerity and confidence.

definitions: To speak to oneself, either aloud or mentally, often as a form of reflection, rehearsal, or interior dialogue.

examples.sentence: A veces, me sorprendo hablando conmigo mientras organizo mis ideas para el trabajo.
examples.translation: Sometimes, I surprise myself talking to myself while organizing my ideas for work.

examples.sentence: Antes de la reunión importante, Pedro habló consigo para ensayar lo que iba a decir.
examples.translation: Before the important meeting, Pedro talked to himself to rehearse what he was going to say.

examples.sentence: Cuando estoy solo, suelo hablar conmigo para aclarar mis pensamientos y tomar decisiones.
examples.translation: When I'm alone, I usually talk to myself to clarify my thoughts and make decisions.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes si me ves hablando conmigo en voz baja; es mi forma de concentrarme mejor.
examples.translation: Don't worry if you see me talking quietly to myself; it's my way of concentrating better.

definitions: To engage in self-directed discourse that can indicate solitude or introspection and, in some contexts, may be interpreted as a sign of mental distress or emotional strain.

examples.sentence: Después de la discusión, me encontré hablando conmigo mismo para aclarar mis pensamientos.
examples.translation: After the argument, I found myself talking to myself to clear my thoughts.

examples.sentence: No es raro que Juan hable consigo cuando está concentrado en resolver problemas difíciles.
examples.translation: It's not unusual for Juan to talk to himself when he's focused on solving difficult problems.

examples.sentence: ¿Alguna vez has visto a alguien hablando consigo en público? A veces indica que están pasando por un momento complicado.
examples.translation: Have you ever seen someone talking to themselves in public? Sometimes it indicates they're going through a tough time.

definitions: To discuss matters that are irretrievable or already lost; to dwell on a lost cause or on things that cannot be remedied.

examples.sentence: No vale la pena seguir hablando de bueyes perdidos; ese contrato ya no se puede recuperar.
examples.translation: It's not worth continuing to talk about lost causes; that contract can't be recovered.

examples.sentence: Estuvimos horas hablando de bueyes perdidos, intentando rescatar un proyecto que nunca funcionó.
examples.translation: We spent hours talking about lost causes, trying to salvage a project that never worked.

examples.sentence: Si sigues hablando de bueyes perdidos, nunca avanzarás y te quedarás estancado en el pasado.
examples.translation: If you keep dwelling on lost causes, you'll never move forward and will stay stuck in the past.

definitions: To talk about irrelevant or unproductive topics, thereby wasting time or attention.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, comenzaron a hablar de bueyes perdidos y perdimos tiempo valioso que podíamos usar en soluciones.
examples.translation: In the meeting, they started talking about irrelevant topics and we lost valuable time that we could have used on solutions.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando mis amigos hablan de bueyes perdidos porque nunca llegamos a nada concreto.
examples.translation: I don't like it when my friends talk about unproductive things because we never get to anything concrete.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué seguimos hablando de bueyes perdidos en vez de centrarnos en lo que realmente importa?
examples.translation: Why do we keep talking about irrelevant things instead of focusing on what really matters?

definitions: To speak about the sea, maritime life, sailing, or coastal matters.

examples.sentence: María siempre disfruta hablar de la mar porque creció en un pueblo pesquero.
examples.translation: María always enjoys talking about the sea because she grew up in a fishing village.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase, el profesor empezó a hablar de la mar y sus corrientes para explicar la geografía costera.
examples.translation: During class, the teacher began talking about the sea and its currents to explain coastal geography.

examples.sentence: Cuando viajó a la costa, Pedro no podía dejar de hablar de la mar y las olas gigantes que vio.
examples.translation: When he traveled to the coast, Pedro couldn't stop talking about the sea and the huge waves he saw.

examples.sentence: En la conferencia, el biólogo habló de la mar y la biodiversidad que alberga bajo sus aguas.
examples.translation: At the conference, the biologist spoke about the sea and the biodiversity it holds beneath its waters.

definitions: To tell sea tales or recount maritime adventures, often with an element of exaggeration or boastfulness.

examples.sentence: Mi abuelo solía hablar de la mar con historias increíbles de sus días como marinero.
examples.translation: My grandfather used to tell sea tales with incredible stories from his days as a sailor.

examples.sentence: En la taberna, los pescadores hablaban de la mar, exagerando las tormentas que habían enfrentado.
examples.translation: At the tavern, the fishermen told sea tales, exaggerating the storms they had faced.

examples.sentence: No me creo todo lo que dice Carlos cuando habla de la mar; siempre le gusta añadir un poco de drama.
examples.translation: I don't believe everything Carlos says when he tells sea tales; he always likes to add a bit of drama.

definitions: To speak in expansive or grandiose terms, using the sea as a metaphor for vastness or depth.

examples.sentence: En su discurso, el poeta habló de la mar como símbolo de la inmensidad de la vida y los sueños.
examples.translation: In his speech, the poet spoke of the sea as a symbol of the vastness of life and dreams.

examples.sentence: Cuando habla de la mar, Marta usa imágenes grandiosas para describir la profundidad de sus emociones.
examples.translation: When Marta talks about the sea, she uses grandiose images to describe the depth of her emotions.

examples.sentence: El escritor habló de la mar para expresar la idea de un viaje interminable lleno de misterios y desafíos.
examples.translation: The writer spoke of the sea to express the idea of an endless journey full of mysteries and challenges.

definitions: To speak in general terms; to address broad, non-specific aspects of a subject rather than particular details.

examples.sentence: Hablando en general, los estudiantes prefieren clases prácticas a las teóricas.
examples.translation: Speaking in general terms, students prefer practical classes to theoretical ones.

examples.sentence: Si hablamos en general, la situación económica del país ha mejorado en los últimos años.
examples.translation: If we speak in general, the country's economic situation has improved in recent years.

examples.sentence: En general, hablar en general ayuda a evitar detalles que podrían complicar la conversación.
examples.translation: In general, speaking in general terms helps avoid details that could complicate the conversation.

definitions: To discuss general matters or topics in a non-technical, overview manner.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, el gerente habló en general sobre los objetivos sin entrar en cifras específicas.
examples.translation: During the meeting, the manager spoke generally about the goals without going into specific figures.

examples.sentence: Cuando hablas en general sobre el proyecto, es más fácil que todos comprendan la idea principal.
examples.translation: When you speak in general terms about the project, it's easier for everyone to understand the main idea.

examples.sentence: Prefiero que hablemos en general primero y luego nos enfoquemos en los detalles técnicos.
examples.translation: I prefer we speak generally first and then focus on the technical details.

definitions: To make generalizations or statements that apply broadly rather than to a specific case.

examples.sentence: Hablando en general, se puede decir que los jóvenes de hoy son más tecnológicos que antes.
examples.translation: Speaking generally, one could say that today's youth are more technological than before.

examples.sentence: ¿No crees que hablar en general a veces lleva a hacer demasiadas generalizaciones erróneas?
examples.translation: Don't you think that speaking in general sometimes leads to making too many wrong generalizations?

examples.sentence: El político habló en general para cubrir varios temas sin comprometerse con detalles específicos.
examples.translation: The politician spoke in general terms to cover various topics without committing to specific details.

definitions: To utter speech-like sounds believed to be a supernatural or divinely inspired language (glossolalia), especially in Pentecostal and Charismatic Christian contexts.

examples.sentence: Durante la ceremonia, varios creyentes comenzaron a hablar en lenguas, expresando su fervor espiritual.
examples.translation: During the ceremony, several believers began speaking in tongues, expressing their spiritual fervor.

examples.sentence: Nunca había presenciado a alguien hablar en lenguas hasta que fui a esa iglesia pentecostal el año pasado.
examples.translation: I had never witnessed anyone speaking in tongues until I went to that Pentecostal church last year.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que hablar en lenguas es una señal divina o simplemente una experiencia emocional intensa?
examples.translation: Do you think speaking in tongues is a divine sign or simply an intense emotional experience?

definitions: To speak in a language that is unknown or unintelligible to the listener; to babble or speak incoherently.

examples.sentence: Cuando Juan estaba nervioso, empezó a hablar en lenguas y nadie entendía lo que decía.
examples.translation: When Juan was nervous, he started babbling incoherently and no one understood what he was saying.

examples.sentence: A veces, cuando estoy cansada, hablo en lenguas sin darme cuenta y confundo a mis amigos.
examples.translation: Sometimes, when I'm tired, I babble incoherently without realizing it and confuse my friends.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué hablas en lenguas cuando te estresas? Deberías intentar expresarte con claridad.
examples.translation: Why do you babble incoherently when you're stressed? You should try to express yourself clearly.

definitions: Figuratively, to use obscure, technical, or foreign expressions that others cannot understand.

examples.sentence: El profesor comenzó a hablar en lenguas con términos técnicos que nadie en la clase comprendía.
examples.translation: The professor began to speak in obscure jargon that no one in the class understood.

examples.sentence: Cuando María habla en lenguas durante las reuniones, es difícil seguir su argumento por tanto tecnicismo.
examples.translation: When María uses obscure expressions during meetings, it's hard to follow her argument because of so much technical language.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando los expertos hablan en lenguas; deberían explicar las cosas más claramente para todos.
examples.translation: I don't like it when experts use obscure language; they should explain things more clearly for everyone.

definitions: To speak in the vernacular (a Romance language) rather than in Latin; historically used to indicate speech in the local Romance tongue.

examples.sentence: En la Edad Media, los trovadores solían hablar en romance para que el pueblo entendiera sus canciones.
examples.translation: In the Middle Ages, troubadours used to speak in the vernacular so that the people could understand their songs.

examples.sentence: La escritora insiste en hablar en romance para preservar las tradiciones lingüísticas locales.
examples.translation: The writer insists on speaking in the vernacular to preserve local linguistic traditions.

examples.sentence: Los documentos antiguos muestran cómo se empezó a hablar en romance en lugar de latín en ciertas regiones.
examples.translation: Old documents show how people began to speak in the vernacular instead of Latin in certain regions.

examples.sentence: Cuando hablo en romance, me siento más conectado con mis raíces culturales que cuando uso el español formal.
examples.translation: When I speak in the vernacular, I feel more connected to my cultural roots than when I use formal Spanish.

definitions: To speak in a romantic or affectionate manner; to use flirtatious or amorous language.

examples.sentence: Durante la cena, Carlos empezó a hablar en romance para coquetear con Ana de manera divertida.
examples.translation: During dinner, Carlos started speaking romantically to flirt with Ana in a playful way.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre sabe cómo hablar en romance y hacer que todos se sientan especiales a su alrededor.
examples.translation: She always knows how to speak affectionately and make everyone around her feel special.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué no empiezas a hablar en romance cuando le escribes mensajes a Lucía? Seguro le gustará.
examples.translation: Why don't you start speaking romantically when you text Lucía? She'll surely like it.

definitions: To repeat another person's words without understanding them; to relay a message verbatim as if speaking through someone else.

examples.sentence: Pedro habla por boca de ganso cuando repite exactamente lo que escuchó sin entender el mensaje.
examples.translation: Pedro parrots words when he repeats exactly what he heard without understanding the message.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que hables por boca de ganso; prefiero que des tu propia opinión en lugar de repetir a otros.
examples.translation: I don't like it when you parrot others; I prefer you give your own opinion instead of repeating others.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, muchos hablaron por boca de ganso y eso confundió más que aclaró las ideas.
examples.translation: In the meeting, many people repeated others' words verbatim, which confused more than clarified ideas.

definitions: To speak awkwardly, foolishly, or incoherently; to utter remarks that lack sense or polish.

examples.sentence: Cuando intenta explicar el problema, a veces habla por boca de ganso y nadie entiende nada.
examples.translation: When he tries to explain the problem, sometimes he speaks foolishly and no one understands anything.

examples.sentence: No seas tímido ni hables por boca de ganso; expresa tus ideas con claridad y confianza.
examples.translation: Don't be shy or speak foolishly; express your ideas clearly and confidently.

examples.sentence: Me reí porque durante la presentación, el nuevo empleado habló por boca de ganso sin prepararse bien.
examples.translation: I laughed because during the presentation, the new employee spoke foolishly without preparing well.

definitions: To parrot or transmit information secondhand rather than express one's own view.

examples.sentence: No quiero que hables por boca de ganso en mi defensa; necesito que digas lo que realmente piensas.
examples.translation: I don't want you to parrot others in my defense; I need you to say what you really think.

examples.sentence: Algunos políticos solo hablan por boca de ganso, repitiendo discursos sin aportar ideas propias.
examples.translation: Some politicians just parrot speeches, repeating words without offering their own ideas.

examples.sentence: Cuando hablas por boca de ganso, pierdes credibilidad porque parece que no tienes opinión propia.
examples.translation: When you parrot others, you lose credibility because it seems you don't have your own opinion.

definitions: To talk excessively; to speak a great deal or without stopping.

examples.sentence: María habla por los codos cuando se emociona contando sus aventuras de viaje.
examples.translation: María talks excessively when she gets excited telling about her travel adventures.

examples.sentence: No pude interrumpir a Luis porque habla por los codos y nunca para de hablar.
examples.translation: I couldn't interrupt Luis because he talks nonstop and never stops talking.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué hablas por los codos en las reuniones? Deja que otros también expresen sus ideas.
examples.translation: Why do you talk so much in meetings? Let others express their ideas too.

definitions: To be very talkative or loquacious.

examples.sentence: Sofía es muy simpática y habla por los codos, por eso siempre anima las fiestas.
examples.translation: Sofía is very friendly and very talkative, that's why she always livens up parties.

examples.sentence: No es fácil callar a Roberto porque habla por los codos cuando está emocionado.
examples.translation: It's not easy to silence Roberto because he is very talkative when excited.

examples.sentence: Los niños hablan por los codos cuando están juntos y se divierten mucho.
examples.translation: Children talk a lot when they are together and have a great time.

definitions: To cause someone or something to be in a certain state or to perform a certain action; used with que + clause or with a direct object (causative).

examples.sentence: La noticia hizo que todos en la oficina se alegraran por el ascenso de Laura.
examples.translation: The news caused everyone in the office to be happy about Laura's promotion.

examples.sentence: El médico hizo que el paciente descansara para recuperarse mejor.
examples.translation: The doctor made the patient rest to recover better.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes hacer que el equipo termine el proyecto a tiempo?
examples.translation: Can you make the team finish the project on time?

examples.sentence: El entrenador hizo que los jugadores entrenaran más duro para mejorar el rendimiento.
examples.translation: The coach caused the players to train harder to improve performance.

definitions: To cause belief or perception in another person (e.g., to make someone believe something).

examples.sentence: Su sonrisa me hizo creer que todo estaba bien, aunque sabía que no era así.
examples.translation: Her smile made me believe everything was fine, although I knew it wasn't.

examples.sentence: No quiero hacer que pienses mal de mí, pero no puedo explicar lo que pasó.
examples.translation: I don't want to make you think badly of me, but I can't explain what happened.

examples.sentence: Esa película hizo que muchos espectadores reflexionaran sobre la importancia de la amistad.
examples.translation: That movie made many viewers reflect on the importance of friendship.

definitions: To perform, carry out, or execute an action, task, operation, test, stop, visit, or duty.

examples.sentence: Voy a hacer la presentación mañana a las diez en punto.
examples.translation: I am going to give the presentation tomorrow at ten o'clock.

examples.sentence: Hicimos todas las pruebas necesarias antes de lanzar el producto al mercado.
examples.translation: We carried out all the necessary tests before launching the product to the market.

examples.sentence: Ella hace sus tareas con mucha dedicación cada día.
examples.translation: She does her homework with great dedication every day.

examples.sentence: ¿Quién hará la visita al cliente esta semana?
examples.translation: Who will make the visit to the client this week?

definitions: To create, produce, or bring about a result; to make or form something (for example, to make a deal, to make someone into something).

examples.sentence: Juan hizo un trato con la empresa para mejorar las condiciones laborales.
examples.translation: Juan made a deal with the company to improve working conditions.

examples.sentence: La artista hizo una escultura impresionante para la exposición de arte moderna.
examples.translation: The artist created an impressive sculpture for the modern art exhibition.

examples.sentence: Estamos haciendo un esfuerzo para aumentar las ventas este trimestre.
examples.translation: We are making an effort to increase sales this quarter.

examples.sentence: Ella hizo una promesa de ayudar a su comunidad en todo lo que pudiera.
examples.translation: She made a promise to help her community in every way she could.

definitions: To act or behave in a specified way when engaged in a task (to do something).

examples.sentence: Cuando hago la cena, siempre trato de sorprender a mi familia con algo nuevo.
examples.translation: When I cook dinner, I always try to surprise my family with something new.

examples.sentence: ¿Qué haces cuando tienes mucho estrés después del trabajo?
examples.translation: What do you do when you have a lot of stress after work?

examples.sentence: Ella hace su trabajo con mucha responsabilidad y dedicación.
examples.translation: She does her work with a lot of responsibility and dedication.

examples.sentence: Hicimos todo lo posible para que la fiesta fuera un éxito.
examples.translation: We did everything possible to make the party a success.

definitions: To act as or serve as (hacer de + noun): to perform the role or function of someone or something.

examples.sentence: En la obra de teatro, Pedro hizo de villano y sorprendió a todos con su actuación.
examples.translation: In the play, Pedro acted as the villain and surprised everyone with his performance.

examples.sentence: Si no encuentras a nadie más, puedo hacer de guía durante la excursión.
examples.translation: If you don't find anyone else, I can act as a guide during the excursion.

examples.sentence: Ella hizo de intérprete en la reunión para facilitar la comunicación entre los dos grupos.
examples.translation: She acted as an interpreter at the meeting to facilitate communication between the two groups.

definitions: To transform or cause a change in someone or something (causative result).

examples.sentence: El cambio de dieta hizo que Marta se sintiera mucho mejor en pocas semanas.
examples.translation: The change in diet caused Marta to feel much better in a few weeks.

examples.sentence: Hicieron que la antigua fábrica se convirtiera en un centro cultural para la comunidad.
examples.translation: They transformed the old factory into a cultural center for the community.

examples.sentence: El accidente hizo que Carlos perdiera la movilidad en la pierna derecha.
examples.translation: The accident caused Carlos to lose mobility in his right leg.

examples.sentence: Esta experiencia hizo que todos los participantes cambiaran su forma de pensar.
examples.translation: This experience made all the participants change their way of thinking.

definitions: To accomplish, manage, or be able to do something; used to express achievement, effort, or inability to achieve.

examples.sentence: No hice todo lo que quería, pero logré avanzar bastante en el proyecto.
examples.translation: I didn't do everything I wanted, but I managed to make good progress on the project.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que podrás hacer el trabajo antes de la fecha límite?
examples.translation: Do you think you'll be able to get the work done before the deadline?

examples.sentence: Hicimos lo imposible para cumplir con las expectativas del cliente.
examples.translation: We did the impossible to meet the client's expectations.

examples.sentence: Ella no pudo hacer la presentación porque estaba enferma ese día.
examples.translation: She couldn't do the presentation because she was sick that day.

definitions: Part of numerous compound expressions and idioms (for example, to do justice, to do harm), where it contributes the general meaning of 'perform' or 'bring about' in a specific collocation.
