examples.sentence: Si siguen deforestando así, terminarán matando a la gallina de los huevos de oro y perderemos el turismo.
examples.translation: If they keep deforesting like this, they will kill the golden goose and we'll lose tourism.
examples.matched_span: matando a la gallina de los huevos de oro

examples.sentence: No puedes vender todos los productos a precio de ganga; matarías a la gallina de los huevos de oro de la empresa.
examples.translation: You can't sell all the products at bargain prices; you would kill the company's golden goose.
examples.matched_span: matarías a la gallina de los huevos de oro

examples.sentence: El alcalde fue criticado por matar a la gallina de los huevos de oro al cerrar el parque que atraía visitantes.
examples.translation: The mayor was criticized for killing the golden goose by closing the park that attracted visitors.
examples.matched_span: matar a la gallina de los huevos de oro

definitions: To blame, punish, or attack the bearer of unwelcome information instead of addressing the source or content of the message.

examples.sentence: No tiene sentido matar al mensajero solo porque te trae malas noticias.
examples.translation: It makes no sense to kill the messenger just because he brings you bad news.

examples.sentence: Cuando le dije que el proyecto estaba en riesgo, no mató al mensajero sino que buscó soluciones.
examples.translation: When I told him the project was at risk, he didn't kill the messenger but looked for solutions.

examples.sentence: En lugar de matar al mensajero, deberíamos centrarnos en arreglar el problema real.
examples.translation: Instead of killing the messenger, we should focus on fixing the real problem.

definitions: To accomplish two objectives with a single action or effort.
idiom: matar dos pájaros de un tiro

examples.sentence: Con esta reunión matamos dos pájaros de un tiro: resolvimos el contrato y aclaramos el presupuesto.
examples.translation: With this meeting, we killed two birds with one stone: we resolved the contract and clarified the budget.
examples.matched_span: matamos dos pájaros de un tiro

examples.sentence: Si vas a la tienda, aprovecha para comprar pan y leche, así matas dos pájaros de un tiro.
examples.translation: If you go to the store, take the opportunity to buy bread and milk, that way you kill two birds with one stone.
examples.matched_span: matas dos pájaros de un tiro

examples.sentence: Al organizar un evento benéfico y una campaña de concienciación, mataron dos pájaros de un tiro.
examples.translation: By organizing a charity event and an awareness campaign, they killed two birds with one stone.
examples.matched_span: mataron dos pájaros de un tiro

definitions: To quell a slight hunger or craving by eating a small amount of food; to take the edge off one's appetite.

examples.sentence: Antes de la cena, comí una fruta para matar el gusanillo y no llegar con demasiada hambre.
examples.translation: Before dinner, I ate a fruit to quell the slight hunger and not arrive too hungry.

examples.sentence: Cuando salí a correr, llevé una barrita energética para matar el gusanillo durante el entrenamiento.
examples.translation: When I went running, I took an energy bar to take the edge off my appetite during training.

examples.sentence: No pude esperar hasta almorzar, así que maté el gusanillo con un poco de queso y pan.
examples.translation: I couldn't wait until lunch, so I quelled my hunger with some cheese and bread.

definitions: To satisfy or relieve hunger, often temporarily, by eating.

examples.sentence: Después de trabajar todo el día, solo quería matar el hambre con una sopa caliente.
examples.translation: After working all day, I just wanted to satisfy my hunger with a hot soup.

examples.sentence: Nos detuvimos en una cafetería para matar el hambre antes de continuar el viaje.
examples.translation: We stopped at a café to relieve our hunger before continuing the trip.

examples.sentence: Aunque era tarde, decidí matar el hambre con un sándwich rápido para no ir a la cama con hambre.
examples.translation: Although it was late, I decided to satisfy my hunger with a quick sandwich so I wouldn't go to bed hungry.

definitions: To eliminate or reduce hunger on a societal or systemic level, as in discussions of poverty, food security, or public policy.

examples.sentence: Los programas sociales buscan matar el hambre en las comunidades más vulnerables.
examples.translation: Social programs aim to eliminate hunger in the most vulnerable communities.

examples.sentence: Para matar el hambre mundial, es necesario mejorar la distribución de alimentos y reducir el desperdicio.
examples.translation: To eliminate world hunger, it is necessary to improve food distribution and reduce waste.

examples.sentence: La ONG trabaja incansablemente para matar el hambre en zonas afectadas por conflictos.
examples.translation: The NGO works tirelessly to reduce hunger in conflict-affected areas.

definitions: To occupy oneself or engage in an activity in order to pass the time while waiting or until something else happens.

examples.sentence: Mientras esperaba en la sala, maté el tiempo leyendo un libro interesante.
examples.translation: While waiting in the room, I passed the time by reading an interesting book.

examples.sentence: Para matar el tiempo durante el vuelo, descargué varias películas en mi tablet.
examples.translation: To pass the time during the flight, I downloaded several movies on my tablet.

examples.sentence: Cuando los niños se aburren, les doy juegos para matar el tiempo hasta la cena.
examples.translation: When the kids get bored, I give them games to occupy themselves until dinner.

definitions: To use excessively large, disproportionate, or heavy-handed means to solve a trivial problem; to apply overkill.

examples.sentence: Usar un cañón para matar moscas es una exageración total, deberíamos buscar soluciones más medidas.
examples.translation: Using a cannon to kill flies is a total exaggeration; we should look for more measured solutions.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que mates moscas a cañonazos cuando solo se necesita una pequeña corrección.
examples.translation: I don't like that you use excessive means when only a small correction is needed.

examples.sentence: Al despedir a todo el equipo por un error menor, la empresa mató moscas a cañonazos y perdió talento valioso.
examples.translation: By firing the whole team for a minor mistake, the company used overkill and lost valuable talent.

definitions: An expletive expression used to convey anger, frustration, annoyance, or strong emphasis.

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en el mar! No puedo creer que se haya perdido el informe justo antes de la reunión.
examples.translation: Damn it! I can't believe the report got lost right before the meeting.

examples.sentence: Cuando me dijeron que cancelaron el concierto, me cagué en el mar de la frustración.
examples.translation: When they told me the concert was canceled, I was very frustrated.

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en el mar! Otra vez se fue la luz justo cuando estaba cocinando.
examples.translation: Damn it! The power went out again just when I was cooking.

definitions: An exclamation expressing anger, irritation, or annoyance.

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en la leche! Olvidé las llaves dentro del coche otra vez.
examples.translation: Damn it! I forgot the keys inside the car again.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que se rompe algo importante, solo puedo decir: me cago en la leche.
examples.translation: Every time something important breaks, I can only say: damn it.

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en la leche! No esperaba que esa noticia me afectara tanto.
examples.translation: Damn! I didn't expect that news to affect me so much.

definitions: An emphatic interjection expressing surprise, astonishment, or strong emotional emphasis (neutral or positive depending on context).

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en la leche! Este paisaje es increíble, nunca había visto algo así.
examples.translation: Wow! This landscape is incredible, I've never seen anything like it.

examples.sentence: Cuando vi el resultado del examen, pensé: me cago en la leche, ¡qué sorpresa tan buena!
examples.translation: When I saw the exam results, I thought: wow, what a nice surprise!

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en la leche! No esperaba que ganáramos el partido contra el equipo favorito.
examples.translation: Wow! I didn't expect us to win the match against the favorite team.

definitions: A highly offensive expletive used to express intense anger, frustration, or contempt.

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en la puta! No puedo creer que hayan cancelado el vuelo sin avisar.
examples.translation: Fuck! I can't believe they canceled the flight without notice.

examples.sentence: Cuando perdí el contrato importante, solo pude decir: me cago en la puta, esto es inaceptable.
examples.translation: When I lost the important contract, I could only say: fuck, this is unacceptable.

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en la puta! El ordenador se bloqueó y perdí todo mi trabajo.
examples.translation: Fuck! The computer froze and I lost all my work.

definitions: A direct, vulgar insult or exclamation expressing contempt, anger, or hostility toward a specific person.

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en ti! ¿Cómo pudiste traicionarme después de todo lo que hicimos juntos?
examples.translation: Fuck you! How could you betray me after everything we've been through?

examples.sentence: Cuando me engañó, pensé para mis adentros: me cago en ti, no mereces mi confianza.
examples.translation: When he cheated on me, I thought to myself: fuck you, you don't deserve my trust.

examples.sentence: Al ver que sabotearon el proyecto, le grité: me cago en ti, ¿qué pretendes lograr?
examples.translation: Upon seeing that they sabotaged the project, I shouted: fuck you, what are you trying to achieve?

definitions: Literal curse meaning 'I defecate on your dead [relatives],' used as an obscene verbal attack.

examples.sentence: En medio de la pelea, soltó un insulto terrible: me cago en tus muertos, que dejó a todos horrorizados.
examples.translation: In the middle of the fight, he uttered a terrible curse: I defecate on your dead, which horrified everyone.

examples.sentence: No creo que sea apropiado usar expresiones como me cago en tus muertos en la conversación familiar.
examples.translation: I don't think it's appropriate to use expressions like I defecate on your dead in family conversation.

examples.sentence: Al recibir la noticia, reaccionó con un fuerte: me cago en tus muertos, mostrando su profunda ira.
examples.translation: Upon receiving the news, he reacted with a strong: I defecate on your dead, showing his deep anger.

examples.sentence: Aunque es una frase muy ofensiva, algunos la usan sin medir el daño que puede causar: me cago en tus muertos.
examples.translation: Although it's a very offensive phrase, some use it without considering the harm it can cause: I defecate on your dead.

definitions: Figurative exclamation of strong anger, contempt, or frustration equivalent to 'damn you,' 'fuck you,' or 'I curse you.'

examples.sentence: ¡Me cago en tus muertos! No pienso permitir que sigas con esa actitud tan irresponsable.
examples.translation: Damn you! I won't allow you to keep acting so irresponsibly.

examples.sentence: Cuando me engañaron en el trabajo, solo pude pensar: me cago en tus muertos, esto no quedará así.
examples.translation: When I was betrayed at work, I could only think: damn you, this won't stay like this.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que me faltas al respeto, siento ganas de decirte: me cago en tus muertos, pero prefiero mantener la calma.
examples.translation: Every time you disrespect me, I feel like telling you: damn you, but I prefer to stay calm.

definitions: Literal translation 'it peels it for me,' not used in a literal sense and generally meaningless outside the idiom.

examples.sentence: El origen de esta frase es confuso, pero literalmente significa que algo se pela para mí: me la pela.
examples.translation: The origin of this phrase is confusing, but literally it means something peels for me: me la pela.

examples.sentence: Aunque suena extraño, me la pela no se usa en sentido literal, sino como expresión coloquial.
examples.translation: Although it sounds strange, me la pela is not used literally but as a colloquial expression.

examples.sentence: El dicho me la pela no tiene un significado literal coherente fuera de su uso idiomático.
examples.translation: The saying me la pela has no coherent literal meaning outside its idiomatic use.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuché me la pela, pensé en su significado literal, pero luego comprendí que no se usa así.
examples.translation: When I heard me la pela, I thought of its literal meaning, but then I understood it is not used that way.

definitions: Figurative expression of indifference meaning 'I don't care,' 'it does not matter to me,' or 'I couldn't care less.'

examples.sentence: Puedes decirme lo que quieras, pero me la pela totalmente, no me importa tu opinión.
examples.translation: You can say whatever you want, but I don't care at all, your opinion doesn't matter to me.

examples.sentence: Si no vienes a la fiesta, me la pela, yo voy a divertirme igual.
examples.translation: If you don't come to the party, I couldn't care less; I'm going to have fun anyway.

examples.sentence: Me la pela lo que piensen los demás, voy a hacer lo que creo correcto.
examples.translation: I don't care what others think, I'm going to do what I believe is right.

definitions: Literal rendering 'it sweats me,' not used literally and carrying no literal meaning outside the idiom.

examples.sentence: Literalmente, me la suda no tiene sentido, pues no se refiere a que algo sude por mí.
examples.translation: Literally, me la suda doesn't make sense, since it doesn't mean that something sweats for me.

examples.sentence: Aunque la expresión me la suda suena extraña, no se usa en su sentido literal sino figurado.
examples.translation: Although the expression me la suda sounds strange, it is not used literally but figuratively.

examples.sentence: El significado literal de me la suda no es relevante, porque es una expresión coloquial con sentido distinto.
examples.translation: The literal meaning of me la suda is not relevant because it is a colloquial expression with a different meaning.

examples.sentence: Cuando alguien dice me la suda, no piensa en sudor literal, sino que muestra indiferencia.
examples.translation: When someone says me la suda, they don't think about literal sweat but show indifference.

definitions: Figurative declaration of strong indifference or dismissal equivalent to 'I don't give a damn' or 'I couldn't care less.'

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que cambie de opinión? Me la suda completamente lo que digas.
examples.translation: Do you want me to change my mind? I couldn't care less about what you say.

examples.sentence: Si no te gusta cómo hago las cosas, me la suda, yo sigo a mi manera.
examples.translation: If you don't like how I do things, I don't give a damn; I go my own way.

examples.sentence: Cuando me ignoraron en la reunión, pensé: me la suda, haré lo que considere mejor.
examples.translation: When they ignored me at the meeting, I thought: I don't give a damn, I'll do what I think is best.

definitions: Literal meaning 'it sounds Chinese to me,' referring to something that actually resembles the Chinese language in sound.

examples.sentence: El profesor nos enseñó un texto en mandarín que realmente me suena a chino, no entiendo nada.
examples.translation: The teacher showed us a text in Mandarin that literally sounds Chinese to me; I don't understand anything.

examples.sentence: El idioma que se escucha en ese documental me suena a chino, probablemente sea un dialecto que no conozco.
examples.translation: The language heard in that documentary literally sounds Chinese to me; it's probably a dialect I don't know.

examples.sentence: Cuando viajé a China, la pronunciación me sonaba a chino en el sentido literal, era difícil distinguir palabras.
examples.translation: When I traveled to China, the pronunciation literally sounded Chinese to me; it was hard to distinguish words.

examples.sentence: En la clase de idiomas, algunas frases en cantonés me suenan a chino, pues nunca las he escuchado antes.
examples.translation: In language class, some phrases in Cantonese literally sound Chinese to me because I've never heard them before.

definitions: Figurative expression meaning 'it is incomprehensible to me' or 'it sounds like gibberish,' used when something is confusing or unintelligible.

examples.sentence: Cuando me explicó la fórmula matemática, me sonó a chino y no pude seguir la explicación.
examples.translation: When he explained the mathematical formula to me, it sounded like gibberish and I couldn't follow the explanation.

examples.sentence: Las instrucciones del dispositivo me suenan a chino, creo que necesito ayuda para entenderlas.
examples.translation: The device instructions sound like gibberish to me; I think I need help to understand them.

examples.sentence: No entiendo nada de ese contrato, me suena a chino todo el lenguaje legal que usan.
examples.translation: I don't understand anything in that contract; all the legal language sounds like gibberish to me.

definitions: Literal phrase 'to urinate holy water,' a nonsensical image when taken literally and rarely used in a literal sense.

examples.sentence: La expresión mear agua bendita no tiene sentido literal, pues nadie orina agua bendita realmente.
examples.translation: The expression 'to urinate holy water' has no literal sense, since nobody actually urinates holy water.

examples.sentence: En el texto antiguo, se menciona mear agua bendita, una imagen absurda que no debe tomarse literalmente.
examples.translation: In the old text, it mentions urinating holy water, an absurd image that should not be taken literally.

examples.sentence: Cuando leí la frase mear agua bendita, pensé en lo extraño que sería hacerlo en sentido literal.
examples.translation: When I read the phrase 'to urinate holy water,' I thought about how strange it would be literally.

examples.sentence: Aunque mear agua bendita parece una acción imposible, a veces se usa para ilustrar hipocresía en textos antiguos.
examples.translation: Although urinating holy water seems impossible, it is sometimes used to illustrate hypocrisy in old texts.

definitions: Figurative expression meaning 'to feign piety or righteousness' or 'to act sanctimonious,' used critically to describe hypocritical moral posturing.

examples.sentence: No soporto cuando la gente mea agua bendita para parecer más moral que los demás.
examples.translation: I can't stand when people feign righteousness to seem morally superior.

examples.sentence: El político estuvo toda la campaña meando agua bendita, pero sus actos fueron contradictorios.
examples.translation: The politician was sanctimonious throughout the campaign, but his actions were contradictory.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, varios mearon agua bendita para ocultar sus verdaderas intenciones.
examples.translation: In the meeting, several feigned piety to hide their real intentions.

definitions: Literal: to urinate outside the flowerpot or pot, i.e., to relieve oneself in the wrong place.

examples.sentence: El perro se escapó y meó fuera del tiesto, justo en medio del jardín de las flores.
examples.translation: The dog escaped and urinated outside the flowerpot, right in the middle of the flower garden.

examples.sentence: Cuando el niño no encontraba el baño, terminó meando fuera del tiesto en el pasillo.
examples.translation: When the child couldn't find the bathroom, he ended up urinating outside the flowerpot in the hallway.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, alguien meó fuera del tiesto y causó un gran disgusto entre los invitados.
examples.translation: At the party, someone urinated outside the flowerpot and caused great displeasure among the guests.

examples.sentence: La vieja fuente está rota y agua meó fuera del tiesto, mojando todo alrededor.
examples.translation: The old fountain is broken and water spilled outside the flowerpot, wetting everything around.

definitions: Figurative: to behave or speak inappropriately, to make a blunder, or to go beyond acceptable bounds (to put one’s foot in it or to go off-topic).

examples.sentence: Cuando intentó explicar el proyecto, realmente estaba meando fuera del tiesto y nadie entendió su punto.
examples.translation: When he tried to explain the project, he was really putting his foot in it and no one understood his point.

examples.sentence: No quiero que meares fuera del tiesto en la reunión de mañana; es mejor que te ciñas al tema principal.
examples.translation: I don't want you to go off-topic in tomorrow's meeting; it's better if you stick to the main subject.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre meó fuera del tiesto con sus comentarios inapropiados, y eso le ha costado varias oportunidades laborales.
examples.translation: She always behaves inappropriately with her comments, and that has cost her several job opportunities.

definitions: Literal: to laugh so hard that one wets oneself.

examples.sentence: El chiste fue tan gracioso que casi me meo de risa en medio de la clase.
examples.translation: The joke was so funny that I almost wet myself laughing in the middle of class.

examples.sentence: Cuando vimos el video, nos meábamos de risa sin poder parar.
examples.translation: When we watched the video, we were laughing so hard we were wetting ourselves and couldn't stop.

examples.sentence: No me reía tanto desde hace años, literalmente me meé de risa con esa comedia.
examples.translation: I hadn't laughed that much in years, I literally wet myself laughing at that comedy.

examples.sentence: ¿Te acuerdas de la anécdota? Casi me meo de risa cuando la contaste en la fiesta.
examples.translation: Do you remember the anecdote? I almost wet myself laughing when you told it at the party.

definitions: Figurative: to find something extremely funny; to laugh uncontrollably.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que escucho ese chiste, me meo de risa sin poder controlarlo.
examples.translation: Every time I hear that joke, I laugh uncontrollably.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes, a todos nos nos hemos meado de risa con sus ocurrencias alguna vez.
examples.translation: Don't worry, we have all found ourselves laughing uncontrollably at his antics at some point.

examples.sentence: Si te cuento lo que pasó, seguro que te meás de risa.
examples.translation: If I tell you what happened, you're sure to laugh uncontrollably.

definitions: Literal: half an orange, i.e., one half of a whole orange.

examples.sentence: Compré una media naranja para preparar el jugo de esta mañana.
examples.translation: I bought half an orange to prepare juice this morning.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes pasarme la media naranja que quedó en la mesa?
examples.translation: Can you pass me the half orange that was left on the table?

examples.sentence: Durante el almuerzo, corté una media naranja para añadir a la ensalada.
examples.translation: During lunch, I cut half an orange to add to the salad.

examples.sentence: La receta lleva una media naranja exprimida para darle sabor.
examples.translation: The recipe calls for half an orange squeezed to add flavor.

definitions: Figurative: a soulmate or perfect complement; the ideal romantic partner.

examples.sentence: Desde que conocí a Ana, supe que era mi media naranja, la persona perfecta para mí.
examples.translation: Since I met Ana, I knew she was my soulmate, the perfect person for me.

examples.sentence: No creía en el amor hasta que encontré a mi media naranja y todo cambió.
examples.translation: I didn't believe in love until I found my soulmate and everything changed.

examples.sentence: Juan siempre dice que su esposa es su media naranja y que no podría vivir sin ella.
examples.translation: Juan always says that his wife is his soulmate and that he couldn't live without her.

definitions: Literal: half tones or partial shades (in painting, printing, or color description).

examples.sentence: El artista usó medias tintas para dar profundidad y textura a su pintura.
examples.translation: The artist used half tones to give depth and texture to his painting.

examples.sentence: En la impresión, las medias tintas permiten reproducir imágenes con gradaciones suaves.
examples.translation: In printing, half tones allow reproducing images with smooth gradations.

examples.sentence: Para el diseño gráfico, es importante dominar las medias tintas para un buen acabado.
examples.translation: For graphic design, mastering half tones is important for a good finish.

examples.sentence: La fotografía en blanco y negro destaca por sus medias tintas que resaltan los contrastes.
examples.translation: Black and white photography stands out for its half tones that highlight contrasts.

definitions: Figurative: partial measures, lack of decisiveness, or a refusal to take a firm or clear position (doing things by halves).

examples.sentence: No podemos hacer medias tintas en este proyecto, necesitamos una decisión clara ya.
examples.translation: We can't do things by halves in this project; we need a clear decision now.

examples.sentence: Si sigues tomando medias tintas, nunca resolverás el problema de raíz.
examples.translation: If you keep being indecisive, you'll never solve the problem at its root.

examples.sentence: El jefe criticó a los empleados por hacer medias tintas en la entrega del informe.
examples.translation: The boss criticized the employees for taking partial measures in delivering the report.

definitions: Literal: in the middle of nowhere; located in an isolated or remote place far from towns or landmarks.

examples.sentence: La cabaña está situada en medio de la nada, lejos de cualquier pueblo o señal de vida.
examples.translation: The cabin is located in the middle of nowhere, far from any town or sign of life.

examples.sentence: Durante nuestro viaje, acampamos en medio de la nada sin cobertura ni electricidad.
examples.translation: During our trip, we camped in the middle of nowhere without coverage or electricity.

examples.sentence: El restaurante está en medio de la nada; no hay otras opciones para comer cerca.
examples.translation: The restaurant is in the middle of nowhere; there are no other dining options nearby.

examples.sentence: Encontramos una fuente de agua potable en medio de la nada, lo que nos salvó la caminata.
examples.translation: We found a drinking water source in the middle of nowhere, which saved our hike.

definitions: Figurative: in a situation of isolation, obscurity, or insignificance; removed from attention, resources, or support.

examples.sentence: Después de ser despedido, se sintió como en medio de la nada sin apoyo ni recursos.
examples.translation: After being fired, he felt like he was in the middle of nowhere with no support or resources.

examples.sentence: El artista emergente estaba en medio de la nada, sin reconocimiento ni oportunidades para mostrar su trabajo.
examples.translation: The emerging artist was in obscurity, without recognition or opportunities to showcase his work.

examples.sentence: No quiero quedarme en medio de la nada durante la crisis, necesito estar conectado con alguien que me ayude.
examples.translation: I don't want to be isolated during the crisis; I need to be connected with someone who can help me.

definitions: Half of the world; one half of the Earth's surface or population.

examples.sentence: Medio mundo quedó sorprendido con las noticias del descubrimiento científico.
examples.translation: Half the world was surprised by the news of the scientific discovery.

examples.sentence: El virus se propagó rápidamente afectando a medio mundo en cuestión de meses.
examples.translation: The virus spread quickly, affecting half the world in a matter of months.

examples.sentence: Medio mundo habla diferentes idiomas, pero todos entienden la música.
examples.translation: Half the world speaks different languages, but everyone understands music.

examples.sentence: Durante la conferencia, representantes de medio mundo estuvieron presentes para discutir el cambio climático.
examples.translation: During the conference, representatives from half the world were present to discuss climate change.

definitions: A very large number of people; many people (used hyperbolically to indicate wide public exposure or popularity).

examples.sentence: En la fiesta había medio mundo, desde colegas hasta familiares y amigos de la infancia.
examples.translation: There were tons of people at the party, from coworkers to family and childhood friends.

examples.sentence: Cuando lanzó su nuevo álbum, medio mundo lo estaba escuchando y hablando de él en redes sociales.
examples.translation: When he released his new album, tons of people were listening and talking about it on social media.

examples.sentence: No puedo creer que medio mundo se haya enterado de nuestra sorpresa antes de tiempo.
examples.translation: I can't believe so many people found out about our surprise ahead of time.

definitions: A very great distance or a large part of the world; used to indicate travel across many countries or long journeys.

examples.sentence: Para su trabajo, ha viajado medio mundo buscando inspiración en diferentes culturas.
examples.translation: For his work, he has traveled half the world seeking inspiration in different cultures.

examples.sentence: María contó que recorrió medio mundo durante sus vacaciones de verano, visitando más de veinte países.
examples.translation: Maria said she traveled half the world during her summer vacation, visiting over twenty countries.

examples.sentence: He conocido gente de medio mundo gracias a mi trabajo en la embajada.
examples.translation: I've met people from all over the world thanks to my work at the embassy.

definitions: A very large quantity or extent; used hyperbolically to emphasize magnitude.

examples.sentence: La empresa invirtió medio mundo en publicidad para lanzar su nuevo producto.
examples.translation: The company spent a huge amount on advertising to launch their new product.

examples.sentence: Para organizar la boda, gastaron medio mundo en decoraciones y banquetes.
examples.translation: To organize the wedding, they spent a lot of money on decorations and banquets.

examples.sentence: Cuando vi el precio del coche, pensé que costaba medio mundo.
examples.translation: When I saw the price of the car, I thought it cost a fortune.

definitions: A chicken's memory (literal).

examples.sentence: Los pollos tienen memoria de pollo y olvidan rápidamente dónde pusieron el alimento.
examples.translation: Chickens have a chicken's memory and quickly forget where they put the food.

examples.sentence: Durante el experimento, notaron que la memoria de pollo de las aves afectaba los resultados.

examples.sentence: La memoria de pollo de este animal hace que no recuerde el camino de regreso al corral.

examples.sentence: Comparado con otros animales, el gallo tiene una memoria de pollo bastante limitada.
examples.translation: Compared to other animals, the rooster has a fairly limited memory.

definitions: A very short or poor memory; used to describe someone who is forgetful or quickly forgets things.

examples.sentence: Olvidas todo tan rápido que parece que tienes memoria de pollo.
examples.translation: You forget everything so fast it seems like you have a very poor memory.

examples.sentence: Con esa memoria de pollo, no me extraña que se haya olvidado del cumpleaños de su mejor amigo.
examples.translation: With such a poor memory, it's no surprise he forgot his best friend's birthday.

examples.sentence: Si no tomas notas, tu memoria de pollo te jugará en contra durante el examen.
examples.translation: If you don't take notes, your poor memory will work against you during the exam.

definitions: To masturbate (of a male); to stimulate one's own penis sexually.

examples.sentence: Durante la adolescencia, muchos chicos empiezan a meneársela como parte de su desarrollo sexual.
examples.translation: During adolescence, many boys start masturbating as part of their sexual development.

examples.sentence: No es raro que los jóvenes se meneen para descubrir sus gustos y sensaciones.
examples.translation: It's not unusual for young people to masturbate to discover their tastes and sensations.

examples.sentence: El terapeuta explicó que meneársela es una práctica común y natural en la sexualidad humana.
examples.translation: The therapist explained that masturbating is a common and natural practice in human sexuality.

definitions: To perform a sexual act on another person, usually as a favor or to obtain advantage (vulgar).

examples.sentence: Le dije que me la meneaba si me conseguía ese favor, aunque fue algo incómodo discutirlo.
examples.translation: I told him I would do him a sexual favor if he got me that favor, although it was uncomfortable to discuss.

examples.translation: In the movie, the character performs a sexual favor to his boss to get a promotion, showing a dark side.

examples.translation: I don't like people thinking I perform sexual favors to get benefits; I prefer to do things on my own merit.

definitions: To tamper with, fiddle with, or manipulate something (for example figures, records, or mechanisms); to handle something in an irregular or improvised way.

examples.sentence: El contador se la meneó con los números para ajustar los balances y esconder gastos.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que me la meneen con las cifras, prefiero transparencia en las cuentas.
examples.translation: I don't like people tampering with the figures; I prefer transparency in the accounts.

examples.sentence: El técnico se la meneó con el motor hasta que logró que arrancara, aunque no fue un arreglo profesional.
examples.translation: The technician fiddled with the engine until it started, although it wasn't a professional fix.

definitions: Literally 'less bad'; indicating that something is not as bad as it could have been.

examples.sentence: Menos mal que no llovió durante el picnic, así pudimos disfrutar sin problemas.
examples.translation: Luckily it didn't rain during the picnic, so we could enjoy it without problems.

examples.sentence: Llegué tarde, pero menos mal que la reunión también empezó tarde.
examples.translation: I arrived late, but fortunately the meeting also started late.

examples.sentence: Menos mal que revisaste los documentos antes de enviarlos, evitamos un error grave.
examples.translation: Good thing you checked the documents before sending them; we avoided a serious mistake.

examples.sentence: Perdí el autobús, pero menos mal que el siguiente llegaba en diez minutos.
examples.translation: I missed the bus, but fortunately the next one arrived in ten minutes.

definitions: Fortunately; used to express relief or gratitude that an undesirable outcome was avoided or that the situation turned out acceptably.

examples.sentence: Menos mal que encontraste las llaves, estaba a punto de llamar al cerrajero.
examples.translation: Fortunately, you found the keys; I was about to call the locksmith.

examples.sentence: Menos mal que avisaron del cambio de horario, sino hubiera llegado muy temprano.
examples.translation: Luckily they informed us about the schedule change, otherwise I would have arrived very early.

examples.sentence: Menos mal que me acompañaste al médico, no sabía cómo llegar al lugar.
examples.translation: It's a relief you accompanied me to the doctor; I didn't know how to get there.

definitions: To mention or name someone's mother (literal reference to the mother).

examples.sentence: En la carta mencionó a su madre con mucho cariño y respeto.
examples.translation: In the letter, he mentioned his mother with much affection and respect.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, alguien mentó la madre de uno de los presentes, lo que generó tensión.
examples.translation: During the meeting, someone named the mother of one of the attendees, which caused tension.

examples.sentence: No es común mentar la madre en conversaciones formales o profesionales.
examples.translation: It is not common to mention one's mother in formal or professional conversations.

examples.sentence: En el libro, el autor mentó la madre de un personaje para explicar sus orígenes familiares.
examples.translation: In the book, the author mentioned a character's mother to explain their family background.

definitions: To insult or curse someone's mother; to utter an offensive expression directed at a person's family as a personal attack.

examples.sentence: Cuando se pelearon, él no dudó en mentar la madre, lo que empeoró la discusión.
examples.translation: When they fought, he didn't hesitate to insult his mother, which worsened the argument.

examples.sentence: No es correcto mentar la madre de alguien, eso solo genera más conflictos.
examples.translation: It's not right to curse someone's mother; that only creates more conflicts.

examples.sentence: El conductor se enfadó tanto que empezó a mentar la madre del otro automovilista.
examples.translation: The driver got so angry that he started cursing the other driver's mother.

definitions: To mention the rope in the house of the hanged (literal phrasing of the proverb).
idiom: mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado

examples.sentence: El viejo refrán dice que no se debe mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado para no empeorar la situación.
examples.translation: The old saying goes that you shouldn't mention the rope in the house of the hanged so as not to worsen the situation.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, alguien mentó la soga en casa del ahorcado al recordar el accidente fatal.

examples.sentence: No es prudente mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado cuando alguien está atravesando un mal momento.
examples.translation: It's not wise to bring up a sensitive topic when someone is going through a tough time.
examples.matched_span: mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado

examples.sentence: Al hablar de sus errores, Carlos mentó la soga en casa del ahorcado y empeoró su imagen.

examples.matched_span: mentó la soga en casa del ahorcado

definitions: To bring up a subject that is especially inappropriate, insensitive, or hurtful given someone's misfortune; to aggravate a person by referring to a particularly sore topic.
idiom: mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado

examples.sentence: Cuando le recordaron su despido en la fiesta, él dijo que era mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado.
examples.translation: When they reminded him of his firing at the party, he said it was like bringing up a sore subject.
examples.matched_span: mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado

examples.sentence: No deberías mentar la soga en casa del ahorcado hablando de sus problemas económicos frente a ella.

definitions: To lie in the manner of a 'bellaco' (a scoundrel or rogue) (literal wording).

examples.sentence: Se dice que ese político miente como un bellaco para ocultar sus verdaderas intenciones.
examples.translation: They say that politician lies shamelessly to hide his true intentions.

examples.sentence: Durante el juicio, el acusado mintió como un bellaco para evitar la condena.
examples.translation: During the trial, the defendant lied boldly to avoid conviction.

examples.sentence: No confíes en lo que dice, miente como un bellaco sin ningún remordimiento.
examples.translation: Don't trust what he says; he lies shamelessly without any remorse.

examples.sentence: La prensa acusó al empresario de mentir como un bellaco para manipular el mercado.
examples.translation: The press accused the businessman of lying shamelessly to manipulate the market.

definitions: To tell bold, shameless, or habitual lies; to be extremely dishonest in speech.

examples.sentence: No puedo creer que siga mintiendo como un bellaco, parece no importarle la verdad.
examples.translation: I can't believe he keeps lying shamelessly; he seems not to care about the truth.

examples.sentence: Es frustrante trabajar con alguien que miente como un bellaco y nunca asume responsabilidad.
examples.translation: It's frustrating to work with someone who lies shamelessly and never takes responsibility.

examples.sentence: Cuando le preguntaron, respondió mintiendo como un bellaco para salvar su reputación.
examples.translation: When asked, he responded by lying shamelessly to save his reputation.

definitions: To lie more than one speaks (literal composition of the phrase).

examples.sentence: Dicen que él mentir más que hablar, siempre inventa historias imposibles de creer.
examples.translation: They say he lies more than he talks; he always invents unbelievable stories.

examples.sentence: No confíes en María, porque mentir más que hablar es su costumbre desde hace años.
examples.translation: Don't trust Maria because she has been a habitual liar for years.

examples.sentence: Algunos políticos parecen mentir más que hablar para ganar votos a cualquier costo.
examples.translation: Some politicians seem to lie more than they speak to win votes at any cost.

examples.sentence: Es evidente que en esta situación él mentir más que hablar y busca confundir a todos.
examples.translation: It's obvious that in this situation he is lying more than speaking and trying to confuse everyone.

definitions: To be a habitual liar; to utter falsehoods more often than truthful statements.

examples.sentence: No es fácil convivir con alguien que miente más que habla y nunca dice la verdad.
examples.translation: It's not easy to live with someone who lies more than they speak and never tells the truth.

examples.sentence: Durante la entrevista, mostró que miente más que habla para impresionar al entrevistador.
examples.translation: During the interview, he showed that he lies more than he speaks to impress the interviewer.

examples.sentence: Si sigues mintiendo más que hablando, nadie te creerá cuando digas la verdad.
examples.translation: If you keep lying more than speaking, no one will believe you when you tell the truth.

definitions: To lie by the beard (literal wording, referring to the words themselves).

examples.sentence: El barbero cortó el cabello y también recortó la barba con mucho cuidado.
examples.translation: The barber cut the hair and also trimmed the beard very carefully.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes peinar esa barba para que no se vea desordenada en la foto?
examples.translation: Can you comb that beard so it doesn't look messy in the photo?

examples.sentence: Ella notó que la barba del actor estaba teñida para la película histórica.
examples.translation: She noticed that the actor's beard was dyed for the historical movie.

examples.sentence: El anciano se acariciaba la barba mientras pensaba profundamente en la respuesta.
examples.translation: The old man stroked his beard while thinking deeply about the answer.

definitions: To tell an outrageous or brazen lie; to lie shamelessly.

examples.sentence: No le creas, siempre está mintiendo por la barba para salirse con la suya.
examples.translation: Don't believe him, he's always telling outrageous lies to get his way.

examples.sentence: Cuando le preguntaron sobre el accidente, mintió por la barba sin ningún remordimiento.
examples.translation: When they asked him about the accident, he shamelessly told a brazen lie.

examples.sentence: Si sigues mintiendo por la barba, nadie confiará en ti jamás.
examples.translation: If you keep telling outrageous lies, no one will ever trust you.

definitions: Literally, a 'snack' or 'tea' involving Black people; a phrase that refers to people of African descent and is considered racially offensive.

examples.sentence: En el museo, vimos una exhibición sobre la merienda de negros en el siglo XIX.
examples.translation: At the museum, we saw an exhibit about the 'merienda de negros' in the 19th century.

examples.sentence: La historia documenta cómo se organizaba la merienda de negros en las plantaciones antiguas.
examples.translation: The history documents how the 'merienda de negros' was organized on old plantations.

examples.sentence: El libro describe la comida típica servida durante la merienda de negros en esa época.
examples.translation: The book describes the typical food served during the 'merienda de negros' in that era.

examples.sentence: Se encontraron utensilios usados para la merienda de negros en la excavación arqueológica.
examples.translation: Utensils used for the 'merienda de negros' were found in the archaeological excavation.

definitions: A disorderly, chaotic gathering or situation in which rules are ignored and many people act independently; a noisy free-for-all or shambles (usage is idiomatic and carries offensive connotations).

examples.sentence: La reunión terminó siendo una verdadera merienda de negros, con todos hablando a la vez y sin orden.
examples.translation: The meeting ended up being a real chaotic free-for-all, with everyone talking at once and no order.

examples.sentence: No invites a esos dos juntos, siempre hacen una merienda de negros y arruinan la fiesta.
examples.translation: Don't invite those two together, they always create a noisy shambles and ruin the party.

examples.sentence: Cuando el jefe no está, la oficina se convierte en una merienda de negros, sin respeto por las reglas.
examples.translation: When the boss is not around, the office turns into a chaotic mess with no respect for the rules.

definitions: Literally, the act of putting a paw or foot in; a figurative extension of physically putting one's foot somewhere inappropriate.

examples.sentence: El gato tuvo una metedura de pata cuando intentó subirse a la mesa y casi tira el jarrón.
examples.translation: The cat literally put its paw in the wrong place when it tried to jump on the table and almost knocked over the vase.

examples.sentence: Mientras caminaba por el campo, tuve una metedura de pata y pisé un charco de barro.
examples.translation: While walking through the field, I literally put my foot in a puddle of mud.

examples.sentence: El cachorro metió la pata dentro de la caja y rompió algunas cosas sin querer.
examples.translation: The puppy put its paw inside the box and accidentally broke some things.

examples.sentence: No te metas con el perro cuando tiene una metedura de pata, podría asustarse y morder.
examples.translation: Don't bother the dog when it has its paw stuck somewhere; it might get scared and bite.

definitions: An embarrassing mistake, blunder, or social faux pas; an error that causes awkwardness or trouble.

examples.sentence: Fue una verdadera metedura de pata mencionar el tema del despido durante la cena familiar.
examples.translation: It was a real blunder to bring up the subject of the firing during the family dinner.

examples.sentence: Si no quieres causar problemas, evita esa metedura de pata en la reunión de trabajo.
examples.translation: If you don't want to cause trouble, avoid that embarrassing mistake at the work meeting.

examples.sentence: Juan cometió una metedura de pata al enviar el correo equivocado a todo el departamento.
examples.translation: Juan made a blunder by sending the wrong email to the entire department.

definitions: Literally, to put or push the belly in a particular position.

examples.sentence: Durante la sesión de yoga, nos enseñaron a meter barriga para mejorar la postura.
examples.translation: During the yoga session, they taught us to push in the belly to improve posture.

examples.sentence: Ella metió la barriga antes de salir para que el vestido le quedara mejor ajustado.
examples.translation: She sucked in her stomach before going out so the dress would fit better.

examples.sentence: Puedes meter la barriga mientras caminas para ejercitar los músculos abdominales.
examples.translation: You can hold in your stomach while walking to exercise the abdominal muscles.

examples.sentence: Los bailarines metían la barriga para mantener la línea y el equilibrio en el escenario.
examples.translation: The dancers pulled in their stomachs to maintain the line and balance on stage.

definitions: To suck in or hold in one's stomach in order to appear slimmer or to improve one's posture or appearance.

examples.sentence: Cuando vio la cámara, rápidamente metió barriga para parecer más delgado en la foto.
examples.translation: When he saw the camera, he quickly sucked in his stomach to look slimmer in the photo.

examples.sentence: Si quieres verte mejor en la entrevista, no olvides meter barriga y mantener la espalda recta.
examples.translation: If you want to look better in the interview, don't forget to hold in your stomach and keep your back straight.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre mete barriga antes de salir porque quiere que su figura luzca perfecta.
examples.translation: She always sucks in her stomach before going out because she wants her figure to look perfect.

definitions: Literally, to put in a 'baza' (baza can mean a card or turn), implying insertion into a sequence or play.

examples.sentence: En el juego de cartas, le tocó meter baza en la tercera ronda para intentar ganar.
examples.translation: In the card game, it was his turn to play a card in the third round to try to win.

examples.sentence: Ella metió su baza justo cuando todos pensaban que el equipo había perdido.
examples.translation: She put in her card just when everyone thought the team had lost.

examples.sentence: El jugador decidió meter baza con una carta inesperada que cambió el resultado.
examples.translation: The player decided to play a card unexpectedly that changed the outcome.

examples.sentence: Después de que metieron sus bazas, el juego se volvió mucho más interesante y competitivo.
examples.translation: After they played their cards, the game became much more interesting and competitive.

definitions: To intervene in a conversation or discussion, to interject, or to try to have a say or influence the outcome of a matter.

examples.sentence: No pude evitar meter baza en la discusión porque sentía que estaban ignorando un punto importante.
examples.translation: I couldn't help but interject in the discussion because I felt they were ignoring an important point.

examples.sentence: Si quieres que te escuchen, tienes que meter baza y expresar tus ideas con claridad.
examples.translation: If you want to be heard, you have to intervene and express your ideas clearly.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre mete baza en las reuniones para asegurarse de que sus intereses estén representados.
examples.translation: She always interjects in meetings to make sure her interests are represented.

definitions: Literally, to sow tares or noxious weeds; cizaña refers to tare plants in agricultural or biblical contexts.

examples.sentence: El agricultor se dedicó a meter cizaña en el campo para separar el trigo de las malas hierbas.
examples.translation: The farmer sowed tares in the field to separate the wheat from the weeds.

examples.sentence: Durante la siembra, es importante no meter cizaña para evitar que las plantas dañinas crezcan entre el cultivo.
examples.translation: During sowing, it's important not to plant tares to prevent harmful plants from growing among the crops.

examples.sentence: El texto bíblico menciona cómo se mete cizaña entre el trigo para simbolizar el mal entre el bien.
examples.translation: The biblical text mentions how tares are sown among the wheat to symbolize evil among good.

examples.sentence: El campesino advirtió que alguien había metido cizaña en su terreno para arruinar la cosecha.
examples.translation: The farmer warned that someone had sown tares on his land to ruin the harvest.

definitions: To sow discord or create friction between people or groups, often by spreading rumors, provoking misunderstandings, or deliberately encouraging conflict.

examples.sentence: No dejes que Pedro meta cizaña entre los compañeros; siempre está creando conflictos innecesarios.
examples.translation: Don't let Pedro sow discord among the coworkers; he's always creating unnecessary conflicts.

examples.sentence: Cuando Ana empezó a meter cizaña en el grupo, la amistad se volvió tensa y difícil.
examples.translation: When Ana began to stir up trouble in the group, the friendship became tense and difficult.

examples.sentence: Si alguien intenta meter cizaña, lo mejor es ignorarlo para no empeorar la situación.
examples.translation: If someone tries to sow discord, the best thing is to ignore it to avoid worsening the situation.

definitions: To insert or fit something by force or with a tool such as a shoehorn; to force a physical object into a space where it does not fit naturally.

examples.sentence: Tuve que meter la llave con calzador porque estaba oxidada y no entraba en la cerradura.
examples.translation: I had to force the key in with a tool because it was rusty and wouldn't fit in the lock.

examples.sentence: El zapato no entraba bien, así que tuve que meterlo con calzador para que mi pie cupiera.
examples.translation: The shoe didn't fit well, so I had to force it on to fit my foot.

examples.sentence: Metieron la tabla con calzador para que encajara en el marco antiguo de la puerta.
examples.translation: They forced the plank in to fit the old door frame.

examples.sentence: No se puede meter el mueble con calzador en ese espacio tan pequeño sin dañarlo.
examples.translation: You can't force the furniture into that small space without damaging it.

definitions: To force an idea, detail, scene, or element into a text, conversation, plan, or situation in an awkward, unconvincing, or inappropriate way.

examples.sentence: El guionista metió esa escena con calzador; no encajaba con el resto de la película.
examples.translation: The screenwriter forced that scene in awkwardly; it didn't fit with the rest of the movie.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando alguien mete con calzador argumentos que no tienen sentido en la conversación.
examples.translation: I don't like it when someone awkwardly forces arguments that don't make sense into the conversation.

examples.sentence: Intentaron meter con calzador una cláusula en el contrato que realmente no era necesaria.
examples.translation: They tried to awkwardly force a clause into the contract that really wasn't necessary.

definitions: To put a spoon into something, literally inserting a spoon into a container, dish, or similar receptacle.

examples.sentence: Por favor, mete la cuchara en la sopa para probar si le falta sal.
examples.translation: Please put the spoon into the soup to check if it lacks salt.

examples.sentence: Ella metió la cuchara en el frasco para sacar un poco de miel para el té.
examples.translation: She put the spoon into the jar to get some honey for the tea.

examples.sentence: Antes de servir, mete la cuchara en la mezcla para asegurarte de que está bien homogénea.
examples.translation: Before serving, put the spoon into the mixture to make sure it is well blended.

examples.sentence: Metí la cuchara con cuidado para no derramar el arroz en la bandeja.
examples.translation: I put the spoon in carefully so as not to spill the rice on the tray.

definitions: To meddle in, interfere with, or insert oneself into another person's affairs or into a situation without being asked.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando mi hermana mete cuchara en mis asuntos personales sin que se lo pida.
examples.translation: I don't like it when my sister meddles in my personal affairs without being asked.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que hay una discusión, Juan mete cuchara y empeora las cosas en vez de ayudar.
examples.translation: Every time there's an argument, Juan meddles and makes things worse instead of helping.

examples.sentence: Por favor, no metas cuchara en esta negociación; es un asunto privado entre ellos.
examples.translation: Please don't interfere in this negotiation; it's a private matter between them.

definitions: To put or insert the neck into something, as when passing the neck through an opening or into clothing (literal physical action).

examples.sentence: Para ponerse el abrigo, primero metió el cuello en la solapa con cuidado.
examples.translation: To put on the coat, he first put his neck into the collar carefully.

examples.sentence: El perro metió el cuello en el arnés antes de salir a pasear por el parque.
examples.translation: The dog put its neck into the harness before going for a walk in the park.

examples.sentence: Metimos el cuello del suéter dentro de la chaqueta para protegernos del frío intenso.
examples.translation: We put the sweater's neck inside the jacket to protect ourselves from the intense cold.

examples.sentence: El niño metió el cuello en el cuello de la camiseta para no mojarse con la lluvia.
examples.translation: The child put his neck into the shirt collar to avoid getting wet in the rain.

definitions: To attack or assault someone physically by applying force to the neck (to throttle or strangle) or, more generally, to assault another person.

examples.sentence: Durante la pelea, uno de los chicos intentó meter cuello y estrangular a su oponente.
examples.translation: During the fight, one of the boys tried to attack by strangling his opponent.

examples.sentence: No permitas que nadie te meta cuello; defiéndete si alguien intenta agredirte.
examples.translation: Don't let anyone assault you; defend yourself if someone tries to attack you.

examples.sentence: El acusado fue condenado por meter cuello y causar lesiones graves a la víctima.
examples.translation: The defendant was convicted of assaulting and causing serious injuries to the victim.

definitions: To place a finger into a wound, literally touching or probing an open or sore area.
idiom: meter el dedo en la llaga

examples.sentence: Al limpiar la herida, metió el dedo en la llaga para quitar la suciedad acumulada.
examples.translation: When cleaning the wound, he put his finger into the sore to remove the accumulated dirt.
examples.matched_span: metió el dedo en la llaga

examples.sentence: No metas el dedo en la llaga mientras examinas la quemadura para no causar dolor extra.
examples.translation: Don't put your finger into the wound while examining the burn so as not to cause extra pain.
examples.matched_span: metas el dedo en la llaga

examples.sentence: El médico metió el dedo en la llaga para comprobar la profundidad de la herida.
examples.translation: The doctor put his finger into the wound to check its depth.
examples.matched_span: metió el dedo en la llaga

examples.sentence: Ella metió el dedo en la llaga con cuidado al tratar de limpiar la cortadura de su hijo.
examples.translation: She carefully put her finger into the wound while trying to clean her son's cut.
examples.matched_span: metió el dedo en la llaga

definitions: To mention, highlight, or return to a painful, sensitive, or embarrassing subject in a way that aggravates emotional hurt or embarrassment; to rub salt in the wound.
idiom: meter el dedo en la llaga

examples.sentence: Cuando le recordé el error que cometió, realmente metí el dedo en la llaga y lo hice sentir mal.
examples.translation: When I reminded him of the mistake he made, I really rubbed salt in the wound and made him feel bad.
examples.matched_span: metí el dedo en la llaga

examples.sentence: No metas el dedo en la llaga hablando de su fracaso en público; es un tema muy sensible para él.
examples.translation: Don't rub salt in the wound by talking about his failure in public; it's a very sensitive subject for him.
examples.matched_span: metas el dedo en la llaga

examples.sentence: Cada vez que sacan ese asunto en la reunión, meten el dedo en la llaga y generan tensión entre todos.
examples.translation: Every time they bring up that topic in the meeting, they rub salt in the wound and create tension among everyone.
examples.matched_span: meten el dedo en la llaga

definitions: To put one's shoulder into something in a literal, physical sense, especially to push or brace against an object.

examples.sentence: Para mover el pesado mueble, metió el hombro y empujó con todas sus fuerzas.
examples.translation: To move the heavy furniture, he put his shoulder into it and pushed with all his strength.

examples.sentence: El jugador metió el hombro en la defensa rival para abrir espacio hacia la portería.
examples.translation: The player used his shoulder against the rival defense to open space toward the goal.

examples.sentence: Durante la construcción, todos metieron el hombro para terminar antes del plazo establecido.
examples.translation: During the construction, everyone pitched in to finish before the deadline.

examples.sentence: Metimos el hombro para empujar el coche que se había quedado sin gasolina en la carretera.
examples.translation: We put our shoulders into pushing the car that had run out of gas on the road.

definitions: To help, contribute effort, or pitch in to a collective task or endeavor; to lend practical support through physical or energetic participation.

examples.sentence: Si todos meten el hombro, podremos organizar el evento sin problemas y a tiempo.
examples.translation: If everyone pitches in, we will be able to organize the event without problems and on time.

examples.sentence: Cuando la comunidad metió el hombro, lograron reconstruir el parque después de la tormenta.
examples.translation: When the community contributed effort, they managed to rebuild the park after the storm.

examples.sentence: Para sacar adelante el proyecto, necesitamos que todos metan el hombro y trabajen en equipo.
examples.translation: To move the project forward, we need everyone to pitch in and work as a team.

definitions: Literal: to place one’s foot into or onto something (a shoe, container, water, a doorway, etc.).

examples.sentence: Antes de entrar, metió el pie en el charco sin darse cuenta y se mojó todo el pantalón.
examples.translation: Before entering, he stepped into the puddle without realizing and got his pants wet.

examples.sentence: Metí el pie en el zapato nuevo y me quedó un poco apretado al principio.
examples.translation: I put my foot into the new shoe and it was a bit tight at first.

examples.sentence: El niño metió el pie dentro de la caja para alcanzar el juguete que estaba en el fondo.
examples.translation: The child put his foot inside the box to reach the toy at the bottom.

examples.sentence: Ella metió el pie en la puerta para evitar que la cerraran mientras hablaba con su amiga.
examples.translation: She put her foot in the door to prevent it from closing while she was talking to her friend.

definitions: Figurative: to commit a social or verbal blunder; to say or do something awkward or embarrassing (equivalent to 'put one’s foot in one’s mouth').

examples.sentence: Creo que metiste el pie cuando mencionaste el tema del dinero en la fiesta; fue incómodo para todos.
examples.translation: I think you put your foot in your mouth when you mentioned money at the party; it was uncomfortable for everyone.

examples.sentence: No quiero meter el pie, pero me parece que ese comentario fue inapropiado en la reunión.
examples.translation: I don't want to put my foot in my mouth, but I think that comment was inappropriate in the meeting.

examples.sentence: Cuando hablé sin pensar, metí el pie y ofendí a mi jefe sin querer.
examples.translation: When I spoke without thinking, I put my foot in my mouth and offended my boss unintentionally.

definitions: Figurative: to gain an initial foothold or entry into a place, position, or opportunity (equivalent to 'get a foot in the door').

examples.sentence: Con esta pasantía, logré meter el pie en la empresa y espero obtener un contrato fijo pronto.
examples.translation: With this internship, I managed to get a foot in the door at the company and hope to get a permanent contract soon.

examples.sentence: Si quieres meter el pie en el mercado internacional, necesitas una buena estrategia de marketing.
examples.translation: If you want to get a foothold in the international market, you need a good marketing strategy.

examples.sentence: Ella metió el pie en el mundo de la moda gracias a su trabajo como asistente en una revista importante.
examples.translation: She got her foot in the door of the fashion world thanks to her job as an assistant at a major magazine.

definitions: Figurative: to bring someone or something under control; to discipline, restrain, or make conform to rules or authority.

examples.sentence: El director tuvo que meter en cintura a los empleados para que cumplieran con los horarios establecidos.
examples.translation: The director had to bring the employees under control so they would comply with the established schedules.

examples.sentence: Si no metes en cintura a los niños, la situación en la escuela se volverá incontrolable.
examples.translation: If you don't discipline the children, the situation at school will become uncontrollable.

examples.sentence: La policía logró meter en cintura a la pandilla que causaba problemas en el barrio.
examples.translation: The police managed to bring the gang causing trouble in the neighborhood under control.

definitions: Literal: to tighten or fit something around the waist.

examples.sentence: El sastre metió en cintura el vestido para que le quedara perfecto a la clienta.
examples.translation: The tailor tightened the dress around the waist so it would fit the client perfectly.

examples.sentence: Para la sesión de fotos, metieron en cintura la chaqueta para resaltar la figura del modelo.
examples.translation: For the photo session, they cinched the jacket at the waist to highlight the model's figure.

examples.sentence: Ella metió en cintura el cinturón del vestido para darle un toque más elegante al atuendo.
examples.translation: She tightened the belt of the dress at the waist to give the outfit a more elegant touch.

examples.sentence: Antes de salir, metió en cintura el abrigo para protegerse mejor del frío.
examples.translation: Before going out, she cinched the coat around her waist to better protect herself from the cold.

definitions: Figurative: to group two or more people or things together as if they were the same, often unfairly or without distinction (equivalent to 'to lump together' or 'put in the same bag').

examples.sentence: No puedes meter en el mismo saco a todos los estudiantes solo porque algunos no entregaron la tarea.
examples.translation: You can't lump all the students together just because some didn't submit the homework.

examples.sentence: Es injusto meter en el mismo saco a los empleados que trabajan duro y a los que no cumplen con sus responsabilidades.
examples.translation: It's unfair to put employees who work hard and those who don't fulfill their responsibilities in the same bag.

examples.sentence: Muchas veces la prensa mete en el mismo saco a políticos de diferentes ideologías sin hacer distinciones.
examples.translation: Often the press lumps politicians of different ideologies together without making distinctions.

definitions: Literal: to place multiple items or persons into the same sack or bag.

examples.sentence: Metieron en el mismo saco todas las frutas para facilitar el transporte al mercado.
examples.translation: They put all the fruits in the same sack to facilitate transport to the market.

examples.sentence: Durante la cosecha, los agricultores metieron en el mismo saco los granos recogidos de diferentes campos.
examples.translation: During the harvest, the farmers placed the grains collected from different fields into the same bag.

examples.sentence: El vendedor metió en el mismo saco las manzanas y las peras para ofrecer una mejor oferta.
examples.translation: The seller put the apples and pears in the same sack to offer a better deal.

examples.sentence: Los productos defectuosos fueron metidos en el mismo saco para ser retirados del almacén.
examples.translation: The defective products were put in the same sack to be removed from the warehouse.

definitions: Literal: to insert a token, chip, coin, or card into a machine or system.

examples.sentence: Para jugar, metió ficha en la máquina y empezó la partida inmediatamente.
examples.translation: To play, he inserted a token into the machine and the game started immediately.

examples.sentence: Metimos fichas en las máquinas recreativas del centro comercial para divertirnos un rato.
examples.translation: We put coins into the arcade machines at the mall to have some fun for a while.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que meto ficha en esa máquina, me sorprende con un premio inesperado.
examples.translation: Every time I insert a token into that machine, it surprises me with an unexpected prize.

examples.sentence: Antes de empezar el juego, asegúrate de meter ficha para activar el sistema correctamente.
examples.translation: Before starting the game, make sure to insert a token to activate the system properly.

definitions: Figurative: to make a romantic or sexual advance toward someone; to try to pick someone up.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, Carlos no dudó en meter ficha con Ana para conocerla mejor.
examples.translation: At the party, Carlos didn't hesitate to make a move on Ana to get to know her better.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué siempre metes ficha con las chicas del trabajo? Eso puede ser incómodo.
examples.translation: Why do you always hit on the girls at work? That can be uncomfortable.

examples.sentence: Cuando Juan vio a Marta, empezó a meter ficha sin perder tiempo, intentando invitarla a salir.
examples.translation: When Juan saw Marta, he started making advances without wasting time, trying to ask her out.

definitions: Literal: to insert multiple tokens, chips, coins, or cards into a machine or container.

examples.sentence: Para jugar en la máquina, primero debes meter fichas y luego elegir tu juego.
examples.translation: To play on the machine, you first have to insert coins and then choose your game.

examples.sentence: Ayer en el casino, metimos varias fichas en la ruleta antes de que cerraran.
examples.translation: Yesterday at the casino, we inserted several chips into the roulette before they closed.

examples.sentence: No olvides meter fichas en la máquina expendedora si quieres un refresco.
examples.translation: Don't forget to put coins into the vending machine if you want a soda.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que metemos fichas en la máquina, esperamos ganar algo de dinero.
examples.translation: Every time we insert tokens into the machine, we hope to win some money.

definitions: Figurative: to make repeated romantic or flirtatious advances; to persistently try to win someone’s favor.

examples.sentence: Aunque Marta no parecía interesada, Luis seguía metiendo fichas sin rendirse.
examples.translation: Even though Marta didn't seem interested, Luis kept making flirtatious advances without giving up.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que me metan fichas todo el tiempo cuando solo quiero ser amiga.
examples.translation: I don't like it when people keep hitting on me all the time when I just want to be friends.

examples.sentence: Si quieres conquistarla, tendrás que meter fichas con más paciencia y dedicación.
examples.translation: If you want to win her over, you'll have to make persistent advances with more patience and dedication.

definitions: Figurative: to invest resources, effort, or stakes in an endeavor (equivalent to 'putting chips in' or 'staking one's claim').

examples.sentence: La empresa decidió meter fichas en el desarrollo de tecnología renovable para el futuro.
examples.translation: The company decided to invest resources in renewable technology development for the future.

examples.sentence: Nosotros hemos metido fichas importantes en este proyecto porque creemos en su éxito.
examples.translation: We have put significant stakes into this project because we believe in its success.

examples.sentence: Si vas a meter fichas en ese negocio, asegúrate de entender todos los riesgos involucrados.
examples.translation: If you are going to invest effort in that business, make sure you understand all the risks involved.

definitions: To insert a spoon into something or to take a spoonful from a dish (literal action of placing a spoon).

examples.sentence: Por favor, mete la cuchara en la sopa para probar si ya está bien sazonada.
examples.translation: Please put the spoon in the soup to check if it's well seasoned.

examples.sentence: Mientras cocinaba, María metió la cuchara para mezclar todos los ingredientes.
examples.translation: While cooking, María inserted the spoon to mix all the ingredients.

examples.sentence: No metas la cuchara en la cazuela todavía, la comida necesita más tiempo para cocinarse.
examples.translation: Don't put the spoon into the pot yet; the food needs more time to cook.

examples.sentence: Cuando metí la cuchara en el postre, me di cuenta de que estaba delicioso.
examples.translation: When I put the spoon into the dessert, I realized it was delicious.

definitions: To interpose oneself in a conversation or situation without being invited; to butt in, intervene, or meddle.

examples.sentence: No metas la cuchara en nuestra conversación, esta es una discusión entre amigos.
examples.translation: Don't butt into our conversation; this is a discussion among friends.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que hablan de política, Pedro mete la cuchara sin que nadie lo invite.
examples.translation: Every time they talk about politics, Pedro butts in without anyone inviting him.

examples.sentence: Aunque intenté no meter la cuchara, no pude evitar dar mi opinión sobre el asunto.
examples.translation: Although I tried not to butt in, I couldn't help giving my opinion about the matter.

definitions: To place or put a shrimp (gamba) (literal, seldom used outside concrete contexts).

examples.sentence: Para preparar la paella, primero mete la gamba en la sartén caliente con aceite.
examples.translation: To prepare the paella, first put the shrimp into the hot pan with oil.

examples.sentence: Cuando metí la gamba en el plato, parecía fresca y bien cocida.
examples.translation: When I placed the shrimp on the plate, it looked fresh and well cooked.

examples.sentence: Por favor, mete la gamba con cuidado para que no se rompa durante la cocción.
examples.translation: Please put the shrimp carefully so it doesn't break during cooking.

examples.sentence: El chef metió la gamba justo en el momento perfecto para que quedara al dente.
examples.translation: The chef put the shrimp in at just the right moment so it would be al dente.

definitions: To commit a mistake or blunder; to err, especially in a conspicuous or embarrassing way.

examples.sentence: Creo que metiste la gamba al olvidar el cumpleaños de tu mejor amigo.
examples.translation: I think you messed up by forgetting your best friend's birthday.

examples.sentence: No metas la gamba en la reunión de mañana; revisa bien tus documentos antes.
examples.translation: Don't make a blunder at tomorrow's meeting; review your documents carefully beforehand.

examples.sentence: Cuando habló sin saber, realmente metió la gamba y causó un malentendido grande.
examples.translation: When he spoke without knowing, he really screwed up and caused a big misunderstanding.

definitions: To put or push one's nose into or toward something (literal act of inserting the nose).

examples.sentence: El perro metió la nariz en la caja para descubrir qué había dentro.
examples.translation: The dog put its nose into the box to find out what was inside.

examples.sentence: Metí la nariz en el libro para oler el papel antiguo y disfrutar su aroma.
examples.translation: I put my nose into the book to smell the old paper and enjoy its aroma.

examples.sentence: Mientras caminaba, metió la nariz en el aire para captar el aroma de las flores.
examples.translation: While walking, he put his nose in the air to catch the scent of the flowers.

examples.sentence: No metas la nariz en la comida hasta que esté lista para evitar quemaduras.
examples.translation: Don't put your nose near the food until it's ready to avoid burns.

definitions: To pry into or interfere with other people's affairs; to be nosy or meddlesome.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que metas la nariz en mis asuntos personales sin que te lo pida.
examples.translation: I don't like you prying into my personal matters without me asking.

examples.sentence: Cuando veo que alguien mete la nariz donde no debe, prefiero alejarme para evitar problemas.
examples.translation: When I see someone meddling where they shouldn't, I prefer to stay away to avoid problems.

examples.sentence: Si sigues metiendo la nariz en la oficina, podrías ganarte una reprimenda del jefe.
examples.translation: If you keep poking your nose around the office, you might get a reprimand from the boss.

definitions: To place one's foot or paw somewhere (literal meaning).

examples.sentence: Para alcanzar la mesa, metió la pata bajo el mantel sin que nadie lo notara.
examples.translation: To reach the table, he put his foot under the tablecloth without anyone noticing.

examples.sentence: El gato metió la pata en la maceta y tiró la planta al suelo.
examples.translation: The cat placed its paw in the flowerpot and knocked the plant to the floor.

examples.sentence: Cuando metí la pata en el charco, me mojé los zapatos completamente.
examples.translation: When I put my foot in the puddle, my shoes got completely wet.

examples.sentence: ¿Viste cómo metió la pata en el agujero mientras caminaba por el jardín?
examples.translation: Did you see how he put his foot into the hole while walking through the garden?

definitions: To make a mistake, blunder, or tactless remark; to commit an error that causes embarrassment or problems.

examples.sentence: Perdón, metí la pata en la reunión cuando mencioné un tema confidencial sin querer.
examples.translation: Sorry, I made a blunder in the meeting when I mentioned a confidential topic unintentionally.

examples.sentence: No metas la pata con tus comentarios si quieres mantener buenas relaciones en el trabajo.
examples.translation: Don't slip up with your comments if you want to keep good relationships at work.

examples.sentence: Cuando dijo eso delante de todos, realmente metió la pata y se sintió muy avergonzado.
examples.translation: When he said that in front of everyone, he really messed up and felt very embarrassed.

definitions: To insert one's nose into something (literal physical action, rarely used figuratively in this exact form).

examples.sentence: Metí las narices en el pequeño agujero para ver qué había al otro lado de la pared.
examples.translation: I stuck my nose into the small hole to see what was on the other side of the wall.

examples.sentence: El niño metió las narices en el frasco para intentar oler la fragancia del perfume.
examples.translation: The boy put his nose into the jar to try to smell the fragrance of the perfume.

examples.sentence: Cuando metió las narices en la caja, descubrió que había un regalo escondido.
examples.translation: When he put his nose into the box, he discovered there was a hidden gift.

examples.sentence: No metas las narices en lugares peligrosos para evitar accidentes innecesarios.
examples.translation: Don't put your nose into dangerous places to avoid unnecessary accidents.

definitions: To intrude into or pry into the affairs or matters of others; to meddle where one is not wanted.

examples.sentence: No metas las narices en lo que no te importa; esta es una cuestión privada.
