examples.translation: Don't pry into what doesn't concern you; this is a private matter.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que metes las narices en nuestras discusiones, las cosas se complican más.
examples.translation: Every time you meddle in our discussions, things get more complicated.

examples.sentence: Si sigues metiendo las narices en la oficina, podrías crear problemas innecesarios.
examples.translation: If you keep interfering at the office, you might create unnecessary problems.

definitions: To place one's hand on or into someone or something; literally to put a hand to.

examples.sentence: Metí la mano en el bolsillo para sacar las llaves del auto rápidamente.
examples.translation: I put my hand in my pocket to quickly take out the car keys.

examples.sentence: Cuando metiste la mano en la caja, ¿encontraste lo que buscabas?
examples.translation: When you put your hand in the box, did you find what you were looking for?

examples.sentence: Ella metió la mano en la bolsa para agarrar su teléfono móvil.
examples.translation: She put her hand in the bag to grab her mobile phone.

examples.sentence: Por favor, no metas la mano en la nevera sin lavártelas antes para evitar contagios.
examples.translation: Please don't put your hand in the fridge without washing them first to avoid contamination.

definitions: To grope or fondle someone sexually without consent; to molest.

examples.sentence: El hombre fue arrestado por meter mano a una mujer en el transporte público sin su consentimiento.
examples.translation: The man was arrested for groping a woman on public transport without her consent.

examples.sentence: Si alguien te mete la mano sin permiso, debes denunciarlo inmediatamente para protegerte.
examples.translation: If someone fondles you without permission, you should report it immediately to protect yourself.

examples.sentence: Nunca está bien que alguien meta mano a otra persona; el respeto es fundamental.
examples.translation: It's never right for someone to grope another person; respect is fundamental.

definitions: To interfere with, tamper with, or appropriate something (for example, another's possessions, finances, machinery, or data).

examples.sentence: Alguien metió mano en la cuenta bancaria y retiró dinero sin autorización.
examples.translation: Someone tampered with the bank account and withdrew money without authorization.

examples.sentence: La empresa descubrió que un empleado metió mano en los archivos confidenciales.
examples.translation: The company discovered that an employee interfered with the confidential files.

examples.sentence: No permitas que nadie meta mano en tus pertenencias cuando no estás presente.
examples.translation: Don't allow anyone to tamper with your belongings when you're not around.

definitions: To put it (feminine) folded; literally to place something folded.

examples.sentence: Para guardar la servilleta, mete la doblada dentro del cajón para que no se arrugue.
examples.translation: To store the napkin, put the folded one inside the drawer so it doesn't get wrinkled.

examples.sentence: Cuando termines de usar la toalla, métela doblada en la cesta de la ropa sucia.
examples.translation: When you finish using the towel, put it folded into the laundry basket.

examples.sentence: Ella metió la carta doblada en el sobre antes de enviarla por correo.
examples.translation: She put the folded letter in the envelope before sending it by mail.

examples.sentence: Por favor, mete la ropa doblada en el armario para mantener todo ordenado.
examples.translation: Please put the folded clothes in the closet to keep everything tidy.

definitions: To deceive, trick, or take advantage of someone by cunning or surprise; to pull a fast one.

examples.sentence: Me metió la doblada al venderme un producto defectuoso sin decirme nada.
examples.translation: He tricked me by selling me a defective product without telling me.

examples.sentence: Si crees que no te van a meter la doblada en ese trato, estás muy equivocado.
examples.translation: If you think they won't pull a fast one on you in that deal, you're very mistaken.

examples.sentence: Nos metieron la doblada cuando nos cobraron un precio mucho más alto del acordado.
examples.translation: They tricked us when they charged a much higher price than agreed.

definitions: To dive headfirst into water or a space; literally to enter head-first.

examples.sentence: El niño se metió de cabeza en la piscina para impresionar a sus amigos.
examples.translation: The boy dove headfirst into the pool to impress his friends.

examples.sentence: Cuando metí de cabeza el pie en el agua, sentí que estaba muy fría.
examples.translation: When I put my foot headfirst into the water, I felt it was very cold.

examples.sentence: Ella se metió de cabeza en el hueco para rescatar al gato atrapado.
examples.translation: She went headfirst into the hole to rescue the trapped cat.

examples.sentence: Para evitar la caída, metió de cabeza las manos frente a ella y logró sostenerse.
examples.translation: To avoid falling, she put her hands headfirst in front of her and managed to hold on.

definitions: To commit oneself fully and promptly to an activity or course of action; to plunge into something energetically or without hesitation.

examples.sentence: Después de escuchar la propuesta, se metió de cabeza en el proyecto sin dudarlo.
examples.translation: After hearing the proposal, he plunged headfirst into the project without hesitation.

examples.sentence: Si quieres aprender a tocar guitarra rápido, tienes que meterte de cabeza y practicar mucho.
examples.translation: If you want to learn to play guitar quickly, you have to commit yourself fully and practice a lot.

examples.sentence: Nos metimos de cabeza en la organización del evento para que todo saliera perfecto.
examples.translation: We threw ourselves energetically into organizing the event so everything would turn out perfect.

definitions: To put on a shirt made from eleven varas (an old unit of measure); literal, historical phrasing.
idiom: meterse en camisa de once varas

examples.sentence: En tiempos antiguos, la gente se metía en camisa de once varas para protegerse del frío.
examples.translation: In ancient times, people put on a shirt made of eleven varas to protect themselves from the cold.
examples.matched_span: se metía en camisa de once varas

examples.sentence: El sastre metió la tela en camisa de once varas para hacer la camisa más larga.
examples.translation: The tailor folded the fabric into a shirt of eleven varas to make the shirt longer.

examples.sentence: Para la fiesta tradicional, se metieron en camisa de once varas, siguiendo la costumbre antigua.
examples.translation: For the traditional party, they put on shirts made of eleven varas, following the old custom.
examples.matched_span: se metieron en camisa de once varas

examples.sentence: Cuando metí la camisa de once varas en el armario, noté que estaba muy vieja y desgastada.
examples.translation: When I put the eleven-varas shirt into the closet, I noticed it was very old and worn out.

definitions: To involve oneself in an unnecessarily complicated, risky, or troublesome matter; to create or enter into needless difficulties.
idiom: meterse en camisa de once varas

examples.sentence: No quiero meterme en camisa de once varas discutiendo con ellos sobre ese tema complicado.
examples.translation: I don't want to get involved in unnecessary trouble arguing with them about that complicated issue.
examples.matched_span: meterme en camisa de once varas

examples.sentence: Si decides aceptar ese contrato sin leerlo bien, te estarás metiendo en camisa de once varas.
examples.translation: If you decide to accept that contract without reading it carefully, you'll be getting yourself into unnecessary trouble.
examples.matched_span: metiendo en camisa de once varas

examples.sentence: Marta se metió en camisa de once varas cuando intentó arreglar el problema sin ayuda profesional.
examples.translation: Marta got herself into trouble when she tried to fix the problem without professional help.
examples.matched_span: se metió en camisa de once varas

definitions: To enter deep places or depths; literally to go into deep waters or cavities.

examples.sentence: El buzo se metió en honduras para explorar el arrecife de coral más profundo.
examples.translation: The diver went into deep waters to explore the deepest coral reef.

examples.sentence: Metimos en honduras la sonda para medir la profundidad del lago en ese punto.
examples.translation: We lowered the probe into the depths to measure the lake's depth at that point.

examples.sentence: Cuando metí la mano en honduras, sentí que tocaba una roca fría y húmeda.
examples.translation: When I put my hand into the depths, I felt I was touching a cold, wet rock.

examples.sentence: Los exploradores se metieron en honduras de la cueva para descubrir nuevas galerías.
examples.translation: The explorers entered the deep parts of the cave to discover new galleries.

definitions: To examine, discuss, or engage with the deeper, more serious, or complex aspects of a subject; to become deeply involved in an issue.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, nos metimos en honduras del problema para encontrar una solución eficaz.
examples.translation: In the meeting, we delved into the depths of the problem to find an effective solution.

examples.sentence: No podemos quedarnos en la superficie; debemos meternos en honduras para entender el asunto.
examples.translation: We can't stay on the surface; we must get deeply involved to understand the matter.

examples.sentence: El profesor nos pidió que nos metiéramos en honduras del texto para analizar su significado oculto.
examples.translation: The teacher asked us to delve deeply into the text to analyze its hidden meaning.

definitions: To place or insert a feminine‑marked object or entity ('la') into a location or recipient; the literal act of putting something into something else.

examples.sentence: Metí la llave en la cerradura para abrir la puerta de la casa de mi abuela.
examples.translation: I put the key into the lock to open my grandmother's house door.

examples.sentence: Cuando metí la carta en el buzón, sentí que finalmente había terminado el trámite.
examples.translation: When I put the letter in the mailbox, I felt I had finally finished the process.

examples.sentence: Ella metió la mano en la mochila para sacar su cuaderno de apuntes.
examples.translation: She put her hand into the backpack to take out her notebook.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes meter la tarjeta en el lector para que podamos pagar la cuenta?
examples.translation: Can you insert the card into the reader so we can pay the bill?

definitions: To penetrate someone sexually (vulgar), typically by means of penile penetration.

examples.sentence: La escena fue muy explícita cuando el actor le metió la en la película, causando controversia.
examples.translation: The scene was very explicit when the actor penetrated her in the movie, causing controversy.

examples.sentence: En la novela, describieron cómo el villano le metía la con violencia, lo que generó mucha tensión.
examples.translation: In the novel, they described how the villain violently penetrated her, which generated a lot of tension.

examples.sentence: No es apropiado hablar de cómo le metieron la en público, es un tema muy íntimo y privado.
examples.translation: It's not appropriate to talk about how they penetrated her in public; it's a very intimate and private matter.

definitions: To force or thrust something into a person's body orifices or cavities (for example mouth, throat, anus, or vein), often implying violence or coercion.

examples.sentence: El médico metió la aguja en la vena para administrar la medicina al paciente.
examples.translation: The doctor inserted the needle into the vein to administer medicine to the patient.

examples.sentence: Durante la operación, metieron el tubo en la garganta para ayudar con la respiración.
examples.translation: During the operation, they put the tube into the throat to assist with breathing.

examples.sentence: El equipo de rescate metió la mano en la grieta para sacar al niño atrapado.
examples.translation: The rescue team put their hand into the crack to pull out the trapped child.

examples.sentence: Metí la pajilla en el vaso para poder beber el jugo sin derramarlo.
examples.translation: I put the straw into the glass to be able to drink the juice without spilling it.

definitions: To humiliate, cheat, or treat someone very badly; to 'screw someone over' figuratively.

examples.sentence: Nos metieron la doblada en ese negocio y terminamos perdiendo mucho dinero.
examples.translation: They screwed us over in that deal and we ended up losing a lot of money.

examples.sentence: Si no tienes cuidado, alguien te la va a meter doblada en el trabajo y no lo notarás hasta que sea tarde.
examples.translation: If you’re not careful, someone will screw you over at work and you won’t notice until it’s too late.
examples.matched_span: te la va a meter doblada

examples.sentence: Después de confiar tanto en él, me la metió doblada y me traicionó de la peor manera.
examples.translation: After trusting him so much, he screwed me over and betrayed me in the worst way.

definitions: Literally, to insert or place something that has been folded or doubled.

examples.sentence: Metí la carta doblada dentro del sobre para enviarla por correo esta mañana.
examples.translation: I put the folded letter inside the envelope to send it by mail this morning.

examples.sentence: Ella metió la servilleta doblada en la bolsa antes de salir del restaurante.
examples.translation: She put the folded napkin into the bag before leaving the restaurant.

examples.sentence: Por favor, mete la toalla doblada en el cajón para que quede todo ordenado.
examples.translation: Please put the folded towel in the drawer so everything stays neat.

examples.sentence: Cuando metí la ropa doblada en la maleta, me di cuenta de que aún tenía espacio para más cosas.
examples.translation: When I put the folded clothes into the suitcase, I realized there was still space for more things.

definitions: To deceive, double‑cross, or take advantage of someone in a cunning or underhanded way; to pull a particularly sharp or unfair trick on someone.

examples.sentence: No puedo creer que Juan me metiera la doblada vendiéndome un coche que ya estaba dañado.
examples.translation: I can't believe Juan double-crossed me by selling me a car that was already damaged.

examples.sentence: Si no tienes cuidado, te la van a meter doblada en ese negocio, porque ellos solo buscan aprovecharse.
examples.translation: If you're not careful, they're going to pull a fast one on you in that deal, because they just want to take advantage.
examples.matched_span: te la van a meter doblada

examples.sentence: Cuando me enteré de la verdad, supe que me la habían metido doblada desde el principio.
examples.translation: When I found out the truth, I knew they had deceived me from the start.

definitions: Literally, an act of placing a foot or paw into something.

examples.sentence: Al entrar al lago, sentí una metida de pata cuando pisé un charco de lodo sin darme cuenta.
examples.translation: When entering the lake, I had a foot-in act when I stepped into a mud puddle without realizing.

examples.sentence: La metida de pata del perro en el charco hizo que toda la alfombra se ensuciara.
examples.translation: The dog's paw stepping into the puddle caused the whole carpet to get dirty.

examples.sentence: Durante la caminata, Carlos tuvo una metida de pata al pisar sin querer una colonia de hormigas.
examples.translation: During the hike, Carlos literally put his foot in an ant colony by accident.

examples.sentence: La metida de pata de mi gato en la planta me sorprendió esta mañana, estaba todo desordenado.
examples.translation: My cat's paw in the plant surprised me this morning; everything was messy.

definitions: An embarrassing mistake, blunder, or slip-up; an error that causes awkwardness or problems.

examples.sentence: Hice una metida de pata enorme al enviar el correo con información confidencial a todo el equipo.
examples.translation: I made a huge blunder by sending the email with confidential information to the entire team.

examples.sentence: ¿Recuerdas cuando Marta tuvo esa metida de pata en la reunión y confundió los datos? Fue incómodo para todos.
examples.translation: Do you remember when Marta made that slip-up in the meeting and confused the data? It was awkward for everyone.

examples.sentence: Si quieres evitar una metida de pata, revisa bien tus números antes de presentar el informe.
examples.translation: If you want to avoid a blunder, double-check your numbers before presenting the report.

definitions: Literally, placed among or into meats.

examples.sentence: En la carnicería, la carne estaba metida en carnes frescas para mantener su sabor intacto.
examples.translation: At the butcher shop, the meat was placed among fresh meats to keep its flavor intact.

examples.sentence: El jamón curado estaba cuidadosamente metido en carnes seleccionadas para su maduración.
examples.translation: The cured ham was carefully placed among selected meats for its maturation.

examples.sentence: Durante la receta, el chef metió el pollo en carnes marinadas para potenciar su aroma.
examples.translation: During the recipe, the chef put the chicken among marinated meats to enhance its aroma.

examples.sentence: Los embutidos se metieron en carnes finas antes de ser empaquetados para la venta.
examples.translation: The sausages were placed among fine meats before being packaged for sale.

definitions: Having a full, rounded, or fleshy figure; somewhat plump or corpulent.

examples.sentence: Desde que dejó de hacer ejercicio, se ha metido en carnes y ya no entra en su ropa habitual.
examples.translation: Since he stopped exercising, he's gotten a bit plump and no longer fits into his usual clothes.

examples.sentence: Mi abuela siempre dice que estoy metida en carnes porque como mucho postre.
examples.translation: My grandmother always says I'm a little chubby because I eat too many desserts.

examples.sentence: Aunque antes estaba delgado, ahora está más metido en carnes debido al sedentarismo.
examples.translation: Although he used to be thin, now he's gotten fleshier due to a sedentary lifestyle.

definitions: Literally, to mix churras and merinas (two different types of sheep).

examples.sentence: En la granja, mezclaron churras y merinas para mejorar la calidad del rebaño.
examples.translation: At the farm, they mixed churras and merinas to improve the quality of the flock.

examples.sentence: Los pastores siempre saben cómo mezclar churras y merinas para obtener mejores ovejas.
examples.translation: The shepherds always know how to mix churras and merinas to get better sheep.

examples.sentence: Durante la feria, varios criadores mostraron la mezcla de churras y merinas en sus animales.
examples.translation: During the fair, several breeders showed the mix of churras and merinas in their animals.

examples.sentence: El ganado estaba perfectamente mezclado, con churras y merinas en un mismo corral.
examples.translation: The livestock was perfectly mixed, with churras and merinas in the same pen.

definitions: To confuse, conflate, or mix together two distinct or unrelated things; to fail to distinguish between different categories or cases.

examples.sentence: No mezcles churras y merinas; estamos hablando de dos problemas distintos que no tienen relación.
examples.translation: Don't confuse things; we're talking about two different problems that aren't related.

examples.sentence: Cuando discutes política, a veces la gente mezcla churras y merinas y eso complica el debate.
examples.translation: When discussing politics, sometimes people conflate unrelated issues and that complicates the debate.

examples.sentence: María siempre mezcla churras y merinas cuando habla de su trabajo y su vida personal.
examples.translation: María always mixes unrelated things when she talks about her work and personal life.

definitions: The excrement produced by a bull; bull feces.

examples.sentence: El granjero limpió la mierda de toro del establo antes de alimentar a los animales.
examples.translation: The farmer cleaned the bull's dung from the stable before feeding the animals.

examples.sentence: Durante la caminata por el campo, pisamos sin querer mierda de toro y tuvimos que limpiar las botas.
examples.translation: During the walk in the countryside, we accidentally stepped on bull feces and had to clean the boots.

examples.sentence: La mierda de toro es usada a veces como fertilizante en las tierras agrícolas de la región.
examples.translation: Bull manure is sometimes used as fertilizer in the agricultural lands of the region.

examples.sentence: El olor de la mierda de toro fresca es fuerte y difícil de soportar para quienes no están acostumbrados.
examples.translation: The smell of fresh bull dung is strong and hard to bear for those not used to it.

definitions: An offensive term meaning nonsense or falsehood; used to dismiss statements, claims, or ideas as 'bullshit'.

examples.sentence: Lo que dice ese político es pura mierda de toro, no hay verdad en sus palabras.
examples.translation: What that politician says is pure bullshit, there's no truth in his words.

examples.sentence: No me vengas con mierda de toro, solo quiero que seas sincero conmigo.
examples.translation: Don't give me any nonsense, I just want you to be honest with me.

examples.sentence: Esa excusa es mierda de toro para evitar responsabilidades.
examples.translation: That excuse is bullshit to avoid responsibilities.

definitions: A contemptuous label applied to a person or thing regarded as worthless, contemptible, or despicable.

examples.sentence: Para mí, ese jefe es mierda de toro, nunca valora el trabajo de nadie.
examples.translation: To me, that boss is contemptible, he never values anyone's work.

examples.sentence: No pierdas tiempo con esa mierda de toro que solo trae problemas y nada bueno.
examples.translation: Don't waste time with that worthless crap that only brings problems and nothing good.

examples.sentence: Ese producto es una mierda de toro, no funciona como promete la publicidad.
examples.translation: That product is worthless junk; it doesn't work like the ads claim.

definitions: Feces impaled on a stick; literally, excrement stuck on a pole.

examples.sentence: En la granja, encontraron mierda pinchada en un palo cerca del corral de los caballos.
examples.translation: At the farm, they found excrement stuck on a stick near the horse pen.

examples.sentence: La mierda pinchada en un palo estaba seca y parecía que llevaba días allí sin moverse.
examples.translation: The feces impaled on a stick were dry and seemed to have been there for days without moving.

examples.sentence: Durante la limpieza, hallaron mierda pinchada en un palo detrás del cobertizo.
examples.translation: During the cleaning, they found excrement stuck on a stick behind the shed.

examples.sentence: El olor de la mierda pinchada en un palo era insoportable para los visitantes de la finca.
examples.translation: The smell of the excrement stuck on a stick was unbearable for the farm visitors.

definitions: An insulting expression for a person or thing considered insignificant, worthless, or of no consequence.

examples.sentence: Ese cantante es una mierda pinchada en un palo, no tiene talento ni carisma.
examples.translation: That singer is a nobody, he has neither talent nor charisma.

examples.sentence: No me importa lo que diga ese político, es una mierda pinchada en un palo en el gobierno.
examples.translation: I don't care what that politician says; he's insignificant in the government.

examples.sentence: Para ella, su exnovio siempre fue una mierda pinchada en un palo y no vale la pena recordarlo.
examples.translation: For her, her ex-boyfriend was always worthless and not worth remembering.

definitions: An exclamation of strong contempt, disgust, or dismissal equivalent to 'what a load of crap' or 'what nonsense'.

examples.sentence: ¡Mierda pinchada en un palo! No puedo creer que hayamos perdido otra vez el partido de esta manera.
examples.translation: What a load of crap! I can't believe we lost the game like that again.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuché su explicación, solo pensé: 'mierda pinchada en un palo, no tiene sentido'.
examples.translation: When I heard his explanation, I just thought: 'what nonsense, it makes no sense.'

examples.sentence: No le des importancia a sus comentarios, son pura mierda pinchada en un palo.
examples.translation: Don't pay attention to his comments; they're just pure nonsense.

definitions: Literally, 'a thousand milks'; a phrase without a common literal referent.

examples.sentence: El postre lleva mil leches en su receta, lo que le da un sabor muy cremoso.
examples.translation: The dessert contains a thousand milks in its recipe, which gives it a very creamy flavor.

examples.sentence: En la repostería tradicional, algunos pasteles llevan mezclas de mil leches para la cobertura.
examples.translation: In traditional baking, some cakes have mixtures of milks for the frosting.

examples.sentence: La tarta que probé tenía mil leches, una combinación de leche condensada, evaporada y crema.
examples.translation: The tart I tried had 'a thousand milks', a combination of condensed milk, evaporated milk, and cream.

examples.sentence: Para preparar el flan, usamos la mezcla de mil leches que le da su textura característica.
examples.translation: To prepare the flan, we use the mixture of milks that gives it its characteristic texture.

definitions: A colloquial expletive or intensifier expressing annoyance, surprise, emphasis, or mild anger, comparable to 'damn', 'blast', or 'goodness'.

examples.sentence: ¡Mil leches! Se me olvidó la reunión y ahora tendré que llamar para disculparme.
examples.translation: Damn! I forgot the meeting and now I'll have to call to apologize.

examples.sentence: Si mil leches no te apuras, vamos a perder el tren y llegar tarde al evento.
examples.translation: If you don't hurry, blast it, we'll miss the train and be late for the event.

examples.sentence: Estaba tan enojado que soltó un 'mil leches' antes de salir de la habitación.
examples.translation: He was so angry that he muttered a 'damn' before leaving the room.

definitions: A mine from which gold is extracted; a physical deposit of gold.

examples.sentence: La mina de oro en las montañas ha sido explotada durante más de cien años.
examples.translation: The gold mine in the mountains has been exploited for over a hundred years.

examples.sentence: Encontraron una nueva mina de oro que promete grandes beneficios para la región.
examples.translation: They found a new gold mine that promises great benefits for the region.

examples.sentence: Los mineros trabajan día y noche para extraer oro de la mina de oro abandonada.
examples.translation: The miners work day and night to extract gold from the abandoned gold mine.

examples.sentence: La mina de oro está situada en un terreno difícil de acceder pero muy rentable.
examples.translation: The gold mine is located on difficult-to-access terrain but very profitable.

definitions: A highly lucrative source of wealth, profit, advantage, or valuable resources; a 'goldmine' in a figurative sense.

examples.sentence: Esa tienda online es una mina de oro, siempre encuentro ofertas increíbles y ganancias para mi negocio.
examples.translation: That online store is a goldmine; I always find incredible deals and profits for my business.

examples.sentence: El proyecto de software resultó ser una mina de oro para la empresa, generando muchos clientes nuevos.
examples.translation: The software project turned out to be a goldmine for the company, attracting many new clients.

examples.sentence: Si sabes aprovechar las oportunidades, esta red social puede ser una verdadera mina de oro para ti.
examples.translation: If you know how to seize opportunities, this social network can be a real goldmine for you.

definitions: A literal imperative meaning 'look where you are going' or 'watch where you walk', used to tell someone to pay attention to their path or surroundings.

examples.sentence: Mira por dónde caminas; hay un bache enorme en la acera que podría hacerte tropezar.
examples.translation: Watch where you walk; there's a huge pothole on the sidewalk that could make you trip.

examples.sentence: Antes de cruzar la calle, siempre le digo a mi hijo: 'mira por dónde'.
examples.translation: Before crossing the street, I always tell my son: 'look where you're going.'

examples.sentence: El anciano caminaba despacio y le advertí que mirara por dónde pisaba para no caer.
examples.translation: The elderly man was walking slowly and I warned him to watch where he stepped to avoid falling.

examples.sentence: Mira por dónde pasas, que el suelo está resbaladizo después de la lluvia.
examples.translation: Be careful where you walk, the floor is slippery after the rain.

definitions: An idiomatic expression used to introduce or comment on an unexpected development or mild surprise, roughly equivalent to 'well, would you look at that' or 'as it happens'.

examples.sentence: Mira por dónde, al final conseguimos el contrato que todos daban por perdido.
examples.translation: Well, would you look at that, we finally got the contract everyone thought was lost.

examples.sentence: Pensé que no vendría nadie, pero mira por dónde, la sala se llenó de gente.
examples.translation: I thought no one would come, but as it happens, the room filled up with people.

examples.sentence: Mira por dónde, justo cuando pensaba renunciar, recibí una oferta mejor.
examples.translation: Would you look at that, just when I was thinking of quitting, I got a better offer.

definitions: To look successively at fixed points or markers; literally to look from one landmark to another.

examples.sentence: Para orientarnos en el bosque, miramos de hito en hito para no perdernos.
examples.translation: To navigate in the forest, we looked from landmark to landmark so as not to get lost.

examples.sentence: El topógrafo miraba de hito en hito para medir con precisión el terreno.
examples.translation: The surveyor looked at each marker to measure the land precisely.

examples.sentence: Durante la excursión, los guías miraban de hito en hito para mantener el grupo en el camino correcto.
examples.translation: During the excursion, the guides looked from landmark to landmark to keep the group on the right path.

examples.sentence: Mirando de hito en hito, logramos calcular la distancia exacta entre los puntos clave.
examples.translation: By looking from landmark to landmark, we managed to calculate the exact distance between key points.

definitions: To stare fixedly at someone or something, typically with astonishment, intense attention, or disbelief.

examples.sentence: Cuando entré a la habitación, todos me miraban de hito en hito como si fuera un extraño.
examples.translation: When I entered the room, everyone stared fixedly at me as if I were a stranger.

examples.sentence: El artista miraba de hito en hito a su obra, buscando cada detalle con atención.
examples.translation: The artist stared intently at his work, scrutinizing every detail carefully.

examples.sentence: No soportaba que la miraran de hito en hito en la reunión, se sentía incómoda y expuesta.
examples.translation: She couldn't stand being stared at in the meeting; she felt uncomfortable and exposed.

definitions: To daydream or be absentminded; to stare into space and fail to pay attention to what is happening.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase, Pedro estaba mirando las musarañas y no prestaba atención al profesor.
examples.translation: During class, Pedro was daydreaming and not paying attention to the teacher.

examples.sentence: No le preguntes nada a Ana ahora; está mirando las musarañas y parece distraída.
examples.translation: Don't ask Ana anything now; she's daydreaming and seems distracted.

examples.sentence: Mientras la junta avanzaba, varios empleados miraban las musarañas pensando en otras cosas.
examples.translation: While the meeting went on, several employees were daydreaming, thinking about other things.

examples.sentence: Me di cuenta de que estaba mirando las musarañas cuando no respondí a la pregunta del jefe.
examples.translation: I realized I was daydreaming when I didn't answer the boss's question.

definitions: Literally, to look at shrews (an archaic literal image underlying the idiom).

examples.sentence: En el campo, vimos cómo un niño miraba las musarañas que correteaban entre los arbustos.
examples.translation: In the countryside, we saw a boy watching the shrews scurrying among the bushes.

examples.sentence: La bióloga explicó que mirar las musarañas ayuda a entender el comportamiento de estos pequeños mamíferos.
examples.translation: The biologist explained that observing the shrews helps understand the behavior of these small mammals.

examples.sentence: Durante la excursión, varios participantes se detuvieron a mirar las musarañas que se escondían en la hierba.
examples.translation: During the excursion, several participants stopped to look at the shrews hiding in the grass.

examples.sentence: Mirar las musarañas puede ser una actividad relajante para quienes disfrutan de la naturaleza.
examples.translation: Watching the shrews can be a relaxing activity for those who enjoy nature.

definitions: To see or perceive something out of the corner of the eye without turning the head; a sideways glance.
idiom: mirar por el rabillo del ojo

examples.sentence: Vi pasar a alguien sospechoso y lo miré por el rabillo del ojo sin que se diera cuenta.
examples.translation: I saw someone suspicious pass by and glanced at him out of the corner of my eye without him noticing.
examples.matched_span: miré por el rabillo del ojo

examples.sentence: Mientras hablaban, ella miraba por el rabillo del ojo para asegurarse de que nadie los escuchara.
examples.translation: While they talked, she glanced sideways to make sure no one was listening.
examples.matched_span: miraba por el rabillo del ojo

examples.sentence: Con miedo, miraba por el rabillo del ojo los movimientos extraños en la oscuridad.
examples.translation: Fearfully, he looked out of the corner of his eye at the strange movements in the dark.
examples.matched_span: miraba por el rabillo del ojo

examples.sentence: No es bueno mirar por el rabillo del ojo cuando alguien te está observando, mejor enfrenta la situación.
examples.translation: It's not good to look out of the corner of your eye when someone is watching you; better face the situation.
examples.matched_span: mirar por el rabillo del ojo

definitions: To observe someone or something surreptitiously or with suspicion by glancing from the corner of the eye.
idiom: mirar por el rabillo del ojo

examples.sentence: El jefe siempre me mira por el rabillo del ojo cuando llego tarde, como si desconfiara de mí.
examples.translation: The boss always watches me out of the corner of his eye when I arrive late, as if he distrusts me.
examples.matched_span: mira por el rabillo del ojo

examples.sentence: Ella miraba por el rabillo del ojo a sus compañeros, sospechando que hablaban de ella.
examples.translation: She glanced sideways at her coworkers, suspecting they were talking about her.
examples.matched_span: miraba por el rabillo del ojo

examples.sentence: No puedes trabajar tranquilo si tus colegas te miran por el rabillo del ojo con mala intención.
examples.translation: You can't work peacefully if your colleagues look at you out of the corner of their eye with ill intent.
examples.matched_span: miran por el rabillo del ojo

definitions: To look over someone's shoulder, literally to glance past or above another person's shoulder to see what is behind or beside them.

examples.sentence: Miró por encima del hombro para ver qué estaba escribiendo su compañero en el cuaderno.
examples.translation: He looked over his shoulder to see what his colleague was writing in the notebook.

examples.sentence: Antes de salir, ella miró por encima del hombro para asegurarse de que nadie la seguía.
examples.translation: Before leaving, she glanced over her shoulder to make sure no one was following her.

examples.sentence: El detective miraba por encima del hombro mientras caminaba por la calle oscura.
examples.translation: The detective looked over his shoulder while walking down the dark street.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase, el estudiante miraba por encima del hombro para copiar las respuestas del compañero.
examples.translation: During class, the student looked over his shoulder to copy his classmate's answers.

definitions: To regard someone with disdain or condescension; to behave as if one is superior to another.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que me miren por encima del hombro como si yo no supiera nada.
examples.translation: I don't like being looked down on as if I didn't know anything.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre mira por encima del hombro a quienes considera inferiores, lo cual resulta desagradable.
examples.translation: She always regards those she considers inferior with disdain, which is unpleasant.

examples.sentence: Aunque somos colegas, a veces me mira por encima del hombro y eso afecta nuestra relación.
examples.translation: Although we're colleagues, sometimes she looks down on me and that affects our relationship.

definitions: Literally, to look at one's navel.

examples.sentence: Al hacer yoga, uno debe mirarse el ombligo para mantener la concentración y el equilibrio.
examples.translation: When doing yoga, one should look at their navel to maintain concentration and balance.

examples.sentence: Es curioso cómo los bebés se miran el ombligo mientras exploran su propio cuerpo.
examples.translation: It's curious how babies look at their navel while exploring their own body.

examples.sentence: Durante la meditación, algunos instructores sugieren mirarse el ombligo para conectar con uno mismo.
examples.translation: During meditation, some instructors suggest looking at the navel to connect with oneself.

examples.sentence: En la clase de anatomía, nos pidieron mirarnos el ombligo para entender mejor la estructura corporal.
examples.translation: In anatomy class, we were asked to look at our navel to better understand the body structure.

definitions: To be self-absorbed or excessively focused on oneself; to engage in navel-gazing and ignore broader concerns or the needs of others.

examples.sentence: No podemos seguir mirándonos el ombligo y debemos pensar en las necesidades de los demás.
examples.translation: We can't keep being self-absorbed and must think about the needs of others.

examples.sentence: Él se la pasa mirándose el ombligo, sin darse cuenta de lo que ocurre a su alrededor.
examples.translation: He spends all his time navel-gazing, unaware of what's happening around him.

examples.sentence: Para resolver el problema, es necesario dejar de mirarse el ombligo y colaborar en equipo.
examples.translation: To solve the problem, it's necessary to stop being self-centered and collaborate as a team.

definitions: To urinate involuntarily in bed during sleep (bedwetting).

examples.sentence: Mi sobrino pequeño mojaba la cama hasta que aprendió a controlarse durante la noche.
examples.translation: My little nephew used to wet the bed until he learned to control himself during the night.

examples.sentence: Durante la infancia, muchos niños mojan la cama y eso es algo normal que suele superarse.
examples.translation: During childhood, many children wet the bed, and that is something normal that is usually outgrown.

examples.sentence: El doctor explicó que mojar la cama es común en algunos niños y no debe preocupar demasiado a los padres.
examples.translation: The doctor explained that bedwetting is common in some children and parents shouldn't worry too much.

examples.sentence: Después de una noche muy fría, mi gato mojó la cama y tuve que cambiar las sábanas al instante.
examples.translation: After a very cold night, my cat wet the bed and I had to change the sheets immediately.

definitions: To suffer an embarrassing regression or behave in a childishly shameful way; to experience a conspicuous failure often implying immaturity.

examples.sentence: Después de prometer que no fallaría, Juan realmente mojó la cama al olvidarse de todo en la presentación.
examples.translation: After promising he wouldn't fail, Juan really embarrassed himself by forgetting everything in the presentation.

examples.sentence: No quiero que mojes la cama en la reunión con los inversores; necesitas mostrar madurez y profesionalismo.
examples.translation: I don't want you to embarrass yourself at the meeting with the investors; you need to show maturity and professionalism.

examples.sentence: Cuando Marta intentó defender su punto sin pruebas, todos pensaron que estaba mojando la cama en esa discusión.
examples.translation: When Marta tried to defend her point without evidence, everyone thought she was failing embarrassingly in that argument.

definitions: To wet an ear literally, as with water or liquid.

examples.sentence: El niño se mojó la oreja cuando la lluvia empezó de repente durante el recreo.
examples.translation: The boy got his ear wet when the rain started suddenly during recess.

examples.sentence: No olvides mojar la oreja del perro antes de limpiarle para que se calme un poco.
examples.translation: Don't forget to wet the dog's ear before cleaning it so it calms down a bit.

examples.sentence: Mientras lavaba los platos, accidentalmente me mojé la oreja con agua caliente.
examples.translation: While washing the dishes, I accidentally got my ear wet with hot water.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué te mojaste la oreja? ¿Te cayó agua del grifo cuando lavabas el cabello?
examples.translation: Why did you get your ear wet? Did water fall on you from the faucet when you were washing your hair?

definitions: To get the better of someone, to outdo, defeat, or humiliate someone in a contest, argument, or confrontation.

examples.sentence: En el debate, Clara le mojó la oreja a su oponente con argumentos claros y contundentes.
examples.translation: In the debate, Clara outdid her opponent with clear and strong arguments.

examples.sentence: No creas que ganaste; yo te mojaré la oreja en el próximo partido de tenis.
examples.translation: Don't think you won; I'll get the better of you in the next tennis match.

examples.sentence: Cuando Juan empezó a hablar, rápidamente le mojaron la oreja en la reunión y no pudo defenderse.
examples.translation: When Juan started speaking, they quickly outdid him in the meeting and he couldn't defend himself.

definitions: To grind corn into meal or flour using a mill, grinder, or similar implement.

examples.sentence: Cada mañana, mi abuela se levanta temprano para moler el maíz y preparar las tortillas frescas.
examples.translation: Every morning, my grandmother gets up early to grind the corn and prepare fresh tortillas.

examples.sentence: Cuando molieron el maíz anoche, la harina quedó perfecta para hacer tamales hoy.
examples.translation: When they ground the corn last night, the flour came out perfect to make tamales today.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes moler el maíz mientras yo preparo los ingredientes para la mazamorra?
examples.translation: Can you grind the corn while I prepare the ingredients for the corn pudding?

examples.sentence: No se molió el maíz todavía porque el molino está descompuesto desde la semana pasada.
examples.translation: The corn hasn't been ground yet because the mill has been broken since last week.

definitions: Completely naked or stripped of clothing or possessions.

examples.sentence: Entró en la casa mondo y lirondo, sin llevar nada más que su ropa interior.
examples.translation: He entered the house completely naked, wearing nothing but his underwear.

examples.sentence: Los niños salieron del río mondo y lirondo después de nadar sin ropa.
examples.translation: The children came out of the river completely naked after swimming without clothes.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, el viento arrancó las ramas y dejó el árbol mondo y lirondo.
examples.translation: During the storm, the wind tore off the branches and left the tree completely bare.

examples.sentence: Encontraron el armario mondo y lirondo, sin ningún objeto en su interior.
examples.translation: They found the wardrobe completely empty, with nothing inside.

definitions: Utterly or entirely; with nothing left out or remaining.

examples.sentence: Después de revisar todos los documentos, entregamos el informe mondo y lirondo sin omitir ningún detalle.
examples.translation: After reviewing all the documents, we submitted the report utterly complete without leaving out any detail.

examples.sentence: Te contaré la verdad mondo y lirondo, sin esconder nada de lo que pasó esa noche.
examples.translation: I will tell you the whole truth, utterly and without hiding anything about what happened that night.

examples.sentence: El contrato fue firmado mundo y lirondo, incluyendo todas las cláusulas acordadas por ambas partes.
examples.translation: The contract was signed entirely, including all the clauses agreed upon by both parties.

definitions: Legal tender or circulating currency used for regular transactions.

examples.sentence: En la tienda aceptan solo moneda corriente, no tarjetas de crédito ni cheques.
examples.translation: The store only accepts legal tender, not credit cards or checks.

examples.sentence: El cajero contó toda la moneda corriente antes de cerrar la caja al final del día.
examples.translation: The cashier counted all the circulating currency before closing the register at the end of the day.

examples.sentence: Necesito cambiar estos billetes por moneda corriente para pagar en el mercado local.
examples.translation: I need to exchange these bills for legal tender to pay at the local market.

examples.sentence: No aceptan monedas antiguas, solo moneda corriente que esté en circulación actualmente.
examples.translation: They don't accept old coins, only legal tender currently in circulation.

definitions: A commonplace or customary occurrence; something widespread or generally accepted.

examples.sentence: En esta ciudad, las discusiones políticas acaloradas son moneda corriente durante las elecciones.
examples.translation: In this city, heated political discussions are commonplace during elections.

examples.sentence: El retraso en los proyectos es moneda corriente cuando no hay una buena planificación.
examples.translation: Delays in projects are commonplace when there is poor planning.

examples.sentence: Los rumores sobre cambios en la empresa son moneda corriente entre los empleados últimamente.
examples.translation: Rumors about changes in the company have been commonplace among employees lately.

definitions: To put on a brief, attention-seeking performance or display, literally staging a small act or skit.

examples.sentence: Para la fiesta, los niños montaron el numerito con disfraces y canciones divertidas.
examples.translation: For the party, the children put on a little show with costumes and fun songs.

examples.sentence: Ayer en la escuela, los alumnos montaron un numerito breve para celebrar el fin de curso.
examples.translation: Yesterday at school, the students staged a short performance to celebrate the end of term.

examples.sentence: ¿Viste cómo montaron el numerito en la plaza? Fue una obra muy entretenida y corta.
examples.translation: Did you see how they put on the little show in the square? It was a very entertaining and short play.

examples.sentence: No se montó el numerito hasta que llegaron todos los invitados y se encendieron las luces.
examples.translation: The little show wasn't staged until all the guests arrived and the lights were turned on.

definitions: To create a loud, embarrassing scene or public fuss in order to attract attention or manipulate others.

examples.sentence: Cuando Ana se enteró de la noticia, montó el numerito en medio del restaurante y todos la miraron.
examples.translation: When Ana found out the news, she made a scene in the middle of the restaurant and everyone looked at her.

examples.sentence: No es necesario montar el numerito solo porque no obtuviste lo que querías en la reunión.
examples.translation: It's not necessary to cause a fuss just because you didn't get what you wanted in the meeting.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que discuten, Luis monta el numerito para llamar la atención de todos en la casa.
examples.translation: Every time they argue, Luis makes a scene to get everyone's attention at home.

definitions: To cause a noisy, dramatic commotion or make a big scene, often involving anger, complaints, or public embarrassment.

examples.sentence: Durante la fiesta, mi primo montó el pollo frito con una receta secreta que todos disfrutaron.
examples.translation: During the party, my cousin prepared the fried chicken with a secret recipe that everyone enjoyed.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes ayudarme a montar el pollo para la cena? Necesito que esté listo a las ocho.
examples.translation: Can you help me prepare the chicken for dinner? I need it ready by eight.

examples.sentence: Ellos montaron el pollo en la parrilla mientras nosotros preparábamos las ensaladas.
examples.translation: They set up the chicken on the grill while we prepared the salads.

definitions: To set up or assemble something literally involving a chicken or poultry (literal but rare).

examples.sentence: Cuando vio que no le prestaban atención, montó el pollo y empezó a gritar en público.
examples.translation: When he saw they weren't paying attention, he made a big scene and started shouting in public.

examples.sentence: No montes el pollo por un error tan pequeño; mejor hablamos con calma y solucionamos el problema.
examples.translation: Don't make a big fuss over such a small mistake; let's talk calmly and solve the problem.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, Marta montó el pollo cuando le cuestionaron su proyecto frente a todos.
examples.translation: In the meeting, Marta caused a big scene when her project was questioned in front of everyone.

definitions: To take up guard duty or stand watch, remaining alert to protect a place, person, or group.

examples.sentence: Durante la noche, los soldados montaron la guardia para proteger el campamento de posibles ataques.
examples.translation: During the night, the soldiers stood watch to protect the camp from possible attacks.

examples.sentence: Yo monto la guardia en la entrada principal mientras tú revisas los documentos adentro.
examples.translation: I take guard duty at the main entrance while you check the documents inside.

examples.sentence: No se montó la guardia porque el grupo creyó que el área era segura y sin riesgos.
examples.translation: The guard wasn't set because the group believed the area was safe and risk-free.

examples.sentence: ¿Quién montó la guardia durante el turno de la madrugada en el hospital ayer?
examples.translation: Who stood watch during the early morning shift at the hospital yesterday?

definitions: To establish or organize a watch or security detail for a particular purpose or event (figurative extension).

examples.sentence: Para el evento, montaron la guardia con seguridad privada para controlar el acceso de los invitados.
examples.translation: For the event, they organized a security detail with private guards to control guest access.

examples.sentence: Nos montaron la guardia en la entrada del edificio para evitar que entraran personas no autorizadas.
examples.translation: They set up a watch at the building's entrance to prevent unauthorized people from entering.

examples.sentence: ¿Montaron la guardia en la zona después del incidente o todavía no han tomado medidas?
examples.translation: Did they establish a watch in the area after the incident or have they not taken measures yet?

definitions: To create or provoke a big disturbance, uproar, or chaotic commotion.

examples.sentence: Los estudiantes montaron un jaleo cuando suspendieron las clases sin previo aviso.
examples.translation: The students caused a big uproar when classes were cancelled without prior notice.

examples.sentence: En la manifestación, los manifestantes montaron un jaleo que llamó la atención de los medios.
examples.translation: In the protest, the demonstrators created a disturbance that attracted media attention.

examples.sentence: No permitas que se monte un jaleo en la reunión; necesitamos mantener el orden para avanzar.
examples.translation: Don't allow a commotion to arise in the meeting; we need to keep order to move forward.

definitions: To assemble or set up a situation that results in confusion or disorder (more literal compositional sense).

examples.sentence: Para la fiesta sorpresa, montaron un jaleo con decoraciones y música que confundieron a todos.
examples.translation: For the surprise party, they set up a chaotic situation with decorations and music that confused everyone.

examples.sentence: Montaron un jaleo en la cocina mientras intentaban preparar varios platillos al mismo tiempo.
examples.translation: They created confusion in the kitchen while trying to prepare several dishes at the same time.

examples.sentence: No se debe montar un jaleo cuando hay visitas importantes; mejor organizar todo con calma.
examples.translation: One should not cause disorder when there are important visitors; it's better to organize everything calmly.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué montaron un jaleo con tantos cables y aparatos en la sala de conferencias?
examples.translation: Why did they set up a mess with so many cables and devices in the conference room?

definitions: To stage or perform a short spectacle or act, literally putting on a little show.

examples.sentence: Para el festival, los actores montaron un numerito que duró apenas diez minutos y encantó al público.
examples.translation: For the festival, the actors staged a short act that lasted only ten minutes and delighted the audience.

examples.sentence: Montaron un numerito improvisado en la plaza para recaudar fondos para la escuela local.
examples.translation: They put on an improvised little show in the square to raise funds for the local school.

examples.sentence: Antes de que llegaran los invitados, ya habían montado el numerito de bienvenida en el escenario.
examples.translation: Before the guests arrived, they had already set up the little welcoming act on the stage.

examples.sentence: No se había montado el numerito cuando el director pidió que comenzara la función oficialmente.
examples.translation: The little show hadn't been staged yet when the director asked for the performance to officially start.

definitions: To make a scene or cause an emotional, attention-seeking fuss, typically perceived as excessive or embarrassing.

examples.sentence: No necesito que montes un numerito solo porque no te gusta la decisión tomada.
examples.translation: I don't need you to make a scene just because you don't like the decision made.

examples.sentence: Durante la fiesta, Carlos montó un numerito cuando le preguntaron sobre su ex pareja.
examples.translation: During the party, Carlos made a fuss when he was asked about his ex-partner.

examples.sentence: Si sigues montando un numerito en cada reunión, nadie te tomará en serio.
examples.translation: If you keep making a scene at every meeting, no one will take you seriously.

definitions: To organize, produce, or put on a public entertainment event or performance.

examples.sentence: El equipo de producción montó un show impresionante para la inauguración del teatro.
examples.translation: The production team organized an impressive show for the theater's opening.

examples.sentence: Vamos a montar un show para recaudar fondos para la organización benéfica el próximo mes.
examples.translation: We are going to put on a show to raise funds for the charity next month.

examples.sentence: ¿Ya montaron el show para la feria o falta preparar algunos detalles técnicos?
examples.translation: Have they already organized the show for the fair or are some technical details still missing?

examples.sentence: No se ha montado el show todavía porque están esperando que lleguen los artistas invitados.
examples.translation: The show hasn't been set up yet because they are waiting for the guest artists to arrive.

definitions: To create an ostentatious or exaggerated display; to put on a spectacle in order to attract attention or provoke a reaction.

examples.sentence: Para llamar la atención, siempre monta un show exagerado cuando no consigue lo que quiere.
examples.translation: To get attention, he always puts on an exaggerated display when he doesn't get what he wants.

examples.sentence: No necesito que montes un show en público; podemos resolver el problema en privado con calma.
examples.translation: I don't need you to put on a spectacle in public; we can solve the problem calmly in private.

examples.sentence: La cantante montó un show increíble durante el concierto que dejó a todos maravillados.
examples.translation: The singer put on an incredible spectacle during the concert that left everyone amazed.

definitions: To establish, set up, or finance a theatre institution or venue, or to organize a theatrical production.

examples.sentence: La compañía decidió montar un teatro en el centro de la ciudad para promover las artes escénicas.
examples.translation: The company decided to establish a theater downtown to promote the performing arts.

examples.sentence: Estamos montando un teatro para la próxima temporada y ya seleccionamos el elenco principal.
examples.translation: We are setting up a theater for the upcoming season and have already selected the main cast.

examples.sentence: ¿Sabías que montaron un teatro nuevo en el barrio y están buscando voluntarios para las obras?
examples.translation: Did you know they set up a new theater in the neighborhood and are looking for volunteers for the plays?

examples.sentence: No se ha montado el teatro todavía porque están esperando la aprobación del ayuntamiento.
examples.translation: The theater hasn't been set up yet because they are waiting for the city council's approval.

definitions: To stage a dramatic display; to behave in an overly theatrical or exaggerated manner in public.

examples.sentence: Cuando Ana no obtuvo lo que quería, montó un teatro en medio de la tienda para llamar la atención.
examples.translation: When Ana didn't get what she wanted, she put on a dramatic display in the middle of the store to get attention.

examples.sentence: No tiene sentido montar un teatro por algo tan trivial; mejor habla con calma para resolverlo.
examples.translation: There's no point in making a big fuss over something so trivial; it's better to talk calmly to solve it.

examples.sentence: Pedro siempre monta un teatro cada vez que no está de acuerdo con la decisión del grupo.
examples.translation: Pedro always behaves theatrically every time he disagrees with the group's decision.

definitions: To stage or set up a scene for a play, film, or other dramatic presentation.

examples.sentence: El director pidió montar una escena intensa para la próxima función de la obra de teatro.
examples.translation: The director asked to stage an intense scene for the next performance of the play.

examples.sentence: Montaron una escena en el set de grabación que duró varias horas para conseguir la toma perfecta.
examples.translation: They set up a scene on the film set that lasted several hours to get the perfect shot.

examples.sentence: ¿Quién se encargó de montar la escena del crimen para la película de misterio que estamos filmando?
examples.translation: Who was in charge of setting up the crime scene for the mystery movie we're filming?

examples.sentence: No se ha montado la escena aún porque faltan algunos elementos del decorado por instalar.
examples.translation: The scene hasn't been set up yet because some set pieces still need to be installed.

definitions: To make a scene; to cause a public disturbance by reacting in an exaggerated, dramatic, or confrontational way.

examples.sentence: Cuando Laura descubrió la traición, montó una escena en el restaurante que todos recordarán.
examples.translation: When Laura discovered the betrayal, she made a scene in the restaurant that everyone will remember.

examples.sentence: No montes una escena por un malentendido; mejor hablamos tranquilamente para aclararlo.
examples.translation: Don't make a scene over a misunderstanding; let's talk calmly to clear it up.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que discuten, Pedro monta una escena que termina en gritos y reproches en público.
examples.translation: Every time they argue, Pedro makes a scene that ends in shouting and accusations in public.

definitions: To invent or fabricate stories or scenarios, often to explain, justify, or imagine events that did not occur.

examples.sentence: Para el proyecto, los estudiantes montaron historias imaginativas que ilustraban conceptos científicos.
examples.translation: For the project, the students invented imaginative stories that illustrated scientific concepts.

examples.sentence: María se pasó la tarde montando historias sobre sus vacaciones en la playa para impresionar a sus amigos.
examples.translation: María spent the afternoon fabricating stories about her beach vacation to impress her friends.

examples.sentence: No se montaron historias falsas en el informe; todo está basado en hechos comprobables.
examples.translation: No fabricated stories were included in the report; everything is based on verifiable facts.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué montas historias cuando la verdad es mucho más simple y creíble?
examples.translation: Why do you make up stories when the truth is much simpler and more believable?

definitions: To imagine, devise, or compose narratives or tales, whether for entertainment or personal reflection.

examples.sentence: A veces se monta historias en la mente para justificar decisiones difíciles que hemos tomado.
examples.translation: Sometimes we imagine stories in our minds to justify difficult decisions we've made.

examples.sentence: No te montes historias innecesarias; mejor enfrenta la realidad tal como es sin exagerar.
examples.translation: Don't invent unnecessary stories; better face reality as it is without exaggerating.

examples.sentence: Para entretener a los niños, el abuelo se montó historias fantásticas sobre dragones y héroes.
examples.translation: To entertain the children, the grandfather made up fantastic stories about dragons and heroes.

definitions: To stage or reenact events related to the historical Battle of Saint-Quentin.

examples.sentence: Los estudiantes montaron la de San Quintín en la clase de historia para entender mejor la batalla.
examples.translation: The students reenacted the Battle of Saint-Quentin in history class to better understand the battle.

examples.sentence: Para la exposición, montaron la de San Quintín con vestuarios y maquetas que mostraban la época.
examples.translation: For the exhibition, they staged the Battle of Saint-Quentin with costumes and models showing the era.

examples.sentence: No se montó la de San Quintín este año porque faltaron los recursos para la representación teatral.
examples.translation: The reenactment of the Battle of Saint-Quentin wasn't staged this year due to lack of resources.

examples.sentence: ¿Cuándo piensan montar la de San Quintín en el museo para atraer más visitantes?
examples.translation: When do they plan to stage the Battle of Saint-Quentin at the museum to attract more visitors?

definitions: To provoke or cause a major commotion, uproar, or chaotic incident; to make a huge fuss or scandal.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, se montó la de San Quintín cuando empezaron a discutir todos al mismo tiempo.
examples.translation: During the meeting, a huge commotion broke out when everyone started arguing at once.
examples.matched_span: se montó la de San Quintín

examples.sentence: Si sigues montando la de San Quintín por cada error, no lograrás avanzar en tu trabajo.
examples.translation: If you keep making a huge fuss over every mistake, you won't make progress at work.

examples.sentence: Cuando anunciaron los cambios inesperados, se montó la de San Quintín entre los empleados preocupados.
examples.translation: When they announced the unexpected changes, a big uproar broke out among the worried employees.
examples.matched_span: se montó la de San Quintín

definitions: Literal: to mount it; to put or fix something in place by mounting.

examples.sentence: El carpintero montó la repisa en la pared con mucho cuidado para que quedara bien fija.
examples.translation: The carpenter mounted the shelf on the wall very carefully so it would be well fixed.

examples.sentence: ¿Ya montaste el cuadro en el pasillo o necesitas ayuda con los tornillos?
examples.translation: Have you mounted the picture in the hallway yet or do you need help with the screws?

examples.sentence: No se montó la antena en el techo porque faltaban las herramientas adecuadas para fijarla.
examples.translation: The antenna wasn't mounted on the roof because the proper tools were missing to fix it.

examples.sentence: Montamos el dispositivo en la mesa para probar su funcionamiento antes de enviarlo.
examples.translation: We mounted the device on the table to test its operation before sending it.

definitions: Figurative: to arrange or manage one’s affairs resourcefully in order to prosper or get by; to set things up for one’s own advantage.

examples.sentence: A pesar de las dificultades, Marta se lo montó para conseguir un buen empleo en la ciudad.
examples.translation: Despite the difficulties, Marta managed to arrange things to get a good job in the city.

examples.sentence: Si quieres triunfar, tienes que montártelo bien y aprovechar todas las oportunidades que te den.
examples.translation: If you want to succeed, you have to manage things resourcefully and take advantage of every opportunity.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes por el dinero; él se lo montó para vivir cómodo sin depender de nadie.
examples.translation: Don't worry about money; he arranged things to live comfortably without depending on anyone.

definitions: Figurative: to have sexual relations with someone; to hook up or sleep with (often coarse or pejorative).

examples.sentence: Anoche en la fiesta, Pedro se lo montó con la chica nueva del trabajo y nadie se lo esperaba.
examples.translation: Last night at the party, Pedro hooked up with the new girl from work and nobody expected it.

examples.sentence: No creo que Marta quiera montárselo con alguien tan pronto después de su ruptura.
examples.translation: I don't think Marta wants to sleep with someone so soon after her breakup.

examples.sentence: Si te montas algo con ella, asegúrate de que sea consensuado y respetuoso.
examples.translation: If you hook up with her, make sure it is consensual and respectful.

definitions: Figurative: to set up a scheme or enterprise for personal profit; to make a killing by organizing or exploiting an opportunity.

examples.sentence: Juan se lo montó muy bien con esa empresa de importación; ahora gana mucho dinero.
examples.translation: Juan set up a very good business with that import company; now he makes a lot of money.

examples.sentence: Si montarías algo así, podrías ganar mucho más que trabajando para otros.
examples.translation: If you set up something like that, you could make much more than working for others.

examples.sentence: Ellos se lo montaron para vender entradas falsas y terminaron arrestados.
examples.translation: They schemed to sell fake tickets and ended up arrested.

definitions: Literal: to bite the dust; to fall dead or die.

examples.sentence: Al disparar al blanco, la bala mordió el polvo y se detuvo justo al lado.
examples.translation: When shooting at the target, the bullet bit the dust and stopped right next to it.

examples.sentence: Los soldados cayeron al suelo y varios mordieron el polvo durante la batalla.
examples.translation: The soldiers fell to the ground and several bit the dust during the battle.

examples.sentence: Si la bala no muerde el polvo, puede causar daños graves.
examples.translation: If the bullet doesn’t bite the dust, it can cause serious harm.

examples.sentence: El cazador vio cómo la bala mordió el polvo después de rebotar en la roca.
examples.translation: The hunter saw how the bullet bit the dust after bouncing off the rock.

definitions: Figurative: to be defeated, humbled, or proven wrong; to suffer a decisive loss or disgrace.

examples.sentence: En el partido de ayer, nuestro equipo mordió el polvo contra un rival inesperado.
examples.translation: In yesterday’s game, our team bit the dust against an unexpected opponent.

examples.sentence: Nunca pensé que el proyecto del jefe iba a morder el polvo tan rápido.
examples.translation: I never thought the boss’s project would bite the dust so quickly.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que esa empresa va a morder el polvo después de la crisis financiera?
examples.translation: Do you think that company will bite the dust after the financial crisis?

definitions: Literal: to bite the bullet; to clamp one’s teeth on a bullet (literal physical action).

examples.sentence: Durante la película de guerra, el soldado mordió la bala para soportar el dolor.
examples.translation: During the war movie, the soldier bit the bullet to endure the pain.

examples.sentence: Yo he tenido que morder la bala varias veces en el dentista este mes.
examples.translation: I have had to bite the bullet several times at the dentist this month.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué no muerdes la bala y aceptas la inyección sin miedo?
examples.translation: Why don’t you bite the bullet and accept the injection without fear?

examples.sentence: Ella mordió la bala mientras le cosían la herida en el hospital.
examples.translation: She bit the bullet while they stitched her wound at the hospital.

definitions: Figurative: to accept and endure an unpleasant necessity or difficult decision; to summon the resolve to do something unpleasant but required.

examples.sentence: Tendremos que morder la bala y despedir a algunos empleados para salvar la empresa.
examples.translation: We will have to bite the bullet and lay off some employees to save the company.

examples.sentence: Si quieres mejorar, tendrás que morder la bala y aceptar las críticas constructivas.
examples.translation: If you want to improve, you will have to bite the bullet and accept constructive criticism.

examples.sentence: No me gusta, pero voy a morder la bala y pagar la multa por aparcar mal.
examples.translation: I don’t like it, but I’m going to bite the bullet and pay the fine for parking incorrectly.

definitions: Literal: to bite the hand that feeds one; to physically bite someone who is giving food or help.
idiom: morder la mano que se da de comer

examples.sentence: El perro mordió la mano que se da de comer cuando intentó darle la comida.
examples.translation: The dog bit the hand that feeds it when I tried to give it food.
examples.matched_span: mordió la mano que se da de comer

examples.sentence: Mientras le acariciaba, el gato mordió la mano que se da de comer sin aviso.
examples.translation: While I was petting it, the cat bit the hand that feeds it without warning.
examples.matched_span: mordió la mano que se da de comer

examples.sentence: No entiendo por qué el loro mordió la mano que se da de comer esta mañana.
examples.translation: I don’t understand why the parrot bit the hand that feeds it this morning.
examples.matched_span: mordió la mano que se da de comer

examples.sentence: El bebé mordió la mano que se da de comer cuando le ofrecí la comida por primera vez.
examples.translation: The baby bit the hand that feeds it when I offered food for the first time.
examples.matched_span: mordió la mano que se da de comer

definitions: Figurative: to act ungratefully or betray someone who provides help, support, or sustenance.
idiom: morder la mano que se da de comer

examples.sentence: No deberías morder la mano que se da de comer; tu jefe siempre ha sido generoso contigo.
examples.translation: You shouldn’t bite the hand that feeds you; your boss has always been generous with you.
examples.matched_span: morder la mano que se da de comer

examples.sentence: Ellos mordieron la mano que se da de comer al criticar públicamente al benefactor.
examples.translation: They bit the hand that feeds them by publicly criticizing their benefactor.
examples.matched_span: mordieron la mano que se da de comer

examples.sentence: Si montas un negocio, no muerdas la mano que se da de comer y agradece la ayuda recibida.
examples.translation: If you start a business, don’t bite the hand that feeds you and be thankful for the help you receive.
examples.matched_span: muerdas la mano que se da de comer

definitions: Literal: to cease living; to die.

examples.sentence: Mi abuelo murió hace diez años y siempre lo recuerdo con cariño.
examples.translation: My grandfather died ten years ago and I always remember him fondly.

examples.sentence: Cuando el árbol murió, el jardín perdió mucho de su sombra y frescura.
examples.translation: When the tree died, the garden lost much of its shade and coolness.

examples.sentence: No quiero que esta tradición muera con nuestra generación.
examples.translation: I don’t want this tradition to die with our generation.

examples.sentence: Si no cuidas esa planta, morirá en pocos días debido a la falta de agua.
examples.translation: If you don’t take care of that plant, it will die in a few days due to lack of water.

definitions: Figurative: to stop functioning, to come to an end, or to fail (applied to machines, projects, feelings, or situations).

examples.sentence: El proyecto murió cuando se quedaron sin fondos para continuar.
examples.translation: The project died when they ran out of funds to continue.

examples.sentence: No quiero que esta amistad muera por un malentendido tonto.
examples.translation: I don’t want this friendship to die because of a silly misunderstanding.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que el interés por ese deporte morirá pronto entre los jóvenes?
examples.translation: Do you think the interest in that sport will die soon among the youth?

definitions: To die in the manner of a dog; to succumb to death as an animal would, often implying physical neglect or brutality.

examples.sentence: El animal murió como un perro, abandonado bajo la lluvia sin nadie que lo ayudara.
examples.translation: The animal died like a dog, abandoned in the rain with no one to help it.

examples.sentence: Durante la guerra, muchos murieron como perros sin recibir atención médica.
examples.translation: During the war, many died like dogs without receiving medical attention.

examples.sentence: El gato callejero murió como un perro en la esquina, sin comida ni cariño.
examples.translation: The stray cat died like a dog on the corner, with no food or affection.

examples.sentence: No quiero que mi viejo amigo muera como un perro en el olvido y la soledad.
examples.translation: I don’t want my old friend to die like a dog in oblivion and loneliness.

definitions: To die in disgrace, abandonment, or misery; to suffer an undignified, humiliating, or neglected death; also used emphatically to express a refusal to accept such a fate (e.g., 'I would rather die like a dog than...').

examples.sentence: Prefiero morir como un perro antes que perder mi dignidad y honor.
examples.translation: I would rather die like a dog than lose my dignity and honor.

examples.sentence: Después de la traición, sintió que había muerto como un perro, sin respeto ni apoyo.
examples.translation: After the betrayal, he felt he had died like a dog, without respect or support.

examples.sentence: No quiero que este negocio muera como un perro, sin clientes ni futuro.
examples.translation: I don’t want this business to die like a dog, without customers or a future.

definitions: To die from lack of food; to perish from starvation.

examples.sentence: Durante la hambruna, muchas personas murieron de hambre debido a la falta de recursos.
examples.translation: During the famine, many people died of hunger due to lack of resources.

examples.sentence: Si no consiguen comida pronto, los animales podrían morir de hambre en el refugio.
examples.translation: If they don’t get food soon, the animals could die of hunger in the shelter.

examples.sentence: El explorador casi muere de hambre en el desierto antes de ser rescatado.
examples.translation: The explorer almost died of hunger in the desert before being rescued.

examples.sentence: Muchos niños mueren de hambre en zonas de conflicto por la escasez de alimentos.
examples.translation: Many children die of hunger in conflict zones due to food scarcity.

definitions: To be extremely hungry; an emphatic way to say one is very hungry.

examples.sentence: Después de tanto ejercicio, estoy muriéndome de hambre y necesito comer algo ya.
examples.translation: After so much exercise, I’m starving and need to eat something now.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres un bocadillo? Pareces que vas a morir de hambre.
examples.translation: Do you want a snack? You look like you’re going to starve.

examples.sentence: Si sigues sin comer, vas a morir de hambre antes de que llegue la cena.
examples.translation: If you keep not eating, you’re going to starve before dinner arrives.

definitions: To suffer severe poverty or want; to be in a situation of material deprivation where one risks starvation.

examples.sentence: La familia vivía en condiciones tan precarias que parecía que iban a morir de hambre.
examples.translation: The family lived in such precarious conditions that it seemed they were going to starve.

examples.sentence: Muchos campesinos mueren de hambre en esas regiones por la falta de ayuda estatal.
examples.translation: Many peasants starve in those regions due to lack of government aid.

examples.sentence: No podemos permitir que nadie muera de hambre mientras haya comida disponible.
examples.translation: We can’t allow anyone to die of hunger while there is food available.

definitions: To die from laughing; a literal formulation describing death caused by excessive laughter (rare, usually hyperbolic).

examples.sentence: Aunque es difícil, hay casos registrados de personas que murieron de risa en situaciones extremas.
examples.translation: Although rare, there are recorded cases of people who died from laughter in extreme situations.

examples.sentence: El comediante contó un chiste tan gracioso que casi muero de risa en el escenario.
examples.translation: The comedian told such a funny joke that I almost died from laughter on stage.

examples.sentence: Dicen que murió de risa debido a un ataque cardíaco provocado por la alegría extrema.
examples.translation: They say he died of laughter due to a heart attack caused by extreme joy.

examples.sentence: No es común, pero algunas personas han muerto de risa por episodios incontrolables.
examples.translation: It’s not common, but some people have died from laughter due to uncontrollable episodes.

definitions: To laugh uncontrollably or to be caused to laugh intensely; used to indicate that something is extremely funny.
