examples.sentence: Cada vez que veo esa película, muero de risa porque es muy divertida.
examples.translation: Every time I watch that movie, I laugh uncontrollably because it’s very funny.

examples.sentence: ¡Me muero de risa con las bromas que hacen en esa serie de televisión!
examples.translation: I laugh so hard at the jokes they make in that TV series!

examples.sentence: No puedo parar, me muero de risa con los videos que compartiste ayer.
examples.translation: I can’t stop, I’m dying of laughter at the videos you shared yesterday.

definitions: To experience overwhelming laughter; an emphatic, reflexive form used to indicate that something is hilariously funny or that one is nearly overcome by laughter.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, me morí de risa cuando Juan contó su anécdota graciosa.
examples.translation: During the meeting, I was overwhelmed with laughter when Juan told his funny story.

examples.sentence: Nos morimos de risa viendo las ocurrencias de los niños en el parque.
examples.translation: We laughed uncontrollably watching the kids’ antics in the park.

examples.sentence: Ella se murió de risa al ver el disfraz que llevaba su hermano para la fiesta.
examples.translation: She was nearly overcome with laughter when she saw the costume her brother wore for the party.

definitions: To die as a result of laughter; a literal but uncommon reading, generally understood as hyperbole rather than a real occurrence.

examples.sentence: Dicen que se murió de risa, aunque probablemente sea solo una exageración.
examples.translation: They say he died of laughter, although it’s probably just an exaggeration.

examples.sentence: No es común que alguien se muera de risa, pero la expresión se usa para enfatizar.
examples.translation: It’s not common for someone to die of laughter, but the expression is used for emphasis.

examples.sentence: Algunos autores mencionan casos ficticios donde personajes mueren de risa en sus relatos.
examples.translation: Some authors mention fictional cases where characters die of laughter in their stories.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuché la noticia, pensé que me iba a morir de risa, aunque fue solo una forma de hablar.
examples.translation: When I heard the news, I thought I was going to die laughing, although it was just a way of speaking.

definitions: A dead fly; the literal animal sense.

examples.sentence: Encontré una mosca muerta sobre la mesa de la cocina esta mañana.
examples.translation: I found a dead fly on the kitchen table this morning.

examples.sentence: Después de limpiar, había varias moscas muertas en el rincón del salón.
examples.translation: After cleaning, there were several dead flies in the corner of the living room.

examples.sentence: El científico estudió la mosca muerta para analizar posibles causas de su muerte.
examples.translation: The scientist studied the dead fly to analyze possible causes of its death.

examples.sentence: Nunca había visto tantas moscas muertas juntas en una sola habitación.
examples.translation: I had never seen so many dead flies together in a single room.

definitions: A person who feigns innocence, meekness, or harmlessness while actually being cunning, deceitful, or morally questionable.

examples.sentence: No te fíes de Luis, parece una mosca muerta pero en realidad es muy astuto.
examples.translation: Don’t trust Luis; he seems innocent but is actually very cunning.

examples.sentence: Ese político es una mosca muerta; siempre actúa como si no supiera nada, pero mueve todo tras bambalinas.
examples.translation: That politician is a dead fly; he always acts clueless but moves everything behind the scenes.

examples.sentence: No te dejes engañar por su actitud de mosca muerta, sabe cómo sacar provecho de cualquier situación.
examples.translation: Don’t be fooled by his dead-fly attitude; he knows how to take advantage of any situation.

definitions: A person who is perceived as dull, timid, or lifeless; someone lacking energy or interest.

examples.sentence: No puedo contar con ella para animar la fiesta, es una mosca muerta que no participa en nada.
examples.translation: I can’t count on her to liven up the party; she’s a dull person who doesn’t participate in anything.

examples.sentence: En la clase, Juan es una mosca muerta que nunca dice nada ni muestra interés.
examples.translation: In class, Juan is a lifeless person who never says anything or shows interest.

examples.sentence: Aunque parecía una mosca muerta al principio, luego mostró mucha energía y entusiasmo.
examples.translation: Although she seemed dull at first, she later showed a lot of energy and enthusiasm.

definitions: To move heaven and earth in a literal sense; to imagine or describe the sky and the ground being set in motion.

examples.sentence: En el dibujo infantil, se ve cómo mover cielo y tierra para alcanzar las estrellas.
examples.translation: In the child’s drawing, you can see how heaven and earth are moved to reach the stars.

examples.sentence: Cuando el terremoto comenzó, parecía que mover cielo y tierra estaba ocurriendo en la ciudad.
examples.translation: When the earthquake started, it seemed like heaven and earth were moving in the city.

examples.sentence: El artista creó una obra que representa mover cielo y tierra con colores vivos y formas dinámicas.
examples.translation: The artist created a work that represents moving heaven and earth with vivid colors and dynamic shapes.

examples.sentence: En la leyenda, el héroe logró mover cielo y tierra para salvar a su pueblo de la destrucción.
examples.translation: In the legend, the hero managed to move heaven and earth to save his people from destruction.

definitions: To do everything possible; to make every effort or take every measure to achieve a goal or solve a problem.

examples.sentence: Para conseguir ese contrato, hemos movido cielo y tierra durante meses.
examples.translation: To get that contract, we have done everything possible for months.

examples.sentence: Si quieres aprobar el examen, tendrás que mover cielo y tierra para estudiar bien.
examples.translation: If you want to pass the exam, you’ll have to do everything possible to study well.

examples.sentence: El equipo movió cielo y tierra para encontrar una solución antes de la fecha límite.
examples.translation: The team did everything possible to find a solution before the deadline.

definitions: To move one's skeleton; to move one's body or limbs.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase de anatomía, nos enseñaron cómo mover el esqueleto para entender la postura.
examples.translation: During anatomy class, they taught us how to move the skeleton to understand posture.

examples.sentence: El robot puede mover el esqueleto con precisión gracias a sus motores hidráulicos.
examples.translation: The robot can move its skeleton precisely thanks to its hydraulic motors.

examples.sentence: Para mejorar la movilidad, el fisioterapeuta nos pidió mover el esqueleto lentamente.
examples.translation: To improve mobility, the physiotherapist asked us to move the skeleton slowly.

examples.sentence: El médico explicó que el movimiento del esqueleto es fundamental para el equilibrio del cuerpo.
examples.translation: The doctor explained that moving the skeleton is fundamental for body balance.

definitions: To dance or to dance energetically.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, todos movieron el esqueleto al ritmo de la música hasta el amanecer.
examples.translation: At the party, everyone danced energetically to the music until dawn.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres salir a bailar? Vamos a mover el esqueleto un rato en la discoteca.
examples.translation: Do you want to go dancing? Let’s move our bodies for a while at the club.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuchó su canción favorita, no pudo evitar mover el esqueleto alegremente.
examples.translation: When he heard his favorite song, he couldn’t help but dance energetically.

definitions: To move game pieces or tokens on a board or in a game.

examples.sentence: En el ajedrez, mover fichas con cuidado es clave para ganar la partida.
examples.translation: In chess, moving pieces carefully is key to winning the game.

examples.sentence: Durante la partida de damas, Ana movió las fichas rápidamente para ganar tiempo.
examples.translation: During the checkers game, Ana moved the pieces quickly to gain time.

examples.sentence: El niño aprendió a mover fichas en el tablero para jugar con sus amigos.
examples.translation: The child learned to move pieces on the board to play with his friends.

examples.sentence: Al mover fichas en el juego de mesa, debemos pensar en la estrategia para no perder.
examples.translation: When moving pieces in the board game, we must think about the strategy not to lose.

definitions: To make strategic, tactical, or behind-the-scenes moves designed to influence events or outcomes, especially in politics, business, or negotiations.

examples.sentence: En la empresa, el director movió fichas para conseguir una alianza estratégica importante.
examples.translation: In the company, the director made strategic moves to secure an important alliance.

examples.sentence: Los políticos mueven fichas tras bambalinas para influir en las decisiones del gobierno.
examples.translation: Politicians make behind-the-scenes moves to influence government decisions.

examples.sentence: Para ganar las elecciones, el candidato movió fichas y logró el apoyo de varios sectores clave.
examples.translation: To win the elections, the candidate made strategic moves and gained support from several key sectors.

definitions: A large quantity of excrement; literal feces.

examples.sentence: El granjero encontró mucha mierda en el establo después de limpiar el corral.
examples.translation: The farmer found a lot of manure in the barn after cleaning the pen.

examples.sentence: Durante la caminata, pisé mucha mierda y tuve que cambiarme los zapatos.
examples.translation: During the walk, I stepped on a lot of poop and had to change my shoes.

examples.sentence: El olor de mucha mierda en el basurero era insoportable para los vecinos.
examples.translation: The smell of a lot of manure in the garbage dump was unbearable for the neighbors.

examples.sentence: Los niños jugaron cerca del corral y se ensuciaron con mucha mierda de vaca.
examples.translation: The children played near the barn and got dirty with a lot of cow manure.

definitions: A great deal of nonsense, rubbish, or trouble; used to describe worthless matters or to accuse someone of speaking or doing rubbish.

examples.sentence: No me gusta escuchar tanta mucha mierda cuando trato de entender el problema.
examples.translation: I don’t like hearing so much nonsense when I try to understand the problem.

examples.sentence: Ese político habla mucha mierda para distraer a la gente de los verdaderos asuntos.
examples.translation: That politician talks a lot of rubbish to distract people from the real issues.

examples.sentence: No pierdas el tiempo con mucha mierda; mejor concéntrate en lo que realmente importa.
examples.translation: Don’t waste time with so much nonsense; better focus on what really matters.

definitions: An expression used to wish someone good luck before a performance, equivalent to 'break a leg'.

examples.sentence: Antes de salir al escenario, mi amigo me dijo '¡mucha mierda!' para desearme suerte en la obra.
examples.translation: Before going on stage, my friend told me 'mucha mierda!' to wish me luck in the play.

examples.sentence: No olvides decirle a Carla mucha mierda antes del concierto, siempre le da confianza.
examples.translation: Don't forget to say mucha mierda to Carla before the concert; it always gives her confidence.

examples.sentence: Aunque suene extraño, en el teatro es común desear mucha mierda en lugar de buena suerte.
examples.translation: Although it sounds strange, in theater it's common to say mucha mierda instead of good luck.

definitions: A large amount of noise combined with only a few nuts; literal contrast between great noise and few results.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta hubo mucho ruido y pocas nueces: todos gritaban pero casi no había comida.
examples.translation: At the party there was much noise and few nuts: everyone was shouting but there was hardly any food.

examples.sentence: Mientras los niños jugaban, se escuchaba mucho ruido y pocas nueces en el jardín trasero.
examples.translation: While the kids played, there was much noise and few nuts in the backyard.

examples.sentence: La reunión fue un caos con mucho ruido y pocas nueces, porque nadie llevó bocadillos.
examples.translation: The meeting was chaotic with much noise and few nuts because nobody brought snacks.

examples.sentence: En la cocina, el sonido de la máquina hacía mucho ruido y pocas nueces, pues apenas se veía su función.
examples.translation: In the kitchen, the machine made much noise and few nuts, since its function was barely visible.

definitions: Much ado about nothing; considerable fuss, talk, or activity that produces little or no useful result.

examples.sentence: El debate político resultó ser mucho ruido y pocas nueces, porque no propusieron soluciones reales.
examples.translation: The political debate ended up being much ado about nothing, because they didn't propose real solutions.

examples.sentence: No entiendo por qué hicieron tanto escándalo: fue puro mucho ruido y pocas nueces.
examples.translation: I don't understand why they made such a fuss: it was pure much ado about nothing.

examples.sentence: Aunque prometieron cambios, la protesta fue mucho ruido y pocas nueces al final.
examples.translation: Although they promised changes, the protest was much ado about nothing in the end.

definitions: Literally: dead from lack of food; starved to death.

examples.sentence: Durante la hambruna, muchas personas murieron de hambre por la falta de alimentos.
examples.translation: During the famine, many people died of hunger due to the lack of food.

examples.sentence: El documental mostraba cómo en algunas zonas del mundo aún hay niños muertos de hambre.
examples.translation: The documentary showed how in some parts of the world there are still children dead from hunger.

examples.sentence: Se encontraron restos de animales muertos de hambre en el bosque tras el invierno riguroso.
examples.translation: Remains of animals starved to death were found in the forest after the harsh winter.

examples.sentence: No es raro que en las guerras los ciudadanos terminen muertos de hambre cuando no hay suministros.
examples.translation: It's not unusual that in wars citizens end up starved to death when there are no supplies.

definitions: Extremely hungry; starving.

examples.sentence: Después de la caminata de cinco horas, estaba muerto de hambre y no podía esperar para comer.
examples.translation: After the five-hour hike, I was starving and couldn't wait to eat.

examples.sentence: Si sigues saltándote las comidas, vas a estar muerto de hambre en la cena.
examples.translation: If you keep skipping meals, you'll be starving at dinner.

examples.sentence: Los niños en la escuela estaban muertos de hambre porque no habían desayunado.
examples.translation: The children at school were starving because they hadn't had breakfast.

definitions: Figuratively: a very poor or penniless person; also used as an insulting term for a contemptible, worthless, or luckless individual.

examples.sentence: No me hables como si fuera un muerto de hambre; tengo para pagar mis cuentas.
examples.translation: Don't talk to me like I'm a deadbeat; I have money to pay my bills.

examples.sentence: En el barrio le decían muerto de hambre porque siempre pedía sin dar nada a cambio.
examples.translation: In the neighborhood they called him a deadbeat because he always asked without giving anything back.

examples.sentence: Aunque no tiene mucho dinero, no es un muerto de hambre como algunos piensan.
examples.translation: Although he doesn't have much money, he's not a deadbeat like some think.

definitions: Literally: the world characterized by public performances and spectacles.

examples.sentence: El mundo del espectáculo está lleno de luces, escenarios y artistas que fascinan al público.
examples.translation: The world of spectacle is full of lights, stages, and artists that captivate the audience.

examples.sentence: Durante el festival, el mundo del espectáculo se viste de gala con desfiles y conciertos.
examples.translation: During the festival, the world of spectacle dresses up with parades and concerts.

examples.sentence: Los niños disfrutaron del mundo del espectáculo en el circo con acróbatas y payasos.
examples.translation: The children enjoyed the world of spectacle at the circus with acrobats and clowns.

examples.sentence: El teatro es una parte fundamental del mundo del espectáculo en la ciudad.
examples.translation: The theater is a fundamental part of the world of spectacle in the city.

definitions: Figuratively: the entertainment industry; show business.

examples.sentence: Mi hermana trabaja en el mundo del espectáculo como productora de televisión.
examples.translation: My sister works in show business as a television producer.

examples.sentence: Para triunfar en el mundo del espectáculo, se necesita talento y mucha perseverancia.
examples.translation: To succeed in the entertainment industry, you need talent and a lot of perseverance.

examples.sentence: Aunque empezó como actriz amateur, ahora es una figura importante en el mundo del espectáculo.
examples.translation: Although she started as an amateur actress, now she's an important figure in show business.

definitions: Very occasionally; only on rare occasions.

examples.sentence: Muy de vez en cuando, solemos ir a cenar a ese restaurante que tanto nos gusta.
examples.translation: Very occasionally, we tend to go to dinner at that restaurant we like so much.

examples.sentence: Luis visita a sus abuelos muy de vez en cuando, porque vive lejos de ellos.
examples.translation: Luis visits his grandparents very occasionally because he lives far from them.

examples.sentence: Aunque le encanta leer, muy de vez en cuando encuentra tiempo para un libro nuevo.
examples.translation: Although he loves reading, very occasionally he finds time for a new book.

examples.sentence: Muy de vez en cuando, la ciudad organiza ferias culturales que atraen a mucha gente.
examples.translation: Very occasionally, the city organizes cultural fairs that attract many people.

definitions: Literally: to be born with a star (a poetic expression referring to a star associated with one at birth).

examples.sentence: Se dice que él nació con estrella, porque su nacimiento coincidió con un cometa brillante.
examples.translation: It is said he was born with a star because his birth coincided with a bright comet.

examples.sentence: La leyenda cuenta que nacer con estrella da buena suerte y un destino especial.
examples.translation: The legend says that being born with a star gives good luck and a special destiny.

examples.sentence: En la pintura, el bebé aparece rodeado de una estrella, simbolizando que nació con estrella.
examples.translation: In the painting, the baby appears surrounded by a star, symbolizing that he was born with a star.

examples.sentence: Mi bisabuela afirmaba que nacer con estrella era un signo de protección divina.
examples.translation: My great-grandmother claimed that being born with a star was a sign of divine protection.

definitions: Figuratively: to be born lucky or destined for success; to possess innate good fortune.

examples.sentence: María realmente nació con estrella, porque todo le ha ido bien sin mucho esfuerzo.
examples.translation: María was really born lucky, because everything has gone well for her without much effort.

examples.sentence: No creo que haya nacido con estrella; siempre enfrenta dificultades en su carrera.
examples.translation: I don't think he was born lucky; he always faces difficulties in his career.

examples.sentence: Si crees que has nacido con estrella, aprovecha las oportunidades que se te presentan.
examples.translation: If you believe you were born lucky, take advantage of the opportunities that come your way.

definitions: Literally: to be born standing.

examples.sentence: El recién nacido estaba nacer de pie, una rara condición que sorprendió a los médicos.
examples.translation: The newborn was born standing, a rare condition that surprised the doctors.

examples.sentence: En algunas culturas, se considera un signo de buena suerte nacer de pie.
examples.translation: In some cultures, being born standing is considered a sign of good luck.

examples.sentence: El bebé parecía nacer de pie, porque se movía mucho y estaba activo desde el inicio.
examples.translation: The baby seemed to be born standing because he moved a lot and was active from the start.

examples.sentence: Los cuentos antiguos narran casos donde un niño nacer de pie anunciaba su destino especial.
examples.translation: Old tales recount cases where a child born standing announced his special destiny.

definitions: Figuratively: to be born lucky, fortunate, or with a disposition for resilience and success.

examples.sentence: Juana siempre ha sido fuerte y optimista, definitivamente nació de pie.
examples.translation: Juana has always been strong and optimistic; she was definitely born lucky.

examples.sentence: No todos nacen de pie, algunos deben luchar más para alcanzar el éxito.
examples.translation: Not everyone is born lucky; some have to fight harder to achieve success.

examples.sentence: Si quieres salir adelante, tienes que nacer de pie, con actitud y determinación.
examples.translation: If you want to get ahead, you have to be born lucky, with attitude and determination.

definitions: To swim between two plates or dishes; literally to be swimming in the space separating two plates.

examples.sentence: El pez nada entre dos platos en el acuario, disfrutando del espacio entre ellos.
examples.translation: The fish swims between two plates in the aquarium, enjoying the space between them.

examples.sentence: Durante la cena, el niño jugaba con el agua y parecía nadar entre dos platos sin quererlos mojar.
examples.translation: During dinner, the child played with the water and seemed to swim between two plates without wanting to wet them.

examples.sentence: En la fotografía se ve un pato nadando entre dos platos grandes flotando en el lago.
examples.translation: In the photograph, a duck is seen swimming between two large plates floating on the lake.

examples.sentence: El camarero colocó dos platos con sopa y un pez nadaba entre dos platos en el tanque decorativo.
examples.translation: The waiter placed two plates with soup and a fish was swimming between two plates in the decorative tank.

definitions: To occupy an indecisive or intermediate position between two alternatives; to try to reconcile or please two opposing parties without committing to either side.

examples.sentence: Intentar agradar a todos es como nadar entre dos platos: no te comprometes con nadie.
examples.translation: Trying to please everyone is like swimming between two plates: you don't commit to anyone.

examples.sentence: El político está nadando entre dos platos para evitar tomar una posición clara en el debate.
examples.translation: The politician is swimming between two plates to avoid taking a clear position in the debate.

examples.sentence: No puedes nadar entre dos platos si quieres que tu negocio prospere; debes decidir un enfoque.
examples.translation: You can't swim between two plates if you want your business to prosper; you must choose an approach.

definitions: Nothing more and nothing less; exactly that amount or thing, no more and no less.

examples.sentence: El paquete contiene nada más y nada menos que tres libros de edición limitada.
examples.translation: The package contains nothing more and nothing less than three limited edition books.

examples.sentence: Compré el auto por nada más y nada menos de veinte mil dólares, justo el presupuesto que tenía.
examples.translation: I bought the car for nothing more and nothing less than twenty thousand dollars, exactly the budget I had.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, ofreció nada más y nada menos que su renuncia al cargo principal.
examples.translation: In the meeting, he offered nothing more and nothing less than his resignation from the main position.

examples.sentence: El regalo fue nada más y nada menos que un reloj antiguo heredado de la familia.
examples.translation: The gift was nothing more and nothing less than an antique watch inherited from the family.

definitions: Used to emphasize the precise identity, status, or quantity of a person or thing, often to highlight surprise, importance, or exactness.

examples.sentence: El invitado sorpresa fue nada más y nada menos que el famoso director de cine.
examples.translation: The surprise guest was none other than the famous film director.

examples.sentence: Cuando me dijeron que había ganado, no podía creer que fuera nada más y nada menos que el primer premio.
examples.translation: When they told me I had won, I couldn't believe it was nothing less than the first prize.

examples.sentence: Su propuesta fue nada más y nada menos que revolucionaria para el sector tecnológico.
examples.translation: His proposal was nothing less than revolutionary for the tech sector.

definitions: Nothing less; not any smaller amount or lesser degree.

examples.sentence: El resultado fue nada menos que un éxito total en la presentación del producto.
examples.translation: The result was nothing less than a total success in the product presentation.

examples.sentence: Esperaba una multa pequeña, pero la sanción fue nada menos que una gran multa económica.
examples.translation: I expected a small fine, but the penalty was nothing less than a large financial fine.

examples.sentence: El concierto reunió nada menos que a diez mil personas en el estadio central.
examples.translation: The concert gathered no less than ten thousand people in the central stadium.

examples.sentence: Para su cumpleaños le regalaron nada menos que un viaje a Europa, algo que no esperaba.
examples.translation: For his birthday, they gave him nothing less than a trip to Europe, something he didn't expect.

definitions: Used idiomatically to stress that someone or something is surprisingly important, impressive, or substantial, equivalent to 'nothing less than' in English.

examples.sentence: El nuevo jefe es nada menos que un experto con más de veinte años de experiencia.
examples.translation: The new boss is nothing less than an expert with over twenty years of experience.

examples.sentence: Cuando llegó al evento, vio nada menos que a la presidenta en persona saludando a los invitados.
examples.translation: When he arrived at the event, he saw none other than the president herself greeting guests.

examples.sentence: No es cualquier cantante, es nada menos que una estrella internacional reconocida.
examples.translation: He is not just any singer; he is nothing less than a recognized international star.

definitions: To swim in abundance; literally to be swimming amid plentiful resources or wealth.

examples.sentence: Los peces nadan en la abundancia de ese estanque lleno de algas y comida.
examples.translation: The fish swim in the abundance of that pond full of algae and food.

examples.sentence: En el río cristalino, se puede ver a los patos nadar en la abundancia de agua fresca.
examples.translation: In the clear river, you can see ducks swimming in the abundance of fresh water.

examples.sentence: El lago está tan lleno que parece que los peces nadan en la abundancia sin preocuparse por nada.
examples.translation: The lake is so full that it seems the fish swim in abundance without worrying about anything.

examples.sentence: Durante la temporada de lluvias, los animales nadan en la abundancia de recursos naturales que ofrece el bosque.
examples.translation: During the rainy season, animals swim in the abundance of natural resources offered by the forest.

definitions: To have plenty or an abundance of resources, wealth, or goods; to live in affluence or extravagance.

examples.sentence: Después de la venta exitosa, la empresa nada en la abundancia y planea expandirse.
examples.translation: After the successful sale, the company is swimming in abundance and plans to expand.

examples.sentence: Con el aumento de sus ingresos, ahora nadan en la abundancia y disfrutan de una vida cómoda.
examples.translation: With the increase in their income, they now swim in abundance and enjoy a comfortable life.

examples.sentence: Aunque empezó con poco, hoy nada en la abundancia gracias a su esfuerzo y dedicación.
examples.translation: Although he started with little, today he swims in abundance thanks to his effort and dedication.

definitions: To swim between two bodies of water; literally to be in the water dividing two currents or areas.

examples.sentence: El nadador cruzó nadando entre dos aguas, donde se juntaban dos corrientes del río.
examples.translation: The swimmer crossed swimming between two waters, where two river currents met.

examples.sentence: El paisaje mostraba un canal donde los peces nadaban entre dos aguas claras y tranquilas.
examples.translation: The landscape showed a channel where fish swam between two clear and calm waters.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, el bote quedó atrapado nadando entre dos aguas turbulentas.
examples.translation: During the storm, the boat was trapped swimming between two turbulent waters.

examples.sentence: Los kayaks se movían con destreza, nadando entre dos aguas en la bahía protegida.
examples.translation: The kayaks moved skillfully, swimming between two waters in the sheltered bay.

definitions: To remain undecided or to adopt an ambiguous position in order to avoid commitment; to try to please both sides or to sit on the fence.

examples.sentence: No me gusta cuando alguien nada entre dos aguas y no toma una decisión clara.
examples.translation: I don't like it when someone swims between two waters and doesn't make a clear decision.

examples.sentence: Para ganar votos, el candidato está nadando entre dos aguas, intentando agradar a todos.
examples.translation: To win votes, the candidate is swimming between two waters, trying to please everyone.

examples.sentence: Si quieres avanzar en tu carrera, deja de nadar entre dos aguas y elige un camino firme.
examples.translation: If you want to advance in your career, stop swimming between two waters and choose a firm path.

definitions: To swim while keeping one's clothes on or dry; literally, to swim and retain one’s clothing.

examples.sentence: El niño intentaba nadar y guardar la ropa, sin mojar su camiseta mientras jugaba en la piscina.
examples.translation: The boy tried to swim while keeping his clothes dry, without wetting his shirt while playing in the pool.

examples.sentence: Durante el chapuzón, logró nadar y guardar la ropa, evitando que sus zapatos se mojaran.
examples.translation: During the dip, he managed to swim and keep his clothes dry, avoiding getting his shoes wet.

examples.sentence: Los patos nadaban y guardaban la ropa, es decir, permanecían secos a pesar del agua alrededor.
examples.translation: The ducks swam and kept their clothes dry, that is, they stayed dry despite the water around.

examples.sentence: En el espectáculo acuático, los artistas nadaban y guardaban la ropa, saltando sin mojarse demasiado.
examples.translation: In the water show, the performers swam and kept their clothes dry, jumping without getting too wet.

definitions: To try to obtain the benefits of two incompatible positions or to protect one’s interests while avoiding risk or responsibility; to attempt to have it both ways.

examples.sentence: Juan siempre intenta nadar y guardar la ropa para no perder su posición ni asumir riesgos.
examples.translation: Juan always tries to swim and keep his clothes dry to neither lose his position nor take risks.

examples.sentence: No puedes nadar y guardar la ropa en esta situación; debes decidirte y actuar con valentía.
examples.translation: You can't try to have it both ways in this situation; you must decide and act bravely.

examples.sentence: Muchos políticos nadan y guardan la ropa para evitar conflictos con sus aliados y opositores.
examples.translation: Many politicians try to have it both ways to avoid conflicts with their allies and opponents.

definitions: To swim while keeping one’s clothes on or dry; a literal variant meaning to swim and still have one’s clothes.

examples.sentence: Durante el invierno, a veces es necesario nadar y tener la ropa para no perder el calor corporal.
examples.translation: During winter, sometimes it's necessary to swim while keeping your clothes on to avoid losing body heat.

examples.sentence: El niño trató de nadar y tener la ropa, para no mojar su uniforme antes de la escuela.
examples.translation: The boy tried to swim while keeping his clothes on, so he wouldn't wet his uniform before school.

examples.sentence: En algunas competiciones, los concursantes deben nadar y tener la ropa como prueba de resistencia.
examples.translation: In some competitions, contestants have to swim while keeping their clothes on as a test of endurance.

examples.sentence: La fotografía capturó a la mujer nadando y teniendo la ropa, un momento curioso y divertido.
examples.translation: The photograph captured the woman swimming while keeping her clothes on, a curious and funny moment.

definitions: To try to preserve one’s advantage while avoiding the accompanying risks or obligations; to attempt to have it both ways.

examples.sentence: Intentar nadar y tener la ropa no funciona en los negocios; debes comprometerte completamente.
examples.translation: Trying to have it both ways doesn't work in business; you must fully commit.

examples.sentence: Muchos intentan nadar y tener la ropa, buscando beneficios sin asumir responsabilidades.
examples.translation: Many try to have it both ways, seeking benefits without taking responsibility.

examples.sentence: Si quieres progresar, deja de nadar y tener la ropa y enfócate en una sola estrategia.
examples.translation: If you want to progress, stop trying to have it both ways and focus on a single strategy.

definitions: Extremely black in color; very dark.

examples.sentence: El cielo estaba negro como un zapato justo antes de la tormenta que se avecinaba.
examples.translation: The sky was as black as a shoe just before the approaching storm.

examples.sentence: La noche sin luna era negro como un zapato, dificultando encontrar el camino a casa.
examples.translation: The moonless night was as black as a shoe, making it difficult to find the way home.

examples.sentence: El carbón de la chimenea estaba negro como un zapato tras horas de combustión.
examples.translation: The chimney coal was as black as a shoe after hours of burning.

examples.sentence: Los gatos callejeros tenían el pelaje negro como un zapato, camuflándose en la oscuridad.
examples.translation: The stray cats had fur as black as a shoe, camouflaging in the darkness.

definitions: Very dirty, sullied, or soiled; covered with dirt or grime.

examples.sentence: Después de trabajar en el jardín todo el día, sus manos quedaron negro como un zapato de la tierra.
examples.translation: After working in the garden all day, his hands were as black as a shoe from the dirt.

examples.sentence: El mecánico salió del taller negro como un zapato debido al aceite y la grasa en su ropa.
examples.translation: The mechanic came out of the workshop as black as a shoe because of the oil and grease on his clothes.

examples.sentence: No intentes limpiar la mancha, ya está negro como un zapato y no saldrá fácilmente.
examples.translation: Don't try to clean the stain, it's already as black as a shoe and won't come off easily.

definitions: A dark stain or mark beneath or on a fingernail, typically from dirt, ink, or similar substances.

examples.sentence: Tenía un negro de la uña que no se quitaba, probablemente por la tinta derramada en la oficina.
examples.translation: He had a stain under his fingernail that wouldn't come off, probably from spilled ink in the office.

examples.sentence: La pintora notó un negro de la uña después de trabajar con los pigmentos oscuros todo el día.
examples.translation: The painter noticed a stain under her fingernail after working with dark pigments all day.

examples.sentence: El niño tenía un negro de la uña causado por la suciedad acumulada tras jugar en el parque.
examples.translation: The child had a stain under his fingernail caused by dirt accumulated after playing in the park.

examples.sentence: Aunque se lavó las manos, el negro de la uña permanecía visible por más tiempo.
examples.translation: Although he washed his hands, the stain under his fingernail remained visible for a long time.

definitions: Black (ink or print) on white (paper); literally, words or marks printed or written in black on a white background.

examples.sentence: El contrato está negro sobre blanco, así que no hay lugar a dudas.
examples.translation: The contract is in black on white, so there is no room for doubt.

examples.sentence: Prefiero tener todo negro sobre blanco para evitar malentendidos con el cliente.
examples.translation: I prefer to have everything in black on white to avoid misunderstandings with the client.

examples.sentence: En la sala, el profesor mostró negro sobre blanco cómo resolver el problema matemático.
examples.translation: In the classroom, the teacher showed in black on white how to solve the math problem.

examples.sentence: Los documentos están impresos negro sobre blanco, listos para ser firmados por ambas partes.
examples.translation: The documents are printed in black on white, ready to be signed by both parties.

definitions: Explicitly documented or put in writing; clear, verifiable evidence recorded on paper.

examples.sentence: Necesito que el acuerdo esté negro sobre blanco antes de proceder con la inversión.
examples.translation: I need the agreement to be black on white before proceeding with the investment.

examples.sentence: Aunque me lo dijo de palabra, prefiero tener todo negro sobre blanco para no tener problemas después.
examples.translation: Although he told me verbally, I prefer to have everything black on white to avoid problems later.

examples.sentence: El juez pidió que la declaración estuviera negro sobre blanco para admitirla como prueba.
examples.translation: The judge requested that the statement be black on white to admit it as evidence.

definitions: Not even with two tugs or pulls; literally, something that does not come loose or cannot be moved by pulling twice.

examples.sentence: Intenté abrir la tapa, pero ni a dos tirones se soltaba.
examples.translation: I tried to open the lid, but it didn’t come loose even with two tugs.

examples.sentence: La puerta vieja estaba tan oxidada que ni a dos tirones cedió.
examples.translation: The old door was so rusty that it didn’t give way even with two pulls.

examples.sentence: Ni a dos tirones logré que la ventana se abriera esta mañana.
examples.translation: Not even with two tugs did I manage to open the window this morning.

examples.sentence: La cuerda estaba tan firme que ni a dos tirones se rompió.
examples.translation: The rope was so tight that it didn’t break even with two pulls.

definitions: Figuratively, indicating that something cannot be achieved, resolved, or obtained even after repeated or forceful attempts; 'not even with effort.'

examples.sentence: Le ofrecí ayuda varias veces, pero ni a dos tirones aceptó mi apoyo.
examples.translation: I offered help several times, but not even with effort did he accept my support.

examples.sentence: Esta negociación no se va a resolver ni a dos tirones, hay demasiados desacuerdos.
examples.translation: This negotiation won’t be resolved even with effort; there are too many disagreements.

examples.sentence: Ni a dos tirones conseguí que me escucharan en la reunión de hoy.
examples.translation: Not even after trying hard did I get them to listen to me in today’s meeting.

definitions: Not even at the count of three; literally, unable to hit, guess, or do something even when given three counts or three quick tries.

examples.sentence: Le lancé la pelota tres veces, pero ni a la de tres la atrapó.
examples.translation: I threw the ball to him three times, but he didn’t catch it even on the third try.

examples.sentence: Ni a la de tres logró adivinar la respuesta correcta durante el examen.
examples.translation: Not even on the count of three did he manage to guess the correct answer during the exam.

examples.sentence: Intenté encender la fogata ni a la de tres, sin éxito.
examples.translation: I tried to light the fire not even by the count of three, without success.

examples.sentence: La niña no pudo atarse los zapatos ni a la de tres, necesitó ayuda.
examples.translation: The girl couldn’t tie her shoes even at the count of three; she needed help.

definitions: Figuratively, used to express inability, incompetence, or that something will not happen despite multiple attempts; equivalent to 'not at all' or 'no way.'

examples.sentence: Ni a la de tres va a terminar ese proyecto si sigue procrastinando así.
examples.translation: No way will he finish that project even after three tries if he keeps procrastinating like that.

examples.sentence: Le pedí que me ayudara y me dijo que ni a la de tres, que estaba ocupado.
examples.translation: I asked him to help me and he said no way, he was busy.

examples.sentence: Ni a la de tres voy a aceptar ese trato tan injusto.
examples.translation: No way will I accept that unfair deal.

definitions: Not even by shooting; literally, not achieved even by using a gun or firing a shot.

examples.sentence: Ni a tiros conseguí que el perro entrara a la casa.
examples.translation: Not even by shooting did I manage to get the dog inside the house.

examples.sentence: La situación no mejoraba ni a tiros, así que decidimos cambiar de estrategia.
examples.translation: The situation didn’t improve even by shooting, so we decided to change strategy.

examples.sentence: Ni a tiros los ladrones dejaron la casa sin causar daño.
examples.translation: Not even by shooting did the thieves leave the house without causing damage.

examples.sentence: Intentaron detener el vehículo ni a tiros, pero el conductor escapó velozmente.
examples.translation: They tried to stop the vehicle not even by shooting, but the driver escaped quickly.

definitions: Figuratively, an emphatic expression of impossibility or refusal meaning 'no way,' 'under no circumstances,' or 'extremely unlikely'; used to stress that something will not happen or cannot be obtained.

examples.sentence: Ni a tiros voy a prestarte dinero después de lo que pasó la última vez.
examples.translation: No way am I lending you money after what happened last time.

examples.sentence: Cuando le pregunté si cambiaría de opinión, me respondió que ni a tiros.
examples.translation: When I asked if he would change his mind, he told me no way.

examples.sentence: Ni a tiros aceptaré un trabajo que no me gusta solo por el sueldo.
examples.translation: Under no circumstances will I accept a job I don’t like just for the salary.

definitions: Not even with three tugs or pulls; literally, something that does not come loose or be moved after three attempts.

examples.sentence: La llave estaba tan vieja que ni a tres tirones salió del candado.
examples.translation: The key was so old that it didn’t come out of the lock even after three pulls.

examples.sentence: Intenté abrir el cajón ni a tres tirones, pero estaba atascado.
examples.translation: I tried to open the drawer not even with three pulls, but it was stuck.

examples.sentence: El tornillo no se movió ni a tres tirones, necesitaremos herramientas especiales.
examples.translation: The screw didn’t move even after three tugs; we’ll need special tools.

examples.sentence: Ni a tres tirones pude sacar el tapón de la botella de vino.
examples.translation: Not even with three pulls did I manage to remove the wine bottle cork.

definitions: Figuratively, indicating that a task or result will not be achieved quickly or easily, even after repeated tries; similar to 'not even after several attempts.'

examples.sentence: Este problema no se resuelve ni a tres tirones, hay que buscar otra solución.
examples.translation: This problem won’t be solved even after several attempts; we need to find another solution.

examples.sentence: Ni a tres tirones consigo que mi jefe me dé un aumento de sueldo.
examples.translation: Not even after repeated tries do I get my boss to give me a raise.

examples.sentence: Ni a tres tirones logré que cambiara de opinión sobre el proyecto.
examples.translation: Not even after several tries did I manage to get him to change his mind about the project.

definitions: A conjunction meaning 'as soon as,' used to indicate that one action takes place immediately after another.

examples.sentence: Ni bien llegó, comenzó a llover intensamente y tuvimos que refugiarnos.
examples.translation: As soon as he arrived, it began to rain heavily and we had to take shelter.

examples.sentence: Ni bien terminó la reunión, recibí una llamada urgente de la oficina.
examples.translation: As soon as the meeting ended, I received an urgent call from the office.

examples.sentence: Ni bien apagué las luces, el gato saltó sobre la mesa.
examples.translation: As soon as I turned off the lights, the cat jumped onto the table.

examples.sentence: Ni bien empezó la película, todos se quedaron en silencio.
examples.translation: As soon as the movie started, everyone fell silent.

definitions: Used adverbially in negation or comparison to mean 'not even well' or to form contrasts such as 'neither well nor badly,' expressing lack of adequacy or moderate condition.

examples.sentence: No me fue ni bien ni mal en el examen, simplemente fue un resultado promedio.
examples.translation: I did neither well nor badly on the exam; it was just an average result.

examples.sentence: Ni bien manejó el problema, pero al menos no lo empeoró.
examples.translation: He didn’t handle the problem well, but at least he didn’t make it worse.

examples.sentence: No salió ni bien ni mal la fiesta, fue bastante normal para lo que esperábamos.
examples.translation: The party went neither well nor badly; it was quite normal for what we expected.

definitions: Literal: not even drunk; indicating that a person is not intoxicated.

examples.sentence: Ayer revisé el video y se le veía ni borracho ni cansado, estaba completamente sobrio.
examples.translation: Yesterday I checked the video and he looked neither drunk nor tired; he was completely sober.

examples.sentence: Aunque la fiesta fue larga, él ni borracho perdió la compostura en ningún momento.
examples.translation: Although the party was long, he didn’t lose his composure even drunk.

examples.sentence: El conductor estaba ni borracho para manejar, solo había tomado un refresco.
examples.translation: The driver was not even drunk to drive; he had only drunk a soda.

examples.sentence: A pesar de los rumores, esa noche él ni borracho cometió ningún error grave.
examples.translation: Despite the rumors, that night he didn’t make any serious mistakes even drunk.

definitions: Figurative: an emphatic negation meaning 'absolutely not' or 'no way,' often used to say one would not do something even if extremely impaired.

examples.sentence: Ni borracho aceptaría hacer algo tan irresponsable como eso.
examples.translation: No way would I accept doing something so irresponsible, not even drunk.

examples.sentence: Me preguntaron si quería ir a esa fiesta, y respondí que ni borracho.
examples.translation: They asked me if I wanted to go to that party, and I said no way.

examples.sentence: Ni borracho me pondría a conducir después de haber bebido tanto.
examples.translation: Absolutely not would I drive after drinking so much, not even drunk.

definitions: Literal: neither chicha (a fermented or sweet beverage) nor lemonade.

examples.sentence: En la feria había puestos de ni chicha ni limonada, ofreciendo bebidas tradicionales y refrescos.
examples.translation: At the fair there were stands of neither chicha nor lemonade, offering traditional drinks and refreshments.

examples.sentence: Prefiero un vaso de chicha que uno de limonada, aunque hoy no había ni chicha ni limonada disponibles.
examples.translation: I prefer a glass of chicha over lemonade, although today there was neither chicha nor lemonade available.

examples.sentence: El menú incluía ni chicha ni limonada, sino otras opciones de bebidas típicas.
examples.translation: The menu included neither chicha nor lemonade, but other typical beverage options.

examples.sentence: En la reunión no sirvieron ni chicha ni limonada, solo café y agua.
examples.translation: At the meeting they served neither chicha nor lemonade, only coffee and water.

definitions: Figurative (ambiguous identity): lacking a clear or definite character; neither one thing nor another.

examples.sentence: Su propuesta es ni chicha ni limonada, no convence ni a los expertos ni a los novatos.
examples.translation: His proposal is neither fish nor fowl; it doesn’t convince experts nor novices.

examples.sentence: El informe quedó ni chicha ni limonada, sin una conclusión clara que apoye la iniciativa.
examples.translation: The report was neither fish nor fowl, without a clear conclusion to support the initiative.

examples.sentence: Esa película es ni chicha ni limonada; no es buena ni mala, simplemente indiferente.
examples.translation: That movie is neither fish nor fowl; it’s neither good nor bad, just indifferent.

definitions: Figurative (value judgment): bland, unimpressive, or of no consequence; mediocre or inconclusive.

examples.sentence: El sabor del plato era ni chicha ni limonada, demasiado insípido para mi gusto.
examples.translation: The taste of the dish was bland, too tasteless for my liking.

examples.sentence: Su actuación fue ni chicha ni limonada, no destacó en ninguna escena.
examples.translation: His performance was bland, it didn’t stand out in any scene.

examples.sentence: El informe llegó ni chicha ni limonada, sin datos relevantes que aportaran valor al proyecto.
examples.translation: The report came bland, without relevant data that added value to the project.

definitions: Literal: neither eats nor lets others eat.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, Juan ni come ni deja comer, siempre interrumpe y no aporta nada.
examples.translation: During the meeting, Juan neither eats nor lets others eat; he always interrupts and contributes nothing.

examples.sentence: El niño ni come ni deja comer, se niega a probar la comida y tampoco deja que sus hermanos coman tranquilos.
examples.translation: The child neither eats nor lets others eat; he refuses to try the food and doesn’t let his siblings eat peacefully.

examples.sentence: En la oficina hay alguien que ni come ni deja comer, siempre critica pero no colabora.
examples.translation: There is someone in the office who neither eats nor lets others eat, always criticizing but not collaborating.

examples.sentence: Esa máquina ni come ni deja comer, consume energía sin funcionar correctamente y bloquea el sistema.
examples.translation: That machine neither eats nor lets others eat; it consumes energy without functioning properly and blocks the system.

definitions: Figurative: describes a person who neither participates productively nor allows others to do so, thus spoiling or obstructing the situation for everyone.

examples.sentence: Pedro es de los que ni come ni deja comer; no hace nada útil y encima molesta a todos.
examples.translation: Pedro is one of those who neither eats nor lets others eat; he does nothing useful and even annoys everyone.

examples.sentence: En el grupo de trabajo hay un compañero que ni come ni deja comer, dificultando los avances del proyecto.
examples.translation: In the workgroup there is a colleague who neither eats nor lets others eat, making project progress difficult.

examples.sentence: No quiero que esa persona se quede en el equipo porque ni come ni deja comer y solo genera problemas.
examples.translation: I don’t want that person to stay on the team because he neither eats nor lets others eat and only causes problems.

definitions: Literal: not even Christ who founded it.

examples.sentence: En ese pueblo ni Cristo que lo fundó parece estar vivo, está completamente deshabitado.
examples.translation: In that village not even Christ who founded it appears to be alive; it is completely deserted.

examples.sentence: Ni Cristo que lo fundó vino a la inauguración, fue un evento sin invitados.
examples.translation: Not even Christ who founded it came to the inauguration; it was an event without guests.

examples.sentence: El teatro estaba tan vacío que ni Cristo que lo fundó ocupaba un asiento.
examples.translation: The theater was so empty that not even Christ who founded it occupied a seat.

examples.sentence: La fiesta fue un fracaso total, ni Cristo que lo fundó asistió.
examples.translation: The party was a total failure; absolutely nobody attended.

definitions: Figurative: used hyperbolically to mean 'absolutely nobody' or 'not a soul,' or to stress the total absence of people, help, or success.

examples.sentence: En esa manifestación no había ni Cristo que lo fundó, solo unos pocos valientes.
examples.translation: In that demonstration there was absolutely nobody, just a few brave ones.

examples.sentence: Cuando pedí ayuda, no apareció ni Cristo que lo fundó para apoyarme.
examples.translation: When I asked for help, not a soul showed up to support me.

examples.sentence: En ese equipo de trabajo no hay ni Cristo que lo fundó que quiera colaborar realmente.
examples.translation: In that work team, there’s absolutely nobody who genuinely wants to collaborate.

definitions: Literal: not even as a joke.

examples.sentence: Ni de broma voy a permitir que usen mi computadora sin permiso.
examples.translation: Not even as a joke will I allow them to use my computer without permission.

examples.sentence: Ni de broma pensaba que ganaríamos el partido con tanta facilidad.
examples.translation: I didn’t even jokingly think we would win the game so easily.

examples.sentence: Ella me dijo que ni de broma haría algo así, aunque se lo pidieran.
examples.translation: She told me she wouldn’t do something like that even as a joke, even if asked.

examples.sentence: Ni de broma aceptaría trabajar un fin de semana sin pago extra.
examples.translation: Not even as a joke would I accept working a weekend without extra pay.

definitions: Figurative: a categorical refusal or denial meaning 'no way' or 'absolutely not,' often used to reject a suggestion decisively.

examples.sentence: —¿Quieres prestarme tu coche? —Ni de broma, ni lo pienses.
examples.translation: —Do you want to lend me your car? —No way, don’t even think about it.

examples.sentence: Ni de broma voy a asistir a esa reunión tan aburrida.
examples.translation: No way will I attend that boring meeting.

examples.sentence: Si crees que voy a perdonar eso, ni de broma lo haré.
examples.translation: If you think I’m going to forgive that, no way I will.

definitions: Emphatic refusal or denial; absolutely not; no way.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que te ayude con la mudanza? —Ni de coña, tengo otros planes.
examples.translation: Do you want me to help you with the move? —No way, I have other plans.

examples.sentence: Ni de coña me meto en ese lío con ellos, es demasiado complicado.
examples.translation: No way I’m getting involved in that mess with them; it’s too complicated.

examples.sentence: Le ofrecí participar en el proyecto, pero respondió que ni de coña lo haría.
examples.translation: I offered him to participate in the project, but he replied that no way he would.

definitions: Not even as a joke; not even in jest (literal sense).

examples.sentence: Ni de coña dije eso, debes haber entendido mal.
examples.translation: I didn’t say that even as a joke; you must have misunderstood.

examples.sentence: El profesor nunca ni de coña permite usar el móvil en clase.
examples.translation: The teacher never even jokingly allows using the phone in class.

examples.sentence: Ni de coña creí que la broma fuera a ofender a alguien.
examples.translation: I didn’t even as a joke think the joke would offend anyone.

examples.sentence: Ni de coña me imagino que ellos se rindieran tan fácilmente.
examples.translation: Not even as a joke can I imagine they would give up so easily.

definitions: Not even joking; an emphatic denial or rejection.

examples.sentence: Ni de guasa pienso aceptar esa oferta tan baja, es una burla.
examples.translation: Not even joking do I plan to accept that low offer; it’s a mockery.

examples.sentence: Cuando me preguntaron si quería cambiar de trabajo, respondí ni de guasa.
examples.translation: When they asked me if I wanted to change jobs, I replied no way.

examples.sentence: Ni de guasa voy a prestarte mi coche después del último accidente.
examples.translation: I’m definitely not lending you my car, not even joking, after the last accident.

definitions: Not even as a jest; not in jest (literal sense).

examples.sentence: Ni de guasa dije eso, fue un malentendido.
examples.translation: I didn’t say that even as a jest; it was a misunderstanding.

examples.sentence: Ni de guasa permitiría que alguien entrara sin invitación a mi casa.
examples.translation: Not even as a jest would I allow someone to enter my house uninvited.

examples.sentence: Ni de guasa pensaba que la broma iba a causar tanto revuelo.
examples.translation: I didn’t even jokingly think the joke would cause so much fuss.

examples.sentence: Ni de guasa me imagino que ellos aprobaran ese proyecto sin cambios.
examples.translation: Not even as a jest can I imagine they would approve that project without changes.

definitions: By no means; not at all; nowhere near the degree, quality, or truth of what is stated.

examples.sentence: La casa de mis abuelos está ni de lejos cerca del centro de la ciudad.
examples.translation: My grandparents’ house is nowhere near the city center.

examples.sentence: Ni de lejos se veía el mar desde la ventana del hotel en la montaña.
examples.translation: Not even close could you see the sea from the hotel window in the mountains.

examples.sentence: El restaurante estaba ni de lejos a la distancia que dijeron, tuvimos que caminar mucho más.
examples.translation: The restaurant was nowhere near the distance they said; we had to walk much more.

examples.sentence: Ni de lejos llegamos a tiempo para el concierto debido al tráfico pesado.
examples.translation: We didn’t get anywhere near on time for the concert due to heavy traffic.

definitions: Not even close in physical distance; far away (literal sense).

examples.sentence: Su explicación está ni de lejos cerca de ser correcta, cometió varios errores graves.
examples.translation: His explanation is by no means close to being correct; he made several serious mistakes.

examples.sentence: El nuevo modelo ni de lejos es tan eficiente como el anterior que teníamos.
examples.translation: The new model is nowhere near as efficient as the previous one we had.

examples.sentence: Ni de lejos pensé que la película fuera tan mala como resultó ser.
examples.translation: I never thought the movie would be nowhere near as bad as it turned out.

definitions: Strong emphatic refusal or impossibility; no way; not on your life.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que me voy a olvidar de tu cumpleaños? Ni en pedo, lo tengo anotado en mi agenda.
examples.translation: Do you think I’m going to forget your birthday? No way, I have it noted in my agenda.

examples.sentence: Ni en pedo aceptaría un trabajo sin contrato ni garantías legales.
examples.translation: No way would I accept a job without a contract or legal guarantees.

examples.sentence: Cuando me preguntaron si quería salir con él, dije ni en pedo, ni lo conozco bien.
examples.translation: When they asked me if I wanted to go out with him, I said no way, I don’t even know him well.

definitions: Not even when drunk; used literally to indicate that even intoxication would not make something happen.

examples.sentence: Aunque estuviera completamente borracho, ni en pedo me subiría a ese coche tan viejo.
examples.translation: Even if I were completely drunk, not even when drunk would I get into that old car.

examples.sentence: Ni en pedo quiero probar ese plato; sé que no me va a gustar ni aunque lleve vino.
examples.translation: Not even when drunk do I want to try that dish; I know I won't like it even if it has wine.

examples.sentence: María dijo que ni en pedo aceptaría ese trabajo, aunque le pagaran mucho más.
examples.translation: María said she wouldn't accept that job even when drunk, even if they paid her much more.

examples.sentence: No me vas a convencer ni en pedo de que eso es una buena idea, ni aunque estés ebrio.
examples.translation: You won't convince me even when drunk that that's a good idea, not even if you're intoxicated.

definitions: Completely unimaginable; not even in one's wildest dreams; absolutely not.

examples.sentence: Ni en sueños pensaba que iba a ganar la lotería, fue una sorpresa total.
examples.translation: Not even in my wildest dreams did I think I would win the lottery; it was a total surprise.

examples.sentence: Cuando me ofrecieron el puesto, ni en sueños imaginaba que llegaría tan lejos en la empresa.
examples.translation: When they offered me the position, I never imagined in my wildest dreams that I would get this far in the company.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que él te va a perdonar? Ni en sueños, después de lo que pasó.
examples.translation: Do you think he will forgive you? Not even in your wildest dreams, after what happened.

definitions: Not even while dreaming; used literally to state that something does not occur in a person's dreams.

examples.sentence: Ni en sueños vi que mi abuela visitara la ciudad; siempre se quedó en el campo.
examples.translation: Not even while dreaming did I see my grandmother visiting the city; she always stayed in the countryside.

examples.sentence: Esta noche no tuve ni un sueño, ni en sueños apareció esa persona que extraño tanto.
examples.translation: Tonight I didn't have a single dream; not even while dreaming did that person I miss so much appear.

examples.sentence: En sus relatos, ni en sueños se menciona algo sobre aquel incidente extraño.
examples.translation: In their stories, not even in dreams is there mention of that strange incident.

examples.sentence: Ni en sueños pensé que mi perro podría aprender trucos tan complicados.
examples.translation: Not even while dreaming did I think my dog could learn such complicated tricks.

definitions: Literal expression formed by two meaningless interjections ("fu" and "fa") with no specific denotation.

examples.sentence: Cuando le pregunté qué le parecía la película, respondió con un simple 'ni fu ni fa'.
examples.translation: When I asked him what he thought of the movie, he replied with a simple 'ni fu ni fa'.

examples.sentence: El comentario de Juan fue ni fu ni fa, no mostró entusiasmo ni desagrado.
examples.translation: Juan's comment was ni fu ni fa; he showed neither enthusiasm nor displeasure.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, su opinión fue ni fu ni fa, sin aportar nada concreto.
examples.translation: In the meeting, his opinion was ni fu ni fa, without contributing anything concrete.

examples.sentence: Para describir el sabor de la sopa, Marta dijo que estaba ni fu ni fa, bastante insípida.
examples.translation: To describe the soup's taste, Marta said it was ni fu ni fa, quite bland.

definitions: Indicates indifference or mediocrity; neither good nor bad, neither here nor there; expresses that something leaves one unimpressed or unconcerned.

examples.sentence: Esa película me dejó ni fu ni fa, no me emocionó ni me aburrió.
examples.translation: That movie left me indifferent; neither good nor bad.

examples.sentence: Su actitud ante el problema fue ni fu ni fa, como si no le importara mucho.
examples.translation: His attitude towards the problem was indifferent, neither caring nor ignoring it.

examples.sentence: Cuando le pregunté por el concierto, me contestó ni fu ni fa, sin mucho interés.
examples.translation: When I asked him about the concert, he answered ni fu ni fa, without much interest.

definitions: Literal reference to bagpipes (gaitas) used in the phrase without a literal musical meaning.

examples.sentence: En el pueblo, es común escuchar las gaitas durante las fiestas tradicionales.
examples.translation: In the village, it is common to hear bagpipes during traditional festivals.

examples.sentence: Las gaitas son un símbolo importante de la cultura gallega y su música.
examples.translation: The bagpipes are an important symbol of Galician culture and its music.

examples.sentence: Durante el desfile, las gaitas resonaban por toda la ciudad, creando un ambiente festivo.
examples.translation: During the parade, the bagpipes echoed throughout the city, creating a festive atmosphere.

examples.sentence: Mi abuelo aprendió a tocar las gaitas cuando era joven y aún conserva el instrumento.
examples.translation: My grandfather learned to play the bagpipes when he was young and still keeps the instrument.

definitions: An emphatic negation meaning 'no way', 'none of that', or 'don't give me that'; used to reject, dismiss, or forbid something.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que crea esa excusa? ¡Ni gaitas! Sé que estás mintiendo.
examples.translation: You want me to believe that excuse? No way! I know you're lying.

examples.sentence: Me pidió que le prestara dinero, pero le dije ni gaitas, no confío en él.
examples.translation: He asked me to lend him money, but I said no way; I don't trust him.

examples.sentence: Si crees que voy a ayudarte con eso, ni gaitas, hazlo tú mismo.
examples.translation: If you think I'm going to help you with that, no way; do it yourself.

definitions: Used after a coordinated negation to mean 'and nothing else' or 'nor anything whatsoever', e.g., to intensify the exclusion of alternatives.

examples.sentence: No quiero que vengas ni con tu hermano ni con tus amigos ni gaitas; esta es una reunión privada.
examples.translation: I don’t want you to come neither with your brother nor with your friends nor anything else; this is a private meeting.

examples.sentence: Ella no acepta regalos ni favores, ni de sus padres ni de nadie ni gaitas.
examples.translation: She doesn’t accept gifts or favors, neither from her parents nor from anyone else.

examples.sentence: En la entrevista, no aceptaron ni la experiencia ni la educación ni gaitas; querían otra cosa.
examples.translation: In the interview, they didn’t accept experience or education or anything else; they wanted something different.

definitions: Strong refusal or rejection: 'no way', 'absolutely not', or 'out of the question'.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que te preste mi coche? Ni hablar, lo necesito para el trabajo.
examples.translation: Do you want me to lend you my car? No way, I need it for work.

examples.sentence: Cuando me pidieron que mintiera por ellos, les dije ni hablar.
examples.translation: When they asked me to lie for them, I said absolutely not.

examples.sentence: Ni hablar de cambiar los planes a última hora sin avisar a nadie.
examples.translation: No way we'll change the plans at the last minute without telling anyone.

definitions: Indicates inability or impossibility to speak with or about someone or something (literal or situational inability to talk).

examples.sentence: Desde ayer ni hablar con él, está enojado y no quiere que nadie se acerque.
examples.translation: Since yesterday, no talking with him; he's angry and doesn't want anyone near.

examples.sentence: Estaba tan nerviosa que ni hablar con nadie antes de la presentación.
examples.translation: She was so nervous that she couldn't talk to anyone before the presentation.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, ni hablar por teléfono porque se cortaba la señal constantemente.
examples.translation: During the storm, there was no talking on the phone because the signal kept cutting out.

examples.sentence: Me dijeron que ni hablar con los testigos hasta que llegue la policía.
examples.translation: They told me not to talk with the witnesses until the police arrive.

definitions: Literal: even if one were filled or intoxicated with wine (harto de vino = full/drunk on wine).

examples.sentence: Ni harto de vino haría algo así, eso va contra mis principios.
examples.translation: Not even if I were drunk would I do something like that; it goes against my principles.

examples.sentence: ¿Te gustaría robar del trabajo? Ni harto de vino, jamás me arriesgaría.
examples.translation: Would you like to steal from work? No way, not even drunk; I'd never risk it.

examples.sentence: Ni harto de vino aceptaría una propuesta tan injusta.
examples.translation: Not even under the influence of wine would I accept such an unfair proposal.

definitions: Figurative: emphatic refusal meaning 'not even under the influence' or 'I would never do that, not even if I were drunk'; denotes absolute rejection or distrust.

examples.sentence: Cuando me pidieron que mintiera, respondí ni harto de vino, no voy a hacerlo.
examples.translation: When they asked me to lie, I answered 'not even if I were drunk, I won't do it.'

examples.sentence: Ni harto de vino confiaría en alguien que me ha engañado tantas veces.
examples.translation: Not even if I were drunk would I trust someone who has deceived me so many times.

examples.sentence: Él dijo que ni harto de vino se quedaría en ese trabajo tan agotador.
examples.translation: He said that not even if he were drunk would he stay in that exhausting job.

definitions: Variant of 'ni harto de vino'; used to convey emphatic refusal or impossibility, equivalent to 'not even if I were full/drunk on wine'—i.e., 'absolutely not'.

examples.sentence: Ni harto vino aceptaría que me traten de esa manera.
examples.translation: Not even if I were drunk would I accept being treated that way.

examples.sentence: Aunque me ofrecieran mucho dinero, ni harto vino trabajaría en ese lugar.
examples.translation: Even if they offered me a lot of money, not even drunk would I work there.

examples.sentence: Ni harto vino iría a esa fiesta si no me invitan personalmente.
examples.translation: Not even if I were drunk would I go to that party if they don't invite me personally.

definitions: Literally: neither to go nor to come; used to describe movement that does not go in either direction.

examples.sentence: El ventilador estaba roto y ni iba ni venía el aire, simplemente estaba parado.
examples.translation: The fan was broken and neither did air go nor come, it was simply stopped.

examples.sentence: En el mapa, el camino que tomaron ni va ni viene hacia el destino correcto.
examples.translation: On the map, the path they took neither goes nor comes towards the correct destination.

examples.sentence: El carrito ni iba ni venía, parecía que estaba atascado en el mismo lugar.
examples.translation: The cart neither went nor came, it seemed stuck in the same place.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, la lancha ni iba ni venía debido a la fuerte corriente.
examples.translation: During the storm, the boat neither went nor came due to the strong current.

definitions: Figuratively: of no consequence or relevance; it makes no difference either way.

examples.sentence: Si decides venir o no, ni va ni viene para mí, yo haré lo mismo de todos modos.
examples.translation: Whether you decide to come or not makes no difference to me; I'll do the same anyway.

examples.sentence: Que él gane o pierda ni va ni viene para el resultado final del equipo.
examples.translation: Whether he wins or loses makes no difference to the team's final result.

examples.sentence: La opinión de los demás ni va ni viene cuando uno está seguro de sus decisiones.
examples.translation: The opinion of others makes no difference when one is sure of their decisions.

definitions: Literally: neither slow nor lazy; describing someone who is not dull or idle.

examples.sentence: Juan es ni lerdo ni perezoso; siempre cumple con sus responsabilidades a tiempo.
examples.translation: Juan is neither slow nor lazy; he always meets his responsibilities on time.

examples.sentence: Aunque el trabajo es difícil, María no es ni lerda ni perezosa y lo termina rápido.
examples.translation: Although the work is hard, María is neither slow nor lazy and finishes it quickly.

examples.sentence: No podemos decir que el equipo sea ni lerdo ni perezoso, porque han dado lo mejor de sí.
examples.translation: We can't say the team is slow or lazy because they have given their best.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué llamas a Pedro ni lerdo ni perezoso? Siempre está activo y atento.
examples.translation: Why do you call Pedro neither slow nor lazy? He is always active and attentive.

definitions: Figuratively: without hesitation or delay; promptly and decisively (used to introduce a swift action).

examples.sentence: Ni lerdo ni perezoso, Carlos tomó el teléfono y llamó a la policía en cuanto vio el accidente.
examples.translation: Without hesitation, Carlos took the phone and called the police as soon as he saw the accident.

examples.sentence: Cuando le dijeron que había un problema, ni lerdo ni perezoso, ella se puso a trabajar de inmediato.
examples.translation: When they told her there was a problem, she promptly got to work right away.

examples.sentence: Ni lerdo ni perezoso, el jefe decidió cancelar el proyecto sin pensarlo dos veces.
examples.translation: Without delay, the boss decided to cancel the project without a second thought.

definitions: Literally: not even crazy; denying that one is insane.

examples.sentence: Ni loco aceptaría una oferta tan peligrosa sin pensarlo bien.
examples.translation: Not even crazy would I accept such a dangerous offer without thinking it over.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que me arriesgue a eso? Ni loco, prefiero quedarme tranquilo.
examples.translation: You want me to risk that? No way, I'd rather stay calm.

examples.sentence: Ni loco me metería en ese lío sin tener un plan claro.
examples.translation: Not even crazy would I get into that mess without a clear plan.

examples.sentence: Aunque me pagaran mucho, ni loco trabajaría en ese lugar tan tóxico.
examples.translation: Even if they paid me a lot, not even crazy would I work in such a toxic place.

definitions: Figuratively: emphatic refusal or impossibility; 'no way' or 'I would never' (used to stress that the speaker would not do or accept something under any circumstances).

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres que le preste dinero? Ni loco, sé que no me lo va a devolver.
examples.translation: You want me to lend him money? No way, I know he won't pay me back.

examples.sentence: Ni loco aceptaría ese trabajo, las condiciones son pésimas y el sueldo es bajo.
examples.translation: I would never accept that job; the conditions are terrible and the salary is low.

examples.sentence: Cuando me preguntaron si quería ir a la fiesta con ellos, les dije ni loco, prefiero quedarme en casa.
examples.translation: When they asked me if I wanted to go to the party with them, I said no way, I’d rather stay home.

definitions: Literally: not even dead; denying that someone is dead.

examples.sentence: Ni muerto te voy a prestar mi coche después de lo que pasó la última vez.
examples.translation: Not even dead will I lend you my car after what happened last time.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que voy a perdonar eso? Ni muerto, no lo haré jamás.
examples.translation: Do you think I’m going to forgive that? No way, never will I.

examples.sentence: Ni muerto iría a esa reunión con personas que no respeto.
examples.translation: Not even dead would I go to that meeting with people I don’t respect.

examples.sentence: Ella dijo que ni muerta aceptaría cambiar su forma de pensar solo por complacer a otros.
examples.translation: She said she wouldn’t accept changing her way of thinking just to please others, not even dead.

definitions: Figuratively: emphatic negation meaning 'never' or 'you wouldn't catch me doing that' (used to express strong refusal or impossibility).

examples.sentence: ¿Que me pida que trabaje el fin de semana? Ni muerto lo haría, necesito descansar.
examples.translation: You want me to work on the weekend? Not a chance, I need to rest.

examples.sentence: Ni muerto voy a volver a confiar en esa persona después de lo que hizo.
examples.translation: You wouldn't catch me trusting that person again, no way.

examples.sentence: ¿Que me obliguen a rendir ese examen otra vez? Ni muerto, ya estudié suficiente.
examples.translation: That they force me to take that exam again? No way, I already studied enough.

definitions: Literally: neither to prick nor to cut; referring to actions of piercing or slicing.

examples.sentence: En ese taller no se permite ni pinchar ni cortar los materiales sin supervisión.
examples.translation: In that workshop, neither piercing nor cutting the materials is allowed without supervision.

examples.sentence: La enfermera explicó que durante la operación no se debe ni pinchar ni cortar fuera de lo indicado.
examples.translation: The nurse explained that during the operation neither pricking nor cutting should be done outside what is indicated.

examples.sentence: Para evitar accidentes, el instructor dijo que ni pinchar ni cortar las mangueras sin permiso.
examples.translation: To avoid accidents, the instructor said not to pierce or cut the hoses without permission.

examples.sentence: El artesano trabaja con cuidado para no ni pinchar ni cortar la delicada tela.
examples.translation: The artisan works carefully so as not to prick or cut the delicate fabric.

definitions: Figuratively: worthless or useless; of no practical use or efficacy.

examples.sentence: Este viejo teléfono ni pinchar ni cortar sirve, mejor compro uno nuevo.
examples.translation: This old phone is totally useless; I better buy a new one.

examples.sentence: El plan que propusieron ni pinchar ni cortar aportó nada a la solución del problema.
examples.translation: The plan they proposed was worthless; it didn't contribute anything to solving the problem.

examples.sentence: Su trabajo en el proyecto fue ni pinchar ni cortar, no se notó para nada.
examples.translation: His work on the project was useless; it didn't make any difference.

definitions: Literal: not even by a hint or the slightest suggestion; indicating the complete absence of even the smallest trace or possibility.

examples.sentence: Ni por asomo pensé que me llamarían para la entrevista tan rápido.
examples.translation: Not even by a hint did I think they would call me for the interview so soon.

examples.sentence: Cuando le pregunté si estaba interesado, ni por asomo mostró entusiasmo.
examples.translation: When I asked if he was interested, he didn’t even hint at enthusiasm.

examples.sentence: ¿Creías que iba a cambiar de opinión? Ni por asomo, sigue firme en su decisión.
examples.translation: Did you think I was going to change my mind? Not a chance, he remains firm in his decision.

examples.sentence: Ni por asomo se me pasó por la cabeza dejar el proyecto a medias.
