examples.sentence: La falta de descanso pasó factura en el rendimiento del equipo durante el torneo.
examples.translation: The lack of rest had negative consequences on the team’s performance during the tournament.

examples.sentence: Después de tantos años sin vacaciones, el cuerpo le pasó factura y tuvo que tomarse un descanso largo.
examples.translation: After so many years without vacations, his body paid the price and he had to take a long break.

definitions: To exact punishment or retribution; to make someone suffer the consequences of their actions.

examples.sentence: El juez decidió pasar factura al acusado por sus múltiples faltas y sancionarlo severamente.
examples.translation: The judge decided to exact punishment on the defendant for his multiple offenses and sanction him severely.

examples.sentence: Si sigues incumpliendo las normas, la empresa te pasará factura y podrías perder el empleo.
examples.translation: If you keep breaking the rules, the company will make you suffer the consequences and you could lose your job.

examples.sentence: El entrenador pasó factura a los jugadores que no asistieron a los entrenamientos con la reducción de minutos en el partido.
examples.translation: The coach punished the players who didn’t attend practice by reducing their playing time in the match.

definitions: To pass the ball in a sport or game, i.e., to deliver the ball to another player.

examples.sentence: Durante el partido, Juan pasó la bola rápidamente para evitar que el rival robara el balón.
examples.translation: During the match, Juan passed the ball quickly to prevent the opponent from stealing it.

examples.sentence: El entrenador nos pidió que pasáramos la bola con más precisión para crear mejores jugadas.
examples.translation: The coach asked us to pass the ball more accurately to create better plays.

examples.sentence: María siempre pasa la bola al compañero que está mejor posicionado para anotar.
examples.translation: María always passes the ball to the teammate who is better positioned to score.

examples.sentence: En el último minuto, el capitán pasó la bola al delantero, quien marcó el gol decisivo.
examples.translation: In the last minute, the captain passed the ball to the striker, who scored the decisive goal.

definitions: To transfer responsibility, a task, or a decision to someone else; to pass the buck or delegate.

examples.sentence: No intentes pasar la bola a otro; esta responsabilidad es tuya y debes afrontarla.
examples.translation: Don’t try to pass the buck to someone else; this responsibility is yours and you must face it.

examples.sentence: Cuando la jefa se fue de vacaciones, pasó la bola a su asistente para que resolviera los problemas urgentes.
examples.translation: When the boss went on vacation, she delegated the responsibility to her assistant to handle urgent issues.

examples.sentence: En las reuniones siempre intentan pasar la bola para no asumir las tareas difíciles, pero eso no funciona aquí.
examples.translation: In meetings they always try to pass the buck to avoid taking on difficult tasks, but that doesn’t work here.

definitions: To circulate a hat or container among a group in order to collect voluntary monetary contributions or donations.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta, los músicos pasaron la gorra para recaudar fondos para su próximo álbum.
examples.translation: At the party, the musicians circulated the hat to collect funds for their next album.

examples.sentence: Durante el evento benéfico, varios voluntarios pasaron la gorra entre los asistentes para apoyar a la causa.
examples.translation: During the charity event, several volunteers passed the hat among attendees to support the cause.

examples.sentence: Los artistas callejeros pasaron la gorra con destreza mientras tocaban para la multitud en la plaza.
examples.translation: The street performers skillfully circulated the hat while playing for the crowd in the square.

definitions: To solicit small-scale or informal financial support from acquaintances or the public.

examples.sentence: Cuando organizaron la colecta, decidieron pasar la gorra entre amigos para ayudar a su compañero enfermo.
examples.translation: When they organized the fundraiser, they decided to solicit donations among friends to help their sick colleague.

examples.sentence: La comunidad pasó la gorra para reunir dinero y reparar el parque infantil del barrio.
examples.translation: The community collected informal donations to raise money and fix the neighborhood playground.

examples.sentence: En el concierto improvisado, los músicos pasaron la gorra para cubrir los gastos del equipo de sonido.
examples.translation: At the impromptu concert, the musicians passed the hat to cover the sound equipment expenses.

definitions: To undergo severe suffering, mistreatment, or hardship; to be put through a very difficult or painful experience.

examples.sentence: Pasé las de Caín durante el servicio militar, enfrentando duras condiciones y castigos severos.
examples.translation: I went through very hard times during military service, facing harsh conditions and severe punishments.

examples.sentence: Los presos políticos pasaron las de Caín en la cárcel, soportando maltratos constantes y aislamiento.
examples.translation: The political prisoners endured great suffering in jail, enduring constant mistreatment and isolation.

examples.sentence: Cuando perdió su trabajo y su familia, pasó las de Caín, pero logró salir adelante con esfuerzo y apoyo.
examples.translation: When he lost his job and family, he went through terrible hardship, but managed to move forward with effort and support.

definitions: Literal reading: to experience the sufferings attributed to Cain (biblical reference), often used to emphasize the severity of the ordeal.

examples.sentence: Según la leyenda, aquellos que pasan las de Caín sufren castigos severos y prolongados por sus pecados.
examples.translation: According to the legend, those who experience the sufferings of Cain endure severe and prolonged punishments for their sins.

examples.sentence: En el relato bíblico, pasar las de Caín implica enfrentar consecuencias terribles por actos condenables.
examples.translation: In the biblical story, undergoing Cain’s sufferings means facing terrible consequences for condemnable acts.

examples.sentence: Al leer la historia, comprendí que pasar las de Caín es una metáfora para describir sufrimientos extremos y duraderos.
examples.translation: When reading the story, I understood that passing the sufferings of Cain is a metaphor to describe extreme and lasting suffering.

examples.sentence: Los personajes del cuento pasaron las de Caín, enfrentando pruebas dolorosas que los marcaron de por vida.
examples.translation: The characters in the story went through Cain’s sufferings, facing painful trials that marked them for life.

definitions: To endure serious trouble, humiliation, or hardship; a regional or playful variant used to indicate being made to suffer or to have a very hard time.
idiom: pasar las de Quico y Caco

examples.sentence: Durante la mudanza, pasamos las de Quico y Caco porque todo se rompió y perdimos muchas cajas.
examples.translation: During the move, we had a really hard time because everything broke and we lost many boxes.
examples.matched_span: pasamos las de Quico y Caco

examples.sentence: En la escuela, los novatos pasan las de Quico y Caco cuando los mayores les hacen bromas pesadas.
examples.translation: At school, the newcomers go through tough times when the older students play mean pranks on them.
examples.matched_span: pasan las de Quico y Caco

examples.sentence: No quiero pasar las de Quico y Caco en el trabajo, así que me estoy preparando para la presentación con mucho cuidado.
examples.translation: I don’t want to have a hard time at work, so I’m preparing for the presentation very carefully.
examples.matched_span: pasar las de Quico y Caco

definitions: Literal reading: to experience the difficulties associated with characters named Quico and Caco, used chiefly to convey the idea of going through a difficult or embarrassing situation.
idiom: pasar las de Quico y Caco

examples.sentence: En la narración, los protagonistas pasaron las de Quico y Caco enfrentando situaciones difíciles y cómicas a la vez.
examples.translation: In the story, the protagonists experienced the hardships of Quico and Caco, facing difficult and funny situations at the same time.
examples.matched_span: pasaron las de Quico y Caco

examples.sentence: El cuento describe cómo pasar las de Quico y Caco significa atravesar problemas que parecen sacados de personajes populares de la televisión.
examples.translation: The story describes how going through Quico and Caco’s sufferings means facing problems that seem taken from popular TV characters.
examples.matched_span: pasar las de Quico y Caco

examples.sentence: Cuando le pregunté qué había pasado, me dijo que había pasado las de Quico y Caco y no quería contar detalles.
examples.translation: When I asked what had happened, he told me he had a tough time like Quico and Caco and didn’t want to give details.
examples.matched_span: pasado las de Quico y Caco

examples.sentence: El autor usa la expresión pasar las de Quico y Caco para ilustrar la gravedad y lo cómico de ciertos conflictos sociales.
examples.translation: The author uses the expression to illustrate the severity and comedy of certain social conflicts.
examples.matched_span: pasar las de Quico y Caco

definitions: To call the roll or take attendance by reading a list of names to verify who is present or absent.

examples.sentence: La maestra pasó lista al comenzar la clase para asegurarse de que todos los estudiantes estuvieran presentes.
examples.translation: The teacher called the roll at the beginning of class to make sure all the students were present.

examples.sentence: Cada mañana, el capitán pasa lista para verificar que todos los soldados estén en sus puestos.
examples.translation: Every morning, the captain takes attendance to verify that all soldiers are in their positions.

examples.sentence: Durante el campamento, el monitor pasó lista antes de iniciar las actividades al aire libre.
examples.translation: During the camp, the counselor took attendance before starting the outdoor activities.

examples.sentence: ¿Pasaste lista en la reunión para saber quiénes asistieron y quiénes faltaron?
examples.translation: Did you call the roll in the meeting to know who attended and who was absent?

definitions: To perform a formal count or check of people or items, often implying an official or organized verification.

examples.sentence: En el inventario anual, el encargado pasó lista para contar todos los equipos presentes en el almacén.
examples.translation: In the annual inventory, the manager performed a formal count of all the equipment present in the warehouse.

examples.sentence: La supervisora pasó lista de los asistentes al taller para llevar un control oficial de participación.
examples.translation: The supervisor took attendance of the workshop participants to keep an official record of attendance.

examples.sentence: Antes del desfile, el organizador pasó lista para confirmar la presencia de todos los participantes inscritos.
examples.translation: Before the parade, the organizer took attendance to confirm the presence of all registered participants.

examples.sentence: Durante la auditoría, el equipo pasó lista de todos los materiales para asegurarse de que nada faltara.
examples.translation: During the audit, the team checked off all the materials to make sure nothing was missing.

definitions: To turn a page of a book, document, or other written material.

examples.sentence: Por favor, pasa página para continuar leyendo el siguiente capítulo del libro de texto.
examples.translation: Please turn the page to continue reading the next chapter of the textbook.

examples.sentence: Mientras él pasaba página, recordó que había olvidado marcar una nota importante en el margen.
examples.translation: As he turned the page, he remembered he had forgotten to mark an important note in the margin.

examples.sentence: Cuando pasamos página, encontramos ilustraciones que hicieron más entendible el contenido del manual.
examples.translation: When we turned the page, we found illustrations that made the manual’s content more understandable.

examples.sentence: No olvides pasar página con cuidado para no dañar las hojas antiguas del libro de la biblioteca.
examples.translation: Don’t forget to turn the page carefully so as not to damage the old pages of the library book.

definitions: To move on from a past event or situation emotionally or mentally; to let go of past grievances or preoccupations and begin anew.

examples.sentence: Después de la discusión, decidieron pasar página y enfocarse en resolver los problemas juntos.
examples.translation: After the argument, they decided to move on and focus on solving problems together.

examples.sentence: No podemos seguir lamentándonos; es hora de pasar página y mirar hacia el futuro con optimismo.
examples.translation: We can’t keep regretting; it’s time to turn the page and look to the future with optimism.

examples.sentence: Para superar esa etapa difícil, tuve que pasar página y dejar atrás resentimientos antiguos.
examples.translation: To overcome that difficult stage, I had to move on and leave old resentments behind.

definitions: To pass over the top of something; to go over an obstacle or elevation.

examples.sentence: El sendero pasa por alto una pequeña colina para evitar el terreno rocoso más difícil.
examples.translation: The trail passes over a small hill to avoid the more difficult rocky terrain.

examples.sentence: El río pasa por alto las tierras bajas y sigue su curso hacia el valle principal.
examples.translation: The river passes over the lowlands and continues its course to the main valley.

examples.sentence: El camino pasa por alto un puente viejo y dirige el tráfico hacia una estructura nueva y segura.
examples.translation: The road passes over an old bridge and directs traffic to a new and safe structure.

examples.sentence: Desde el avión, se puede ver cómo la ruta pasa por alto las montañas más elevadas sin dificultad.
examples.translation: From the plane, you can see how the route passes over the highest mountains without difficulty.

definitions: To overlook, omit, or fail to notice something; to ignore or leave out a detail, fault, or requirement, intentionally or unintentionally.

examples.sentence: El inspector pasó por alto varios detalles importantes en la revisión del informe final.
examples.translation: The inspector overlooked several important details in the review of the final report.

examples.sentence: No podemos pasar por alto las quejas de los clientes si queremos mejorar el servicio y la calidad.
examples.translation: We can’t ignore the customer complaints if we want to improve the service and quality.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que el juez pasará por alto esa irregularidad o tomará medidas al respecto?
examples.translation: Do you think the judge will overlook that irregularity or take action about it?

definitions: To pass through a ring or hoop, literally moving through a circular opening.

examples.sentence: El pequeño perro logró pasar por el aro sin ningún problema durante el entrenamiento.
examples.translation: The little dog managed to pass through the hoop without any problem during the training.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes pasar por el aro mientras hacemos el espectáculo de circo esta tarde?
examples.translation: Can you pass through the hoop while we do the circus show this afternoon?

examples.sentence: Ayer, los niños se divirtieron mucho intentando pasar por el aro que colgaba en el patio.
examples.translation: Yesterday, the kids had a lot of fun trying to pass through the hoop hanging in the yard.

examples.sentence: El gato fue cuidadosamente guiado para que pasara por el aro sin lastimarse.
examples.translation: The cat was carefully guided so that it passed through the hoop without hurting itself.

definitions: To submit to someone else's demands, pressure, or humiliating conditions; to give in or comply reluctantly.

examples.sentence: No quería aceptar las condiciones, pero al final tuvo que pasar por el aro para conservar su trabajo.
examples.translation: He didn't want to accept the conditions, but in the end he had to give in to keep his job.

examples.sentence: ¿Vas a pasar por el aro solo porque ellos te lo piden? No deberías ceder tan fácilmente.
examples.translation: Are you going to give in just because they ask you? You shouldn't give in so easily.

examples.sentence: Cuando la empresa impuso las nuevas reglas, todos los empleados pasaron por el aro, aunque no estaban de acuerdo.
examples.translation: When the company imposed the new rules, all the employees gave in, although they did not agree.

definitions: To go across or over a stone or paved surface; the literal act of passing by a stone.

examples.sentence: Para llegar al otro lado del río, tuvimos que pasar por la piedra que estaba en medio del camino.
examples.translation: To get to the other side of the river, we had to go over the stone that was in the middle of the path.

examples.sentence: Marta pasó por la piedra del sendero sin resbalar, a pesar de la lluvia intensa.
examples.translation: Marta walked over the stone on the trail without slipping, despite the heavy rain.

examples.sentence: Los ciclistas deben pasar por la piedra grande que bloquea parcialmente el camino para continuar la ruta.
examples.translation: The cyclists have to go over the big stone partially blocking the road to continue the route.

examples.sentence: Mientras caminábamos por el parque, pasamos por la piedra donde siempre nos sentamos a descansar.
examples.translation: While we were walking through the park, we passed by the stone where we always sit to rest.

definitions: To have sexual intercourse with someone, often used crudely and sometimes implying conquest, roughness, or casual sex.

examples.sentence: Después de la fiesta, Carlos presumió que había pasado por la piedra a varias chicas de la universidad.
examples.translation: After the party, Carlos bragged that he had slept with several girls from the university.

examples.sentence: No me gusta esa expresión porque pasar por la piedra suena muy vulgar y agresivo para referirse a algo íntimo.
examples.translation: I don't like that expression because 'pasar por la piedra' sounds very vulgar and aggressive to refer to something intimate.

examples.sentence: En la novela, el protagonista pasó por la piedra a la villana en una escena muy intensa y polémica.
examples.translation: In the novel, the protagonist slept with the villainess in a very intense and controversial scene.

definitions: To defeat, crush, or treat someone harshly; to subject someone to severe humiliation or punishment.

examples.sentence: El equipo rival nos pasó por la piedra en el partido, ganando con un marcador abrumador.
examples.translation: The rival team crushed us in the match, winning by an overwhelming score.

examples.sentence: No te dejes pasar por la piedra en la negociación, tienes que defender tus intereses con firmeza.
examples.translation: Don't let yourself be crushed in the negotiation, you have to defend your interests firmly.

examples.sentence: Después de la crítica pública, el político fue pasado por la piedra por los medios de comunicación sin piedad.
examples.translation: After the public criticism, the politician was harshly treated by the media without mercy.

definitions: To pass under the yoke of the Caudine Forks; literally to undergo the humiliating ritual of passing beneath a wooden yoke as imposed on defeated troops in antiquity.

examples.sentence: En la representación histórica, los soldados romanos pasaron por las horcas caudinas como símbolo de su derrota.
examples.translation: In the historical reenactment, the Roman soldiers passed under the Caudine Forks as a symbol of their defeat.

examples.sentence: El guía explicó que pasar por las horcas caudinas era un castigo humillante impuesto en la antigüedad.
examples.translation: The guide explained that passing under the Caudine Forks was a humiliating punishment imposed in ancient times.

examples.sentence: Durante el acto teatral, los actores representaron cómo los soldados enemigos pasaban por las horcas caudinas con resignación.
examples.translation: During the theatrical act, the actors portrayed how the enemy soldiers passed under the Caudine Forks with resignation.

examples.sentence: Los historiadores coinciden en que pasar por las horcas caudinas significaba aceptar la derrota sin resistencia.
examples.translation: Historians agree that passing under the Caudine Forks meant accepting defeat without resistance.

definitions: To be forced to accept humiliating terms or to endure a degrading ordeal, especially after defeat or submission.

examples.sentence: Después de perder la disputa, tuvimos que pasar por las horcas caudinas y aceptar todas las condiciones del contrato.
examples.translation: After losing the dispute, we had to endure humiliating terms and accept all the contract conditions.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que vas a pasar por las horcas caudinas si aceptas esas imposiciones injustas sin protestar?
examples.translation: Do you think you will have to endure a humiliating ordeal if you accept those unfair demands without protest?

examples.sentence: El candidato pasó por las horcas caudinas durante el proceso de selección, enfrentando preguntas muy difíciles y críticas severas.
examples.translation: The candidate went through a humiliating ordeal during the selection process, facing very tough questions and harsh criticism.

definitions: To inspect troops, a guard, or military formations formally, checking personnel, uniforms, arms, or readiness.

examples.sentence: El coronel pasó revista a las tropas antes de la ceremonia para asegurarse de que todo estuviera en orden.
examples.translation: The colonel inspected the troops before the ceremony to make sure everything was in order.

examples.sentence: Cada mañana, el sargento pasa revista para comprobar el estado de los uniformes y armas de los soldados.
examples.translation: Every morning, the sergeant inspects to check the condition of the soldiers' uniforms and weapons.

examples.sentence: Durante la visita oficial, el presidente pasó revista a la guardia de honor con gran solemnidad.
examples.translation: During the official visit, the president inspected the honor guard with great solemnity.

examples.sentence: Antes de salir a la misión, el comandante mandó pasar revista para verificar la preparación de sus hombres.
examples.translation: Before going on the mission, the commander ordered an inspection to verify his men's readiness.

definitions: To examine or review people, objects, or a list carefully; to carry out an organized inspection or overview.

examples.sentence: El profesor pasó revista a los trabajos entregados para seleccionar los mejores para la exposición.
examples.translation: The teacher reviewed the submitted works to select the best ones for the exhibition.

examples.sentence: ¿Has pasado revista a todas las propuestas antes de enviar el informe final al comité?
examples.translation: Have you reviewed all the proposals before sending the final report to the committee?

examples.sentence: En la reunión, pasaron revista a cada punto del proyecto para asegurarse de que no quedara nada pendiente.
examples.translation: In the meeting, they reviewed each point of the project to make sure nothing was left pending.

definitions: To endure great hardship or difficulty; to have a very hard time.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, los vecinos pasaron canutas tratando de proteger sus casas del viento y la lluvia.
examples.translation: During the storm, the neighbors had a very hard time trying to protect their houses from the wind and rain.

examples.sentence: Yo pasé canutas cuando me quedé sin dinero en un país extranjero sin conocer a nadie.
examples.translation: I had a really hard time when I ran out of money in a foreign country not knowing anyone.

examples.sentence: Si no estás preparado para las dificultades, vas a pasarlas canutas en este trabajo tan exigente.
examples.translation: If you're not prepared for difficulties, you will have a very hard time in this demanding job.

definitions: To suffer severely or endure extreme trouble; to go through a very difficult or punishing experience.

examples.sentence: Después del accidente, ella las pasó moradas tratando de recuperarse y volver a caminar.
examples.translation: After the accident, she suffered severely trying to recover and walk again.

examples.sentence: Los trabajadores las pasaron moradas cuando la fábrica cerró y se quedaron sin empleo de un día para otro.
examples.translation: The workers endured extreme trouble when the factory closed and they lost their jobs overnight.

examples.sentence: Si no estudias, las vas a pasar moradas en el examen de matemáticas que se viene la próxima semana.
examples.translation: If you don't study, you're going to have a very difficult time on the math exam coming next week.

definitions: To experience grave difficulties or danger; to go through a very bad or trying time.

examples.sentence: Los pescadores las pasaron negras cuando la tormenta los atrapó en alta mar sin posibilidad de regresar.
examples.translation: The fishermen experienced grave difficulties when the storm caught them at sea with no way to return.

examples.sentence: Juan las pasó negras durante su enfermedad, pero finalmente logró recuperarse.
examples.translation: Juan went through a very bad time during his illness, but he finally managed to recover.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué las pasaste negras en ese viaje? Cuéntame qué pasó exactamente.
examples.translation: Why did you have such a hard time on that trip? Tell me exactly what happened.

definitions: Figuratively, to endure great hardship or suffering; to have a very hard time.

examples.sentence: Durante el huracán, las pasé putas porque la casa casi se cae y no sabía qué hacer.
examples.translation: During the hurricane, I endured great hardship because the house almost collapsed and I didn't know what to do.

examples.sentence: No quiero imaginar cómo las pasaron putas los supervivientes del accidente aéreo en esas condiciones tan extremas.
examples.translation: I don't want to imagine how hard the survivors of the plane crash had it in such extreme conditions.

examples.sentence: Si no estudias para el examen final, vas a pasarlas putas tratando de aprobar sin saber nada.
examples.translation: If you don't study for the final exam, you're going to have a very hard time trying to pass without knowing anything.

definitions: Literally, a coarse expression whose literal words refer to 'spending them as whores'; used only idiomatically to convey intense difficulty or distress.

examples.sentence: Aunque algunas personas usan la expresión literalmente, las pasarlas putas es solo un modismo para expresar dificultad extrema.
examples.translation: Although some people use the expression literally, 'pasarlas putas' is only an idiom to express extreme difficulty.

examples.sentence: No es apropiado decir que alguien las pasó putas en público, pero todos entendemos que significa que sufrió mucho.
examples.translation: It is not appropriate to say that someone 'las pasó putas' in public, but we all understand it means they suffered a lot.

examples.sentence: El libro explica que la frase 'pasarlas putas' no debe interpretarse literalmente sino como una forma coloquial de decir que alguien tuvo muchos problemas.
examples.translation: The book explains that the phrase 'pasarlas putas' should not be interpreted literally but as a colloquial way of saying someone had many problems.

examples.sentence: En ciertos contextos, la expresión 'pasarlas putas' se usa para enfatizar el sufrimiento, aunque su origen es vulgar.
examples.translation: In certain contexts, the expression 'pasarlas putas' is used to emphasize suffering, although its origin is vulgar.

definitions: Literal: to pass something or to go past something (with the direct object pronoun 'lo').

examples.sentence: ¿Me puedes pasarlo, por favor? No alcanzo el libro que está en la mesa.
examples.translation: Can you pass it to me, please? I can't reach the book on the table.

examples.sentence: Él lo pasó rápidamente sin detenerse a saludar a nadie en la fiesta.
examples.translation: He passed by quickly without stopping to greet anyone at the party.

examples.sentence: No lo pasaron al siguiente nivel del juego porque no cumplió los requisitos mínimos.
examples.translation: They did not pass him to the next level of the game because he did not meet the minimum requirements.

examples.sentence: Mañana lo pasaré a recoger a las ocho para ir al aeropuerto juntos.
examples.translation: Tomorrow I will pick him up at eight to go to the airport together.

definitions: Figuratively, used with adjectives (e.g., bien, mal) to mean to experience something in a certain way; for example, 'pasarlo bien' = to have a good time, 'pasarlo mal' = to have a hard time.

examples.sentence: La verdad es que lo pasé muy bien en la fiesta de cumpleaños de Ana, me divertí mucho.
examples.translation: The truth is I had a great time at Ana's birthday party, I had a lot of fun.

examples.sentence: ¿Cómo lo pasaste en el concierto anoche? — Lo pasé mal porque había mucha gente y poco espacio.
examples.translation: How did you have it at the concert last night? — I had a hard time because there were too many people and little space.

examples.sentence: Si lo pasamos bien durante las vacaciones, deberíamos planear otro viaje pronto.
examples.translation: If we have a good time during the vacation, we should plan another trip soon.

definitions: To overlook or let something go when used in constructions such as 'pasarlo por alto' ('to pass over' or 'to ignore/overlook').

examples.sentence: El maestro lo pasó por alto cuando vio que el estudiante había cometido un error pequeño sin mala intención.
examples.translation: The teacher overlooked it when he saw the student had made a small mistake without bad intention.

examples.sentence: ¿No crees que deberíamos pasarlo por alto para evitar un conflicto innecesario con el jefe?
examples.translation: Don't you think we should overlook it to avoid an unnecessary conflict with the boss?

examples.sentence: Al revisar el informe, pasaron por alto algunos detalles importantes que afectaron la evaluación final.
examples.translation: When reviewing the report, they overlooked some important details that affected the final evaluation.

definitions: Literal: literally 'to pass it well,' a word-for-word rendering of the verb and object pronoun that has no independent literal use apart from idiomatic senses.

examples.sentence: El concepto de 'pasarlo bien' no tiene un sentido literal independiente sino que se usa como expresión de disfrute.
examples.translation: The concept of 'pasarlo bien' has no independent literal meaning but is used as an expression of enjoyment.

examples.sentence: Se dice que pasarlo bien es fundamental para el bienestar emocional, aunque literalmente significa 'pasar algo bien'.
examples.translation: It is said that having a good time is fundamental for emotional well-being, although literally it means 'to pass something well'.

examples.sentence: En la gramática española, 'pasarlo bien' es una construcción que solo tiene sentido en su uso idiomático.
examples.translation: 'Pasarlo bien' is a construction in Spanish grammar that only makes sense in its idiomatic use.

examples.sentence: Aunque la frase parezca literal, 'pasarlo bien' no se usa para expresar que algo se mueve bien sino para indicar disfrute.
examples.translation: Although the phrase seems literal, 'pasarlo bien' is not used to express that something moves well but to indicate enjoyment.

definitions: Figuratively, to have a good time; to enjoy oneself.

examples.sentence: Durante las vacaciones en la playa, lo pasamos bien con amigos y familia.
examples.translation: During the beach vacation, we had a good time with friends and family.

examples.sentence: ¿Lo pasaste bien en la boda de Laura? — Sí, fue una celebración muy alegre y divertida.
examples.translation: Did you have a good time at Laura's wedding? — Yes, it was a very happy and fun celebration.

examples.sentence: Si quieres que los niños lo pasen bien, organiza juegos y actividades entretenidas.
examples.translation: If you want the kids to have a good time, organize fun games and activities.

definitions: Figuratively, to have an excellent time; to have a blast.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta de anoche lo pasé bomba bailando hasta el amanecer con mis amigos.
examples.translation: At last night's party, I had a blast dancing until dawn with my friends.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres venir al parque de diversiones? Seguro que lo pasarás bomba con todas las atracciones.
examples.translation: Do you want to go to the amusement park? I'm sure you'll have a blast with all the rides.

examples.sentence: Cuando fuimos al concierto, lo pasamos bomba porque la banda tocó todas nuestras canciones favoritas.
examples.translation: When we went to the concert, we had a blast because the band played all our favorite songs.

definitions: Literal: a playful, nonliteral phrase combining 'pasarlo' with 'bomba' ('bomb'), used only idiomatically to intensify the sense of enjoyment.

examples.sentence: Aunque la expresión suena literal, 'pasarlo bomba' se usa solo idiomáticamente para expresar mucha diversión.
examples.translation: Although the expression sounds literal, 'pasarlo bomba' is only used idiomatically to express a lot of fun.

examples.sentence: No digas que vas a 'pasarlo bomba' en la reunión si no te gusta socializar, es solo una frase coloquial.
examples.translation: Don't say you're going to 'have a blast' at the meeting if you don't like socializing, it's just a colloquial phrase.

examples.sentence: El título del artículo era 'Cómo pasarlo bomba en vacaciones' y ofrecía consejos para disfrutar al máximo.
examples.translation: The article's title was 'How to have a blast on vacation' and offered tips to enjoy to the fullest.

examples.sentence: Los niños escucharon que iban a 'pasarlo bomba' en el parque y se emocionaron mucho antes de salir de casa.
examples.translation: The children heard they were going to 'have a blast' at the park and got very excited before leaving home.

definitions: Figuratively, to have a great time; to enjoy oneself hugely or on a grand scale.

examples.sentence: En la boda de mi primo, lo pasamos en grande bailando y celebrando hasta tarde.
examples.translation: At my cousin's wedding, we had a great time dancing and celebrating until late.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que lo pasarás en grande en el festival de música este año? — Sí, será increíble con tantas bandas famosas.
examples.translation: Do you think you'll have a great time at the music festival this year? — Yes, it will be amazing with so many famous bands.

examples.sentence: Si organizas una fiesta sorpresa, seguro que todos lo pasarán en grande y lo recordarán por mucho tiempo.
examples.translation: If you organize a surprise party, everyone will surely have a great time and remember it for a long time.

definitions: Literal: literally 'to pass it in grand style,' a phrase whose literal wording is not used outside the idiomatic meaning of having a large or splendid time.

examples.sentence: Aunque la expresión parece literal, 'pasarlo en grande' no se usa fuera del sentido idiomático de disfrutar mucho.
examples.translation: Although the expression seems literal, 'pasarlo en grande' is not used outside the idiomatic sense of having a lot of fun.

examples.sentence: Los profesores explicaron que 'pasarlo en grande' es una frase compuesta que indica disfrute intenso, no una acción física.
examples.translation: The teachers explained that 'pasarlo en grande' is a compound phrase indicating intense enjoyment, not a physical action.

examples.sentence: En la clase de español, aprendimos que 'pasarlo en grande' es una expresión figurada y no se traduce literalmente.
examples.translation: In Spanish class, we learned that 'pasarlo en grande' is a figurative expression and is not translated literally.

examples.sentence: Aunque 'pasarlo en grande' incluye palabras que parecen literales, su uso correcto es solo para expresar diversión y alegría.
examples.translation: Although 'pasarlo en grande' includes words that seem literal, its correct use is only to express fun and joy.

definitions: Literally, to experience or spend time with something involving a pipe or similar implement.

examples.sentence: El abuelo se sentó a pasarlo pipa mientras fumaba su pipa favorita en el jardín.
examples.translation: Grandpa sat enjoying his time while smoking his favorite pipe in the garden.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, pasé un rato pasándolo pipa charlando sobre viejas anécdotas con mis amigos.
examples.translation: During the meeting, I spent some time having a great time chatting about old stories with my friends.

examples.sentence: Cuando era joven, me gustaba pasar el tiempo pasándolo pipa en el taller de mi tío, donde había muchas pipas antiguas.
examples.translation: When I was young, I liked to spend time enjoying myself in my uncle's workshop, where there were many old pipes.

examples.sentence: Ella lo pasó pipa aprendiendo a usar la pipa de agua que compró en su viaje a Marruecos.
examples.translation: She had a great time learning to use the water pipe she bought on her trip to Morocco.

definitions: To have a great time; to enjoy oneself immensely.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta de cumpleaños de Marta, todos lo pasaron pipa bailando y cantando hasta la madrugada.
examples.translation: At Marta's birthday party, everyone had a great time dancing and singing until dawn.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que lo pasarás pipa en el concierto? Yo estoy seguro de que sí, porque la banda es espectacular.
examples.translation: Do you think you'll have a great time at the concert? I'm sure you will because the band is spectacular.

examples.sentence: Cuando viajamos a la playa, mis hijos lo pasaron pipa construyendo castillos de arena y jugando en el agua.
examples.translation: When we traveled to the beach, my kids had a great time building sandcastles and playing in the water.

definitions: Literally, to experience or spend time with something associated with a breast (teta).

examples.sentence: El bebé se quedó dormido mientras lo pasaban teta en brazos de su madre.
examples.translation: The baby fell asleep while being held closely in his mother's arms.

examples.sentence: Durante la exposición, el artista mostró objetos relacionados con el acto de pasarlo teta, como juguetes y pinturas antiguas.
examples.translation: During the exhibition, the artist showed objects related to the act of 'pasarlo teta,' such as toys and old paintings.

examples.sentence: En la granja, el niño ayudaba a alimentar a las vacas, pasando el tiempo pasándolo teta con animales y naturaleza.
examples.translation: On the farm, the boy helped feed the cows, spending time closely with animals and nature.

examples.sentence: La novela describe cómo el protagonista pasa el día pasándolo teta en una casa rural, disfrutando de la tranquilidad.
examples.translation: The novel describes how the protagonist spends the day relaxing in a country house, enjoying the tranquility.

definitions: To have a fantastic time; to enjoy oneself a lot.

examples.sentence: En las vacaciones de verano, lo pasamos teta recorriendo playas y probando comida local deliciosa.
examples.translation: On summer vacation, we had a fantastic time touring beaches and trying delicious local food.

examples.sentence: ¿Lo pasaste teta en la fiesta de anoche? Me dijeron que estuvo increíble y muy divertida.
examples.translation: Did you have a fantastic time at the party last night? They told me it was amazing and very fun.

examples.sentence: Si quieres que los niños lo pasen teta, organiza actividades que sean entretenidas y creativas.
examples.translation: If you want the kids to have a fantastic time, organize activities that are entertaining and creative.

definitions: Literally, to go past or beyond a physical line or boundary.

examples.sentence: Durante la caminata, nos pasamos de la raya y terminamos entrando en propiedad privada sin darnos cuenta.
examples.translation: During the hike, we went past the line and ended up entering private property without realizing it.

examples.sentence: No debes pasarte de la raya con la pintura para no manchar el piso del vecino.
examples.translation: You shouldn't go beyond the line with the paint so you don't stain the neighbor's floor.

examples.sentence: Ayer, el ciclista se pasó de la raya y chocó contra la acera, causando un pequeño accidente.
examples.translation: Yesterday, the cyclist went past the line and crashed into the sidewalk, causing a minor accident.

examples.sentence: ¿Te has fijado que el perro se pasó de la raya y está en el jardín del vecino jugando con sus flores?
examples.translation: Have you noticed that the dog went beyond the line and is in the neighbor’s garden playing with their flowers?

definitions: To overstep acceptable limits; to behave in a way that is excessive, unacceptable, or beyond what is permitted.

examples.sentence: Carlos se pasó de la raya cuando empezó a insultar a todos en la reunión, y el jefe tuvo que intervenir.
examples.translation: Carlos overstepped the line when he started insulting everyone at the meeting, and the boss had to intervene.

examples.sentence: No creas que puedes pasarte de la raya con tus comentarios; aquí tenemos normas de respeto.
examples.translation: Don’t think you can go too far with your comments; we have rules of respect here.

examples.sentence: Si sigues pasándote de la raya con tus bromas, nadie querrá trabajar contigo.
examples.translation: If you keep overstepping the limits with your jokes, no one will want to work with you.

definitions: Literally, to pass into or beyond the state of being 'clever' or 'smart.'

examples.sentence: En la clase de matemáticas, Pedro se pasó de listo y resolvió un problema que ni el profesor sabía cómo abordar.
examples.translation: In math class, Pedro went beyond being clever and solved a problem that even the teacher didn’t know how to approach.

examples.sentence: No creas que te pasas de listo solo porque aprendiste un truco nuevo, aún te falta mucho por entender.
examples.translation: Don’t think you’re being too clever just because you learned a new trick; you still have a lot to understand.

examples.sentence: Cuando Ana se pasó de lista, decidió presentar un proyecto que nadie había imaginado antes.
examples.translation: When Ana went beyond clever, she decided to present a project that no one had imagined before.

examples.sentence: Si te pasas de listo intentando engañarme, te equivocas, conozco bien tus tácticas.
examples.translation: If you act overly clever trying to fool me, you’re mistaken, I know your tactics well.

definitions: To act overly clever, crafty, or presumptuous in order to outsmart or take advantage of others, often provoking disapproval or retaliation.

examples.sentence: Luis se pasó de listo al intentar cobrar por un servicio que nunca ofreció, y sus clientes se quejaron.
examples.translation: Luis acted too clever when he tried to charge for a service he never provided, and his clients complained.

examples.sentence: No te pases de listo con tus compañeros; si intentas aprovecharte, terminarás perdiendo su confianza.
examples.translation: Don’t act overly clever with your coworkers; if you try to take advantage, you’ll end up losing their trust.

examples.sentence: Cuando Juan se pasó de listo con sus mentiras, sus amigos le dejaron de hablar.
examples.translation: When Juan acted too crafty with his lies, his friends stopped talking to him.

definitions: Literally, to over-tighten a screw or to turn it beyond its threads, potentially damaging the screw or thread.

examples.sentence: Al armar la mesa, me pasé de rosca y dañé la rosca del tornillo principal.
examples.translation: When assembling the table, I over-tightened the screw and damaged the main screw thread.

examples.sentence: No te pases de rosca al ajustar la tapa, porque puede romperse fácilmente.
examples.translation: Don’t over-tighten the cap, because it can easily break.

examples.sentence: El mecánico se pasó de rosca con la tuerca y tuvo que reemplazarla por completo.
examples.translation: The mechanic over-tightened the nut and had to replace it entirely.

examples.sentence: Si te pasas de rosca con el destornillador, el tornillo quedará inutilizable.
examples.translation: If you over-tighten the screw with the screwdriver, the screw will become unusable.

definitions: To go too far or to overdo something; to act excessively or inappropriately.

examples.sentence: María se pasó de rosca con la fiesta y terminó molestando a todos los vecinos.
examples.translation: María went too far with the party and ended up bothering all the neighbors.

examples.sentence: No quiero pasarte de rosca, pero creo que deberías calmarte un poco con tus críticas.
examples.translation: I don’t want to go too far, but I think you should calm down a bit with your criticisms.

examples.sentence: El jefe se pasó de rosca exigiendo que termináramos el proyecto en un día, fue imposible.
examples.translation: The boss went too far demanding we finish the project in one day; it was impossible.

definitions: Literal: to have the rice passed (i.e., for rice to be served or handed from one person to another).

examples.sentence: En la boda, me pasaron el arroz justo después del brindis principal.
examples.translation: At the wedding, they passed me the rice right after the main toast.

examples.sentence: ¿Te has pasado el arroz? Quiero asegurarme de que todos tengan suficiente para comer.
examples.translation: Have you passed the rice? I want to make sure everyone has enough to eat.

examples.sentence: Durante la cena familiar, siempre nos pasamos el arroz varias veces para que nadie quede sin.
examples.translation: During the family dinner, we always pass the rice several times so no one is left without.

examples.sentence: El camarero se pasó el arroz a la mesa de al lado por error y tuvo que corregirlo rápidamente.
examples.translation: The waiter passed the rice to the table next door by mistake and had to fix it quickly.

definitions: Figurative: to become past the age considered appropriate for marriage or to miss an important opportunity; to be out of date or to have missed the boat.

examples.sentence: Después de tantos años soltera, Marta siente que se le pasó el arroz y duda en buscar pareja.
examples.translation: After so many years single, Marta feels like she’s past the age for marriage and hesitates to look for a partner.

examples.sentence: No creas que se te pasó el arroz solo porque no te casaste joven; cada uno a su tiempo.
examples.translation: Don’t think you’ve missed the boat just because you didn’t marry young; everyone has their own time.

examples.sentence: Juan siempre dice que se le pasó el arroz para estudiar en el extranjero, pero nunca es tarde para intentarlo.
examples.translation: Juan always says he missed the chance to study abroad, but it’s never too late to try.

definitions: Literal: to pass one's life; to live through a period of time.

examples.sentence: Nos pasamos la vida trabajando sin descansar lo suficiente.
examples.translation: We spend our lives working without resting enough.

examples.sentence: Mi abuelo se pasó la vida viajando y conociendo diferentes culturas.
examples.translation: My grandfather spent his life traveling and getting to know different cultures.

examples.sentence: ¿No sientes que te pasas la vida atrapado en la rutina diaria?
examples.translation: Don’t you feel like you spend your life trapped in the daily routine?

examples.sentence: Se pasó la vida cuidando de su familia y ahora disfruta de la tranquilidad.
examples.translation: He spent his life taking care of his family and now he enjoys the peace.

definitions: Figurative: to spend one's life doing something (often implying a habitual, continuous, or excessive activity, or that the life is squandered in a particular pursuit or condition).

examples.sentence: Carlos se pasa la vida viendo series en lugar de salir y hacer algo productivo.
examples.translation: Carlos spends his life watching series instead of going out and doing something productive.

examples.sentence: Si te pasas la vida quejándote, no lograrás cambiar nada en tu situación.
examples.translation: If you spend your life complaining, you won’t manage to change anything in your situation.

examples.sentence: Mi hermana se pasa la vida estudiando para ser médico y está muy dedicada a su carrera.
examples.translation: My sister spends her life studying to become a doctor and is very dedicated to her career.

definitions: Literal: to pass seven towns (to go beyond seven towns).

examples.sentence: Para llegar a la ciudad vecina, tenemos que pasarnos siete pueblos y luego girar a la derecha.
examples.translation: To get to the neighboring city, we have to pass seven towns and then turn right.

examples.sentence: En el viaje por carretera, nos pasamos siete pueblos y terminamos en un lugar desconocido.
examples.translation: On the road trip, we went past seven towns and ended up in an unknown place.

examples.sentence: Si te pasas siete pueblos más, llegarás al río donde solíamos pescar de niños.
examples.translation: If you pass seven more towns, you will reach the river where we used to fish as kids.

examples.sentence: El autobús se pasó siete pueblos y tuvimos que caminar varios kilómetros para regresar.
examples.translation: The bus went past seven towns and we had to walk several kilometers to get back.

definitions: Figurative: to go too far; to exceed acceptable limits; to behave in an outrageous, excessive, or unacceptable way.

examples.sentence: Luis se pasó siete pueblos con sus comentarios ofensivos y todos quedaron en silencio.
examples.translation: Luis went way too far with his offensive comments and everyone fell silent.

examples.sentence: No quiero pasarte siete pueblos, pero creo que tu actitud fue inaceptable en esa reunión.
examples.translation: I don’t want to go too far, but I think your attitude was unacceptable in that meeting.

examples.sentence: Cuando Angela se pasó siete pueblos criticando el trabajo de los demás, perdió muchos amigos.
examples.translation: When Angela went too far criticizing others’ work, she lost many friends.

definitions: Literal: to pass three towns (to go beyond three towns).

examples.sentence: El tren se pasó tres pueblos antes de que el conductor se diera cuenta del error.
examples.translation: The train passed three towns before the driver realized the mistake.

examples.sentence: Para llegar al museo, tienes que pasarte tres pueblos y luego tomar el siguiente desvío.
examples.translation: To get to the museum, you have to pass three towns and then take the next detour.

examples.sentence: Nos pasamos tres pueblos y tuvimos que regresar porque olvidamos las entradas del concierto.
examples.translation: We passed three towns and had to go back because we forgot the concert tickets.

examples.sentence: El autobús se pasó tres pueblos y los pasajeros empezaron a quejarse por el retraso.
examples.translation: The bus went past three towns and the passengers began to complain about the delay.

definitions: Figurative: to go too far; to cross the line; to act excessively or unacceptably.

examples.sentence: No te pases tres pueblos con las bromas, que a algunos les pueden molestar mucho.
examples.translation: Don’t go too far with the jokes; some people might get really upset.

examples.sentence: Se pasó tres pueblos al criticar el trabajo del equipo frente al jefe, fue muy inapropiado.
examples.translation: He went too far criticizing the team’s work in front of the boss; it was very inappropriate.

examples.sentence: Cuando Mariana se pasó tres pueblos con sus exigencias, nadie quiso ayudarla.
examples.translation: When Mariana went too far with her demands, no one wanted to help her.

definitions: Literal: to hand or pass feminine plural items (the pronoun las refers to feminine plural direct objects) to someone.

examples.sentence: Por favor, pásame las llaves que están sobre la mesa, necesito salir rápido.
examples.translation: Please pass me the keys that are on the table; I need to leave quickly.

examples.sentence: Cuando llegues, pásales las invitaciones a las chicas que conociste en la fiesta.
examples.translation: When you arrive, pass the invitations to the girls you met at the party.

examples.sentence: ¿Me puedes pasar las toallas limpias? Las que usamos ya están sucias.
examples.translation: Can you pass me the clean towels? The ones we used are dirty.

examples.sentence: El camarero nos pasó las servilletas y los platos para que empezáramos a comer.
examples.translation: The waiter passed us the napkins and plates so we could start eating.

definitions: Figurative: to transmit or pass on something nonmaterial or not strictly physical (for example stories, traits, skills, diseases, or information) to other people or to future generations.

examples.sentence: Mi abuela me pasó las recetas de cocina que ella aprendió de su madre, son un tesoro familiar.
examples.translation: My grandmother passed me the cooking recipes she learned from her mother; they are a family treasure.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, se pasaron las experiencias para que todos aprendieran de los errores comunes.
examples.translation: In the meeting, they passed on experiences so everyone could learn from common mistakes.

examples.sentence: Los padres se pasan sus valores y tradiciones a los hijos para que no se olviden de sus raíces.
examples.translation: Parents pass their values and traditions to their children so they don’t forget their roots.

definitions: A cooked potato that retains heat; a literal hot potato.

examples.sentence: Cuidado con la patata caliente que saqué del horno, está muy caliente y puedo quemarme.
examples.translation: Be careful with the hot potato I took out of the oven; it’s very hot and I might burn myself.

examples.sentence: La patata caliente se enfrió rápidamente, pero todavía estaba tibia cuando la servimos.
examples.translation: The hot potato cooled down quickly, but it was still warm when we served it.

examples.sentence: Me pasaste la patata caliente sin guantes y ahora tengo quemaduras en los dedos.
examples.translation: You passed me the hot potato without gloves and now I have burns on my fingers.

examples.sentence: La patata caliente en la cesta todavía conserva su calor después de salir del microondas.
examples.translation: The hot potato in the basket still retains its heat after coming out of the microwave.

definitions: A sensitive, awkward, or controversial matter that people avoid handling and pass from one person or group to another.

examples.sentence: La responsabilidad del proyecto fue una patata caliente que nadie quiso asumir en la empresa.
examples.translation: The responsibility for the project was a hot potato that no one wanted to take on in the company.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que surge un problema político, el asunto se convierte en una patata caliente que se pasa de un partido a otro.
examples.translation: Whenever a political problem arises, the issue becomes a hot potato that is passed from one party to another.

examples.sentence: No me pongas esa patata caliente encima, yo no tengo tiempo para resolver ese lío ahora.
examples.translation: Don’t put that hot potato on me; I don’t have time to solve that mess right now.

definitions: A person, case, or thing that is quickly abandoned or rejected because it is troublesome or embarrassing.

examples.sentence: Después del escándalo, el alcalde se convirtió en una patata caliente para su propio partido.
examples.translation: After the scandal, the mayor became a hot potato for his own party.

examples.sentence: Cuando el caso judicial empezó a complicarse, fue una patata caliente que nadie quiso defender.
examples.translation: When the legal case became complicated, it was a hot potato that no one wanted to defend.

examples.sentence: El nuevo proyecto fue una patata caliente para el equipo porque implicaba mucho riesgo y presión.
examples.translation: The new project was a hot potato for the team because it involved a lot of risk and pressure.

definitions: A young duckling perceived as ugly or unattractive; the literal 'ugly duckling.'

examples.sentence: El patito feo del estanque estaba separado de los demás patitos por su plumaje grisáceo.
examples.translation: The ugly duckling in the pond was separated from the other ducklings because of its grayish plumage.

examples.sentence: Cuando nacieron los patitos, uno se veía diferente y todos lo llamaban el patito feo.
examples.translation: When the ducklings were born, one looked different and everyone called it the ugly duckling.

examples.sentence: El granjero vio que el patito feo no tenía el típico color amarillo brillante de los demás.
examples.translation: The farmer saw that the ugly duckling didn’t have the typical bright yellow color of the others.

examples.sentence: Aunque el patito feo nadaba con los otros, siempre parecía algo torpe y fuera de lugar.
examples.translation: Although the ugly duckling swam with the others, it always seemed somewhat clumsy and out of place.

definitions: A person regarded as awkward, unattractive, or an outsider who is underestimated but may later improve their appearance, status, or fortunes.

examples.sentence: De niño siempre fue el patito feo de la clase, pero ahora es un exitoso diseñador reconocido.
examples.translation: As a child, he was always the ugly duckling of the class, but now he is a successful and recognized designer.

examples.sentence: Marina era la patito feo del grupo, pero con el tiempo ganó confianza y cambió su estilo completamente.
examples.translation: Marina was the ugly duckling of the group, but over time she gained confidence and completely changed her style.

examples.sentence: No te sientas como el patito feo solo porque eres diferente; a veces eso es una fortaleza oculta.
examples.translation: Don’t feel like the ugly duckling just because you are different; sometimes that is a hidden strength.

definitions: A piece of bread; a literal fragment of baked bread.

examples.sentence: Compré un pedazo de pan recién horneado para el desayuno de esta mañana.
examples.translation: I bought a freshly baked piece of bread for this morning's breakfast.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres un pedazo de pan con queso para la merienda?
examples.translation: Do you want a piece of bread with cheese for the snack?

examples.sentence: El niño dejó caer un pedazo de pan en el suelo sin darse cuenta.
examples.translation: The child dropped a piece of bread on the floor without noticing.

examples.sentence: En la panadería, venden pedazos de pan muy crujientes y sabrosos.
examples.translation: At the bakery, they sell very crunchy and tasty pieces of bread.

definitions: A very kind, generous, or good‑natured person; someone of excellent character.

examples.sentence: Juan es un pedazo de pan, siempre dispuesto a ayudar a quien lo necesite.
examples.translation: Juan is a very kind person, always willing to help anyone in need.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes, ella es un pedazo de pan y nunca te haría daño intencionalmente.
examples.translation: Don’t worry, she’s a very good-natured person and would never hurt you intentionally.

examples.sentence: Mis abuelos son unos pedazos de pan; siempre nos reciben con una sonrisa y cariño.
examples.translation: My grandparents are very kind people; they always welcome us with a smile and affection.

definitions: To make a request that is inappropriate, futile, or unlikely to be fulfilled; literally, to ask for popcorn in the gulf (used figuratively for a misplaced or hopeless demand).

examples.sentence: Pedir cotufas en el golfo es como esperar que te den lo imposible en esta situación.
examples.translation: Asking for popcorn in the gulf is like expecting the impossible in this situation.

examples.sentence: No le pidas ayuda a Carlos para ese proyecto, sería como pedir cotufas en el golfo.
examples.translation: Don’t ask Carlos for help with that project; it would be like asking for popcorn in the gulf.

examples.sentence: Intentar convencerlo de cambiar de opinión es pedir cotufas en el golfo, no va a suceder.
examples.translation: Trying to convince him to change his mind is asking for popcorn in the gulf; it won’t happen.

examples.sentence: Cuando me preguntó si podía ganar la lotería, pensé que estaba pidiendo cotufas en el golfo.
examples.translation: When he asked me if he could win the lottery, I thought he was asking for popcorn in the gulf.

definitions: To ask for something impossible or unattainable; to make an unreasonable or excessive demand.

examples.sentence: Le pediste la luna pidiendo que hiciera todo el trabajo solo en un día.
examples.translation: You asked for the moon by requesting he do all the work alone in one day.

examples.sentence: No puedes pedir la luna esperando que te compren un coche nuevo sin trabajar para ello.
examples.translation: You can’t ask for the moon expecting to be bought a new car without working for it.

examples.sentence: Si sigues pidiendo la luna, la gente dejará de tomarte en serio.
examples.translation: If you keep asking for the moon, people will stop taking you seriously.

definitions: To request something extraordinarily difficult to obtain, often implying that the demander expects too much.

examples.sentence: Estás pidiendo la luna al querer que el proyecto termine en menos de una semana.
examples.translation: You’re asking for the moon by wanting the project finished in less than a week.

examples.sentence: No le pidas la luna a tu jefe cuando sabes que los recursos son limitados.
examples.translation: Don’t ask your boss for the moon when you know resources are limited.

examples.sentence: A veces pedimos la luna sin pensar en las dificultades reales que implica lograrlo.
examples.translation: Sometimes we ask for the moon without thinking about the real difficulties involved in achieving it.

definitions: To request or order potatoes or potato-based dishes, especially French fries, from a restaurant, café, or food service.

examples.sentence: En el restaurante, siempre pido papas fritas como acompañamiento de mi hamburguesa.
examples.translation: At the restaurant, I always order fries as a side dish for my burger.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes pedir papas para la mesa? Creo que a todos nos apetecen hoy.
examples.translation: Can you order potatoes for the table? I think we all feel like having some today.

examples.sentence: Cuando era niño, me encantaba pedir papas al camión de la esquina después de la escuela.
examples.translation: When I was a kid, I loved ordering fries from the corner truck after school.

examples.sentence: El camarero olvidó pedir papas para nosotros, así que tuvimos que recordárselo varias veces.
examples.translation: The waiter forgot to order potatoes for us, so we had to remind him several times.

definitions: Literally, to ask an elm tree to produce pears; an impossible request.

examples.sentence: Pedir peras al olmo es como esperar que un árbol que no da frutos te dé lo que quieres.
examples.translation: Asking for pears from the elm tree is like expecting a tree that doesn’t bear fruit to give you what you want.

examples.sentence: No tiene sentido pedir peras al olmo cuando el proyecto carece de recursos suficientes.
examples.translation: It makes no sense to ask for pears from the elm tree when the project lacks sufficient resources.

examples.sentence: Intentar que cambie de opinión es pedir peras al olmo, él es muy terco.
examples.translation: Trying to make him change his mind is like asking for pears from the elm tree; he is very stubborn.

examples.sentence: Pedir peras al olmo en ese negocio es esperar ganancias donde no hay demanda.
examples.translation: Asking for pears from the elm tree in that business is expecting profits where there is no demand.

definitions: To expect or demand something impossible or unreasonable; to ask for what cannot be provided.

examples.sentence: Estás pidiendo peras al olmo si esperas que te den un aumento sin cumplir tus objetivos.
examples.translation: You’re asking for the impossible if you expect a raise without meeting your goals.

examples.sentence: No le pidas peras al olmo, no va a cambiar su forma de trabajar por nadie.
examples.translation: Don’t ask the impossible; he’s not going to change his way of working for anyone.

examples.sentence: Pedir peras al olmo en esta situación solo te traerá frustración y decepción.
examples.translation: Asking for the impossible in this situation will only bring you frustration and disappointment.

definitions: To join, fasten, or tie a thread; a literal action in sewing or mending.

examples.sentence: María tuvo que pegar la hebra en el vestido porque se le soltó una costura justo antes de la fiesta.
examples.translation: María had to sew the thread onto the dress because a seam came loose right before the party.

examples.sentence: ¿Podrías pegar la hebra en esta chaqueta? Se está descosiendo el borde de la manga.
examples.translation: Could you join the thread on this jacket? The edge of the sleeve is coming undone.

examples.sentence: El sastre está pegando la hebra en el pantalón para que quede perfecto antes de entregarlo.
examples.translation: The tailor is fastening the thread on the pants so that they look perfect before delivering them.

examples.sentence: Ayer pegué la hebra en el suéter roto para que no se deshilachara más.
examples.translation: Yesterday I sewed the thread on the torn sweater so it wouldn’t fray any more.

definitions: To engage in informal conversation; to chat or have a friendly, often prolonged, talk.

examples.sentence: Cuando nos encontramos en el parque, siempre pegamos la hebra por horas sin darnos cuenta del tiempo.
examples.translation: When we meet in the park, we always chat for hours without noticing the time.

examples.sentence: No me gusta ir a esas fiestas donde nadie pega la hebra; prefiero conversaciones más amenas y largas.
examples.translation: I don’t like going to those parties where nobody engages in conversation; I prefer more pleasant and long talks.

examples.sentence: Si quieres, podemos pegar la hebra mientras tomamos un café, así me cuentas cómo te ha ido.
examples.translation: If you want, we can have a chat while we drink coffee, so you can tell me how things have been.

definitions: To attach or sew sleeves to a garment; to affix sleeve pieces in tailoring or mending.

examples.sentence: La modista pegó las mangas con mucha precisión para que el vestido quedara impecable.
examples.translation: The seamstress attached the sleeves very precisely so the dress would look flawless.

examples.sentence: Antes de la presentación, el sastre tuvo que pegar las mangas que se habían desprendido.
examples.translation: Before the presentation, the tailor had to sew the sleeves that had come off.

examples.sentence: Nos pidieron pegar las mangas a todas las camisas que estaban en el taller esta semana.
examples.translation: They asked us to attach the sleeves to all the shirts that were in the workshop this week.

examples.sentence: Ella aprendió a pegar las mangas correctamente durante su curso de costura el verano pasado.
examples.translation: She learned to sew on sleeves correctly during her sewing course last summer.

definitions: Literally, to stick or fasten an eye; a nonstandard literal formulation.

examples.sentence: El dibujo mostraba cómo pegar ojo en la máscara para que no se moviera durante la actuación.
examples.translation: The drawing showed how to fasten the eye on the mask so it wouldn’t move during the performance.

examples.sentence: Para el disfraz, necesitaron pegar ojo en la parte frontal con mucho cuidado.
examples.translation: For the costume, they needed to stick the eye on the front very carefully.

examples.sentence: El artesano pegó ojo en la escultura para que pareciera más realista.
examples.translation: The craftsman glued the eye on the sculpture to make it look more realistic.

examples.sentence: ¿Sabes cómo pegar ojo sin que se note? Estoy haciendo una máscara para Halloween.
examples.translation: Do you know how to fasten an eye without it being noticeable? I’m making a mask for Halloween.

definitions: To sleep or to get any sleep, often used in negative constructions to indicate inability to sleep.

examples.sentence: Anoche no pegué ojo porque escuchaba ruidos extraños en la casa.
examples.translation: Last night I didn’t get any sleep because I heard strange noises in the house.

examples.sentence: ¿Cómo haces para pegar ojo con tanto estrés en el trabajo? Yo no logro dormir bien.
examples.translation: How do you manage to sleep with so much stress at work? I can’t get a good night’s rest.

examples.sentence: Si no pegas ojo durante la noche, mañana no tendrás energía para la reunión importante.
examples.translation: If you don’t get any sleep during the night, you won’t have energy for the important meeting tomorrow.

definitions: To affix a patch to clothing or another surface; to attach a piece of material to cover a hole or reinforce an area.

examples.sentence: Para arreglar los pantalones rotos, pegó un parche en la rodilla con hilo resistente.
examples.translation: To fix the torn pants, he sewed a patch on the knee with strong thread.

examples.sentence: La madre pegó un parche en la chaqueta de su hijo porque tenía un agujero grande.
examples.translation: The mother attached a patch to her son’s jacket because it had a big hole.

examples.sentence: Me enseñaron cómo pegar un parche en la mochila cuando se desgasta la tela.
examples.translation: They taught me how to sew a patch on the backpack when the fabric wears out.

examples.sentence: Ayer pegamos un parche en el sofá para cubrir la mancha y que no se notara tanto.
examples.translation: Yesterday we put a patch on the sofa to cover the stain so it wouldn’t be so noticeable.

definitions: To implement a quick, improvised, or temporary solution to a problem; to apply a makeshift fix rather than a permanent repair.

examples.sentence: El técnico no pudo reparar la máquina, así que solo pudo pegar un parche para que funcionara un rato más.
examples.translation: The technician couldn’t fix the machine, so he could only apply a quick fix so it would work a little longer.

examples.sentence: No confío en ese arreglo, parece que solo pegaron un parche y pronto volverá a fallar.
examples.translation: I don’t trust that repair; it looks like they just put a band-aid on it and it will soon break again.

examples.sentence: Cuando el presupuesto es limitado, a veces solo se puede pegar un parche para salir del apuro momentáneamente.
examples.translation: When the budget is limited, sometimes you can only apply a temporary fix to get by for the moment.

definitions: To fall into or strike against a ravine, gorge, or steep depression; to collide with a steep natural decline.

examples.sentence: Durante la excursión, Carlos se resbaló y se pegó la quebrada mientras bajaba con cuidado.
examples.translation: During the hike, Carlos slipped and fell into the ravine while descending carefully.

examples.sentence: Los senderistas tuvieron que tener mucho cuidado para no pegarse la quebrada en el camino rocoso.
examples.translation: The hikers had to be very careful not to fall into the gorge on the rocky path.

examples.sentence: El guía explicó cómo evitar pegarse la quebrada cuando se atraviesan zonas peligrosas en la montaña.
examples.translation: The guide explained how to avoid falling into the ravine when crossing dangerous areas in the mountain.

examples.sentence: Ayer, mientras escalaba, casi se pega la quebrada porque perdió el equilibrio en una roca suelta.
examples.translation: Yesterday, while climbing, he almost fell into the ravine because he lost balance on a loose rock.

definitions: To experience a sudden collapse, failure, or major setback; to suffer a sharp and damaging reversal of fortunes.

examples.sentence: Después de invertir tanto en el negocio, se pegó la quebrada y perdió casi todo su capital.
examples.translation: After investing so much in the business, he suffered a major setback and lost almost all his capital.

examples.sentence: No quiero pegarme la quebrada en este proyecto; por eso estoy revisando todos los detalles antes de lanzarlo.
examples.translation: I don’t want to experience a failure with this project; that’s why I am reviewing all the details before launching it.

examples.sentence: Cuando la empresa se pegó la quebrada, muchas familias se quedaron sin trabajo de la noche a la mañana.
examples.translation: When the company collapsed, many families were left jobless overnight.

definitions: To shoot oneself with a firearm; to commit suicide by shooting or to suffer an accidental self-inflicted gunshot.

examples.sentence: El detective encontró la pistola con la que el sospechoso se había pegado un tiro en la habitación.
examples.translation: The detective found the gun with which the suspect had shot himself in the room.

examples.sentence: Después del accidente, el hombre se pegó un tiro accidentalmente y fue llevado al hospital de urgencia.
examples.translation: After the accident, the man accidentally shot himself and was rushed to the hospital.

examples.sentence: La novela describe cómo el personaje principal se pegó un tiro tras sufrir una gran depresión.
examples.translation: The novel describes how the main character shot himself after suffering a deep depression.

examples.sentence: ¿Sabes qué hacer si alguien se pega un tiro? Es importante llamar a emergencias inmediatamente.
examples.translation: Do you know what to do if someone shoots themselves? It’s important to call emergency services immediately.

definitions: Used hyperbolically to express extreme frustration, exasperation, or despair (equivalent to 'it makes one want to kill oneself'); an emphatic way to indicate that a situation is intolerable or highly distressing.

examples.sentence: Este tráfico me está volviendo loco, de verdad que quiero pegarme un tiro de la frustración.
examples.translation: This traffic is driving me crazy, I really want to shoot myself out of frustration.

examples.sentence: Si tengo que hacer otro informe más esta semana, me voy a pegar un tiro, no aguanto más tanto trabajo.
examples.translation: If I have to do one more report this week, I’m going to shoot myself; I can’t stand so much work anymore.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuché la noticia, casi me pego un tiro del disgusto que sentí.
examples.translation: When I heard the news, I almost wanted to shoot myself out of the distress I felt.

definitions: To attach or stick an object to oneself or to someone else (the clitic 'la' refers to a feminine object); a literal action of affixing.

examples.sentence: El niño se pegó la pegatina en la camiseta sin que su mamá se diera cuenta.
examples.translation: The boy stuck the sticker on his shirt without his mom noticing.

examples.sentence: ¿Me ayudas a pegarme la etiqueta en este cuaderno? Se me está cayendo.
examples.translation: Can you help me stick the label on this notebook? It’s falling off.

examples.sentence: Ella se pegó la flor en el pelo para la fiesta de disfraces.
examples.translation: She attached the flower in her hair for the costume party.

examples.sentence: El cartel fue pegado en la pared por los voluntarios para anunciar el evento.
examples.translation: The poster was stuck on the wall by the volunteers to announce the event.

definitions: To gain the advantage over someone, to get the better of someone, or to outsmart or swindle another person; to 'get one over' on someone.

examples.sentence: En la negociación, Carlos logró pegársela al cliente y consiguió mejores condiciones para la empresa.
examples.translation: In the negotiation, Carlos got the better of the client and secured better conditions for the company.

examples.sentence: No te dejes engañar, porque Marta siempre intenta pegársela a los demás en los juegos.
examples.translation: Don’t let yourself be fooled, because Marta always tries to get one over on others in games.

examples.sentence: Si quieres ganar, tendrás que ser más astuto para pegársela a tus oponentes.
examples.translation: If you want to win, you’ll have to be smarter to get the advantage over your opponents.

definitions: To have sexual intercourse with someone (crude or slang usage).

examples.sentence: En la película, el personaje principal se la pegó a la chica de la fiesta sin que nadie lo notara.
examples.translation: In the movie, the main character hooked up with the girl at the party without anyone noticing.

examples.sentence: No hables con ellos sobre eso, ya sabes que se la pegaron el fin de semana pasado y prefieren mantenerlo en secreto.
examples.translation: Don’t talk to them about that, you know they slept together last weekend and prefer to keep it secret.

examples.sentence: Cuando Pedro y Ana se la pegaron, todos en la oficina comenzaron a hacer rumores al día siguiente.
examples.translation: When Pedro and Ana hooked up, everyone in the office started gossiping the next day.

definitions: To defeat or beat someone in a game, contest, or competition.

examples.sentence: El equipo local le pegó la se a sus rivales en el partido final y ganó el campeonato.
examples.translation: The local team beat their rivals in the final match and won the championship.

examples.sentence: Si quieres pegársela a los otros jugadores, tendrás que practicar mucho más.
examples.translation: If you want to beat the other players, you’ll have to practice a lot more.

examples.sentence: Ayer me la pegué en el torneo de ajedrez, pero aprendí mucho para la próxima vez.
examples.translation: Yesterday I lost badly in the chess tournament, but I learned a lot for next time.

definitions: Literally, for a blanket or cover to stick to someone or cling to them.

examples.sentence: Al despertar, la cobija se me pegó a la espalda porque había sudado mucho durante la noche.
examples.translation: Upon waking up, the blanket stuck to my back because I had sweated a lot during the night.

examples.sentence: No puedo moverme bien porque la cobija se me pegó en los pies y me tiene atrapado.
examples.translation: I can’t move well because the blanket stuck to my feet and has me trapped.

examples.sentence: Cuando hace frío, la cobija se me pega más porque el cuerpo genera más humedad.
examples.translation: When it’s cold, the blanket sticks to me more because the body produces more moisture.

examples.sentence: A veces la cobija se me pega tanto que no logro despegarla sin que me despierte.
examples.translation: Sometimes the blanket clings to me so much that I can’t pull it off without waking up.

definitions: Figuratively, to be left without protection, support, or advantages; to find oneself deprived of customary safeguards or privileges, often as the result of someone else taking them or of a sudden change.
