examples.translation: When I criticized the work, I noticed several got uncomfortable; those who react are usually implicated.

examples.sentence: No te ofendas por lo que dije; quien se pica, ajos come, es solo una expresión.
examples.translation: Don’t be offended by what I said; those who get upset usually have something to do with it; it’s just an expression.

definitions: An invocation expressing submission to or appeal for God's will: 'may God...' or 'God willing'; used to ask that God grant or allow something to happen.

examples.sentence: Mañana tendremos la reunión importante, quiera Dios que todo salga bien.
examples.translation: Tomorrow we will have the important meeting, God willing everything goes well.

examples.sentence: Quiera Dios que Ana se recupere pronto después de la operación.
examples.translation: May God grant that Ana recovers quickly after the surgery.

examples.sentence: Si quiera Dios que podamos viajar juntos este verano, será una gran aventura.
examples.translation: If God wills that we can travel together this summer, it will be a great adventure.

definitions: An exclamatory formula used to express a strong wish that something not occur: 'God forbid' or 'let us hope not.'

examples.sentence: Quiera Dios que no vuelva a pasar un accidente como ese en la carretera.
examples.translation: God forbid that an accident like that happens again on the road.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que habrá problemas? Quiera Dios que no, porque ya tenemos suficiente estrés.
examples.translation: Do you think there will be problems? Let us hope not, because we already have enough stress.

examples.sentence: Quiera Dios que no llueva durante la boda al aire libre de Marta.
examples.translation: God forbid it rains during Marta's outdoor wedding.

definitions: A phrase used with a deity or fate to express the wish that something not happen: 'may [God/Allah] not...' or 'God forbid; hopefully not.'

examples.sentence: Quiera que no ocurra ningún accidente durante el viaje de regreso.
examples.translation: May [God/Allah] not let any accident happen during the return trip.

examples.sentence: Le pedí a Dios que quiera que no nos falle la luz esta noche tan importante.
examples.translation: I asked God that hopefully the power doesn't fail us this important night.

examples.sentence: Quiera que no tengamos que enfrentar más problemas después de todo lo que pasó.
examples.translation: God forbid we have to face more problems after everything that happened.

definitions: A concessive connector meaning 'no matter how much' or 'however much ... (someone may do or claim),' used to indicate that that action will not change the stated result.

examples.sentence: Quiera que no me digas que ya terminaste, porque aún falta mucho trabajo.
examples.translation: No matter how much you tell me you finished, there is still a lot of work left.

examples.sentence: Quiera que no intentes convencerme otra vez; mi decisión está tomada.
examples.translation: However much you try to convince me again; my decision is made.

examples.sentence: Quiera que no insistan en cambiar las reglas, el acuerdo es claro tal como está.
examples.translation: No matter how much they insist on changing the rules, the agreement is clear as it is.

definitions: A concessive expression meaning 'whether you like it or not' or 'regardless of whether you want it,' used to assert inevitability or insist on a fact.

examples.sentence: Quieras que no, tendrás que enfrentarte a las consecuencias de tus decisiones.
examples.translation: Whether you like it or not, you will have to face the consequences of your decisions.

examples.sentence: Sabes que, quieras que no, este problema afectará a todo el equipo.
examples.translation: You know that, whether you like it or not, this problem will affect the whole team.

examples.sentence: Quieras que no, el tiempo pasa y debemos adaptarnos a los cambios.
examples.translation: Whether you like it or not, time passes and we must adapt to changes.

definitions: A phrase meaning 'as many/much as you want' when describing quantity or choice, often followed by a clause stating a consequence.

examples.sentence: Puedes comer quieras que no, pero si abusas del postre, te dolerá el estómago.
examples.translation: You can eat as much as you want, but if you overdo the dessert, your stomach will hurt.

examples.sentence: Quieras que no, podrás elegir cuantos libros quieras para tu colección personal.
examples.translation: You may choose as many books as you want for your personal collection.

examples.sentence: Toma quieras que no, pero recuerda que hay un límite en la cantidad permitida.
examples.translation: Take as much as you want, but remember there's a limit on the allowed quantity.

definitions: A literal statement of intent meaning 'I want to say' or 'I intend to say,' used when introducing what the speaker wishes to express.

examples.sentence: Quiero decir que estoy muy agradecido por todo el apoyo que me han dado.
examples.translation: I want to say that I am very grateful for all the support you have given me.

examples.sentence: Cuando digo 'mañana', quiero decir que será en las primeras horas del día.
examples.translation: When I say 'tomorrow,' I mean it will be in the early hours of the day.

examples.sentence: Quiero decir algo importante antes de que termine la reunión de hoy.
examples.translation: I want to say something important before today's meeting ends.

examples.sentence: Si quieres entender mi punto, quiero decir que necesitamos más tiempo para analizar.
examples.translation: If you want to understand my point, I mean that we need more time to analyze.

definitions: A discourse marker used to clarify, restate, or emphasize a previous remark: 'I mean,' 'that is to say.'

examples.sentence: No me gustó la película, quiero decir, esperaba algo mucho mejor.
examples.translation: I didn't like the movie, I mean, I expected something much better.

examples.sentence: Ella está muy ocupada, quiero decir, no ha tenido tiempo para llamar a nadie esta semana.
examples.translation: She is very busy, I mean, she hasn't had time to call anyone this week.

examples.sentence: Fue una decisión difícil; quiero decir, no todos estaban de acuerdo con el plan.
examples.translation: It was a difficult decision; I mean, not everyone agreed with the plan.

definitions: The literal designation 'fifth pine,' referring to a specific tree counted as fifth in a sequence.

examples.sentence: El quinto pino del jardín está justo al lado del rosal que plantamos el año pasado.
examples.translation: The fifth pine in the garden is right next to the rose bush we planted last year.

examples.sentence: Conté los árboles y el quinto pino es el que tiene la forma más peculiar.
examples.translation: I counted the trees and the fifth pine is the one with the most peculiar shape.

examples.sentence: En el parque, el quinto pino es el que marca el límite con el bosque natural.
examples.translation: In the park, the fifth pine marks the boundary with the natural forest.

examples.sentence: Nos sentamos bajo el quinto pino para protegernos un poco del sol de la tarde.
examples.translation: We sat under the fifth pine to protect ourselves a bit from the afternoon sun.

definitions: A figurative expression meaning a very remote, out-of-the-way place; the middle of nowhere; used to indicate great distance or inconvenience.

examples.sentence: La casa de mi tío queda en el quinto pino, es casi imposible llegar sin GPS.
examples.translation: My uncle's house is in the middle of nowhere; it's almost impossible to get there without GPS.

examples.sentence: Nos enviaron a trabajar en una oficina en el quinto pino, lejos de la ciudad y sin transporte público.
examples.translation: They sent us to work in an office in the middle of nowhere, far from the city and without public transport.

examples.sentence: ¿Quieres venir a la fiesta? Está en el quinto pino, pero valdrá la pena el viaje.
examples.translation: Do you want to come to the party? It's in the middle of nowhere, but the trip will be worth it.

definitions: To remove the puff-pastry layer from a cake; a literal culinary action.

examples.sentence: Para hacer la tarta más suave, debes quitar el hojaldre al pastel antes de añadir la crema.
examples.translation: To make the cake softer, you have to remove the puff pastry from the cake before adding the cream.

examples.sentence: El chef nos explicó que quitar el hojaldre al pastel es un paso importante en esta receta tradicional.
examples.translation: The chef explained to us that removing the puff pastry from the cake is an important step in this traditional recipe.

examples.sentence: Mientras preparaba el postre, se quedó sin paciencia y quitó el hojaldre al pastel demasiado rápido.
examples.translation: While preparing the dessert, she ran out of patience and removed the puff pastry from the cake too quickly.

examples.sentence: Para decorar, primero tienes que quitar el hojaldre al pastel sin romper la base.
examples.translation: To decorate, first you have to remove the puff pastry from the cake without breaking the base.

definitions: To take away the most attractive, enjoyable, or essential part of something, thereby diminishing its value or appeal.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que le quiten el hojaldre al pastel, eso arruina la esencia de la fiesta.
examples.translation: I don't like when they take away the best part, it ruins the essence of the party.

examples.sentence: El jefe quitó el hojaldre al pastel al cancelar los beneficios que habíamos ganado con esfuerzo.
examples.translation: The boss took away the best part by canceling the benefits we had earned with effort.

examples.sentence: Si sigues quitando el hojaldre al pastel, nadie querrá participar en el proyecto.
examples.translation: If you keep taking away the best part, no one will want to join the project.

definitions: To remove iron from something; a literal, physical action.

examples.sentence: Para fabricar el acero, primero hay que quitar hierro del mineral extraído.
examples.translation: To make steel, first you have to remove iron from the extracted ore.

examples.sentence: El proceso industrial consiste en quitar hierro de la mezcla para obtener un material más puro.
examples.translation: The industrial process consists of removing iron from the mixture to obtain a purer material.

examples.sentence: En el taller, se utilizó una máquina especial para quitar hierro de las piezas defectuosas.
examples.translation: In the workshop, a special machine was used to remove iron from the defective parts.

examples.sentence: Antes de continuar con la soldadura, el operario tuvo que quitar hierro oxidado de la superficie.
examples.translation: Before continuing with the welding, the worker had to remove rusted iron from the surface.

definitions: To downplay or minimize the seriousness, importance, or emotional impact of an event or statement; to play something down.

examples.sentence: Aunque la situación es grave, prefiero quitar hierro y buscar una solución positiva.
examples.translation: Although the situation is serious, I prefer to downplay it and look for a positive solution.

examples.sentence: No le quites hierro al problema; necesitamos enfrentarlo con sinceridad.
examples.translation: Don't downplay the problem; we need to face it honestly.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre quita hierro cuando hablamos de sus errores para no sentir culpa.
examples.translation: She always plays down her mistakes when we talk about them to avoid feeling guilty.

definitions: To remove a literal weight from one's body or from above oneself.

examples.sentence: Después de hacer ejercicio, sentí cómo se me quitaba un peso de encima al quitarme la mochila.
examples.translation: After exercising, I felt a weight lifted off me when I took off my backpack.

examples.sentence: El médico me ayudó a quitar un peso de encima al extraer el objeto extraño de mi pierna.
examples.translation: The doctor helped me remove a literal weight from my leg by extracting the foreign object.

examples.sentence: Cuando me quité el casco, sentí que se me quitaba un peso de encima después de horas de trabajo.
examples.translation: When I took off the helmet, I felt a weight lifted off me after hours of work.
examples.matched_span: quité el casco, sentí que se me quitaba un peso de encima

examples.sentence: Los mineros se quitaban un peso de encima al salir de la mina después de largas jornadas.
examples.translation: The miners removed a literal weight from above themselves when they left the mine after long shifts.

definitions: To feel relieved after removing a burden, worry, or obligation; to be freed from emotional or practical pressure.

examples.sentence: Al terminar el examen, me quité un peso de encima y pude relajarme por fin.
examples.translation: After finishing the exam, I felt relieved and could finally relax.

examples.sentence: Cuando le conté la verdad a mis padres, se me quitó un peso de encima que llevaba meses cargando.
examples.translation: When I told my parents the truth, a burden I had carried for months was lifted off me.
examples.matched_span: se me quitó un peso de encima

examples.sentence: Si hablas con el jefe y aclaras la situación, te quitarás un peso de encima seguro.
examples.translation: If you talk to the boss and clear things up, you'll definitely feel relieved.

definitions: The tail of a lizard; a literal anatomical description.

examples.sentence: En el museo de ciencias, mostraron un rabo de lagartija conservado en formol para estudiar su anatomía.
examples.translation: At the science museum, they showed a lizard's tail preserved in formalin to study its anatomy.

examples.sentence: Cuando la lagartija perdió el rabo, quedó más vulnerable ante los depredadores.
examples.translation: When the lizard lost its tail, it became more vulnerable to predators.

examples.sentence: El biólogo explicó cómo el rabo de lagartija puede regenerarse después de ser cortado.
examples.translation: The biologist explained how the lizard's tail can regenerate after being cut off.

examples.sentence: El niño encontró un rabo de lagartija en el jardín y lo llevó a la escuela para mostrárselo a la profesora.
examples.translation: The boy found a lizard's tail in the garden and took it to school to show his teacher.

definitions: A small, insignificant remnant or leftover; something minor or negligible.

examples.sentence: Después de repartir los premios, sólo quedó un rabo de lagartija, una pequeña medalla para el último lugar.
examples.translation: After handing out the prizes, only a tiny remnant was left, a small medal for last place.

examples.sentence: Me dieron un rabo de lagartija de la herencia, apenas unas monedas que no valen mucho.
examples.translation: I got a negligible part of the inheritance, just a few coins that aren't worth much.

examples.sentence: El descuento que me ofrecieron fue un rabo de lagartija comparado con lo que esperaba.
examples.translation: The discount they offered me was a tiny leftover compared to what I expected.

definitions: Literally, a green tail.

examples.sentence: El camaleón tiene un rabo verde que le ayuda a camuflarse entre las hojas.
examples.translation: The chameleon has a green tail that helps it camouflage among the leaves.

examples.sentence: En el dibujo, el dragón tenía un rabo verde que parecía brillar bajo el sol.
examples.translation: In the drawing, the dragon had a green tail that seemed to shine under the sun.

examples.sentence: Los niños jugaron a atrapar al lagarto con su rabo verde moviéndose rápidamente.
examples.translation: The children played at catching the lizard with its green tail moving quickly.

examples.sentence: El rabo verde del animal es una característica que lo distingue de otras especies similares.
examples.translation: The green tail of the animal is a feature that distinguishes it from other similar species.

definitions: A lecherous or sexually predatory person, typically an older man who makes unwelcome sexual advances; used as an insulting label.

examples.sentence: Cuidado con ese hombre, es un rabo verde que no deja de hacer comentarios inapropiados.
examples.translation: Be careful with that man; he's a lecher who keeps making inappropriate comments.

examples.sentence: No soporto a los rabos verdes que acosan a las mujeres en el transporte público.
examples.translation: I can't stand the lecherous men who harass women on public transport.

examples.sentence: Mi tío es un rabo verde que siempre intenta ligar con las jóvenes en las fiestas familiares.
examples.translation: My uncle is a lecher who always tries to flirt with young women at family parties.

definitions: To grate a potato (literal action of shredding a potato on a grater).

examples.sentence: Para preparar la receta, primero tienes que rallar la papa finamente con este rallador.
examples.translation: To prepare the recipe, first you have to grate the potato finely with this grater.

examples.sentence: María estuvo rallando la papa durante media hora para hacer las tortitas perfectas.
examples.translation: María was grating the potato for half an hour to make perfect pancakes.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes rallar la papa mientras yo corto las cebollas para la sopa?
examples.translation: Can you grate the potato while I chop the onions for the soup?

examples.sentence: Antes de freírlas, es importante rallar la papa y escurrir el exceso de agua.
examples.translation: Before frying them, it's important to grate the potato and drain the excess water.

definitions: To annoy, pester, or bother someone persistently; to get on someone's nerves.

examples.sentence: Deja de rallarme la papa con tus preguntas, que ya entendí lo que dijiste.
examples.translation: Stop bothering me with your questions; I already understood what you said.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano no para de rallarme la papa cuando estoy estudiando para el examen.
examples.translation: My brother doesn’t stop pestering me when I’m studying for the exam.

examples.sentence: Si sigues rallando la papa, voy a pedir que te calles de una vez por todas.
examples.translation: If you keep annoying me, I’m going to ask you to be quiet once and for all.

definitions: A branch from an olive tree (literal object).

examples.sentence: El artista talló una rama de olivo para decorar el altar de la iglesia.
examples.translation: The artist carved an olive branch to decorate the church altar.

examples.sentence: Durante la ceremonia, el sacerdote sostuvo una rama de olivo como símbolo de paz.
examples.translation: During the ceremony, the priest held an olive branch as a symbol of peace.

examples.sentence: Encontraron una rama de olivo seca en el jardín que había caído del árbol antiguo.
examples.translation: They found a dry olive branch in the garden that had fallen from the old tree.

examples.sentence: La rama de olivo fue colocada cuidadosamente sobre la mesa para el ritual ancestral.
examples.translation: The olive branch was carefully placed on the table for the ancestral ritual.

definitions: A symbol or offer of peace, truce, reconciliation, or conciliation.

examples.sentence: Después de la discusión, Juan le ofreció a Pedro una rama de olivo para hacer las paces.
examples.translation: After the argument, Juan offered Pedro an olive branch to make peace.

examples.sentence: En la reunión, la empresa lanzó una rama de olivo proponiendo renegociar el contrato.
examples.translation: In the meeting, the company extended an olive branch by proposing to renegotiate the contract.

examples.sentence: Ella decidió dar una rama de olivo a su hermana para superar el malentendido que tenían.
examples.translation: She decided to offer an olive branch to her sister to overcome the misunderstanding they had.

definitions: Infrequently; on few occasions; seldom.

examples.sentence: Rara vez salgo los fines de semana porque prefiero descansar en casa.
examples.translation: I rarely go out on weekends because I prefer to rest at home.

examples.sentence: ¿Sabías que Pedro rara vez come dulces por su dieta estricta?
examples.translation: Did you know that Pedro seldom eats sweets because of his strict diet?

examples.sentence: Aunque me gusta el cine, rara vez tengo tiempo para ir al estreno de una película.
examples.translation: Although I like the movies, I rarely have time to go to a film premiere.

definitions: To be on equal terms or directly opposed one to another; head-to-head or matched closely.

examples.sentence: En el campeonato de ajedrez, los dos finalistas estaban ras con ras hasta el último movimiento.
examples.translation: In the chess championship, the two finalists were neck and neck until the last move.

examples.sentence: No podemos permitir que estas empresas estén ras con ras, necesitamos una ventaja competitiva clara.
examples.translation: We can’t allow these companies to be evenly matched; we need a clear competitive advantage.

examples.sentence: Durante el debate, los candidatos estuvieron ras con ras en sus argumentos, sin que ninguno dominara.
examples.translation: During the debate, the candidates were head-to-head in their arguments, with neither dominating.

definitions: Literal rendering of two similar surfaces or edges rubbing or scraping against each other.

examples.sentence: Mientras caminaba, noté que las dos tablas del suelo estaban ras con ras y se rozaban con cada paso.
examples.translation: As I walked, I noticed that the two floorboards were edge to edge and rubbed against each other with every step.

examples.sentence: El carpintero explicó que cuando las puertas están ras con ras, pueden abrirse sin problemas.
examples.translation: The carpenter explained that when the doors are flush with each other, they can open without problems.

examples.sentence: ¿Viste cómo las hojas de la ventana están ras con ras? Eso evita que entre el viento.
examples.translation: Did you see how the window panes are flush? That prevents wind from coming in.

examples.sentence: Dejaron las piezas ras con ras para que el acabado fuera perfecto y no se notaran las uniones.
examples.translation: They left the pieces flush so the finish would be perfect and the joints wouldn't be noticeable.

definitions: To put one's hand in one's pocket to take out money (literal action).

examples.sentence: Cuando llegó la cuenta, Ana se tuvo que rascar el bolsillo para pagar la cena de todos.
examples.translation: When the bill arrived, Ana had to put her hand in her pocket to pay for everyone's dinner.

examples.sentence: No me gusta rascarme el bolsillo en cafés caros, prefiero lugares más modestos.
examples.translation: I don't like putting my hand in my pocket at expensive cafes; I prefer more modest places.

examples.sentence: ¿Podrías rascarte el bolsillo y darme unas monedas para el estacionamiento?
examples.translation: Could you put your hand in your pocket and give me some coins for the parking?

examples.sentence: Él se rascó el bolsillo y sacó un billete para pagar el boleto del autobús.
examples.translation: He put his hand in his pocket and took out a bill to pay for the bus ticket.

definitions: To pay or be compelled to pay money, often reluctantly; to shell out or contribute funds.

examples.sentence: Para comprar ese teléfono nuevo, voy a tener que rascarme el bolsillo bastante.
examples.translation: To buy that new phone, I'm going to have to shell out quite a bit.

examples.sentence: Aunque no quería, al final se rascó el bolsillo para ayudar a pagar los gastos de la fiesta.
examples.translation: Although he didn't want to, in the end he had to pay up to help cover the party expenses.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que deberemos rascar el bolsillo para la reparación del coche este mes?
examples.translation: Do you think we'll have to shell out for the car repair this month?

definitions: To scratch one's belly or stomach.

examples.sentence: El bebé se rascó la barriga mientras dormía plácidamente en su cuna.
examples.translation: The baby scratched his belly while sleeping peacefully in his crib.

examples.sentence: Me rascaba la barriga porque tenía un poco de picazón después de la caminata.
examples.translation: I scratched my belly because it was a bit itchy after the hike.

examples.sentence: Durante la clase, Juan se rascó la barriga sin darse cuenta de que todos lo miraban.
examples.translation: During class, Juan scratched his belly without realizing everyone was watching.

examples.sentence: Ella se rascó la barriga lentamente mientras se relajaba en el sofá después del almuerzo.
examples.translation: She scratched her belly slowly while relaxing on the sofa after lunch.

definitions: To be idle or lazy; to loaf around and avoid work or effort.

examples.sentence: Carlos se pasó todo el día rascándose la barriga en lugar de terminar el trabajo.
examples.translation: Carlos spent the whole day lazing around instead of finishing the work.

examples.sentence: No podemos permitir que el equipo se rasque la barriga mientras nosotros nos esforzamos.
examples.translation: We can't allow the team to loaf around while we put in effort.

examples.sentence: Si sigues rascándote la barriga, nunca vas a avanzar en el proyecto.
examples.translation: If you keep being lazy, you'll never move forward with the project.

definitions: To tear one's garments, a traditional gesture of extreme grief or mourning.

examples.sentence: En la antigua tragedia, la actriz se rasgó las vestiduras para mostrar su dolor profundo.
examples.translation: In the ancient tragedy, the actress tore her garments to show her deep sorrow.

examples.sentence: Durante el funeral, algunos familiares se rasgaban las vestiduras como señal de luto intenso.
examples.translation: During the funeral, some relatives tore their clothes as a sign of intense mourning.

examples.sentence: El sacerdote se rasgó las vestiduras cuando recibió la noticia de la destrucción del templo.
examples.translation: The priest tore his garments when he received the news of the temple's destruction.

examples.sentence: Al ver las ruinas, el anciano se rasgó las vestiduras en señal de desesperación.
examples.translation: Seeing the ruins, the old man tore his garments as a sign of despair.

definitions: To express exaggerated grief, outrage, or moral indignation, often publicly and dramatically.

examples.sentence: No hace falta rasgarse las vestiduras por un error tan pequeño, podemos solucionarlo fácilmente.
examples.translation: There's no need to tear one's clothes over such a small mistake; we can fix it easily.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuchó las críticas, se rasgó las vestiduras como si el mundo se acabara.
examples.translation: When he heard the criticism, he expressed exaggerated outrage as if the world was ending.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué te estás rasgando las vestiduras? No es para tanto, solo es una discusión normal.
examples.translation: Why are you making such a fuss? It's not that serious; it's just a normal argument.

definitions: A small rodent (mouse) found in or around a library.

examples.sentence: El ratón de biblioteca salió de detrás de los estantes y corrió hacia el rincón oscuro.
examples.translation: The library mouse came out from behind the shelves and ran toward the dark corner.

examples.sentence: Encontramos un ratón de biblioteca que había estado comiendo migas entre los libros viejos.
examples.translation: We found a library mouse that had been eating crumbs among the old books.

examples.sentence: Mientras limpiaban la biblioteca, descubrieron un pequeño ratón de biblioteca escondido en un cajón.
examples.translation: While cleaning the library, they discovered a small library mouse hidden in a drawer.

examples.sentence: El ratón de biblioteca se desplazaba sigilosamente entre las estanterías sin ser visto.
examples.translation: The library mouse moved stealthily among the bookshelves without being seen.

definitions: A studious person or bookworm; someone who spends a great deal of time reading or studying and tends to be bookish or reserved.

examples.sentence: María es una ratona de biblioteca; pasa horas leyendo en la universidad y casi no sale.
examples.translation: María is a bookworm; she spends hours reading at the university and hardly goes out.

examples.sentence: No me sorprende que Juan haya sacado esa nota, siempre ha sido un ratón de biblioteca.
examples.translation: I'm not surprised Juan got that grade; he's always been a bookworm.

examples.sentence: Aunque a veces se siente solo, ser ratón de biblioteca le ha dado mucho conocimiento y paciencia.
examples.translation: Although he sometimes feels lonely, being a bookworm has given him a lot of knowledge and patience.

definitions: To coil, pull in, or gather up a cable, rope, or line.

examples.sentence: Después de usar el cable para conectar el equipo, lo recogí cuidadosamente para guardarlo.
examples.translation: After using the cable to connect the equipment, I carefully coiled it up to store it.

examples.sentence: Siempre recogemos el cable del micrófono para evitar que alguien tropiece con él.
examples.translation: We always gather up the microphone cable to prevent someone from tripping over it.

examples.sentence: El marinero recogió el cable que había quedado suelto en la cubierta del barco.
examples.translation: The sailor pulled in the cable that had been loose on the ship's deck.

examples.sentence: No olvides recoger el cable de la luz antes de salir, para que no se dañe ni se enrede.
examples.translation: Don't forget to coil up the power cable before leaving, so it doesn't get damaged or tangled.

definitions: To retract a statement or position, to backtrack, or to attempt to undo or cover up a verbal or tactical mistake.

examples.sentence: Después de decir tantas cosas, tuvo que recoger cable y admitir que se había equivocado.
examples.translation: After saying so many things, he had to backtrack and admit he was wrong.

examples.sentence: Cuando la prensa cuestionó sus declaraciones, el político recogió cable rápidamente para evitar problemas.
examples.translation: When the press questioned his statements, the politician quickly retracted to avoid trouble.

examples.sentence: No puedes recoger cable cada vez que alguien te critica; tienes que ser firme en tus ideas.
examples.translation: You can't backtrack every time someone criticizes you; you have to stand firm in your ideas.

definitions: To pick up a glove, historically an act that signified readiness to fight or duel.

examples.sentence: En la época medieval, recoger el guante era una manera de aceptar un duelo formalmente.
examples.translation: In medieval times, picking up the glove was a way to formally accept a duel.

examples.sentence: El caballero recogió el guante que le lanzó su adversario y se preparó para el combate.
examples.translation: The knight picked up the glove his adversary threw at him and prepared for the fight.

examples.sentence: Cuando vio el desafío, el joven recogió el guante para demostrar su valentía ante la multitud.
examples.translation: When he saw the challenge, the young man picked up the glove to show his courage before the crowd.

examples.sentence: Ella recogió el guante del invitado a la fiesta, aceptando así la broma en tono amistoso.
examples.translation: She picked up the guest's glove at the party, thus accepting the joke in a friendly tone.

definitions: To accept a challenge or respond to a provocation; to take up an offered contest, task, or dare.

examples.sentence: Cuando le propusieron el reto, Ana no dudó en recoger el guante y demostrar su talento.
examples.translation: When they proposed the challenge, Ana didn't hesitate to accept it and show her talent.

examples.sentence: Al escuchar las críticas, el director recogió el guante y mejoró la producción para la siguiente temporada.
examples.translation: Upon hearing the criticism, the director took up the challenge and improved the production for the next season.

examples.sentence: ¿Vas a recoger el guante y participar en la competencia de este año o te vas a quedar atrás?
examples.translation: Are you going to accept the challenge and participate in this year's competition or will you stay behind?

definitions: To make a reconnaissance of an area; to scout or survey physical terrain to obtain information about features, obstacles, or enemy presence.

examples.sentence: Antes de la expedición, el grupo salió a reconocer el terreno para evitar sorpresas.
examples.translation: Before the expedition, the group went out to scout the terrain to avoid surprises.

examples.sentence: Los soldados reconocieron el terreno durante la noche para planificar la estrategia de ataque.
examples.translation: The soldiers made a reconnaissance of the terrain during the night to plan the attack strategy.

examples.sentence: El equipo de rescate recorrió y reconoció el terreno accidentado antes de iniciar la búsqueda.
examples.translation: The rescue team surveyed and scouted the rough terrain before starting the search.

examples.sentence: Los geólogos reconocieron el terreno para estudiar la composición del suelo en la zona afectada.
examples.translation: The geologists surveyed the terrain to study the soil composition in the affected area.

definitions: To assess a situation or environment in order to learn its conditions, opportunities, or risks; to get the lay of the land before acting.

examples.sentence: Antes de invertir, es importante reconocer el terreno y entender bien el mercado local.
examples.translation: Before investing, it's important to assess the situation and understand the local market well.

examples.sentence: El nuevo gerente reconoció el terreno durante sus primeras semanas para identificar oportunidades de mejora.
examples.translation: The new manager evaluated the environment during his first weeks to identify improvement opportunities.

examples.sentence: ¿Has reconocido el terreno antes de presentar tu proyecto? Es fundamental conocer los riesgos.
examples.translation: Have you scoped out the situation before presenting your project? It's essential to know the risks.

definitions: To go through one's memory; to mentally review past events or recollections in order to retrieve information.

examples.sentence: Para escribir su autobiografía, Ana tuvo que recorrer la memoria y revivir momentos de su infancia.
examples.translation: To write her autobiography, Ana had to go through her memory and relive moments from her childhood.

examples.sentence: Durante la reunión, el anciano recorrió la memoria para contar historias de la guerra.
examples.translation: During the meeting, the elderly man went through his memory to tell stories from the war.

examples.sentence: Antes de contestar la pregunta, el profesor recorrió la memoria para recordar el dato exacto.
examples.translation: Before answering the question, the professor mentally reviewed his memory to recall the exact fact.

definitions: To traverse memories in a reflective or narrative way, often producing a sequence of remembered images or episodes.

examples.sentence: Mientras narraba la historia familiar, Laura recorrió la memoria y describió cada detalle con cariño.
examples.translation: While narrating the family story, Laura traversed her memory and described every detail lovingly.

examples.sentence: El documental recorre la memoria colectiva de la ciudad a través de imágenes y testimonios.
examples.translation: The documentary traverses the collective memory of the city through images and testimonies.

examples.sentence: Para escribir el guion, el director recorrió la memoria de sus experiencias personales y las combinó con ficción.
examples.translation: To write the script, the director traversed the memory of his personal experiences and combined them with fiction.

definitions: To be completely indifferent or unconcerned about something; not to care at all.

examples.sentence: A Juan le refanflinfársela lo que piensen los demás, siempre hace lo que quiere.
examples.translation: Juan couldn't care less what others think; he always does what he wants.

examples.sentence: Nos refanflinfársela la opinión de los críticos, seguimos adelante con nuestro proyecto.
examples.translation: We are completely indifferent to the critics' opinions; we're moving forward with our project.

examples.sentence: ¿Te refanflinfársela la situación actual o piensas involucrarte para cambiarla?
examples.translation: Do you not care at all about the current situation or do you plan to get involved to change it?

examples.sentence: Ella se refanflinfársela de los problemas ajenos y solo piensa en sí misma.
examples.translation: She is totally unconcerned about others' problems and only thinks about herself.

definitions: To remind someone of information or facts they have forgotten or partly forgotten.

examples.sentence: Para refrescar la memoria de los estudiantes, la profesora repasó los puntos clave antes del examen.
examples.translation: To refresh the students’ memory, the teacher reviewed key points before the exam.

examples.sentence: Cuando no recordaba bien los detalles, Pedro le pidió a su amigo que le refrescara la memoria.
examples.translation: When he didn’t remember the details well, Pedro asked his friend to refresh his memory.

examples.sentence: Antes de la reunión, envié un resumen para refrescar la memoria a todos los participantes.
examples.translation: Before the meeting, I sent a summary to refresh everyone’s memory.

definitions: To review material or cues in order to restore or sharpen one's own recollection.

examples.sentence: Para preparar la presentación, tuve que refrescar la memoria repasando antiguos documentos.
examples.translation: To prepare the presentation, I had to refresh my memory by reviewing old documents.

examples.sentence: Ella refrescó la memoria leyendo notas que había tomado durante la conferencia anterior.
examples.translation: She refreshed her memory by reading notes she had taken during the previous conference.

examples.sentence: Antes de contestar el cuestionario, el alumno refrescó la memoria con un breve repaso de la materia.
examples.translation: Before answering the questionnaire, the student refreshed his memory with a brief review of the subject.

definitions: So-so; mediocre; neither good nor terrible—adequate but unimpressive.

examples.sentence: El rendimiento de Pedro en el último examen fue regulín regulán; no estuvo ni bien ni mal.
examples.translation: Pedro's performance on the last exam was so-so; it wasn't good nor bad.

examples.sentence: ¿Cómo te fue en la entrevista? – Regulín regulán, no me sentí muy seguro.
examples.translation: How did the interview go? – So-so, I didn't feel very confident.

examples.sentence: La película estuvo regulín regulán, esperaba algo más emocionante.
examples.translation: The movie was mediocre; I expected something more exciting.

definitions: Literal: a woman who is the 'queen' of a house, taken as the female head, hostess, or titular figure of a household.

examples.sentence: En nuestra casa, mi madre siempre ha sido la reina de la casa, organizando todo con paciencia.
examples.translation: In our home, my mother has always been the queen of the house, organizing everything patiently.

examples.sentence: Aunque mi padre trabaja mucho, es mi abuela la reina de la casa y la que manda en todo.
examples.translation: Although my father works a lot, it’s my grandmother who is the queen of the house and who rules everything.

examples.sentence: La reina de la casa decidió redecorar la sala para que luzca más acogedora este invierno.
examples.translation: The queen of the house decided to redecorate the living room to make it cozier this winter.

examples.sentence: En la fiesta familiar, todos reconocieron a Marta como la reina de la casa por su hospitalidad.
examples.translation: At the family party, everyone recognized Marta as the queen of the house for her hospitality.

definitions: Figurative: a woman who is treated as the central, dominant, or most pampered person in a household, often implying authority over domestic matters or special privilege.

examples.sentence: En su casa, Marta es la reina de la casa; todos escuchan sus decisiones sin cuestionarlas.
examples.translation: At home, Marta is the queen of the house; everyone listens to her decisions without questioning.

examples.sentence: Aunque no lo diga, Ana se siente como la reina de la casa, siempre cuidando cada detalle familiar.
examples.translation: Even if she doesn't say it, Ana feels like the queen of the house, always taking care of every family detail.

examples.sentence: En nuestra familia, la abuela es la reina de la casa y tiene autoridad sobre todos los asuntos domésticos.
examples.translation: In our family, grandma is the queen of the house and has authority over all domestic matters.

definitions: Literal: the 'queen' of the home, referring to a woman regarded as the principal female figure within a household.

examples.sentence: María siempre ha sido la reina del hogar, cuidando que todo esté en orden y que su familia se sienta cómoda.
examples.translation: María has always been the queen of the home, making sure everything is in order and her family feels comfortable.

examples.sentence: En esta casa, la reina del hogar es mi abuela, que se encarga de preparar las mejores comidas y mantener la tradición.
examples.translation: In this house, the queen of the home is my grandmother, who is in charge of preparing the best meals and keeping the tradition.

examples.sentence: Aunque ahora vive sola, sigue siendo la reina del hogar en cada rincón que cuida con tanto cariño.
examples.translation: Although she now lives alone, she continues to be the queen of the home in every corner she lovingly takes care of.

examples.sentence: Cuando alguien entra en la casa, se nota la presencia de la reina del hogar en la decoración y el ambiente acogedor.
examples.translation: When someone enters the house, you can feel the presence of the queen of the home in the decoration and the cozy atmosphere.

definitions: Figurative: a homemaker or woman who is recognized as the emotional or managerial center of family life, often used to praise her role or influence in the home.

examples.sentence: Mi madre es la reina del hogar; se encarga de que todo funcione y que estemos unidos.
examples.translation: My mother is the queen of the home; she makes sure everything runs smoothly and that we stay united.

examples.sentence: Después de tantos años, ella sigue siendo la reina del hogar, cuidando con amor a toda la familia.
examples.translation: After so many years, she continues to be the queen of the home, lovingly caring for the whole family.

examples.sentence: En esa casa, la reina del hogar tiene la última palabra en las decisiones importantes.
examples.translation: In that house, the homemaker has the final say in important decisions.

definitions: Literal: to laugh with the mouth wide or full, producing an abundant, uninhibited sound.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuchó el chiste, no pudo evitar reír a boca llena junto a sus amigos.
examples.translation: When she heard the joke, she couldn't help but laugh out loud with her friends.

examples.sentence: Durante la película cómica, todos en la sala reían a boca llena sin parar.
examples.translation: During the comedy movie, everyone in the theater laughed heartily without stopping.

examples.sentence: Me encanta oír a mi abuelo reír a boca llena; su alegría es contagiosa.
examples.translation: I love hearing my grandfather laugh out loud; his joy is contagious.

examples.sentence: Aunque estaba cansado, al ver aquel video gracioso no pudo evitar reír a boca llena.
examples.translation: Although he was tired, upon seeing that funny video he couldn't help laughing out loud.

definitions: Figurative: to laugh heartily and without restraint; to laugh aloud with evident pleasure.

examples.sentence: Cuando escuchó el chiste de Carlos, no pudo evitar reír a boca llena durante varios minutos.
examples.translation: When she heard Carlos's joke, she couldn't help but laugh heartily for several minutes.

examples.sentence: Nos reímos a boca llena en la fiesta anoche; hacía tiempo que no me divertía tanto.
examples.translation: We laughed heartily at the party last night; I hadn't had so much fun in a long time.

examples.sentence: Si supieras lo que me contó, te reirías a boca llena sin parar.
examples.translation: If you knew what he told me, you would laugh heartily without stopping.

definitions: Literal: to emit loud, explosive bursts of laughter known as 'carcajadas'.

examples.sentence: Cuando Pepe contó aquella anécdota tan graciosa, todos nos reímos a carcajadas.
examples.translation: When Pepe told that very funny story, we all laughed out loud.

examples.sentence: No pude evitar reírme a carcajadas al ver el video cómico que me enviaste.
examples.translation: I couldn't help laughing out loud when I saw the funny video you sent me.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué te ríes a carcajadas? ¿Acaso pasó algo realmente divertido?
examples.translation: Why are you laughing out loud? Did something really funny happen?

examples.sentence: Ella se reía a carcajadas mientras veía la comedia en el teatro anoche.
examples.translation: She was laughing out loud while watching the comedy at the theater last night.

definitions: Figurative: to laugh uproariously or uncontrollably, often with a tone of mockery or derision toward someone or something.

examples.sentence: Los chicos se reían a carcajadas del profesor cuando este cometió ese error tan tonto.
examples.translation: The boys laughed uproariously at the teacher when he made that silly mistake.

examples.sentence: No puedo creer que te rías a carcajadas de mis problemas, eso no es nada amable.
examples.translation: I can't believe you laugh uproariously at my problems; that's not very kind.

examples.sentence: Se reían a carcajadas mientras imitaban a su jefe con exageración y burla.
examples.translation: They laughed uproariously as they exaggeratedly mocked their boss.

definitions: Literal: to lick again or repeatedly, as with the tongue over a surface or an object.

examples.sentence: El perro relamió el plato después de que terminamos de darle su comida.
examples.translation: The dog licked the plate after we finished giving him his food.

examples.sentence: María relamió el caramelo lentamente para disfrutar mejor su sabor dulce.
examples.translation: María licked the candy slowly to better enjoy its sweet flavor.

examples.sentence: El gato relamía con insistencia el vaso donde había quedado un poco de leche.
examples.translation: The cat repeatedly licked the glass where there was some milk left.

examples.sentence: Cuando terminé de comer, relamí los dedos para no desperdiciar ni una gota de la salsa.
examples.translation: When I finished eating, I licked my fingers so as not to waste a drop of the sauce.

definitions: Figurative: to relish or savor something with visible pleasure or anticipation, often expressed as figuratively licking one's lips or displaying eager enjoyment.

examples.sentence: Al ver el postre que prepararon, Juan se relamía de gusto anticipando el primer bocado.
examples.translation: Upon seeing the dessert they made, Juan was savoring it with obvious pleasure, anticipating the first bite.

examples.sentence: Ella se relamía de gusto mientras describía el viaje soñado que planeaba hacer el próximo verano.
examples.translation: She was savoring with delight as she described the dream trip she planned to take next summer.

examples.sentence: Nos relamíamos de gusto al imaginar el éxito que tendría nuestro proyecto en el mercado.
examples.translation: We were savoring with eagerness as we imagined the success our project would have in the market.

definitions: Literal: to lick one's lips or mouth visibly as an expression of pleasure or enjoyment.

examples.sentence: Después de probar el pastel, se relamió de gusto con una sonrisa satisfecha.
examples.translation: After tasting the cake, he licked his lips with a satisfied smile.

examples.sentence: El niño se relamía de gusto mientras comía el helado bajo el sol de verano.
examples.translation: The boy licked his lips with pleasure while eating ice cream under the summer sun.

examples.sentence: Me relamía de gusto al recordar el aroma y sabor de la paella que preparó mi abuela.
examples.translation: I licked my lips in delight remembering the aroma and flavor of the paella my grandmother made.

examples.sentence: Los gatos suelen relamerse de gusto después de una buena comida casera.
examples.translation: Cats usually lick their lips with pleasure after a good homemade meal.

definitions: Figurative: to savor or relish something with obvious delight; to take great pleasure in or derive conspicuous satisfaction from an event, situation, or outcome.

examples.sentence: Se relamía de gusto al pensar en la promoción que pronto recibiría en el trabajo.
examples.translation: He was savoring with obvious delight thinking about the promotion he would soon receive at work.

examples.sentence: Nos relamíamos de gusto al enterarnos de la victoria de nuestro equipo favorito en el campeonato.
examples.translation: We were savoring with pleasure upon learning about our favorite team's victory in the championship.

examples.sentence: Ella se relamió de gusto al escuchar que el restaurante abriría una sucursal cerca de su casa.
examples.translation: She savored with delight upon hearing that the restaurant would open a branch near her house.

definitions: Literal/Scientific: an internal physiological mechanism that regulates biological rhythms, such as circadian cycles of sleep and wakefulness.

examples.sentence: El reloj biológico de las personas regula sus ciclos de sueño y vigilia de forma natural.
examples.translation: People's biological clock naturally regulates their sleep and wake cycles.

examples.sentence: Durante el jet lag, el reloj biológico tarda varios días en adaptarse al nuevo horario.
examples.translation: During jet lag, the biological clock takes several days to adjust to the new schedule.

examples.sentence: Los científicos estudian cómo el reloj biológico influye en la salud y el metabolismo humano.
examples.translation: Scientists study how the biological clock influences human health and metabolism.

examples.sentence: Cuando el reloj biológico se desajusta, las personas pueden sentir fatiga y falta de concentración.
examples.translation: When the biological clock is out of sync, people may feel fatigue and lack of concentration.

definitions: Figurative: an internal sense of timing or urgency related to life stages (commonly reproduction or aging), often used to denote a perceived deadline for biological events.

examples.sentence: María siente que su reloj biológico le apremia para formar una familia antes de los 35 años.
examples.translation: María feels that her biological clock urges her to start a family before she turns 35.

examples.sentence: Aunque aún está joven, Pedro nota su reloj biológico y quiere aprovechar para viajar y vivir nuevas experiencias.
examples.translation: Although he is still young, Pedro notices his biological clock and wants to take advantage to travel and live new experiences.

examples.sentence: El reloj biológico no perdona, y muchos sienten la presión de cumplir ciertas metas en un tiempo limitado.
examples.translation: The biological clock doesn't forgive, and many feel the pressure to achieve certain goals within a limited time.

definitions: Literal: a mechanical clock or watch equipped with a repeater mechanism that chimes the hours (and sometimes minutes and quarters) on demand.

examples.sentence: El reloj de repetición permite escuchar las horas con solo activar una palanca en el lado del reloj.
examples.translation: The repeater clock allows you to hear the hours just by activating a lever on the side of the watch.

examples.sentence: Mi abuelo tiene un reloj de repetición que suena cada cuarto de hora con un tono muy agradable.
examples.translation: My grandfather has a repeater clock that chimes every quarter hour with a very pleasant tone.

examples.sentence: Los relojes de repetición son piezas mecánicas complejas que fascinan a los coleccionistas por su precisión y sonido.
examples.translation: Repeater clocks are complex mechanical pieces that fascinate collectors for their precision and sound.

examples.sentence: El artesano ajustó cuidadosamente el mecanismo del reloj de repetición para que el sonido fuera claro y armonioso.
examples.translation: The craftsman carefully adjusted the repeater clock mechanism so the sound was clear and harmonious.

definitions: Literal: to hammer a nail again or to secure a nail more firmly by driving it further.

examples.sentence: Para que nadie olvidara la importancia de la seguridad, el profesor remachó el clavo con un ejemplo extra.
examples.translation: So that no one would forget the importance of safety, the teacher reinforced the point with an extra example.

examples.sentence: Cuando Juan explicó la razón de su decisión, remachó el clavo insistiendo en las consecuencias negativas.
examples.translation: When Juan explained the reason for his decision, he emphasized it by stressing the negative consequences.

examples.sentence: No hace falta remachar el clavo, ya entendimos perfectamente el mensaje que querías transmitir.
examples.translation: There's no need to hammer the nail again; we perfectly understood the message you wanted to convey.

definitions: Figurative (emphasis): to reinforce or underscore a point by adding an additional remark or action that makes the original point more forceful.

examples.sentence: Al criticarlo frente a todos, remachó el clavo y lo hizo sentir aún peor que antes.
examples.translation: By criticizing him in front of everyone, he delivered the final blow and made him feel even worse than before.

examples.sentence: No quería discutir, pero con ese comentario remachaste el clavo y empeoraste la situación.
examples.translation: I didn't want to argue, but with that comment you made things worse and delivered the final blow.

examples.sentence: Cuando agregó esa última acusación, remachó el clavo y la confianza entre ellos se rompió definitivamente.
examples.translation: When he added that last accusation, he made things worse and the trust between them broke definitively.

definitions: Figurative (negative consequence): to make a situation worse or to deliver a final damaging blow by adding an action or comment that exacerbates an existing problem.

examples.sentence: No debiste recordar ese detalle en la reunión, solo remachaste el clavo y empeoraste la situación.
examples.translation: You shouldn't have mentioned that detail in the meeting; you only drove the nail in and made the situation worse.

examples.sentence: Cuando Ana criticó el proyecto frente a todos, realmente remachó el clavo y hundió la moral del equipo.
examples.translation: When Ana criticized the project in front of everyone, she really drove the nail in and crushed the team's morale.

examples.sentence: Si sigues remachando el clavo con tus comentarios negativos, nadie querrá colaborar contigo en el futuro.
examples.translation: If you keep driving the nail in with your negative comments, no one will want to collaborate with you in the future.

definitions: Literal: to reopen or aggravate a physical wound so that it becomes fresh or inflamed again.

examples.sentence: Al hacer ejercicio demasiado pronto, renovó la herida que tenía en la rodilla y tuvo que ir al médico.
examples.translation: By exercising too soon, he reopened the wound in his knee and had to go to the doctor.

examples.sentence: El ciclista renovó la herida en el brazo cuando se cayó durante la carrera de ayer.
examples.translation: The cyclist aggravated the wound on his arm when he fell during yesterday's race.

examples.sentence: No debes renovar la herida frotándola; mejor déjala sanar tranquilamente para evitar infecciones.
examples.translation: You shouldn't reopen the wound by rubbing it; better let it heal quietly to avoid infections.

examples.sentence: El doctor advirtió que si continuaba con ese tratamiento, podría renovar la herida y retardar la recuperación.
examples.translation: The doctor warned that if he continued with that treatment, he could aggravate the wound and delay recovery.

definitions: Figurative: to reopen or revive emotional pain or past trauma, causing feelings associated with the original hurt to resurface.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que hablan de ese tema, parece que renuevan la herida y vuelven los malos recuerdos.
examples.translation: Every time they talk about that topic, it seems they reopen the wound and the bad memories come back.

examples.sentence: No quiso renovar la herida trayendo a colación aquella discusión del pasado durante la reunión familiar.
examples.translation: He didn't want to reopen the emotional wound by bringing up that past argument during the family meeting.

examples.sentence: Al leer la carta, renovó la herida que creía olvidada y se sintió triste nuevamente.
examples.translation: Reading the letter reopened the wound he thought was forgotten and he felt sad again.

definitions: To refresh or restore one's recollection of information; to cause someone to remember something previously known or forgotten.

examples.sentence: Para el examen, hice un resumen que me ayudó a renovar la memoria sobre los conceptos más importantes.
examples.translation: For the exam, I made a summary that helped me refresh my memory about the most important concepts.

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes ayudarme a renovar la memoria? No recuerdo bien los detalles de esa reunión pasada.
examples.translation: Can you help me refresh my memory? I don't quite remember the details of that past meeting.

examples.sentence: El documental me sirvió para renovar la memoria acerca de los eventos históricos de esa época.
examples.translation: The documentary helped me refresh my memory about the historical events of that era.

definitions: To update, clear, or reinitialize stored memory in a computing or electronic system.

examples.sentence: Para mejorar el rendimiento, el técnico decidió renovar la memoria del sistema y borrar los datos corruptos.
examples.translation: To improve performance, the technician decided to refresh the system's memory and erase corrupted data.

examples.sentence: Cada vez que el dispositivo se congela, es necesario renovar la memoria para que funcione correctamente.
examples.translation: Every time the device freezes, it's necessary to clear the memory so it works correctly.

examples.sentence: El programa incluye una opción para renovar la memoria automáticamente cuando detecta errores.
examples.translation: The program includes an option to refresh the memory automatically when it detects errors.

examples.sentence: Antes de instalar el nuevo software, es recomendable renovar la memoria para evitar conflictos en el sistema.
examples.translation: Before installing new software, it's advisable to clear the memory to avoid system conflicts.

definitions: A small tropical country economically dependent on the export of a single agricultural product (historically bananas) and heavily influenced by foreign commercial interests.

examples.sentence: Costa Verde es un país pequeño, conocido por ser una república bananera que depende casi exclusivamente de la exportación de café.
examples.translation: Costa Verde is a small country known for being a banana republic that depends almost exclusively on coffee exports.

examples.sentence: Las repúblicas bananeras suelen tener economías vulnerables debido a su alta dependencia de un solo producto agrícola.
examples.translation: Banana republics usually have vulnerable economies due to their high dependence on a single agricultural product.

examples.sentence: En la clase de historia, estudiamos cómo algunas repúblicas bananeras sufrieron la influencia de empresas extranjeras en su desarrollo económico.
examples.translation: In history class, we studied how some banana republics suffered foreign companies' influence on their economic development.

examples.sentence: La inestabilidad política en esa república bananera se debe en parte a la desigualdad económica derivada del monocultivo.
examples.translation: The political instability in that banana republic is partly due to economic inequality derived from monoculture.

definitions: A derogatory term for a country perceived as politically unstable, corrupt, lacking effective institutions or the rule of law, and subject to manipulation by private or foreign powers.

examples.sentence: No quiero que pienses que digo esto por molestar, pero su gobierno parece una auténtica república bananera.
examples.translation: I don't want you to think I'm saying this to annoy you, but their government seems like a true banana republic.

examples.sentence: La corrupción generalizada y la falta de instituciones sólidas convierten al país en una república bananera a los ojos de los analistas.
examples.translation: Widespread corruption and lack of strong institutions turn the country into a banana republic in the eyes of analysts.

examples.sentence: Al criticar la gestión pública, el periodista calificó al país de república bananera por su desorden y favoritismos.
examples.translation: When criticizing public management, the journalist labeled the country a banana republic because of its disorder and favoritism.

definitions: To rub a small onion or scallion, literally, as an action in food preparation.

examples.sentence: Para preparar la salsa, primero hay que restregar la cebolleta para liberar su aroma y sabor.
examples.translation: To prepare the sauce, first you have to rub the scallion to release its aroma and flavor.

examples.sentence: En la receta tradicional, se indica restregar la cebolleta sobre el pan antes de añadir el pescado.
examples.translation: In the traditional recipe, it says to rub the scallion on the bread before adding the fish.

examples.sentence: Mientras cocinaba, restregó la cebolleta con un poco de sal para suavizar su sabor fuerte.
examples.translation: While cooking, she rubbed the scallion with a bit of salt to soften its strong flavor.

examples.sentence: Antes de añadirla a la ensalada, es recomendable restregar la cebolleta para que no quede tan picante.
examples.translation: Before adding it to the salad, it's advisable to rub the scallion so it isn't too spicy.

definitions: To masturbate (male), used as a crude or vulgar expression for self-stimulation.

examples.sentence: En la conversación privada, él usó la expresión 'restregar la cebolleta' para referirse a un tema muy incómodo y vulgar.
examples.translation: In private conversation, he used the expression 'restregar la cebolleta' to refer to a very uncomfortable and vulgar topic.

examples.sentence: No es apropiado mencionar 'restregar la cebolleta' en público porque es un término que se asocia con la masturbación masculina.
examples.translation: It's not appropriate to mention 'restregar la cebolleta' in public because it's a term associated with male masturbation.

examples.sentence: Al bromear con sus amigos, hizo un comentario sobre 'restregar la cebolleta' que causó risas y algo de incomodidad.
examples.translation: Joking with his friends, he made a comment about 'restregar la cebolleta' that caused laughter and some discomfort.

definitions: To search through the stalls or goods at a fair or market, literally rummaging among items on offer.

examples.sentence: En la feria, me gusta revolver la feria para encontrar artesanías únicas y baratas.
examples.translation: At the fair, I like to rummage through the stalls to find unique and cheap crafts.

examples.sentence: El niño revolvió la feria buscando una pelota que había perdido entre los puestos.
examples.translation: The boy rummaged through the fair looking for a ball he had lost among the stalls.

examples.sentence: Durante horas, revolvieron la feria intentando localizar a su amigo que se había separado del grupo.
examples.translation: For hours, they rummaged through the fair trying to locate their friend who had separated from the group.

examples.sentence: Antes de comprar, siempre me gusta revolver la feria para comparar precios y calidad.
examples.translation: Before buying, I always like to rummage through the fair to compare prices and quality.

definitions: To rummage through a place or container in search of something; to search thoroughly or ransack.

examples.sentence: Busqué por todas partes y tuve que revolver la feria en mi bolso para encontrar las llaves del coche.
examples.translation: I looked everywhere and had to rummage through my bag to find the car keys.

examples.sentence: Cuando llegó a casa, revolvió la feria en el cajón del escritorio hasta hallar el documento perdido.
examples.translation: When he got home, he rummaged through the desk drawer until he found the lost document.

examples.sentence: No me gusta que revolvieran la feria en mi habitación sin permiso, dejaron todo desordenado.
examples.translation: I don't like that they rummaged through my room without permission; they left everything messy.

definitions: A person regarded as the head or principal authority of a household, often used to describe the primary decision-maker at home.

examples.sentence: Mi padre siempre ha sido el rey del hogar, tomando las decisiones importantes y cuidando a la familia.
examples.translation: My father has always been the head of the household, making important decisions and taking care of the family.

examples.sentence: En esa casa, la abuela es considerada la reina y el rey del hogar por su sabiduría y autoridad moral.
examples.translation: In that house, the grandmother is considered the queen and head of the household for her wisdom and moral authority.

examples.sentence: Aunque es joven, Pedro es el rey del hogar porque es quien administra las finanzas familiares con eficiencia.
examples.translation: Although he's young, Pedro is the head of the household because he manages the family finances efficiently.

examples.sentence: La figura del rey del hogar ha cambiado mucho con el tiempo, ahora se valora más la igualdad en las tareas domésticas.
examples.translation: The figure of the head of the household has changed a lot over time; now equality in household tasks is more valued.

definitions: A sarcastic or ironic label for someone who expects special treatment at home or behaves as if they rule the household, despite not having formal authority.

examples.sentence: Mi hermano se cree el rey del hogar, pero en realidad todos sabemos que mamá es quien manda.
examples.translation: My brother acts like the king of the house, but actually, we all know mom is the one in charge.

examples.sentence: No lo tomes en serio cuando dice que es el rey del hogar; solo está bromeando porque quiere que le hagan caso.
examples.translation: Don't take it seriously when he says he's the king of the house; he's just joking because he wants attention.

examples.sentence: Aunque es el rey del hogar en su mente, no se responsabiliza de ninguna tarea doméstica ni decisiones importantes.
examples.translation: Although he's the king of the house in his mind, he doesn't take responsibility for any household tasks or important decisions.

definitions: Literal: persons regarded as the principal figures or authorities within a household, often used humorously or affectionately to denote those who 'rule' the home.

examples.sentence: Los abuelos son considerados los reyes del hogar porque siempre reciben un trato especial y cariño en la familia.
examples.translation: Grandparents are considered the kings of the household because they always receive special treatment and affection in the family.

examples.sentence: En casa de los Martínez, los niños son los reyes del hogar y disfrutan de muchas libertades y mimos.
examples.translation: In the Martínez household, the children are the kings of the home and enjoy many freedoms and pampering.

examples.sentence: Se dice que las mascotas son los reyes del hogar, ya que todos se preocupan por su bienestar y comodidad.
examples.translation: It is said that pets are the kings of the household since everyone cares about their well-being and comfort.

examples.sentence: En la reunión familiar, bromeamos diciendo que los abuelos son los reyes del hogar porque siempre deciden qué hacer.
examples.translation: At the family gathering, we joked that grandparents are the kings of the home because they always decide what to do.

definitions: Figurative: people who dominate domestic life or enjoy special privileges at home, used ironically to criticize or tease their perceived dominance or pampering.

examples.sentence: Mis primos son los reyes del hogar cuando visitan a mis tíos; les consienten demasiado y se salen con la suya.
examples.translation: My cousins are the kings of the household when they visit my uncles; they are spoiled too much and get their way.

examples.sentence: No soporto que se comporten como reyes del hogar solo porque son los hijos mayores; todos deben colaborar igualmente.
examples.translation: I can't stand that they act like kings of the household just because they are the eldest children; everyone should contribute equally.

examples.sentence: Aunque sean los reyes del hogar, no deberían abusar de su posición para evitar conflictos familiares.
examples.translation: Even if they are the kings of the household, they shouldn't abuse their position to avoid family conflicts.

definitions: Literal: to curl again something that has already been curled, especially hair; to add an additional curl.

examples.sentence: Para la fiesta, Marta decidió rizar el rizo y hacerse unos rizos más definidos que la última vez.
examples.translation: For the party, Marta decided to curl her hair again and make the curls more defined than last time.

examples.sentence: El peluquero rizó el rizo varias veces para lograr el estilo perfecto que pidió el cliente.
examples.translation: The hairdresser curled the hair again several times to achieve the perfect style the client requested.

examples.sentence: No quiero rizar más el rizo; el peinado ya está suficientemente elaborado para la sesión de fotos.
examples.translation: I don't want to curl it again; the hairstyle is already elaborate enough for the photo shoot.

examples.sentence: Antes de salir, Ana se rizó el rizo para darle un toque extra de volumen a su cabello.
examples.translation: Before going out, Ana curled her hair again to give it an extra touch of volume.

definitions: Figurative: to make something more complicated or elaborate than necessary; to overcomplicate, overdo, or take an action to an extreme or excessive degree.

examples.sentence: En su informe, Juan rizó el rizo al añadir detalles innecesarios que solo complicaron la presentación.
examples.translation: In his report, Juan overcomplicated things by adding unnecessary details that only complicated the presentation.

examples.sentence: No rices el rizo con tantas reglas; a veces lo simple es más efectivo y fácil de entender.
examples.translation: Don't overdo it with so many rules; sometimes simplicity is more effective and easier to understand.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre riza el rizo cuando discute, haciendo que un problema menor parezca una crisis mayor.
examples.translation: She always overcomplicates things when arguing, making a minor problem seem like a bigger crisis.

definitions: Literal: the physical position of having a knee on the ground.

examples.sentence: Durante la ceremonia, el soldado se arrodilló con la rodilla en tierra para rendir homenaje a los caídos.
examples.translation: During the ceremony, the soldier knelt down with his knee on the ground to pay homage to the fallen.

examples.sentence: Para pedir perdón sinceramente, se presentó con la rodilla en tierra frente a sus padres.
examples.translation: To sincerely ask for forgiveness, he appeared kneeling before his parents.

examples.sentence: El jugador terminó la carrera con la rodilla en tierra, agotado pero feliz por el esfuerzo realizado.
examples.translation: The player finished the race with his knee on the ground, exhausted but happy for the effort made.

examples.sentence: En la pintura, el rey aparece con la rodilla en tierra ante el altar, mostrando devoción y humildad.
examples.translation: In the painting, the king appears kneeling before the altar, showing devotion and humility.

definitions: Figurative: an act of submission, homage, or obeisance; to kneel as a sign of respect, fealty, or supplication.

examples.sentence: Durante la ceremonia, el caballero puso rodilla en tierra para jurar lealtad al rey.
examples.translation: During the ceremony, the knight went down on one knee to swear loyalty to the king.

examples.sentence: No esperes que me ponga rodilla en tierra ante sus demandas injustas.
examples.translation: Don't expect me to kneel in submission to his unfair demands.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre ha mantenido la rodilla en tierra frente a las tradiciones familiares, mostrando respeto profundo.
examples.translation: She has always kept one knee on the ground before family traditions, showing deep respect.

definitions: Specific usage: the posture adopted when proposing marriage (kneeling on one knee) or performing certain ceremonial or sporting actions that require a knee-on-ground stance.

examples.sentence: Cuando Juan decidió pedirle matrimonio a María, se arrodilló con rodilla en tierra y sacó el anillo.
examples.translation: When Juan decided to propose to María, he knelt down on one knee and took out the ring.

examples.sentence: En el entrenamiento de caza, los soldados adoptaron la postura de rodilla en tierra para estabilizar sus disparos.
examples.translation: In the hunting training, the soldiers took the kneeling position to stabilize their shots.

examples.sentence: Durante la competencia de esgrima, el atleta mantuvo rodilla en tierra para mejorar su equilibrio y defensa.
examples.translation: During the fencing competition, the athlete kept one knee on the ground to improve balance and defense.

examples.sentence: La tradición exige que el novio esté con rodilla en tierra antes de entregar el ramo a la novia.
examples.translation: Tradition requires the groom to be on one knee before handing the bouquet to the bride.

definitions: Practical usage: a command or description of a tactical or firing position in which one knee is on the ground for stability or cover.

examples.sentence: El instructor ordenó que todos los soldados tomaran posición rodilla en tierra para protegerse mejor.
examples.translation: The instructor ordered all soldiers to take the kneeling position for better protection.

examples.sentence: Mientras avanzaban bajo fuego enemigo, los combatientes adoptaron rodilla en tierra para disparar con precisión.
examples.translation: While advancing under enemy fire, the fighters took the kneeling position to shoot accurately.

examples.sentence: En el simulacro, cada participante debía permanecer rodilla en tierra hasta recibir la señal para avanzar.
examples.translation: In the drill, each participant had to stay kneeling until receiving the signal to move forward.

examples.sentence: Rodilla en tierra es la posición que se recomienda para disparar con mayor estabilidad en terreno irregular.
examples.translation: Kneeling is the recommended position to shoot with more stability on uneven ground.

definitions: Literal: to begin crying suddenly or abruptly; to burst into tears.

examples.sentence: Al recibir la noticia, Marta rompió a llorar sin poder contener sus lágrimas.
examples.translation: Upon receiving the news, Marta suddenly burst into tears, unable to hold them back.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué rompiste a llorar justo en medio de la presentación? Todos se quedaron sorprendidos.
examples.translation: Why did you start crying right in the middle of the presentation? Everyone was surprised.

examples.sentence: Los niños rompieron a llorar cuando se apagaron las luces y el juego terminó inesperadamente.
examples.translation: The children suddenly began to cry when the lights went out and the game ended unexpectedly.

examples.sentence: No es común que él rompa a llorar, pero aquella película logró conmoverlo profundamente.
examples.translation: He rarely bursts into tears, but that movie deeply moved him.

definitions: Figurative: to have an emotional breakdown or yield to strong emotion, often implying loss of composure or vulnerability.

examples.sentence: Después de semanas de estrés, finalmente rompió a llorar en la oficina al sentirse abrumado.
examples.translation: After weeks of stress, he finally had an emotional breakdown at the office, feeling overwhelmed.

examples.sentence: No quiero que pienses que soy débil, pero a veces rompo a llorar cuando todo me supera.
examples.translation: I don't want you to think I'm weak, but sometimes I break down in tears when everything overwhelms me.

examples.sentence: Cuando rompieron la noticia, varios empleados rompieron a llorar por la incertidumbre del futuro.
examples.translation: When the news was broken, several employees emotionally broke down because of the uncertainty about the future.

definitions: Literal: to open fire; to discharge weapons or initiate shooting, typically as the first hostile act.

examples.sentence: El ejército rompió el fuego justo al amanecer, iniciando el conflicto armado.
examples.translation: The army opened fire right at dawn, starting the armed conflict.

examples.sentence: Cuando el grupo insurgente rompió el fuego, la base respondió con artillería pesada.
examples.translation: When the insurgent group opened fire, the base responded with heavy artillery.

examples.sentence: El francotirador rompió el fuego desde la colina, sorprendiendo a las tropas enemigas.
examples.translation: The sniper opened fire from the hill, surprising the enemy troops.

examples.sentence: En la película, el protagonista rompió el fuego para proteger a sus compañeros en la emboscada.
examples.translation: In the movie, the protagonist opened fire to protect his companions during the ambush.

definitions: Figurative: to be the first to begin an action, discussion, or offensive move; to initiate or break the ice in a confrontational or energetic way.

examples.sentence: Para romper el fuego en la reunión, Laura contó un chiste que hizo reír a todos los presentes.
examples.translation: To break the ice at the meeting, Laura told a joke that made everyone present laugh.

examples.sentence: El nuevo director rompió el fuego con una propuesta audaz que cambió la dinámica del equipo.
examples.translation: The new director initiated the action with a bold proposal that changed the team's dynamics.

examples.sentence: Si nadie rompe el fuego en la conversación, la ceremonia se pondrá muy incómoda.
examples.translation: If no one breaks the ice in the conversation, the ceremony will become very awkward.

definitions: To cause a piece of ice or a frozen surface to break; to physically fracture ice.

examples.sentence: El hielo del lago comenzó a romperse con el aumento de las temperaturas primaverales.
examples.translation: The lake ice began to break as spring temperatures rose.

examples.sentence: Durante el invierno, es peligroso caminar sobre el hielo que puede romperse bajo el peso.
examples.translation: During winter, it's dangerous to walk on ice that can break under weight.
