definitions: An imperative expression of contempt telling someone to go away in a highly offensive manner; equivalent to 'fuck off' in English.

examples.sentence: Cuando Juan comenzó a criticar mi trabajo sin razón, le dije claramente: vete a tomar por culo.
examples.translation: When Juan started unfairly criticizing my work, I clearly told him: fuck off.

examples.sentence: No voy a aguantar más tus insultos, así que vete a tomar por culo y no vuelvas.
examples.translation: I won't tolerate your insults anymore, so fuck off and don't come back.

examples.sentence: ¿De verdad crees que voy a ayudarte? Mejor vete a tomar por culo con esa actitud.
examples.translation: Do you really think I'm going to help you? Better fuck off with that attitude.

definitions: Literal coarse phrase meaning 'go take it up the ass' used emphatically as an insult or dismissal.

examples.sentence: Después de la discusión, me dijo vete a tomar por culo sin ningún respeto.
examples.translation: After the argument, he told me to go take it up the ass without any respect.

examples.sentence: No acepto que me hables así, vete a tomar por culo si eso quieres.
examples.translation: I don't accept you speaking to me like that, go take it up the ass if that's what you want.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre usa la expresión vete a tomar por culo para rechazar cualquier propuesta que no le gusta.
examples.translation: She always uses the expression 'go take it up the ass' to reject any proposal she doesn't like.

examples.sentence: Si no te gusta cómo van las cosas, simplemente vete a tomar por culo y déjanos en paz.
examples.translation: If you don't like how things are going, just go take it up the ass and leave us alone.

definitions: A figurative dismissal telling someone to take their business, act, or complaint elsewhere because they are unwelcome or their behavior will not be tolerated; equivalent to 'take your act somewhere else.'
idiom: vete con la música a otra parte

examples.sentence: Cuando comenzó a contar sus problemas sin parar, Marta le dijo vete con la música a otra parte.
examples.translation: When he started endlessly telling his problems, Marta told him to take his act somewhere else.
examples.matched_span: vete con la música a otra parte

examples.sentence: No pienso aguantar tus excusas, vete con la música a otra parte porque aquí no te creo.
examples.translation: I won't put up with your excuses, take your act somewhere else because I don't believe you here.
examples.matched_span: vete con la música a otra parte

examples.sentence: Si vas a seguir con esas quejas, mejor vete con la música a otra parte y no molestes más.
examples.translation: If you're going to keep with those complaints, better take your act somewhere else and don't bother anymore.
examples.matched_span: vete con la música a otra parte

definitions: Literally, 'go with the music to another place,' used when referring to physically moving a musical performance or accompaniment to a different location.
idiom: vete con la música a otra parte

examples.sentence: El grupo decidió vete con la música a otra parte porque el ruido molestaba a los vecinos.
examples.translation: The band decided to go with the music to another place because the noise was bothering the neighbors.
examples.matched_span: vete con la música a otra parte

examples.sentence: Mañana tendremos que vete con la música a otra parte, ya que la plaza estará ocupada por otro evento.
examples.translation: Tomorrow we will have to go with the music to another place since the plaza will be occupied by another event.
examples.matched_span: vete con la música a otra parte

examples.sentence: ¿Puedes vete con la música a otra parte? Aquí no es adecuado para tocar.
examples.translation: Can you go with the music to another place? This is not suitable for playing.
examples.matched_span: vete con la música a otra parte

examples.sentence: Nos van a pedir que vete con la música a otra parte porque el parque está cerrado por mantenimiento.
examples.translation: They are going to ask us to go with the music to another place because the park is closed for maintenance.
examples.matched_span: vete con la música a otra parte

definitions: A literal reference to the Virgin Mary used in devotional contexts to invoke or address her.

examples.sentence: Virgen Santa, ruega por nosotros para que encontremos paz en estos tiempos difíciles.
examples.translation: Holy Virgin, pray for us so that we find peace in these difficult times.

examples.sentence: En la iglesia, la gente rezaba fervientemente a la Virgen Santa durante la procesión.
examples.translation: In the church, people fervently prayed to the Holy Virgin during the procession.

examples.sentence: Cada mañana, mi abuela enciende una vela en honor a la Virgen Santa para pedir protección.
examples.translation: Every morning, my grandmother lights a candle in honor of the Holy Virgin to ask for protection.

examples.sentence: El altar estaba decorado con flores frescas dedicadas a la Virgen Santa en la festividad local.
examples.translation: The altar was decorated with fresh flowers dedicated to the Holy Virgin during the local festival.

definitions: An interjection expressing surprise, shock, dismay, or a plea for help, comparable to 'good heavens' or 'oh my God' in English.

examples.sentence: ¡Virgen Santa! No puedo creer que haya pasado eso en tan poco tiempo.
examples.translation: Good heavens! I can't believe that happened in such a short time.

examples.sentence: Cuando vio el accidente, exclamó: ¡Virgen Santa, qué horror!
examples.translation: When she saw the accident, she exclaimed: Oh my God, how horrible!

examples.sentence: Virgen Santa, ¿cómo vamos a solucionar este problema tan grave?
examples.translation: Good heavens, how are we going to solve this serious problem?

definitions: A literal borrowing from French meaning 'face to face' or 'in front of each other.'

examples.sentence: Los dos políticos se sentaron vis a vis para discutir el acuerdo bilateral.
examples.translation: The two politicians sat face to face to discuss the bilateral agreement.

examples.sentence: En la entrevista, el candidato y el entrevistador estuvieron vis a vis durante una hora.
examples.translation: In the interview, the candidate and the interviewer were face to face for an hour.

examples.sentence: Colocaron las sillas vis a vis para facilitar la conversación entre los participantes.
examples.translation: They placed the chairs face to face to facilitate the conversation among participants.

examples.sentence: Durante el debate, los oradores se posicionaron vis a vis para mantener contacto visual directo.
examples.translation: During the debate, the speakers positioned themselves face to face to maintain direct eye contact.

definitions: A meeting or interview between two people, often private or one-on-one.

examples.sentence: La reunión vis a vis con el director fue muy productiva para aclarar dudas importantes.
examples.translation: The face-to-face meeting with the director was very productive to clarify important doubts.

examples.sentence: Solicitaron un vis a vis con el abogado para hablar en privado sobre el caso.
examples.translation: They requested a one-on-one meeting with the lawyer to talk privately about the case.

examples.sentence: El periodista tuvo un vis a vis con el cantante para la entrevista exclusiva del mes.
examples.translation: The journalist had a one-on-one interview with the singer for the month's exclusive interview.

definitions: In the prison context, a supervised visit between an inmate and a visitor (which may include family members, lawyers, or intimate partners).

examples.sentence: El preso pidió un vis a vis con su familia para poder hablar cara a cara y sin barreras.
examples.translation: The inmate requested a supervised visit with his family to be able to speak face to face and without barriers.

examples.sentence: Durante el vis a vis, la esposa del recluso pudo entregarle libros y ropa limpia.
examples.translation: During the visit, the inmate's wife was able to give him books and clean clothes.

examples.sentence: El abogado solicitó un vis a vis con su cliente para preparar la estrategia legal confidencialmente.
examples.translation: The lawyer requested a private visit with his client to prepare the legal strategy confidentially.

definitions: A regulated visit permitted to a prisoner by their spouse or legal partner, intended to allow private conjugal contact and intimacy.

examples.sentence: La visita conyugal permitió a los presos mantener el vínculo con sus parejas en un espacio privado.
examples.translation: The conjugal visit allowed inmates to maintain their bond with their partners in a private space.

examples.sentence: Durante la visita conyugal, se les otorga privacidad para fortalecer su relación sentimental.
examples.translation: During the conjugal visit, they are granted privacy to strengthen their romantic relationship.

examples.sentence: El reglamento establece que la visita conyugal debe ser solicitada con anticipación y aprobada por la prisión.
examples.translation: The regulations establish that the conjugal visit must be requested in advance and approved by the prison.

definitions: A general term for a private or intimate visit between married partners or romantic partners, not necessarily in a prison context.

examples.sentence: En la visita conyugal que tuvimos el fin de semana, disfrutamos de un momento íntimo sin distracciones.
examples.translation: In the private visit we had over the weekend, we enjoyed an intimate moment without distractions.

examples.sentence: Los esposos organizaron una visita conyugal en su casa para celebrar su aniversario con tranquilidad.
examples.translation: The spouses organized a private visit at home to celebrate their anniversary peacefully.

examples.sentence: Aunque no estaban en prisión, valoraban mucho las visitas conyugales para mantener viva su relación.
examples.translation: Although they weren't in prison, they highly valued private visits to keep their relationship alive.

examples.sentence: Cada mes, la pareja se asegura de tener una visita conyugal para compartir tiempo de calidad juntos.
examples.translation: Every month, the couple makes sure to have a private visit to share quality time together.

definitions: To pay a literal visit to a man whose surname is Roca.

examples.sentence: Esta tarde iremos a visitar al señor Roca para discutir el contrato de arrendamiento.
examples.translation: This afternoon we will visit Mr. Roca to discuss the lease contract.

examples.sentence: Ayer visité al señor Roca en su oficina para aclarar algunas dudas sobre el proyecto.
examples.translation: Yesterday I visited Mr. Roca in his office to clarify some doubts about the project.

examples.sentence: ¿Has pensado en visitar al señor Roca antes de tomar una decisión final?
examples.translation: Have you thought about visiting Mr. Roca before making a final decision?

examples.sentence: Se recomienda visitar al señor Roca para obtener más información sobre el terreno.
examples.translation: It is recommended to visit Mr. Roca to obtain more information about the land.

definitions: A euphemistic expression for going to the restroom.

examples.sentence: Perdona, necesito visitar al señor Roca, ¿sabes dónde está el baño más cercano?
examples.translation: Excuse me, I need to visit Mr. Roca, do you know where the nearest bathroom is?

examples.sentence: Antes de continuar, me voy a visitar al señor Roca y vuelvo en un momento.
examples.translation: Before continuing, I am going to visit Mr. Roca and I'll be back in a moment.

examples.sentence: Cuando alguien dice que va a visitar al señor Roca, generalmente está usando un eufemismo para ir al baño.
examples.translation: When someone says they're going to visit Mr. Roca, they are usually using a euphemism to go to the bathroom.

definitions: The literal visual acuity characteristic of an eagle.

examples.sentence: Con su vista de águila, el guardabosques detectó el nido desde muy lejos.
examples.translation: With his eagle eye, the ranger spotted the nest from very far away.

examples.sentence: La vista de águila de María le permitió encontrar el error en el documento con facilidad.
examples.translation: María's eagle eye allowed her to easily find the mistake in the document.

examples.sentence: Los pilotos necesitan tener una vista de águila para percibir señales a gran distancia.
examples.translation: Pilots need to have eagle eyesight to perceive signals at great distances.

examples.sentence: El águila posee una vista de águila que le permite cazar con gran precisión.
examples.translation: The eagle has eagle eyesight that allows it to hunt with great precision.

definitions: Exceptional eyesight or the ability to notice small or distant details.

examples.sentence: Tienes vista de águila para notar detalles que otros pasan por alto.
examples.translation: You have eagle eyes to notice details that others overlook.

examples.sentence: Con vista de águila, el detective descubrió pistas clave en la escena del crimen.
examples.translation: With eagle eyesight, the detective discovered key clues at the crime scene.

examples.sentence: Si tuviera vista de águila, no me habría perdido ese pequeño error en el informe.
examples.translation: If I had eagle eyesight, I wouldn't have missed that small error in the report.

definitions: The literal visual sharpness attributed to a lynx.

examples.sentence: La vista de lince de este felino le permite detectar movimientos imperceptibles para otros animales.
examples.translation: The lynx's sharp eyesight allows it to detect imperceptible movements for other animals.

examples.sentence: Durante la noche, la vista de lince de los cazadores les ayudó a encontrar su presa.
examples.translation: During the night, the hunters' lynx-like vision helped them find their prey.

examples.sentence: El naturalista explicó que la vista de lince es esencial para la supervivencia de esta especie.
examples.translation: The naturalist explained that the lynx's sharp eyesight is essential for the survival of this species.

examples.sentence: Gracias a su vista de lince, el animal puede acechar sin ser detectado.
examples.translation: Thanks to its lynx eyesight, the animal can stalk without being detected.

definitions: Keen observation or the ability to detect subtle, concealed, or easily missed details.

examples.sentence: Con vista de lince, Laura detectó la falsificación en los documentos legales.
examples.translation: With lynx-like vision, Laura detected the forgery in the legal documents.

examples.sentence: No cualquiera tiene vista de lince para notar las pequeñas inconsistencias en los informes.
examples.translation: Not everyone has lynx-like eyesight to notice the small inconsistencies in the reports.

examples.sentence: Si tuvieras vista de lince, habrías visto que el cuadro estaba colgado torcido.
examples.translation: If you had lynx-like eyesight, you would have seen that the painting was hung crooked.

definitions: A literal view from above, as if seen by a bird in flight.

examples.sentence: Desde la cima, disfrutamos de una vista de pájaro del valle y sus ríos serpenteantes.
examples.translation: From the summit, we enjoyed a bird's-eye view of the valley and its winding rivers.

examples.sentence: El mapa muestra una vista de pájaro de toda la ciudad con sus principales avenidas y plazas.
examples.translation: The map shows a bird's-eye view of the entire city with its main avenues and squares.

examples.sentence: El fotógrafo capturó una impresionante vista de pájaro de la costa desde el dron.
examples.translation: The photographer captured an impressive bird's-eye view of the coast from the drone.

examples.sentence: La vista de pájaro desde el avión permitió observar las montañas y lagos con gran claridad.
examples.translation: The bird's-eye view from the plane allowed observing the mountains and lakes very clearly.

definitions: An overview or broad perspective that shows the general layout or main features rather than fine detail.

examples.sentence: El informe ofrece una vista de pájaro de los resultados financieros del último trimestre.
examples.translation: The report offers an overview of the financial results of the last quarter.

examples.sentence: Para entender el proyecto, primero necesitamos una vista de pájaro antes de entrar en detalles.
examples.translation: To understand the project, we first need a broad overview before going into details.

examples.sentence: La presentación dio una vista de pájaro de las tendencias del mercado actual.
examples.translation: The presentation gave an overview of current market trends.

definitions: A mark, signature, or notation indicating that a document or item has been examined and approved.

examples.sentence: El gerente estampó su visto bueno en el contrato para autorizar la compra de materiales.
examples.translation: The manager stamped his approval on the contract to authorize the purchase of materials.

examples.sentence: Sin el visto bueno del director, no podemos continuar con el proyecto.
examples.translation: Without the director's approval, we cannot continue with the project.

examples.sentence: Recibí el visto bueno del departamento legal para publicar el anuncio mañana.
examples.translation: I received the legal department's approval to publish the ad tomorrow.

definitions: Official approval or authorization to proceed with an action, project, or expenditure.

examples.sentence: Esperamos el visto bueno de la junta para iniciar la construcción del nuevo edificio.
examples.translation: We are waiting for the board's approval to start construction of the new building.

examples.sentence: La propuesta recibió el visto bueno oficial y comenzará a implementarse el próximo mes.
examples.translation: The proposal received official approval and will begin to be implemented next month.

examples.sentence: ¿Ya tienes el visto bueno para gastar el presupuesto asignado este trimestre?
examples.translation: Do you already have the approval to spend the budget allocated this quarter?

definitions: Literal: having seen what has been seen; acknowledging that one has observed the facts or events in question.

examples.sentence: Visto lo visto, creo que debemos cambiar nuestra estrategia de marketing.
examples.translation: Having seen what has been seen, I think we should change our marketing strategy.

examples.sentence: Visto lo visto hasta ahora, la reunión será más larga de lo esperado.
examples.translation: Considering what has been seen so far, the meeting will be longer than expected.

examples.sentence: Visto lo visto, la situación no mejorará sin un esfuerzo conjunto.
examples.translation: Given what has been seen, the situation won't improve without joint effort.

examples.sentence: He revisado todos los informes y, visto lo visto, hay que tomar medidas urgentes.
examples.translation: I have reviewed all the reports and, having seen everything, urgent measures must be taken.

definitions: Figurative: in view of what has occurred; considering the circumstances and therefore drawing a conclusion or deciding on a course of action.

examples.sentence: Visto lo visto, creo que lo mejor es cancelar el evento por la lluvia.
examples.translation: In view of what has happened, I think the best is to cancel the event due to the rain.

examples.sentence: Visto lo visto, parece que no hay otra opción que aceptar el acuerdo propuesto.
examples.translation: Considering the circumstances, it seems there's no other choice but to accept the proposed agreement.

examples.sentence: ¿No crees que, visto lo visto, deberíamos buscar alternativas diferentes para el proyecto?
examples.translation: Don't you think that, given what has happened, we should look for different alternatives for the project?

definitions: Literal: seen and then immediately not seen; describing something observed one moment and gone the next.

examples.sentence: El cometa fue visto y no visto, desapareciendo en segundos tras el horizonte.
examples.translation: The comet was seen and then immediately gone, disappearing in seconds beyond the horizon.

examples.sentence: El ladrón pasó por la calle visto y no visto, sin que nadie pudiera reaccionar a tiempo.
examples.translation: The thief went down the street seen and then gone, without anyone reacting in time.

examples.sentence: Vi la sombra fugaz del ave visto y no visto mientras caminaba por el bosque.
examples.translation: I saw the fleeting shadow of the bird seen and then gone while walking through the forest.

examples.sentence: El rayo iluminó el cielo visto y no visto, dejando a todos sorprendidos.
examples.translation: The lightning lit up the sky seen and then gone, leaving everyone surprised.

definitions: Figurative: very quickly or in an instant; done or completed in no time.

examples.sentence: Prepararon la fiesta visto y no visto, sin que los invitados sospecharan nada.
examples.translation: They prepared the party in no time, without the guests suspecting anything.

examples.sentence: El técnico arregló el problema visto y no visto, y todo volvió a funcionar perfectamente.
examples.translation: The technician fixed the problem in an instant, and everything worked perfectly again.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes, hago esa tarea visto y no visto para que puedas salir temprano.
examples.translation: Don't worry, I'll do that task very quickly so you can leave early.

definitions: Literal: a living picture or vivid likeness, understood as a striking visual representation.

examples.sentence: El retrato es una viva estampa de su abuelo cuando era joven.
examples.translation: The portrait is a living picture of his grandfather when he was young.

examples.sentence: Visitar el museo es como contemplar una viva estampa de la historia local.
examples.translation: Visiting the museum is like beholding a vivid likeness of local history.

examples.sentence: La estatua refleja una viva estampa de la personalidad del héroe nacional.
examples.translation: The statue reflects a vivid likeness of the national hero's personality.

examples.sentence: Este cuadro es una viva estampa que captura la esencia del paisaje otoñal.
examples.translation: This painting is a living picture that captures the essence of the autumn landscape.

definitions: Figurative: a striking resemblance or the spitting image of someone.

examples.sentence: Eres una viva estampa de tu padre, con sus mismos gestos y mirada.
examples.translation: You are the spitting image of your father, with the same gestures and gaze.

examples.sentence: Cuando vi a los hermanos juntos, pensé que eran una viva estampa el uno del otro.
examples.translation: When I saw the brothers together, I thought they were the spitting image of each other.

examples.sentence: Ese niño es una viva estampa de su madre, no solo en apariencia sino también en carácter.
examples.translation: That boy is the spitting image of his mother, not only in appearance but also in character.

definitions: Literal: a living image; an expression emphasizing a clear visual likeness to another person.

examples.sentence: El niño es la viva imagen de su abuelo cuando tenía su edad.
examples.translation: The boy is the living image of his grandfather when he was his age.

examples.sentence: En la foto antigua, ella es la viva imagen de su bisabuela con el mismo peinado.
examples.translation: In the old photo, she is the living image of her great-grandmother with the same hairstyle.

examples.sentence: La estatua representa la viva imagen de un guerrero legendario de la región.
examples.translation: The statue represents the living image of a legendary warrior from the region.

examples.sentence: Su rostro es la viva imagen de la pintura renacentista que vimos en el museo.
examples.translation: His face is the living image of the Renaissance painting we saw at the museum.

definitions: Figurative: an exact likeness or the spitting image, often applied to physical resemblance or strong similarity of demeanor.

examples.sentence: María es la viva imagen de su madre en la forma de hablar y de comportarse.
examples.translation: María is the spitting image of her mother in the way she talks and behaves.

examples.sentence: Ese joven es la viva imagen de su abuelo, no solo en lo físico sino también en sus valores.
examples.translation: That young man is the spitting image of his grandfather, not only physically but also in his values.

examples.sentence: Cuando caminas, eres la viva imagen de tu padre, con su mismo paso decidido.
examples.translation: When you walk, you are the spitting image of your father, with his same determined stride.

definitions: Figurative: a person who embodies the qualities, traits, or character of another.

examples.sentence: Juan es la viva imagen de un líder, siempre dispuesto a ayudar y tomar decisiones justas.
examples.translation: Juan embodies the qualities of a leader, always willing to help and make fair decisions.

examples.sentence: Ella es la viva imagen de la perseverancia, nunca se rinde ante los obstáculos.
examples.translation: She is the embodiment of perseverance, never giving up in the face of obstacles.

examples.sentence: Ese profesor es la viva imagen de la dedicación, entregando siempre lo mejor a sus alumnos.
examples.translation: That teacher embodies dedication, always giving his best to his students.

definitions: Literal: to live one day at a time; to subsist on daily income without long-term savings.

examples.sentence: Después de perder su trabajo, Juan tuvo que vivir al día, sin poder ahorrar nada para el futuro.
examples.translation: After losing his job, Juan had to live one day at a time, unable to save anything for the future.

examples.sentence: No vivimos al día; siempre guardamos algo para emergencias y planes a largo plazo.
examples.translation: We don't live day to day; we always save something for emergencies and long-term plans.

examples.sentence: Si sigues viviendo al día, nunca podrás comprar una casa propia ni planear tus vacaciones soñadas.
examples.translation: If you keep living day to day, you'll never be able to buy your own house or plan your dream vacations.

examples.sentence: María vivía al día mientras estudiaba, usando su pequeño trabajo para cubrir solo los gastos esenciales.
examples.translation: María lived day to day while studying, using her small job to cover only essential expenses.

definitions: Figurative: to keep up with current events or trends; to stay up to date with changing circumstances.

examples.sentence: Me gusta vivir al día con las noticias para no perderme nada importante del mundo.
examples.translation: I like to keep up to date with the news so I don't miss anything important in the world.

examples.sentence: Aunque no soy experto, trato de vivir al día en cuanto a tecnología para poder ayudar a mis hijos.
examples.translation: Although I'm not an expert, I try to stay up to date with technology to be able to help my kids.

examples.sentence: ¿Cómo haces para vivir al día con todas las tendencias que cambian tan rápido en la moda?
examples.translation: How do you manage to keep up with all the trends that change so quickly in fashion?

definitions: To live with physical ease or comfort, without excessive restrictions on daily life.

examples.sentence: Desde que se mudaron a esa casa grande, Ana y Carlos viven con desahogo, disfrutando de espacio y tranquilidad.
examples.translation: Since moving to that big house, Ana and Carlos live comfortably, enjoying space and tranquility.

examples.sentence: No me gusta vivir con desahogo; prefiero una vida sencilla pero sin preocupaciones excesivas.
examples.translation: I don't like living with ease; I prefer a simple life but without excessive worries.

examples.sentence: Después de la operación, el doctor le recomendó vivir con desahogo para facilitar su recuperación.
examples.translation: After the surgery, the doctor recommended living with physical ease to facilitate recovery.

definitions: To live comfortably and without significant financial worries; to have sufficient means to meet needs and occasional extras.

examples.sentence: Gracias al buen trabajo de su esposa, Pablo puede vivir con desahogo y sin preocupaciones económicas.
examples.translation: Thanks to his wife's good job, Pablo can live comfortably and without financial worries.

examples.sentence: Si quieres vivir con desahogo, es importante controlar tus gastos y ahorrar para imprevistos.
examples.translation: If you want to live comfortably, it is important to control your expenses and save for unforeseen events.

examples.sentence: Aunque vive con desahogo, siempre es modesto y ayuda a quienes lo necesitan en su comunidad.
examples.translation: Although he lives comfortably, he is always modest and helps those in need in his community.

definitions: Literally, to live from the story or narrative.

examples.sentence: El cuentacuentos vive del cuento, narrando historias en plazas y eventos culturales.
examples.translation: The storyteller lives from the story, narrating tales in plazas and cultural events.

examples.sentence: En la novela, el personaje principal vive del cuento que inventa para sobrevivir en la ciudad.
examples.translation: In the novel, the main character literally lives from the story he invents to survive in the city.

examples.sentence: Los escritores freelance a menudo viven del cuento, ganando dinero con sus relatos y artículos.
examples.translation: Freelance writers often live from the story, earning money with their tales and articles.

examples.sentence: Aunque pareciera que vive del cuento, en realidad trabaja duro para crear sus relatos y ganar su sustento.
examples.translation: Although it seems he lives from the story, in reality he works hard to create his tales and earn his living.

definitions: To make a living by deceiving, scheming, or exploiting others; to obtain benefits through charm, lies, or manipulation.

examples.sentence: Luis siempre vive del cuento, engañando a sus amigos para conseguir dinero fácil.
examples.translation: Luis always makes a living by scheming, tricking his friends to get easy money.

examples.sentence: No quiero vivir del cuento ni aprovecharme de nadie; prefiero trabajar honestamente por lo mío.
examples.translation: I don't want to live by deceiving or exploiting others; I prefer to work honestly for what is mine.

examples.sentence: Ella vivió del cuento durante años, hasta que la descubrieron y perdió la confianza de todos.
examples.translation: She made a living by manipulating others for years, until she was found out and lost everyone's trust.

definitions: To avoid honest work and live at the expense of others; to be a freeloader or shirker.

examples.sentence: Mi primo vive del cuento, siempre esperando que su familia le dé dinero sin hacer nada.
examples.translation: My cousin freeloads, always expecting his family to give him money without doing anything.

examples.sentence: No seas como él, que vive del cuento y nunca asume responsabilidades ni trabaja en serio.
examples.translation: Don't be like him, who shirks work and never takes responsibility or works seriously.

examples.sentence: Durante años vivieron del cuento, pero al final tuvieron que buscar empleo para sostenerse.
examples.translation: For years they lived freeloading, but in the end they had to find jobs to support themselves.

definitions: To spend more money than one can afford; to live beyond one's financial means.
idiom: vivir por encima de sus posibilidades

examples.sentence: María siempre ha vivido por encima de sus posibilidades, comprando cosas que no puede pagar.
examples.translation: María has always lived beyond her means, buying things she can't afford.
examples.matched_span: vivido por encima de sus posibilidades

examples.sentence: Si seguimos viviendo por encima de nuestras posibilidades, pronto tendremos problemas financieros graves.
examples.translation: If we keep living beyond our means, soon we will have serious financial problems.
examples.matched_span: viviendo por encima de nuestras posibilidades

examples.sentence: Él admitió que vivió por encima de sus posibilidades durante años, pero ahora busca cambiar su estilo de vida.
examples.translation: He admitted that he lived beyond his means for years, but now he seeks to change his lifestyle.
examples.matched_span: vivió por encima de sus posibilidades

definitions: To maintain an unsustainable lifestyle that depends on credit or external support rather than available income.
idiom: vivir por encima de sus posibilidades

examples.sentence: Vivir por encima de sus posibilidades es insostenible si solo dependes del crédito para pagar tus gastos.
examples.translation: Living beyond your means is unsustainable if you depend only on credit to pay your expenses.
examples.matched_span: Vivir por encima de sus posibilidades

examples.sentence: La familia vivía por encima de sus posibilidades, acumulando deudas que no pudieron pagar después.
examples.translation: The family lived beyond their means, accumulating debts they couldn't pay later.
examples.matched_span: vivía por encima de sus posibilidades

examples.sentence: Muchos jóvenes caen en la trampa de vivir por encima de sus posibilidades porque quieren aparentar más de lo que tienen.
examples.translation: Many young people fall into the trap of living beyond their means because they want to appear richer than they are.
examples.matched_span: vivir por encima de sus posibilidades

definitions: Literally, alive and wriggling or vigorous.

examples.sentence: A pesar del accidente, el gato quedó vivito y coleando, corriendo por la casa como siempre.
examples.translation: Despite the accident, the cat was alive and well, running around the house as usual.

examples.sentence: Los médicos dijeron que el paciente estaba vivito y coleando después de la cirugía complicada.
examples.translation: The doctors said the patient was alive and kicking after the complicated surgery.

examples.sentence: El pez salió del agua por un momento, pero volvió vivito y coleando al acuario.
examples.translation: The fish jumped out of the water for a moment, but came back alive and well to the aquarium.

examples.sentence: Aunque parecía muerto, el insecto estaba vivito y coleando cuando lo pusimos bajo la lupa.
examples.translation: Although it seemed dead, the insect was alive and wriggling when we put it under the magnifying glass.

definitions: Figuratively, to be very much alive and well; to have survived an ordeal or be unexpectedly still active.

examples.sentence: Después de años sin noticias, me alegra saber que tu abuelo está vivito y coleando.
examples.translation: After years without news, I'm glad to know your grandfather is alive and well.

examples.sentence: Pensé que el proyecto había fracasado, pero sigue vivito y coleando gracias al esfuerzo del equipo.
examples.translation: I thought the project had failed, but it's still alive and kicking thanks to the team's effort.

examples.sentence: Aunque parecía que la empresa iba a quebrar, ahora está vivita y coleando en el mercado.
examples.translation: Although it seemed the company was going to go bankrupt, now it's alive and well in the market.

definitions: To fly into the sky; to travel through the air toward the heavens.

examples.sentence: El pájaro extendió sus alas y comenzó a volar al cielo con gracia y libertad.
examples.translation: The bird spread its wings and began to fly into the sky with grace and freedom.

examples.sentence: Durante la excursión, vimos cómo los planeadores volaban al cielo impulsados por las corrientes de aire.
examples.translation: During the excursion, we saw how the gliders flew into the sky propelled by air currents.

examples.sentence: El dron voló al cielo para capturar imágenes panorámicas de la ciudad desde arriba.
examples.translation: The drone flew into the sky to capture panoramic images of the city from above.

examples.sentence: Los niños lanzaron sus cometas y las vieron volar al cielo en una tarde ventosa y soleada.
examples.translation: The children flew their kites and watched them fly into the sky on a windy, sunny afternoon.

definitions: Figuratively, to die and go to heaven.

examples.sentence: Cuando su abuelo voló al cielo, toda la familia se reunió para recordarlo con amor y tristeza.
examples.translation: When his grandfather passed away (flew to heaven), the whole family gathered to remember him with love and sadness.

examples.sentence: Dicen que volar al cielo es encontrar paz eterna después de una vida llena de esfuerzo y cariño.
examples.translation: They say flying to heaven is finding eternal peace after a life full of effort and love.

examples.sentence: Aunque duele, sabemos que voló al cielo y ahora está en un lugar mejor sin sufrimiento.
examples.translation: Although it hurts, we know he flew to heaven and is now in a better place without suffering.

definitions: To experience intense joy, elation, or exhilaration; to feel as if one is soaring emotionally.

examples.sentence: Cuando recibí la buena noticia, sentí que volaba al cielo de la emoción y la alegría.
examples.translation: When I received the good news, I felt like I was soaring with excitement and joy.

examples.sentence: Ella siempre vuela al cielo cuando escucha su canción favorita en la radio.
examples.translation: She always feels elated when she hears her favorite song on the radio.

examples.sentence: Después de ganar el premio, Juan voló al cielo y no podía dejar de sonreír en todo el día.
examples.translation: After winning the prize, Juan was over the moon and couldn't stop smiling all day.

definitions: Literal: to fly using one's own wings; to move through the air by means of one's own wings.

examples.sentence: El halcón voló con sus propias alas, surcando el cielo con destreza y velocidad.
examples.translation: The hawk flew with its own wings, soaring through the sky with skill and speed.

examples.sentence: Los pichones aprendieron a volar con sus propias alas tras varias semanas de práctica en el nido.
examples.translation: The chicks learned to fly with their own wings after several weeks of practice in the nest.

examples.sentence: Durante la exhibición, el loro voló con sus propias alas, sorprendiendo a todos los espectadores.
examples.translation: During the show, the parrot flew with its own wings, surprising all the spectators.

examples.sentence: El águila no necesita ayuda; vuela con sus propias alas para cazar y desplazarse largas distancias.
examples.translation: The eagle needs no help; it flies with its own wings to hunt and travel long distances.

definitions: Figurative: to become independent or self-sufficient; to manage or succeed without relying on others.

examples.sentence: Después de años dependiendo de sus padres, finalmente decidió volar con sus propias alas y mudarse solo.
examples.translation: After years depending on his parents, he finally decided to become independent and move out on his own.

examples.sentence: Es importante que los jóvenes aprendan a volar con sus propias alas para enfrentar los retos del mundo adulto.
examples.translation: It is important for young people to learn to stand on their own feet to face the challenges of adulthood.

examples.sentence: Aunque tuvo apoyo al principio, ahora Marta vuela con sus propias alas y maneja su negocio exitosamente.
examples.translation: Although she had support at first, now Marta is independent and runs her business successfully.

definitions: Literal: to make a lariat or rope whirl or fly through the air when throwing it.

examples.sentence: El vaquero voló riata con mucha habilidad para atrapar el ganado en la pradera.
examples.translation: The cowboy skillfully swung the lariat through the air to catch the cattle in the prairie.

examples.sentence: En la competencia, Juan voló riata rápidamente para demostrar su destreza ante el público.
examples.translation: In the competition, Juan whirled the lasso quickly to show his skill before the audience.

examples.sentence: Durante la fiesta, los niños aprendieron a volar riata con la ayuda del instructor del rodeo.
examples.translation: During the party, the children learned how to swing the lariat with the help of the rodeo instructor.

examples.sentence: El vaquero voló riata sobre su cabeza antes de lanzarla para atrapar al toro.
examples.translation: The cowboy swung the lariat over his head before throwing it to catch the bull.

definitions: Figurative: to take off quickly or flee suddenly; to depart or escape in haste.

examples.sentence: Cuando vio a la policía, el ladrón voló riata dejando todo atrás para escapar.
examples.translation: When he saw the police, the thief took off quickly leaving everything behind to escape.

examples.sentence: No esperes que se quede mucho tiempo; suele volar riata cuando las cosas se complican.
examples.translation: Don't expect him to stay long; he usually bolts when things get complicated.

examples.sentence: Al terminar la reunión, Marta voló riata sin despedirse porque tenía prisa para otra cita.
examples.translation: After the meeting, Marta took off without saying goodbye because she was in a hurry for another appointment.

definitions: Literal: to return to the same paths or routes previously taken.

examples.sentence: Después de un largo viaje, volvieron a las andadas y recorrieron los caminos que conocían de niños.
examples.translation: After a long trip, they returned to the same old paths they knew as children.

examples.sentence: El sendero se bifurcaba, pero decidieron volver a las andadas por la ruta más segura.
examples.translation: The trail forked, but they decided to go back the same way by the safer route.

examples.sentence: Los exploradores volvieron a las andadas para encontrar el campamento base perdido en la montaña.
examples.translation: The explorers retraced their steps to find the lost base camp in the mountain.

examples.sentence: Al caer la noche, el grupo decidió volver a las andadas y regresar al refugio antes de que oscureciera.
examples.translation: At nightfall, the group decided to turn back and return to the shelter before it got dark.

definitions: Figurative: to revert to former bad habits, vices, or misconduct after a period of improvement or reform.

examples.sentence: Después de meses sin fumar, Pedro volvió a las andadas y encendió un cigarrillo en la fiesta.
examples.translation: After months without smoking, Pedro fell back into old habits and lit a cigarette at the party.

examples.sentence: No quiero que vuelvas a las andadas; sé que esta vez puedes mantenerte en el buen camino.
examples.translation: I don't want you to revert to your old ways; I know this time you can stay on the right path.

examples.sentence: La empresa volvió a las andadas con prácticas poco éticas tras el cambio de directivos.
examples.translation: The company reverted to bad practices after the change in management.

definitions: Literal: to regain consciousness after fainting, sleep, or stupor.

examples.sentence: Cuando lo encontraron desmayado, tardó unos minutos en volver en sí y responder a las preguntas.
examples.translation: When they found him unconscious, it took a few minutes to regain consciousness and respond to questions.

examples.sentence: Después de la anestesia, la paciente volvió en sí lentamente en la sala de recuperación.
examples.translation: After the anesthesia, the patient gradually regained consciousness in the recovery room.

examples.sentence: El boxeador no volvió en sí hasta que el árbitro detuvo la pelea para darle atención médica.
examples.translation: The boxer did not regain consciousness until the referee stopped the fight to give him medical attention.

examples.sentence: Al caer y golpearse la cabeza, el niño estuvo inconsciente por un momento antes de volver en sí.
examples.translation: After falling and hitting his head, the child was unconscious for a moment before regaining consciousness.

definitions: Figurative: to come to one's senses or regain mental clarity and composure.

examples.sentence: Después de la discusión, finalmente volvió en sí y comprendió que había exagerado su reacción.
examples.translation: After the argument, he finally came to his senses and realized he had overreacted.

examples.sentence: Espero que pronto vuelvas en sí y veas que tus decisiones afectan a toda la familia.
examples.translation: I hope you come to your senses soon and see that your decisions affect the whole family.

examples.sentence: Tras meses de confusión, Marta volvió en sí y comenzó a tomar el control de su vida nuevamente.
examples.translation: After months of confusion, Marta regained mental clarity and began to take control of her life again.

definitions: Literal: to turn so that the hindquarters face forward, as when an animal reverses direction.

examples.sentence: El caballo volvió grupas y salió galopando en dirección contraria al jinete.
examples.translation: The horse turned so that its hindquarters faced forward and galloped in the opposite direction to the rider.

examples.sentence: Cuando el perro escuchó el ruido extraño, volvió grupas y se escondió debajo de la mesa.
examples.translation: When the dog heard the strange noise, it turned around and hid under the table.

examples.sentence: Durante el entrenamiento, el burro volvió grupas varias veces antes de obedecer la orden del pastor.
examples.translation: During training, the donkey repeatedly turned around before obeying the shepherd's command.

examples.sentence: El gato volvió grupas al notar la presencia del perro y decidió buscar otro lugar para descansar.
examples.translation: The cat turned tail when it noticed the dog’s presence and decided to find another place to rest.

definitions: Figurative: to retreat, withdraw, or backtrack from a position, commitment, or confrontation.

examples.sentence: Ante las críticas, el político volvió grupas y modificó su postura para evitar conflictos mayores.
examples.translation: Faced with criticism, the politician backtracked and changed his stance to avoid bigger conflicts.

examples.sentence: No podemos volver grupas ahora que hemos comprometido nuestro apoyo; debemos mantenernos firmes.
examples.translation: We can’t retreat now that we have committed our support; we must stand firm.

examples.sentence: Ella volvió grupas cuando escuchó que la propuesta no tenía el respaldo necesario para aprobarse.
examples.translation: She backed down when she heard the proposal did not have the necessary support to be approved.

definitions: Literal: to return to one's former legal rights, privileges, jurisdiction, or customary authority.

examples.sentence: Tras ganar el juicio, el señor Pérez volvió por sus fueros y recuperó sus derechos sobre la propiedad.
examples.translation: After winning the lawsuit, Mr. Pérez returned to his former rights and recovered his property rights.

examples.sentence: La región volvió por sus fueros cuando se restauraron las leyes locales que habían sido suspendidas.
examples.translation: The region returned to its former jurisdiction when the local laws that had been suspended were restored.

examples.sentence: Durante siglos, el noble volvió por sus fueros para mantener su autoridad sobre sus tierras y vasallos.
examples.translation: For centuries, the noble returned to his customary privileges to maintain his authority over his lands and vassals.

examples.sentence: Después de la disputa, la comunidad volvió por sus fueros y retomó sus tradiciones ancestrales.
examples.translation: After the dispute, the community resumed its customary authority and traditions.

definitions: Figurative: to reassert one's authority, dignity, or customary behaviour; to resume the confident or dominant attitude one had before being challenged or diminished.

examples.sentence: Tras el incidente, el director volvió por sus fueros y volvió a imponer disciplina en la escuela.
examples.translation: After the incident, the principal reasserted his authority and restored discipline at the school.

examples.sentence: Cuando lo desafiaron, Marta volvió por sus fueros y defendió su posición con firmeza y seguridad.
examples.translation: When challenged, Marta reasserted her dignity and defended her position firmly and confidently.

examples.sentence: Después de meses de dudas, la empresa volvió por sus fueros y recuperó la confianza de sus clientes.
examples.translation: After months of doubts, the company regained its confident stance and the trust of its clients.

definitions: Literal: a complete roll or somersault of a vehicle, boat, or object (a rollover) in which it turns over one or more times.

examples.sentence: El coche sufrió una vuelta de campana tras perder el control en la curva peligrosa.
examples.translation: The car rolled over after losing control on the dangerous curve.

examples.sentence: Durante la tormenta, el barco dio una vuelta de campana por la fuerza de las olas gigantescas.
examples.translation: During the storm, the boat capsized due to the force of the gigantic waves.

examples.sentence: El ciclista perdió el equilibrio y dio una vuelta de campana antes de detenerse en el suelo.
examples.translation: The cyclist lost balance and did a somersault before stopping on the ground.

examples.sentence: Vimos cómo el camión hizo una vuelta de campana en la autopista debido a la velocidad excesiva.
examples.translation: We saw how the truck rolled over on the highway due to excessive speed.

definitions: Figurative: a sudden, dramatic reversal or turnaround of circumstances, fortunes, or events.

examples.sentence: La situación económica dio una vuelta de campana cuando la empresa principal cerró sus puertas.
examples.translation: The economic situation took a sudden turn when the main company closed its doors.

examples.sentence: Con la llegada del nuevo director, la organización dio una vuelta de campana y mejoró notablemente su gestión.
examples.translation: With the arrival of the new director, the organization underwent a dramatic turnaround and notably improved its management.

examples.sentence: Después de perder clientes importantes, el negocio dio una vuelta de campana y tuvo que replantear su estrategia.
examples.translation: After losing important clients, the business experienced a dramatic reversal and had to rethink its strategy.

definitions: Used to indicate that a list or enumeration ends there, implying no more items or details will be added; equivalent to 'and that's it' or 'and that's all'.

examples.sentence: Compré frutas, verduras, pan y para de contar; ya no necesitaba nada más para la cena.
examples.translation: I bought fruits, vegetables, bread, and that's it; I didn't need anything else for dinner.

examples.sentence: En la reunión hablaron de los problemas financieros, las soluciones posibles y para de contar, no hubo tiempo para más.
examples.translation: In the meeting they talked about financial problems, possible solutions, and that's all; there was no time for more.

examples.sentence: El profesor explicó los conceptos básicos, las reglas principales y para de contar, dejando el resto para el próximo curso.
examples.translation: The teacher explained the basic concepts, the main rules, and that's it, leaving the rest for the next course.

examples.sentence: Hizo una lista de tareas: limpiar la casa, hacer la compra, preparar la comida y para de contar.
examples.translation: She made a list of tasks: clean the house, do the shopping, prepare the food, and that's all.

definitions: Literal: used in lists to mean 'and an egg' as an additional item.

examples.sentence: Para el desayuno compré leche, pan, mantequilla y un huevo para completar la lista.
examples.translation: For breakfast I bought milk, bread, butter, and an egg to complete the list.

examples.sentence: En la receta necesitas harina, azúcar, leche y un huevo para que la mezcla quede perfecta.
examples.translation: In the recipe you need flour, sugar, milk, and an egg for the mixture to be perfect.

examples.sentence: La cesta llevaba manzanas, naranjas, plátanos y un huevo que alguien había olvidado poner en la nevera.
examples.translation: The basket contained apples, oranges, bananas, and an egg that someone had forgotten to put in the fridge.

examples.sentence: En la lista de la compra anoté arroz, frijoles, aceite y un huevo para preparar la cena rápida.
examples.translation: On the shopping list I wrote rice, beans, oil, and an egg to prepare a quick dinner.

definitions: Colloquial quantifier: used after a noun to mean 'a lot' or 'a great deal' (equivalent to 'a ton of' or 'loads of').

examples.sentence: En la fiesta había comida y un huevo, todos quedaron satisfechos.
examples.translation: At the party, there was food and a ton of it; everyone was satisfied.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes por los libros, tengo y un huevo para prestarte si quieres.
examples.translation: Don't worry about the books, I have loads of them to lend you if you want.

examples.sentence: Cuando fuimos a la playa, llevamos toallas y un huevo para la familia.
examples.translation: When we went to the beach, we brought towels and a great deal more for the family.

definitions: Dismissive exclamation: used to express refusal, disagreement, or disbelief, equivalent to 'yeah, right' or 'no way' in English.

examples.sentence: ¿Crees que Juan va a cambiar de opinión? — ¡Y un huevo! Él nunca cambia.
examples.translation: Do you think Juan is going to change his mind? — Yeah, right! He never changes.

examples.sentence: Me dijo que me ayudaría mañana, pero yo le respondí: '¡Y un huevo!' No confío en él.
examples.translation: He told me he'd help me tomorrow, but I replied, 'No way!' I don't trust him.

examples.sentence: ¿Vas a llegar temprano esta vez? — ¡Y un huevo! Siempre llego tarde.
examples.translation: Are you going to arrive early this time? — No way! I always arrive late.

definitions: Used to express resignation or acceptance when something cannot be changed; equivalent to 'there's nothing to be done', 'oh well', or 'too bad'.

examples.sentence: Perdimos el tren y ya ni modo, tuvimos que esperar el siguiente.
examples.translation: We missed the train and oh well, we had to wait for the next one.

examples.sentence: Si no te quieren en el trabajo, ya ni modo, busca otro lugar donde te valoren.
examples.translation: If they don't want you at the job, there's nothing to be done; look for another place that values you.

examples.sentence: Intenté arreglar la computadora, pero no funcionó, ya ni modo.
examples.translation: I tried to fix the computer, but it didn't work, oh well.

examples.sentence: Ya ni modo quejarse, el examen fue difícil para todos.
examples.translation: There's nothing to be done about complaining; the exam was hard for everyone.

definitions: Literally, given that we are (here or in this situation); used to point out the current circumstance.

examples.sentence: Ya que estamos en la oficina, podríamos aprovechar para organizar los archivos.
examples.translation: Given that we are in the office, we could take the opportunity to organize the files.

examples.sentence: Ya que estamos en la ciudad, ¿quieres que te muestre los mejores lugares para comer?
examples.translation: Since we are in the city, do you want me to show you the best places to eat?

examples.sentence: Ya que estamos aquí, vamos a visitar el museo antes de que cierre.
examples.translation: Since we are here, let's visit the museum before it closes.

examples.sentence: Ya que estamos en el parque, ¿por qué no hacemos un picnic?
examples.translation: Given that we are in the park, why don't we have a picnic?

definitions: Figuratively, a discourse marker meaning 'while we're at it' or 'since this is the case,' used to introduce an additional request, action, or comment that follows naturally from the present situation.

examples.sentence: Ya que estamos hablando de dinero, ¿podrías ayudarme con un préstamo pequeño?
examples.translation: While we're at it talking about money, could you help me with a small loan?

examples.sentence: Ya que estamos en la reunión, aprovecho para comentar el proyecto que tengo en mente.
examples.translation: Since this is the case in the meeting, I'll take the chance to mention the project I have in mind.

examples.sentence: Ya que estamos arreglando la casa, sería bueno pintar las paredes también.
examples.translation: While we're fixing the house, it would be good to paint the walls too.

definitions: Literally, the phrase 'we'll see,' said the blind man; a quoted utterance with no idiomatic implication when taken at face value.

examples.sentence: —¿Crees que lloverá mañana? —Ya veremos, dijo el ciego.
examples.translation: —Do you think it will rain tomorrow? —We'll see, said the blind man.

examples.sentence: Cuando le preguntaron si terminaría el proyecto a tiempo, respondió: 'Ya veremos, dijo el ciego.'
examples.translation: When they asked him if he would finish the project on time, he answered: 'We'll see, said the blind man.'

examples.sentence: Mi abuelo siempre decía 'Ya veremos, dijo el ciego' cuando no estaba seguro de algo.
examples.translation: My grandfather always said 'We'll see, said the blind man' when he wasn't sure about something.

examples.sentence: Le pregunté si vendría a la fiesta y me contestó con un 'Ya veremos, dijo el ciego.'
examples.translation: I asked him if he would come to the party and he answered me with a 'We'll see, said the blind man.'

definitions: Figuratively, an ironic or skeptical retort meaning 'we'll see' while implying doubt, disbelief, or that the stated outcome is unlikely to occur.

examples.sentence: —Dicen que ese nuevo método funciona a la perfección. —Ya veremos, dijo el ciego.
examples.translation: —They say that new method works perfectly. —We'll see, said the blind man.

examples.sentence: Me prometió que llegaría temprano, pero yo sólo pensé, 'Ya veremos, dijo el ciego.'
examples.translation: He promised me he'd arrive early, but I just thought, 'We'll see, said the blind man.'

examples.sentence: Cuando el político aseguró que bajaría los impuestos, respondí: 'Ya veremos, dijo el ciego.'
examples.translation: When the politician assured that he would lower taxes, I replied: 'We'll see, said the blind man.'

definitions: Literally, 'what fault do I have?'; a rhetorical question used to deny personal blame or responsibility for a situation.

examples.sentence: Yo qué culpa tengo si la reunión se atrasó, yo llegué puntual.
examples.translation: What fault do I have if the meeting was delayed? I arrived on time.

examples.sentence: Si el proyecto falló, yo qué culpa tengo, yo seguí todas las indicaciones.
examples.translation: If the project failed, it's not my fault; I followed all the instructions.

examples.sentence: ¿Por qué me culpas de la confusión? Yo qué culpa tengo si no me avisaron.
examples.translation: Why do you blame me for the confusion? What fault do I have if they didn't inform me?

examples.sentence: Yo qué culpa tengo que la impresora se haya descompuesto justo hoy.
examples.translation: What fault do I have that the printer broke down just today?

definitions: Figuratively, an expression meaning 'it's not my fault' or 'I can't help it,' employed to deflect accusation or to excuse one's inability to control events.

examples.sentence: No me culpes por el accidente, yo qué culpa tengo si el semáforo no funcionaba.
examples.translation: Don't blame me for the accident, it's not my fault if the traffic light wasn't working.

examples.sentence: Me dijeron que la reunión era a las 3, no a las 2, yo qué culpa tengo si me equivoqué.
examples.translation: They told me the meeting was at 3, not 2; I can't help it if I got it wrong.

examples.sentence: Si perdimos el partido, yo qué culpa tengo, jugamos con un equipo mucho mejor.
examples.translation: If we lost the game, it's not my fault; we played against a much better team.

definitions: Literally, 'I know you'; a straightforward statement of personal acquaintance or familiarity with someone.

examples.sentence: Yo te conozco desde la infancia, siempre has sido una persona amable.
examples.translation: I have known you since childhood; you have always been a kind person.

examples.sentence: Cuando dije que podrías confiar en ella, fue porque yo te conozco y sé que eres honesto.
examples.translation: When I said you could trust her, it was because I know you and I know you are honest.

examples.sentence: Si necesitas ayuda, dímelo, yo te conozco y sé cómo apoyarte.
examples.translation: If you need help, tell me; I know you and I know how to support you.

examples.sentence: No te preocupes por el examen, yo te conozco y sé que estudiarás duro.
examples.translation: Don't worry about the exam; I know you and I know you'll study hard.

definitions: Figuratively, an assertion that one understands a person's character, habits, or likely behaviour, often used to imply predictability, to issue a warning, or to indicate that further proof is unnecessary.

examples.sentence: No creas que me convencerás con esa excusa, yo te conozco y sé que estás mintiendo.
examples.translation: Don't think you'll convince me with that excuse; I know you and I know you're lying.

examples.sentence: Si decides irte sin avisar, ya sabes que yo te conozco y no me sorprenderé.
examples.translation: If you decide to leave without warning, you know I know you and I won't be surprised.

examples.sentence: No intentes engañarme, yo te conozco y sé cuáles son tus verdaderas intenciones.
examples.translation: Don't try to fool me; I know you and I know what your true intentions are.

definitions: Literally, a vulture watching meat; an image describing a scavenger observing flesh.

examples.sentence: El zamuro cuidando carne espera pacientemente a que la carroña aparezca.
examples.translation: The vulture watching meat waits patiently for the carrion to appear.

examples.sentence: Desde la rama, el zamuro cuidando carne observa todo a su alrededor.
examples.translation: From the branch, the vulture watching meat observes everything around.

examples.sentence: En el documental mostraron un zamuro cuidando carne en el desierto.
examples.translation: In the documentary, they showed a vulture watching meat in the desert.

examples.sentence: Durante horas, el zamuro cuidando carne no se movió de su lugar.
examples.translation: For hours, the vulture watching meat didn't move from its place.

definitions: Figuratively, a pejorative expression for a person entrusted with guarding or overseeing something who actually intends to exploit, appropriate, or take advantage of it—similar in sense to 'the fox guarding the henhouse.'

examples.sentence: No confío en ese gerente, es un zamuro cuidando carne que solo busca beneficio personal.
examples.translation: I don't trust that manager; he's a vulture watching meat who only seeks personal gain.

examples.sentence: Le dieron la cuenta de la empresa a un zamuro cuidando carne y ahora todo está en ruinas.
examples.translation: They gave the company's account to a vulture watching meat, and now everything is in ruins.

examples.sentence: Si permites que ese político maneje los fondos, será un zamuro cuidando carne sin escrúpulos.
examples.translation: If you allow that politician to manage the funds, he will be a vulture watching meat without scruples.

definitions: Literal: to cause something to emit a buzzing sound; literally, "to make it buzz."

examples.sentence: Cada vez que toco la radio, zumbársela para ver si funciona correctamente.
examples.translation: Every time I touch the radio, I make it buzz to see if it works properly.

examples.sentence: El técnico zumbársela a la máquina para detectar el origen del ruido extraño.
examples.translation: The technician buzzed the machine to detect the source of the strange noise.

examples.sentence: Cuando zumbársela el teléfono, se escucha un sonido claro y nítido.
examples.translation: When the phone buzzes, a clear and sharp sound is heard.

examples.sentence: No olvides zumbársela al equipo antes de la demostración para asegurarte que todo esté bien.
examples.translation: Don't forget to make the equipment buzz before the demonstration to make sure everything is fine.

definitions: Figurative (slang): to have sexual intercourse with a woman; to sleep with her (crude, informal).

examples.sentence: En la película, el protagonista le dice a su amigo que va a zumbársela a la chica del bar.
examples.translation: In the movie, the protagonist tells his friend that he's going to sleep with the girl at the bar.

examples.sentence: No me gusta ese tipo porque siempre presume que puede zumbársela a quien quiera.
examples.translation: I don't like that guy because he always brags that he can sleep with whoever he wants.

examples.sentence: Después de la fiesta, se rumoraba que Carlos había zumbársela a la vecina.
examples.translation: After the party, there were rumors that Carlos had slept with the neighbor.
